# Master index of routes toward the sign

Single record of everything attempted to prove the sign of the Paper 46 form (row D): what was attempted,
where, what it gave, why it failed, what works, which constraints the missing object must satisfy, and which ground
remains without an object. It gathers programs RH2017–RH2025, phases 0–212, papers 46–48, the master grid, the
crossword, the plans and context folders of `05-meta-and-planning/`, the literature and the audits.

## Rule of use

**Numbering.** Paper 46 is the paper on the sign (row D) and Paper 47 is the intersection frame; the two
exchanged numbers, and this file uses the current ones. File names of memos that contain `P47` or `PAPER47`
keep their names and refer to the paper on the sign.

**Active phase: 213**, by the project rules. New constructions are stored in
`03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/`; earlier phases keep their results.
Failed paths are not repeated and the discard catalogue is not reset when the phase changes.

1. **Before proposing or launching any construction** the idea is searched for in this file (by object, by
   method and by identifier), as well as in the corpus. Nothing listed here is retried, neither under another
   name nor as a variant, except for a new and explicit reason in writing: which hypothesis, object or class of
   methods changes with respect to the recorded attempt and why that difference avoids the reason for failure.
2. **Every new attempt is recorded here in the same session in which it is obtained**, in Part V, in the
   format indicated there: what was attempted, closest antecedent, result and label, what worked, why
   it failed, reopening condition, detail file. If the attempt changes a constraint, a residue
   or a falsifier, Part I or Part II is updated as well.
3. This file is the only index. The earlier indices (`ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/`) are incorporated
   verbatim in Part IV and no longer exist as separate files. The master grid and the crossword
   keep their structure of cells and clauses, but receive no further records: recording continues here.
4. Labels: PROVED / CITED / CONDITIONAL / ARGUED / OPEN / NO-GO / NUMERICAL. «Repetition» = the idea has an
   antecedent with its closure. «Selection NO-GO» = does not pass the four-point gate; it is not an impossibility.
   «Never executed / never audited» is not a closure (separate list in Part I, section B′).

## Contents

- **Part I — What works, live residues, falsifiers, discrepancies.** Merged list of the whole corpus.
- **Part II — What the object must satisfy.** 241 constraints merged from 508 entries, by topic.
  The current operational specification is in `03-research/phase-212-missing-object/OBJECT_SPEC.md`.
- **Part III — Maps by family.** One table per family of methods for each stretch of the corpus, with
  literal identifiers: phase 212 (III.0) and stretches AMM1 … AMM6C (the acronyms used by Parts I and II;
  MR is III.0).
- **Part IV — Verbatim record.** The files of the earlier index, in full, and the entries of the grid and of the
  crossword that had no counterpart in it.
- **Part VII — Distillate of the verification.** Five work lists drawn from Part VI: label
  corrections, ideas written and never pursued, recovered positive results, antecedents of the rounds
  of phase 212, unresolved discrepancies. **Start here.** It is placed before Part V in the file.
- **Part VI — Verification against the original memos.** Stretch-by-stretch cross-check of the index with the memos:
  missing routes and results and corrected labels. Where it contradicts Parts I–IV, Part VI prevails.
  It is placed before Part V in the file.
- **Part V — Record of new attempts.** Place where everything attempted from now on is added.

File names that appear in the text and are today sections of this file:
`ANNEX_MASTER_MAP_<x>.md` = III.AMM<x>; `MAP_ROUNDS.md` = III.0; `SYNTH_RESIDUES.md` = Part I;
`SYNTH_CONSTRAINTS.md` = Part II; `ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/<archivo>` = section «IV — <archivo>».

## Coverage and limits of this consolidation

Read in full, line by line: the files of the earlier index (≈ 5,000 lines, including the 824
routes of the grid row by row); Paper 48; the specification and open-problem sections of Paper 46;
the complete master grid and crossword; the 24 plans of `05-meta-and-planning/`, `RH-MASTER-CONTEXT/`
(including the 14 fragments), `archive-top-level/` and the plans of `ABCD-CLOSURE-PLAN/`; phase 212.

Limits:

- The indices and maps were consolidated, not the original memos of the phases: each label is the one its
  source assigned. Where sources disagree both versions are kept (Part I, section D, and marks
  «Discrepancy:» in Part II); none was resolved by reopening memos.
- Some rows of the earlier index are truncated in the source itself (noted in III.AMM2B–2D and
  III.AMM5D).
- Of Paper 46 only the indicated sections were read.
- Stretch III.AMM1B was composed from five partial readings joined without a second cross-check against the
  sources; its entries marked «ONLY HERE» were detected by literal search.
- In sections B and C of Part I several nearly identical rows are grouped in one entry; the
  row-by-row detail is in Part III and, verbatim, in Part IV.
- Contradictions that touch the design of the object and remain unresolved: (a) doubly exponential margin
  (PROVED in one stretch, not proved or unverified in three others; the proved bound is
  λ_A ≤ 4·10⁹ T e^{−15.449T}); (b) primes/archimedean coupling («literally false for finite T» versus
  PROVED); (c) composition of the Euler inputs and of the functional equation (refuted as a barrier versus
  requirement of P46 rem:conjunctions); (d) certified frontier (½log5, ½log11, ½log15, 1.035: different
  verification levels, see Part I, section A); (e) first-contact threshold (0.8047 corrected to
  0.74921).

## Phase 212 — Synthesis of residues, falsifiers and discrepancies

Consolidation of existing records. It contains no new mathematics or assessments. Sources:
`MAP_ROUNDS.md` §3–§4; `RULES_AVOID.md` §E, §F, §X–§AB; `README.md` §1 and §3; sections «§3 Live residues»,
«§4 Falsifiers and controls» and «§5 Coverage» (only ambiguities, disagreements, truncated rows and what was never
executed or audited) of `ANNEX_MASTER_MAP_1`, `_1B` (parts A–E), `_2`, `_2B`, `_2C`, `_2D`, `_3`, `_4`, `_5`,
`_5B`, `_5C`, `_5D`, `_6A`, `_6B`, `_6C`.

Provenance acronyms used here: AMM1, AMM1B-A…E, AMM2, AMM2B, AMM2C, AMM2D, AMM3, AMM4, AMM5, AMM5B, AMM5C,
AMM5D, AMM6A, AMM6B, AMM6C, MR (MAP_ROUNDS), RA (RULES_AVOID), RM (README). The identifiers of the sources are
copied as they are. Where a source uses the classical label of the problem «[H]» or «REF» is written (the source declares
a reformulation of the goal; no reasoning is done from it here).

### C. Falsifiers and controls (merged table)

**Extension 212-95-B — no constant self-energy correction.** PROVED: inf_(β integer admissible nonzero) J_sc(β)/A(β)=−infinity. The tests are sums of prime dilations of b_6 weighted by 1/p, with reciprocal mass between 1 and 1+1/Q and primes >Q, scaled afterwards to integer coefficients. Every repair J_sc+cA with fixed real c and every constant substitution ε↦λε of the cutoff, keeping the subtraction A log ε, is excluded. Other counterterms and joint compensations are not excluded; a≥0 and J_sc≤a remain undecided. Detail: Part V, 212-95-B; `03-research/phase-212-missing-object/ROUND_095_B.md`.

**Update 212-95-A — homogeneous cyclotomic finite part.** PROVED: for b=b_6 and X=2^k, k≥4096, the integer test β_X=Σ_(sqrt(X)<p≤X, p prime)D_p b preserves the two moments and all the valuation vanishings, but J_sc(β_X)<0. The general sign of J_sc that remained OPEN at the end of the record of the index-dependent cyclotomic cutoff is refuted. The complete form a, the minorant J_sc≤a, and a different joint compensation are not refuted. Detail and reopening condition: Part V, 212-95-A; `03-research/phase-212-missing-object/ROUND_095_A.md`.

# Part II — What the object must satisfy

> **Notice.** The labels in this Part come from earlier indices and not from the memos. Part VI cross-checked them memo by memo and Part VII.A lists the corrections; lines marked "⚠" have a recorded correction. In case of discrepancy Parts VI and VII prevail.

## What the object must satisfy: constraints gathered from the whole corpus

Duplicate-free merge of `MAP_ROUNDS.md` §2, `OBJECT_SPEC.md` (complete) and the section "§2 Constraints
on the object" of the annexes `ANNEX_MASTER_MAP_1`, `_1B` (parts A–E), `_2`, `_2B`, `_2C`, `_2D`, `_3`,
`_4`, `_5`, `_5B`, `_5C`, `_5D`, `_6A`, `_6B`, `_6C`. It contains no new mathematics.

Conventions. Each item gives: statement; **Label** (the weakest among the sources when they differ, and this is
said); **Class** in which it holds; **Sources** with the identifiers as they appear in the annexes, preceded
by the annex (`MR` = MAP_ROUNDS §2; `OS` = OBJECT_SPEC; `A1`, `A1B-A`…`A1B-E`, `A2`, `A2B`, `A2C`, `A2D`, `A3`,
`A4`, `A5`, `A5B`, `A5C`, `A5D`, `A6A`, `A6B`, `A6C`). The non-canonical labels of the sources (NO-GO,
REF-D, NUMERICAL, FALS, rule, specification) are kept. "[H]" replaces any mention in the sources
of the classical global statement or of the position of zeros relative to a line.

---

### 1. Exactness and margin

**1.1** The identity (G) `a_T(F) = ‖V_T F‖² + ρ_T(F)` is an equality: nothing is bounded in absolute value, by
norm, by Cauchy–Schwarz with loss nor by an o(·) remainder. Preserve the sign before estimating (forbidden:
`|∫gh| ≤ ∫|g||h|`).
Label: specification / OPEN (A1B-A pt 8); PROVED as a constraint in P46 thm:shape (B), cor:shape.
Class: every valid deduction. Sources: OS O1; A1B-A "A3 pt 8"; A5 thm:shape (B), cor:shape (a)–(f),
prob:region (1); A3 "l.151–153, 188–197".

**1.2** Proved margin: `λ_A(T) ≤ 4·10⁹·T·e^{−15.449T}` (T ≥ 1); the precision required of the sign step is
of that order; no margin/compactness/bootstrap argument closes.
Label: PROVED (thm:margin, cor:margin1). Class: margin class W2. Sources: A2 "P46 thm:margin,
cor:margin1; 06 [margin]; 04 l.13"; A3 "l.190–192"; A5 R5; A3 CLASS_001 (O1) "fineness e^{15.449T}" (CITED/ARGUED).
Discrepancy: A2B attributes "Theorem M: λ^A_T ≤ exp(−e^{(2−ε)T}); doubly exponential margin" as PROVED
(G3A-159 G2_B6_R2; G3E-155 thm:margin); A2 says that the doubly exponential bound is CITED not verified;
A3 says "doubly exponential scale NOT proved" (AUDIT l.20–35: "doubly exponential NOT PROVED"); A4 gives the
ceiling `λ^W_T ≤ C μ^{9/2}log μ e^{−4πμ}` as CITED (PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED; uses data from the spectral side; L105;
AUDIT_ZENODO B2). Weakest label retained for the doubly exponential version: CITED not verified.

**1.3** The object cannot be a "bound on Λ + margin" estimate; no main term + remainder unless
exact; main term and remainder equal to the precision of the margin; Schur reductions inherit with
`(1+‖K‖)²`; slack > `𝔄λ_A/|κ_T|` produces the falsifier `(1+δ)Λ`.

### 2. Non-genericity and falsifiers

**2.1 Breaking, not loss of margin.** For each falsifier, the line of (G) that ceases to be
true is pointed out; (G) is false for cΛ with c ≠ 1 however small |c−1| is, and for `a_P` with P > N. An isolated formal
breaking does not suffice to build a certificate. But a complete proved identity with a positive right-hand
side may fail on the falsifier without the auxiliary object losing positivity; that
second failure is not demanded. See the audit of O4/O17 at the end of Part V.
Label: specification (supported by PROVED `REVIEW_003.md` R3-i). Sources: OS O4; A3 "Operative definition
… nonexistent for a_P and c=2" (l.518).

**2.2 Lemma T: the three controls at once.** A certificate whose sign comes from blind squares plus
relations that hold in some control would prove positivity in that control if the
identification with the form and the joint non-negativity of all additional terms also survive; the complete chain must fail
simultaneously at cΛ (c = 2), at the erasure of a prime power and at a Beurling-type weight.
Label: PROVED in the declared class. Sources: MR 1 (`ROUND_013_C` §3); OS O11.

**2.3** It is not an identity valid for every comb / for every weight vector; adding such an identity does not break
closure under O1–O6; identity only together with a property that the modifications destroy; every proof
contains a property destroyed by all the modifications.
Label: PROVED. Sources: A3 "l.196" (lem:shape-ident, B″), "AUDIT l.37–39, 194" thm:shape(C); A5 R4,
thm:shape (B″), cor:shape (f).

**2.4** Classes closed under O1, O2, O3, O4(∀c), O6, O7, O8, O13, O14, O15 do not deduce WP_T; O4^ε, O5
conditional (`κ_T≠0`, `c_{F*}(log n₀)≠0`); O10 CITED/ARGUED; O11 ARGUED; O12 falsifier OPEN; O9 only
curvature of ℓ. Label: PROVED for (A); (A′) CONDITIONAL/ARGUED/OPEN. Sources: A5 thm:shape (A), (A′);
A3 "AUDIT_PHASE193 §0" (AUDIT l.20–35, which lists O1–O4, O6–O8, O13–O15 PROVED; O4^ε, O5 CONDITIONAL; O10
CITED complete/ARGUED primitive; O11 ARGUED; O12 OPEN; (B′)(iv) ARGUED; G1 via (R)(10); H0(b) ARGUED; [crit] NUMERICAL).

**2.5** It cannot depend only on Λ ≥ 0, support, EF, monotonicity; use the exact vector `(Λ(n))_{n<e^{2T}}`,
not membership of a class closed under erasure, amplification, rescaling or Euler erasure; a fixed window does not
distinguish finite modifications.
Label: NO-GO (A2) / PROVED (A2D, A5). Weakest: record NO-GO. Class: classes closed under finite
erasure / amplification of one term; thm:finmod–thm:aP. Sources: A2 "W3, cor:void, thm:finmod, prop:prog";
A2D "G8A-P47 thm:finmod"; A5 R1; OS O2.

**2.6** Not invariant under initial erasure with 0 ≤ a ≤ Λ.
Label: Thm 1 PROVED; Thm 2 CONDITIONAL κ_T≠0. Class: combs with a=Λ on n<n₀. Sources: A2 "W-tail, N_003; P46 cor:wtail".

**2.7** Requirements for a future node: (i) not reducible by (1.4) to zero data; (ii) state which premise fails
at a_P, Epstein, cΛ, DH; (iii) it is not h*, nor tests with coefficients of ζ, nor Möbius inversion, nor pairing
with R_Λ. Forced form (O2): premise false for the null comb with the same Γ_ℝ.
Label: written requirement; CITED/ARGUED. Sources: A3 "l.627" (AUDIT_205), "l.671" (CLASS_001).

**2.8** Separate ζ from every model of tab:cert–tab:models that shares the premises used; separate ζ from the whole

`f_t` and `M_m`; every argument with properties shared with M_m does not separate.
Label: no label (R12) / list / [reading]; A2D PROVED. Weakest: no label. Sources: A5 R12,
S1–S12 "GRID §7", (α)–(μ) "CW §3.2"; A2D "G8F-R162_2501 Thm3".

### 3. Inputs that must be used together (Euler, EF/Γ, integrality, additive structure)

**3.1 The three inputs in one and the same step.** Euler product over all primes, EF with Γ(s/2) at
conductor 1 and integrality enter the proof of (G) in one and the same step, not chained; (E) and (F)
jointly; Euler before regularizing and after resumming EF; Euler over ℕ and EF conductor 1 jointly.
Label: PROVED (R3; thm:shape (B)); (I) within cor:shape ARGUED. Sources: OS O3; A5 R3 "P48; P46
rem:conjunctions", thm:shape (B), cor:shape (c), S1–S12; A5 "P48 §5.5" (descriptive).

**3.2** Use the Euler product over all primes within the sign step (scope correction:
a `p > e^{2T}` does not change the window; fullness is a hypothesis only of the uniform family).
Label: PROVED. Class: `a_P`. Sources: A5 R2.

**3.3 T2.** The axioms A1–A6 (geometry, EF) do not suffice; use A3 and at least one of A7/A8/A9 (Ξ_Q satisfies
A1–A6+A2⁺ and fails); Λ ≥ 0 and/or the line Re s ≥ 1 in a load-bearing step.
Label: PROVED (METHOD-CONSTRAINT). Class: methods that only use A1–A6 (Epstein); axiomatic derivations.
Sources: A2 "P47 §18.2; 139 (T2)"; A2B "G8G-139 R139_005 T2"; A2D "G4G-P46 §18.2 T2"; A1B-D "PTD §3.1(9)";
A1B-E "Phase 139"; A5 prob:region, S1–S12.

**3.4 Arch and the weight from the same object.** Against c = 2 the archimedean part and the weight come from the same
object in the same step (the ring ℤ×ℤ realizes 2Λ only with doubled Arch); against erasure, integrality;
against Beurling, equal spacing of the integers (additive structure, Poisson, 𝓕).
Label: no global label in MR 2; `ROUND_016_B` as a fact. Sources: MR 2 (`ROUND_016_B`); OS O12.

**3.5** The only known identity where the three things enter together is (PC) of R161_001; it sees it as an
equality that breaks; its residues are closed or equivalent to the goal; that no other exists is ARGUED.
Label: ARGUED (depends on `ROUND_010_A` Lemma C). Sources: MR 9.

**3.6** Sign step with ≥ 2 inputs without a common falsifier, including (F) and (E) as a Dirichlet series;
if an input enters only through a prior linear identity, the inequality is excluded in the intermediate object;
a genuine conjunction requires a non-linear step or an input as an inequality (rem:conjunctions). Theorem Φ200/Φ200′:
E (Dirichlet over ℕ) and F (EF degree 1 conductor 1) mandatory by distinct falsifiers.
Label: (i)–(iii) PROVED, (iv) ARGUED; Φ200 ARGUED as a class → Φ200′ PROVED piecewise.
Discrepancy: A3 records "composition REFUTED as a barrier" for Φ200, while A5 rem:conjunctions
keeps it as a requirement. Sources: A5 rem:conjunctions; A3 "l.544, 612, 614"; A3 "l.612" (Theorem O1.A, Prop
O1.B CITED, O1.D, Def O1.2, Lemma O1.E, chaining vs composing: PROVED, O1.B CITED).

**3.7** Integrality: use integrality of multiplicities and of ℤ ((θ)); integrality necessary below 1/3
(without `ε_p ≡ −p^a mod 1` there is a counterexample); theorems "θ<½ ⇒ …" must use integer prime multiplicities;
not coefficient-by-coefficient integrality (Thm I2: 𝒞_ℤ and 𝒞_{01} excluded).
Label: PROVED (R184_014; I2; R163_101c in A2D); A2 gives NO-GO [F3:ζ_θ; W3] for R163_101c → weakest NO-GO.
Sources: A5 (θ) "CW §3.2"; A1B-D "R184_014 Cor B.3′"; A2 "R163_101c (l.891)"; A2D "G5G-R163_101c"; A3
"l.394", "l.67–73" (3); A5 prop:spec (3).

**3.8** N multiplicative + all perfect powers + N(p) integer ≥ 0 + ℓ ≥ 0 forces N ≡ 1 (identifies
Λ, not sign); classes of multiplicative N with perfect powers do not suffice.
Label: PROVED (identification, not sign). Sources: A4, A5C, A6B SQUARE_COMPLETENESS.

**3.9** Couple Λ(n), n < N, with the EF by a route different from the common factor ζ(½+iτ); the strip

**4.1** No finite set of zeros carries a flat-top certificate (row intrinsically infinite); collective
over an infinite set. Label: PROVED (thm:finZ). Sources: A1B-C "PR 47"; A1B-D "PTD §3.1(3)"; A1B-E
"R155_014/018"; A2 "thm:finZ (W8)"; A2B "G7A-155 R155_018"; A2C "l.620"; A2D "G7A-P47 thm:Z/finZ".

Label: PROVED (Lemma R, lem:Rrig, cor:nontermwise). Sources: A1B-D "PTD §3.1(1); P46 lem:Rrig"; A1B-E
"R155_008/010"; A2B G7C-155; A2C "l.621".

**4.3** Dual never attained; no finite ν attains the dual (Theorem O). Label: PROVED. Sources: A1B-E
"Phase 154"; A2B "G7A-154 R154_012"; A2C "l.619".

(net coefficient 0); candidates via moments (A,B) are zero on P_T; every spectral invariant of A_T is window

functional of {λ_A(T′)} in bounded range (bilateral laws NOT excluded).

Sources: OS §3 R-cont (`ROUND_001_C.md` Lemma 1, Theorem R); A2 "06 §R9 phase 212, ROUND_001_C"; A5D "ROUND_001_C (G 2395)".

### 5. Linearity vs non-linearity in the weight and in F

**5.1** Non-linear in Λ: the non-linearity that decides the sign is in how V_T acts on F, not in products
of weights (every polynomial relation on Λ in [2,N) is deduced from the linear atoms); linear use of
Λ∗1 = log is equivalent to shifting the window; linear use with F by autocorrelation is a certificate (λ^prim).
Label: record NO-GO (A2: W6 206/401 PROVED; general R161_018 not proved) / PROVED (R4). Weakest: record
NO-GO. Sources: OS O2 (`ROUND_001_D.md` Lemma A; `ROUND_001_A.md` Lemma B; P46 cor:shape (a)); A2 "W7; W6";
A5 R4, cor:shape (a), prop:spec (1) (exclusion PD/hyperbola/Dirichlet CONDITIONAL); A3 "l.67–73" (1).

**5.2 Polarization.** "Linear in the weight plus non-negative remainder" exists for every weight and that remainder is blind;
`a_T = ‖u‖²` with u containing Λ without its own formula exists iff a_T ≥ 0; V_T is written without inverting or
factorizing the form. Label: PROVED (`ROUND_014_A` Lemma P(c)). Sources: MR 3; OS O13.

**5.3** Anatomy: every term = additive weight × monoid coefficient, linear in Λ; non-linearity only from the
minimizer (REF) or new input; not a functional of the minimizer alone (every first-order discriminant is
linear via `c_{F*}(log n)`); every first-order quantity that distinguishes ζ from a negative is a functional of h*,
not of σ. Label: PROVED (anatomy); PROVED first order (record, R10); unifying fact: record.
Sources: A3 "l.261–264"; A5 R10, "GRID §8 entry 34, 38"; OS O8.

**5.4** R-F1: every A_μ in the exterior form sees Λ only via Λ∗1 = log; R-F2: transversal convexity vanishes by
EF on the full line; R-Q6: the descent of 𝒲 to the gauge quotient already uses exact Λ.
Label: PROVED (R-F1 almost tautological). Sources: A3 "l.520, 522", "l.518".

**5.5** Crosses the logarithmic derivative: the positivities that pass to the logarithmic derivative are only the
infinitely divisible ones (homogeneous cone that cΛ preserves); work on the side of Λ or by a non-homogeneous
mechanism; the first exact non-homogeneous relation in (1, Λ) has degree two: Λ·log + Λ∗Λ = μ∗log²; no cone
condition on log ζ (Thm F2: every conic premise on log ζ or −ζ′/ζ holds for ζ^c).
Label: (6) ARGUED (Identity 5, E2); F2 PROVED. Weakest: ARGUED. Sources: OS O10 (P46 prop:spec (6),
rem:spec-scope); A3 "l.67–73" (2),(6), "l.393"; A5 prop:spec (2),(6).

**5.6** C-hom: window form 0-homogeneous in theta coefficients. Label: PROVED (Lemma H). Sources: A3 "l.539".

**5.7** No Krylov/word subspace from a Λ-free seed with v-homogeneous generators distinguishes cΛ.
Label: PROVED (mechanism). Sources: A4 "P211-5A, P211-6B Prop 4.1".

**5.8** Linear certificates in a fixed basis do not decide a new window (LP/congruence/Schur/inertia).
Label: NO-GO. Sources: A2 "W-lin, rem:bar-lin".

**5.9** Neither linear nor polynomial in the test ((β), S1–S12); non-linear in F (Ω). Label: list/[reading].
Sources: A5 S1–S12 "GRID §7", (β) "CW §3.2", specification Ω "GRID §8 entry 28" (R186_032).

**5.10** Every finite inequality between the weights that separates c = 1 from c = 2 compares the weights with the
archimedean constants; in a fixed window it is a certificate, not a mechanism.
Label: overall reading (not a lemma). Sources: MR 7.

**5.11** Every inequality on Λ that excludes the witness at γ_q is an O-bound of exact strength (circularity N′).
Label: PROVED for unique tests and families of powers; ARGUED in general. Sources: A2 "R166_802; N′ ⚠ [label revised: see Part VII.A / Part VI]
localized; R7"; A5 "CW I1–I18".

**5.12** Every local positive linear lifting is equivalent to a contraction Y = ΘX / Douglas factorization:
only two of three (local positivity, global phase, primitive descent).
Label: weakest REF-D, family withdrawn (A2B); PROVED phase-120 Thm 2.1 (A2C).
Discrepancy: A2B records it as "REF-D, family withdrawn", A2C as "PROVED (phase-120 Thm 2.1)".
Sources: A2B "G8A-phase-120/P3_COMMON_FAILURE_ARCHITECTURE"; A2C "l.652".

"P48 thm:noimport; P46"; A3 "l.576–577, 596".

### 7. Format of the object (Gram, blocks, distributions)

**7.1 Form.** 𝒪 = (ℋ_T, V_T, ρ_T)_{T>0}, ℋ_T explicit Hilbert space, V_T linear, ρ_T manifestly nonnegative
(sum of squares or written positive measure), identity (G) ∀F, ∀T; variant admitted by an exact PROVED
reduction ((L2), 𝔸_M of (S), function 𝖡 of a profile, ladder of powers). Operational definition: operator A_μ
with 𝒲 = ‖A_μ·‖² − ℰ_μ, ℰ_μ ≥ 0 explicit before knowing 𝒲 ≥ 0, nonexistent for a_P and c=2.
Label: specification. Sources: OS §1; A3 «l.518».

**7.2** Deliverable before building: antecedent; ℋ_T, V_T, ρ_T written; why it avoids the difficulty; identity
with (G); for cΛ and a_P the line that breaks. Label: specification. Sources: OS §4.

**7.3 Gram blocks and Schur.** The projection-residue identity and the Schur equivalence do not
exclude a Gram with its own formula whose exact identification with a_Λ is proved independently.
The old general veto on vectors built from F is corrected. Fabricating a block by assuming the sought
sign remains circular. In the class of the following reference, useful Schur requires a block outside the radical with 𝒲_AB ≠ 0 and
positivity proved without passing through 𝒲 on the quotient (Lemma P2-S.3).
Label: PROVED (`ROUND_013_B`). Sources: MR 4; OS O14; A3 «l.600».

**7.4** No sum of per-prime pieces each with a sign: false for Λ past T ≈ 0.697 in the two-position
class; exponential per-prime factors blind; positivity does not localize per prime (N1); each local Q_p
is indefinite, nonnegative sub-comb of mass < 5.37(2) negative on P_T; collective positivity of the full
initial segment; no local unit (prime, finite shell, Laguerre lobe, Fejér–Riesz, positive Gram,
smoothing in n) survives; prime-by-prime or cell-by-cell positivity does not work, a non-local mechanism that
retains archimedean and boundary terms. Label: weakest NUMERICAL (T ≈ 0.697) for the figure; PROVED
(`ROUND_014_B`, Thm SC, N1 computed); ARGUED (A1B-A V.A, A1B-B OA). Sources: OS O14; MR 6; A1 «PL05; NG-E1»;
A2B «G2A-155; G2A-R160_S4 §2.D#40»; A1B-D «PTD §3.1(2); Thm SC»; A1B-E R155_004; A1B-B OA; A1B-A «A3 V.A».

**7.5** Positivity on (0.59, log 2] necessarily crossed between primes. Label: PROVED with T_loc < T*
open. Sources: A2C «l.533».

**7.6** Prime-local carriers empty (Cor H); codimension-one varieties excluded (Cor M1); factorizable in the
tail: at most one critical point per summand (Thm W#); tail wall W# Σ‖S_p‖^{-2} = ∞ sharp; composite wall
G1: carrier interlaced, non-algebraic, non-covariant (excluded prime-local, tail-factorizable,
algebraic, covariant, finite-trace/conformal ergodic, crossed product).
Label: weakest PARTIAL (G1, several not audited); Cor M1 not audited; rest PROVED. Sources: A2B
«G4H-159 G1_B2_R3-R5», «G4H-159 G1_B4_R4», «G8H-159 SYN 1.2»; A2C «l.572».

**7.7** Holomorphic lamination with one pole ⇒ ≤ 1 pair (Thm Z): the carrier must fail Torelli.
Label: PROVED. Sources: A2C «l.690, l.732».

**7.8** R-Π: every Π with kernel 𝒢̄_T is archimedean and blind to the comb (factorization architecture CLOSED);
every A_μ must vanish on 𝒢̄_T; R-Π4: minimal-leakage representative outside the domain of the prime-side formula;
R-K1: every Hankel form using the gap [2,μ) has product structure NN′; R-Q2: levels, classes p,

k ≥ K ⟺ Gram of the primitives E_j ⟺ tails Γ_(J..N); A PSD on R ⟺ K_M PSD in all sizes on an interval;

§18.9 (G 2113, 2122, 2128)», «§19.8, §19.10 (G 2136, 2142)»; A6B «GRAM §§2.1–2.2»; A6C «(§18, §18.9) … (§19.8) … (§19.10)».

### 10. Process rules (restart gates, control substitutions)

**10.1** Restart gate (6 conditions): fails on an arithmetic control of defined class; compatible with the
control without using its atoms; preserves conjugation, transverse support and linear multiplicity; order of
limits; do not use Weil positivity nor real divisor nor adapted metric; contribute a new identity or inequality.
Label: rule. Sources: A1 «MCX "Bibliographic and falsification gate"».

**10.2** 9-point H0 gate (single object; labelled claim; independent mechanism; control with
planted quartet; correct limit object, not mu_ref; explicit uniformity; preservation of conjugation,
support, multiplicity, signed coupling and boundaries; audited transfer; reproducibility).
Label: methodological rule. Sources: A1B-B «XS "Operational H0 gate"».

**10.3** Gate VII (shifted, on axis, information, limits, no-go — no tautological Gram, finite positivity,
single gap, smoothing, pseudoinverse, one level of moments, product of traces —, independence, novelty);
bibliographic gate: every «new mathematics» is UNCERTIFIED NOVELTY until the mechanism is compared.
Label: rule. Sources: A1B-A «A3 Stage VII», «A3 Stage VI».

**10.4** Switching Li → Weil → Pick → Herglotz → index → Hodge, or Cauchy → adjoint, does not count as a new line.
Label: rule. Sources: A1 «NGR "Consequence for the restart"».

**10.5** Each no-go holds only for its class/observable (`𝓗+𝓜 ⇒` does not deliver `𝒞`); it is not used to abandon
statements by equivalence; walls of Paper 36 as class filters, not universal; the `four-way` and
`marginality` theorems do not prove general impossibility.
Label: rule; PROVED in its class; NOT CONFIRMED. Sources: A1 «NGR "Rule of use"»; A1B-A «A3 pt 26; A4
§scope», «A4 §scope»; A1B-B «XS; F00 §6; F26 §6», P36.

**10.6** Progress accounting rule; dependency ledger without circularity; do not open a tenth exploratory
program. Label: rule; guideline. Sources: A1B-A «A2 §Rule», «A3 pt 30», «A1 último párrafo».

**10.7** No hypothesis «there exists a contraction / positive metric / horizontal connection» may remain
unproved; it is not enough to define a metric/measure/current/factorization that exists exactly when there is positivity;
critical transmission and flux vanishing as consequences, not conditions; forbidden to define a star,
metric or correspondence from the divisor of Ξ. Label: closure rule; OPEN; plan requirement; rule.
Sources: A1B-E «PLAN §8 l.331»; A1B-A «A3 pt 9», «A3 V.C»; A1B-D «PP §7(3)».

**10.8** A merely local identity valid for any datum does not select the arithmetic state.
Label: rule. Sources: A1B-E «§8 l.327».

**10.9** Six incompatibilities (Davenport–Heilbronn with mixed variants; unaudited perturbation
law; full form ≠ residue between two truncations; Gram of zeros is not a control of the prime side;
statistical separation does not quantify over all alternatives; partial catalogues not combinable).
Label: PROVED/audit. Sources: A1B-A «A1 §Incompatibilities».

**10.10** The final result cannot be a new coordinate: λ_n^prime ≥ −λ_n^arch ∀n ≥ 8. Label: no label.
Sources: A1B-A «A3 pt 16».

**10.11** Constraints 1–28 (AUDIT_L_SHARP_16 §6): HARD 1, 2, 8, 12, 17, 24(a,b); rest SOFT or
MISLABELLED; constraint 9 (reproduce 2(ξ′/ξ)(1) = 0.046) downgraded to a test object.
Label: see AUDIT_CONSTRAINTS_001. Sources: A3 «l.496–499», «l.456».

**10.12** Barriers every residue must evade: [void], [tail], [sens], [F], [T1/T2],
[lin/det/fam/pat/loc/mom/coh], [margin], [opcalc], [zeros], [crit], [sym]; meta-theorems CW I1–I18.
Label: list; PROVED except where indicated. Sources: A2 «06 cabecera»; A5 «CW §3.1».

**10.13** The only recorded infinite non-uniformity = the exterior (★★). Label: ARGUED. Sources: A3 «l.577».

### Phase 212 — Consolidated map of rounds 1–17

Summary by family of everything that went through the selection gate in this phase. It does not replace
`RULES_AVOID.md` (which prevails in case of discrepancy) nor the memos; it is the quick entry point for deciding
what not to propose and what remains. No round produced a sign mechanism: the global sign of `a_T` on
`P_T` remains OPEN.

Labels: PROVED / CITED / ARGUED / NUMERICAL / OPEN as in the rest of the phase. «Repetition» means
that the idea has an antecedent in the corpus with its closure; «Selection NO-GO» means that it does not pass
the four points of the filter, not that it is impossible.

#### 2. What the rounds establish about the object

Statements that constrain the design. Those marked PROVED are so within the class declared in the cited
memo; the rest is an overall reading.

1. **Lemma T (PROVED in the declared class; `ROUND_013_C` §3).** A certificate whose sign comes only from
   blind squares plus relations that remain valid in some control would prove positivity in that
   control, provided that the identification with the form and the joint nonnegativity
   of the additional terms are also preserved. The full chain has to fail in each of the three controls.
2. **The three controls ask for different things.** `c = 2`: the archimedean part and the weight have to come out
   of the same object in the same step (the ring `ℤ×ℤ` realizes the weight `2Λ` only with doubled Arch;
   `ROUND_016_B`). Deletion of a prime power: integrality. Beurling-type weight: equal spacing
   of the integers (additive structure, Poisson, `𝓕`).
3. **Polarization (PROVED; `ROUND_014_A`).** «Linear in the weight plus nonnegative remainder» exists for every
   weight; that remainder is blind. An identity `a_T = ‖u‖²` in which `u` may contain `Λ` without its own formula
   exists if and only if `a_T ≥ 0`.
4. **Block identities (PROVED; `ROUND_013_B`).** The Schur complement of a Gram is a positive projection
   residue. This does not exclude an own formula identified exactly with a_Λ; nor does the Schur
   equivalence prevent proving the positivity of the block independently. See the correction
   of O14 at the end of Part V.
5. **The set of `c` with positivity is a closed interval containing a neighbourhood of 1 of the size of the
   margin (PROVED; `ROUND_013_A`).** Exact `c = 1` is not needed, only precision of the order of the margin; an
   identity that breaks only outside `c = 1` is not a reason for the sign.
6. **What treats each prime separately, is linear in `F` and affine in the delay is closed or is
   blind** (overall reading of rounds 13–16). Exponential per-prime factors: PROVED blind
   (`ROUND_014_B`). Lemma K: positivity of the Hessians under the declared hypotheses; it does not exclude
   specific identifications of Λ with those positive expressions.
7. **Every finite inequality between the weights that separates `c = 1` from `c = 2` compares the weights with the
   archimedean constants** (overall reading; not a lemma). In a fixed window that is a
   certificate, not a mechanism.
8. **There is no proof by mechanism above the archimedean threshold** (`ROUND_017_A`, verified in
   `R153_001` §1.2): everything the corpus has above `T* ∈ [0.58, 0.60]` is certificates.
9. **The only known identity where the three things of point 2 enter together is (PC) of R161_001.** It sees it
   as an equality that breaks, not as a signed term; all its residues are closed or equivalent to
   the goal (rounds 10–12). That no other relation with that property exists is ARGUED (it depends on the
   completeness of `ROUND_010_A` Lemma C).

#### 3. Ground without a written object and without class closure

None of these has a candidate; each carries the condition a candidate would have to satisfy.

1. **Odd and non-linear pairing in `A_M`** (escapes Theorem 1.1 of R161_002 and is not the
   linear pairing (OR)). The index invariants already proved reduce to `n_−`; another one would be needed.
2. **Positive non-Gram block with its own source of positivity**, not exponential in the weight, coupling
   distinct primes (`ROUND_014_B`).
3. **Potential `V(x,F)` non-quadratic in `x`, convex only for the true weight** (`ROUND_015_C`).
4. **Sieve weights defined by an extremal problem on the exact values of `Λ`**, so that the
   square is non-linear in `Λ`; cross-check first with L2/L4 and with polarization (`ROUND_015_A`).
5. **Maps between windows non-linear in `F`**, with a manifestly nonnegative remainder (`ROUND_014_C`).
6. **Elements built with the additive shift**, not with the dynamics, in an algebra with an exact mixed
   relation between sum and product (`ROUND_016_B`).
7. **Pointwise form `Γ̃ ≥ 0` not coming from nonnegative rates**, with `∫Γ̃ = a_T +` blind term
   (`ROUND_016_A`).
8. **Explicit formula of the per-prime distribution between `T*` and `≈ 0.697`**, where it exists numerically. It would be the
   first proof by mechanism above the threshold, but it is local: the distribution dies at `≈ 0.697` and does not connect
   with global positivity.
9. The slots inherited from `RULES_AVOID.md` §F (O166.802.1, O2601.1, clause (5) of P46 prop:spec).

## III.AMM1 — Programs RH2017–RH2025, phases 0–99, plans 01–24, context summaries

### Annex 1 to the master map — exploratory programs, phases 0–99 and planning documents

Reference note. Consolidates what was attempted toward the sign of the quadratic form in the sources of this
portion of the corpus: the routes index (`05-meta-and-planning/ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/01_…`, `02_…`, `03_…`),
the plans and audits `05-meta-and-planning/01-…` to `24-…`, their `README.md`, and the summaries of the
folders `RH-MASTER-CONTEXT/` and `archive-top-level/`. It contains no new mathematics.

Conventions. The sources phrase almost everything as equivalences with a classical statement; here, by the phase's
isolation rule, those labels are transcribed as **REF** ("ends in a reformulation of the
goal: the global sign") without naming the statement. "Zero side" is used only as the name of the family
closed by P8 Thm C. "Control with violation" designates the Davenport–Heilbronn function `L_DH`, the
deformations `ζ_δ` and the mixtures `F12/F14/F16`, which in the sources are controls where positivity fails.
Result labels: NO-GO with class PROVED / FALSIFIED / CIRCULAR / REF / NUMERICAL / PARTIAL / DEAD without
class / repetition / OPEN. Identifiers are copied exactly as they appear in the source.

File abbreviations: `IDX01`, `IDX02`, `IDX03` = the three index files; `PLnn` = plan
`05-meta-and-planning/nn-….md`; `NGL` = `archive-top-level/NO-GO-LIST.md`; `OPT` = `archive-top-level/OPTIONS.md`;
`NGR` = `RH-MASTER-CONTEXT/NO_GO_AND_RETRACTIONS.md`; `MCX` = `RH-MASTER-CONTEXT/MASTER_CONTEXT.md`.

**Ambiguities and disagreements between sources.**
- Background semibounded modulo log: PL19 §4 calls it "a genuine unconditional result", but in the same paragraph
  says "the precise least admissible power c … is itself part of the frontier, not asserted here"; PL22 §4–5
  presents the almost-all-heights versions as "strategy, solid in form" and "stated here at the level of
  structure". Recorded as PARTIAL, not PROVED.
- Link uniform convergence ↔ LI: PL23 §5 asserts it (day 41) and PL23 §6 retracts it ("is **wrong** at the
  second arrow").
- Phases 70–76: NGL calls them "progress, not further no-gos"; MCX says phases 72–75 are
  "representations of the same signed cancellation, not four distinct closures" and that the QED of phase 65
  is "SUPERSEDED". The correction with proof prevails (precedence rule of 00_SCOPE).
- Boundary triples for W_λ: `OPT` §0 "never attempted, doable now"; IDX03 §E P60-5 "NO-GO
  (PROOF_L_SHARP_OO_001)" and §G "UNTRIED note obsolete".
- R7-03: the index's label "NO-GO (proved, per README)" rests on the README of program 7, not on a
  theorem cited in this portion.
- NG-B3: "DEAD (no anti-Siegel tool)" in IDX03 §A and "remain UNTRIED" in §G (anti-Siegel repulsion as a
  tool was never built).
- MW-5: NGL gives it as OPEN; IDX03 adds "impossible inside the D=Schwartz class, ph113".
- The sources of this portion systematically use equivalences with the classical statement as a closure
  criterion; here they were transcribed as REF without adopting that criterion.

## III.AMM1B — Context folders, historical archive, closure plans (parts A–E)

### Annex 1B to the master map: files of 05-meta-and-planning not read in annex 1

Complements `ANNEX_MASTER_MAP_1.md`, §5. It is divided into five parts, one per group of files. Each part has its sections §1–§5. In the column "Elsewhere?", **ONLY HERE** indicates that the identifier or key phrase does not appear when searched literally with grep in `ANNEX_MASTER_MAP_1…5.md` nor in `ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/`. The search is textual, so the absence of matches does not prove that the idea is not recorded elsewhere.

Parts: (A) RH-MASTER-CONTEXT, top-level files and tools/; (B) RH-MASTER-CONTEXT/fragments/; (C) archive-top-level/; (D) ABCD-CLOSURE-PLAN, eight files; (E) ABCD-CLOSURE-PLAN/PLAN.md, row D parts: l.291–387 and l.388–1362.

### Part A

#### Part 1 — RH-MASTER-CONTEXT: audits of programs, phases, Paper 36 and frontier

Folder: `05-meta-and-planning/RH-MASTER-CONTEXT/`. Files: `RH1_RH9_AUDIT.md` (A1), `PHASES_AUDIT.md` (A2), `LIVE_FRONTIER_AND_RESTART_PLAN.md` (A3), `PAPER36_AUDIT.md` (A4), `tools/omega7_point4_interval_verify.py` (T).

Vocabulary convention: the sources use the label "RH-STRENGTH"; here it is transcribed as **REF (strength of the goal)**. "Ω₇" = positivity λ_n ≥ 0 for all n (Li's criterion with split λ_n = λ_n^arch + λ_n^prime). "Displaced control" = control with an off-axis quartet/divisor, as the sources use it.

`tools/omega7_point4_interval_verify.py`: verifier in rational interval arithmetic that computes λ_n^arch + λ_n^prime for n = 1..7 from the Stieltjes constants γ_0..γ_6, log 4π and ζ(2..7) (Laurent expansion at 1) and checks that the lower endpoint is > 0 (point 4 of the trunk).

Column "Elsewhere?": result of `grep` of the identifier or key phrase in `03-research/phase-212-missing-object/ANNEX_MASTER_MAP_[1-5].md` and `05-meta-and-planning/ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/`. **ONLY HERE** = no textual matches.

Consolidated sources: `05-meta-and-planning/ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/04_PHASES_100-189.md` (curated Part I: universal walls, method theorems, Paper 46 barriers, falsifiers, phases 185–189; Part II: 824 grid routes) and `05-meta-and-planning/ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/06_OPEN_RESIDUES_DEAD_SUBROUTES.md`. Reading and consolidation only; no new mathematics. Labels are those of the source; «REF-D» means the route ends in an internal reformulation of the goal (it is neither a closure nor an impossibility). «l.N» refers to the line of `04_PHASES_100-189.md`.

Common status of row D in both sources: OPEN; no certified negative value; no sign contact.

form `a_T` on `P_T` (row D). Labels are copied from the source without raising them. When the source uses an external
equivalence as a family label (e.g. «E1», «⟺ RH»), here **REF** is written (it ends in a reformulation of the
goal) and the original identifier is kept in quotes so that it is searchable; no reasoning is done from that
equivalence. Source abbreviations: **P48** = `04-papers/48-routes-to-weil-positivity/main.tex`; **P46** =
`04-papers/46-row-d-sign-radial-intersection-form/main.tex`; **GRID** = `03-research/phase-162-row-d-first-contact-closure/grid/R162_2300_MASTER_GRID.md`;

**Ambiguities and disagreements between sources:**
1. **Doubly exponential bound («Theorem M»).** GRID §3 W2: «Theorem M: λ^A_T ≤ exp(−e^{(2−ε)T}), so no margin…» and CW §3.1 I2: «Theorem M (Paper 48 thm:M(b), PROVED in the record…)». P48 §2.6: «A doubly exponential upper bound … is *not* proved; earlier versions of this map stated it as a theorem, and that statement is withdrawn.» GRID §8 entry 51 agrees with P48 («only conditional on Zhu's conjectural law»). The weight of GRID W2 and CW I2 must be read with the withdrawal.
2. **Constant of the contact threshold.** GRID §5/§7 uses «0.8047 < T_c»; GRID §8 entry 50 corrects `T₀(0) = 0.74921 (not 0.8047)`. CW §4.1 keeps 0.8047.
3. **O6 Beurling.** P46 thm:shape lists it in (A) as PROVED via `a_P`; GRID entry 50: «O6 Beurling CITED → ARGUED» (the Beurling sense); P48 prop:EFI: «(E) without (I) by Beurling systems (argued)». Consistent if O6 = `a_P` and the Beurling variant is ARGUED.
4. **W11.** GRID §3 states it as a meta-theorem; GRID entry 22: «W11 corrected: literally false for finite T».
5. **W6.** GRID §3: «caveat: R161_075 says the general exclusion of R161_018 is "unproved as written"»; P48 tab:witness: «general exclusion not claimed».
6. **8D.** Residue phase-37/110 marked PARTIAL in one entry and DEAD in R160_S1 §2.2#12 («unreconciled duplicate», GRID §2).
7. **Number of routes.** P48 abstract: «about seventeen hundred»; grid figure: 1100 (first part of the record); repository rules: ≈1,400.
8. **Row D closed «in the map».** ABCD/ROW-D-REDUCED-STATEMENT §6–§8 and CLOSURE-PLAN §8.6 speak of closing D in the map; the editor's note (§6) clarifies that the map is not a stopping point. The same for «T1 as exclusion» (corrected in §7).
9. The crossword and grid sources still use the label «E1»/«⟺ RH» in several rows (GRID §2–§8); CW replaces it with REF-D. Here it was translated uniformly to REF.

## III.AMM5B — Master grid, lines 901–1629

### Annex 5B to the master map — master grid, lines 901–1629 (late phase 209, phase 211, «Potencias» rounds)

Reference note. Continues `ANNEX_MASTER_MAP_5.md` (which covered GRID 1–900). Consolidates, without new mathematics, the
late entries of the grid. Labels are copied without raising them. Abbreviations: **GRID** =
`03-research/phase-162-row-d-first-contact-closure/grid/R162_2300_MASTER_GRID.md` (number = line of the entry);
**IDX** = `05-meta-and-planning/ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/README.md` (the heading or row identifier is given; «l.» =
line of the IDX when located by grep); **S211** = `03-research/phase-211-sign-sandbox/`; **S209** =
`03-research/phase-209-nonlocal-kernel/`. W = full form (ARCH + POLAR + contact comb); AP = ARCH+POLAR;
`u=63/2=31.5` fixed rate; `f_(N,k,u) = s^k/(s+u)^(N+k)`; `Q = s/(s+u)`; `V_n` = numerators of degree < n.

Result mapping: NO-GO(class) = NO-GO with class PROVED; FALS = FALSIFIED; CIRC; REF; NUM = NUMERICAL; PARTIAL;
DEAD; REP = repetition; OPEN. «PROVED-positive» = sign theorem on a subclass, without global closure.

General observation: almost all entries of the stretch are a literal copy of a block of the IDX (the IDX reproduces the
grid from l.809). The only entries **without a counterpart in the IDX** are the first three of phase 209
(GRID 901, 908, 915: works 006/007, 008/audit008, 009/audit009); they are marked **[NO IDX]**.

## III.AMM5C — Master grid, lines 1630–2098

### Annex 5C to the master map — master grid, lines 1630–2098 (addenda of phase 211)

Reference note. Consolidates, without new mathematics, the late entries of the master grid
`03-research/phase-162-row-d-first-contact-closure/grid/R162_2300_MASTER_GRID.md` (abbreviated **GRID**)
between lines 1630 and 2098. All primary sources cited are in `03-research/phase-211-sign-sandbox/`
unless indicated. Abbreviations: **GRAM** = `POWER_GRAM_SLICES_OBSTRUCTION.md`; **GRR** = `POWER_GLOBAL_ROUTE_REVIEW.md`;
**HYP** = `POWER_HYPERBOLIC_MODEL_GRAM.md`; **IDX** = `05-meta-and-planning/ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/README.md`.

**Counterpart in the index.** This stretch of the GRID is copied literally in IDX (lines ≈1633–2101 of IDX;
constant offset +3 with respect to the GRID; `diff` only shows different relative link paths). Therefore the
column «Where» gives «IDX l.N» = line of the same block in IDX. **No entry of this stretch was found without a
counterpart in the index.** Notation of objects: `Phi` theta density, `A(t,s)` temporal kernel, `K_M` kernel in
exponents, `W` form, `J,K` real pair, `T_h,T_R` Turán-type inequalities, «ECT/Cheb4» extended Chebyshev.

Mapping of results: NO-GO(class) = NO-GO with class PROVED; FALS = FALSIFIED; CIRC; REF; NUM; PARTIAL; DEAD; REP; OPEN.
In this portion almost everything is PARTIAL (PROVED result of local/auxiliary scope that gives no global sign) or NO-GO(class).

Reference note. Consolidates, without new mathematics, the addenda of the crossword
`05-meta-and-planning/ABCD-CLOSURE-PLAN/CROSSWORD-TO-D.md` (**CW**) lines 936–1699. Continues Annex 5
(which covered CW 1–935). Labels are copied from the source without upgrading them. Abbreviations: **IDX** =
`05-meta-and-planning/ROUTES-TRIED-INDEX/README.md` (with line number of the corresponding heading);
**209/** = `03-research/phase-209-nonlocal-kernel/`; **211/** = `03-research/phase-211-sign-sandbox/`. In phase 211
the identifiers are the memo names `POWER_*_NNN` (the index reproduces them literally; it does not use keys
`P211-xx` for these rounds). Notation of the source: W = full form (ARCH + POLAR + comb/contacts);
u = 63/2 = 31.5 base rate; f_{N,k} = atom s^k/(s+u)^{N+k}; «table» = set of atoms (N,k).

Mapping of results: NO-GO(class) = NO-GO with class PROVED; FALS = FALSIFIED; CIRC; REF; NUM = NUMERICAL;
PARTIAL; DEAD; REP = repetition; OPEN. Almost everything in 211 is **PARTIAL** (positive PROVED result of
bounded scope, no global sign, no new window T, papers intact).

**Entries without a counterpart in the index (IDX):** CW «Phase209 — FEΠ and audited contractions» (006/007), CW
«Phase209 — inversion008» and CW «Phase209 — continuous link009» (including SCOPE_P44009). They were not found by grep
(`008`, `LINK009`, `SCOPE_P44`, `FEΠ`, `primorial`) in any file of the index. All other entries of the
stretch have a literal copy or summary in IDX L685–L1650.

#### GUIDING PRINCIPLE (marked by the author as vital)

**The sign has to come from the semiring (ℕ, +, ·): from the interaction between sum and product.** A purely
multiplicative property is not enough (G1, PROVED: the free monoid ℕ^× is indistinguishable from Beurling and from the ideal
monoids of any field → survives O11/O12); a purely additive one is not enough either (comb-generic / generic FE-class: Poisson
over ℤ + Γ holds for Epstein, CA_C_007). The near-coincidences m ≈ kn (residue R9, problem (S)) are exactly the place where
additive proximity meets multiplicative structure. Geometric side (CA_F_003, gap G-F): a ℤ-polarized object whose
positivity comes from amplitude/Riemann–Roch and not from the signature of 𝔞_T — in Weil over 𝔽_q it is C×C, where + and · interact via
Frobenius. **Every new seed must state how it uses the +/· interaction and why it is not purely a monoid property nor purely additive.**

#### Certified frontier

- **Certified positivity (CITED, computationally verified in AUDIT_ZENODO_FRONTIER.md): T ≤ ½log15 ≈ 1.354 (Mori, Zenodo 23281236, margin ≥ 2^{−2904}).** Surpasses Liu (17/16) and Paper 46 (½log5). Plausible quantitative ceiling (Mori 23175060/23363767): window minimum ≲ exp(−4πe^{2T}). Our Galerkin computations at T=1 (μ_even ≤ 2.5e−22) do NOT resolve the real background (~1e−29 according to the prolate model). New falsifier F-DH (Davenport–Heilbronn, a=9/5).

- **Connection layer (SYNTHESIS §4; ARGUED):** (i) the Rankin–Selberg sign (|a_p|² ≥ 0) and FE rigidity (Hamburger/Selberg) share the same blind spot, Kronecker parity d(p^j)↦(−1)^j d(p^j) (X2 of BARRIER_X_001): combining them does not separate Λ from its twins at odd levels; only the residue of even levels p^{2j} < e^{2T} remains (already OPEN in X_001). (ii) **Weight gap:** every built-in positivity found reads the primes at weight ≤ n^{−1} or beyond absolute convergence (FP unitarity, Bombieri–Garrett, Ш/Poisson = Euler at σ=1 (V1.3), Rankin–Selberg σ>1, Knauf β>2, CCM local moments); the only positivity at weight n^{−1/2} is the multiplicative Hilbert matrix (Helson/Perfekt), without FE. The cell «weight ½ + global FE + built-in positivity» is empty in the literature. (iii) Wei (integer-mass quasicrystals) + Kaltenbäck–Woracek: does not apply (a.c. density of Γ_ℝ, signed comb; dead integer invariant, BARRIER_W_001).

bridge can exist. No change in grid states; general node and row D OPEN.

## IV — `01_PROGRAMS_RH1-RH5.md`

### Route index — 01-context/RH2017..RH2021 (prior programs 2017–2021)

Scope: 01-context/RH{1..5}/README.md + all task*/OVERVIEW.md (RH2017 89, RH2018 94, RH2019 83, RH2020 83, RH2021 60 tasks). Paths relative to 01-context/.
Common object: truncated Dirichlet polynomial D_F(t;N)=Σ_{n≤N} a_n n^{-1/2-it}, ω-strata S_k (ω(n)=k), controls ζ, L(χ mod 4/5), random multiplicative f_rand, Liouville λ, Möbius μ, Davenport–Heilbronn L_DH (and ε-perturbations), explicit violators F12/F14/F16, modular L(Δ,s), Maass F13, deformation ζ_δ.
General verdict: none of RH2017–RH2020 carries a sign/positivity statement; all are NUMERICAL-ONLY phenomenology on finite partial sums. Only RH2021 touches Weil-type quadratic forms directly.

Tool families: [RES] resonance/large values; [OMEGA] ω-class/multiplicative decomposition; [EVS] extreme-value statistics (GEV/Gumbel); [RMM] random multiplicative models; [COEF] coefficient-architecture/sign structure; [CLS] ML classification/detectors; [MOM] moments; [PRET] pretentious distance; [CAL] DH/violator calibration; [EF] explicit-formula injection/forward sensitivity; [ISP] inverse spectral/Hilbert–Pólya/Jacobi; [POS] positivity criteria (Weil/Li/GORZ/kernel matrices); [STAT] zero statistics/TDA.

## IV — `06_OPEN_RESIDUES_DEAD_SUBROUTES.md`

### 06 — Open residues of row D: dead sub-routes and admissible directions


REF-D = "the sub-route ends in an internal reformulation of D". It records where a sub-route ends; it does not close the residue.
Labels: PROVED / CITED / CONDITIONAL / ARGUED / OPEN / NO-GO / FALSIFIED / NUMERICAL.
Sources: README "Live residues"; 01–05; SYNTHESIS_188 (Updates 1–3); NT_SYNTHESIS; adversarial reviews 188 (N_011, L2_018, L2_021, L2_023,
L2_024_025) and 189 (NT_001_004, NT_005_007, NT_008_010, NT_011_014); Paper 46 §sec:open; master grid R162_2300 (live cells = rows tagged
OPEN-RESIDUE in 04_, 93 rows).
Abbreviations: P46 = 04-papers/46-row-d-sign-radial-intersection-form/main.tex; 188/ = 03-research/phase-188-closing-D/; 189/ = 03-research/phase-189-new-theory/;
186/ = 03-research/phase-186-toolbox/.

**Barriers that every residue must escape.** Each admissible direction below lists the ones it must escape.
- **[void]** cor:void / thm:finmod (P46): classes closed under finite deletion Λ1_{n≥N} or one-term amplification Λ+c1_{n=n₀}.
- **[tail]** W-tail (N_003; P46 cor:wtail): any comb with a = Λ on n<n₀ and 0 ≤ a ≤ Λ.
- **[sens]** prop:wit-sens: bounded functionals of the weights (a 1e-5 perturbation flips the sign).
- **[F]** F-uniform falsifiers: M_m quartets, f_t, Λ̃, DH/Epstein, ζ̃ = ζ·R (NT_011), a_P, Poisson combs.
- **[T1/T2]** field-uniformity (ζ_K, S₃) and A1–A6 (Epstein).
- **[lin/det/fam/pat/loc/mom/coh]** W-walls (R186; P46 §barriers).
- **[margin]** P46 cor:margin1: λ_A ≤ 4·10⁹ T exp(−15.449T), T≥1 (PROVED). The doubly exponential estimate cited in P46 rem:moriceiling concerns λ_W, is recorded there as unverified, and must not be transferred to λ_A (λ_W≤λ_A has the wrong direction for that transfer). See AUDIT_207_001 and P46 thm:margin with its proof.
- **[opcalc]** prop:opcalc / N_018 meta: linear identities + Bochner/C–S only.
- **[zeros]** zero-information class C_zeros: zero-free regions, density, finite zero sets (thm:finZ).
- **[crit]** exact criticality: centre, packets, mean square (L2_010, N_013, L2_019).
- **[sym]** FE antisymmetry D_{1−σ} = −D_σ (L2_026).

**Statement.** For every T and every F ∈ P_T: Σ_n v_n Re c_F(log n) ≤ 𝔞_∞(F), with v_n = 2Λ(n)n^{−1/2}. Polar-free form: 𝓕_T(F) ≤ 𝔞^♯(F), where
λ^♯(T) ↓ C₀+4 (N_001, P46 prop:sharp). Nyquist form: the coherence 𝒞_T(ω_k) is signed against the samples |F̂(ω_k)|², ω_k = πk/2T (P46 (N)).
(L2) ⟺ (N_loc) (L2_006).
**Status.** OPEN. Main frontier (SYNTHESIS_188 §4.1).

#### R2. (Ω₀): clamped ground-state test
**Statement.** For every T > ½log5: Σ_n 2Λ(n)n^{−½}h_T(log n) < 0, where h_T is the clamped bending ground mode of P_T = (¼−∂²)H²₀
(ĥ_T ≥ 0, double zeros at ±i/2) (L2_008–009).
**Status.** OPEN. Necessary for (L2) at each T, not sufficient (L2_007 §3; rem:bar-loc). The reduction 𝒯₀ ⟺ (Ω₀) is PROVED.
**Dead sub-routes.** PNT-type error terms (cor:void, L2_009 §1(i)); finitely many zeros (§1(ii), thm:finZ); local symbol argument (W-loc);
Tate-free localization (L2_004).
**Admissible directions.** One explicit Weil sum per window, using an individual property of Λ that finite modifications preserving PNT lack.
Must escape: [void], [tail], [zeros]. Nothing has been tried beyond the class statements above.

#### R3. (Ω_{t₀}): fixed fraction / t_∞ > 0
**Statement.** sup_{T,F}(𝓕_T − 𝔞^♯)₊/G_κ < ∞. Equivalently, along λ_t = (1−t)ρ_κ + tΛ with κ > κ*, t_∞ := lim t*(T) > 0 (N_012).
The target is t_∞ = 1 (REF-D). t_∞ > 0 is implied by the target (D ⇒ (Ω_{t₀}), PROVED); whether it is strictly weaker is OPEN (K12_DAMPED_001 Lemma 2.1: (Ω_{t₀}) is invariant under finite comb modifications, so it does not imply D; the dichotomy t_∞ ∈ {0,1} is ARGUED — AUDIT_204_TRACT_E_001).
**Status.** OPEN.
**Dead sub-routes.**
| sub-route | outcome | ref |
|---|---|---|
| decomposition giving t₀ | NO-GO | N_012 |
| concentrating packets (E_γ,C) | collapse to (E_γ) (CONDITIONAL) | N_013 |
| translation / modulation two-copy and multi-copy families | not separable from D (ARGUED); multi-copy → packets | N_014 |
| Ξ unbounded above ⇒ t_∞=0 | PROVED, wrong direction (Thm A) | N_014 |

#### R4. (Ω_Φ): global fixed-point residual
**Statement.** Find a functional inequality controlling the window negativity of a comb λ by its Poisson–Euler residual r(λ) = λ − Φ(λ). Λ is a
fixed point of Φ (N_009; uniqueness CONDITIONAL on Hamburger).
**Status.** OPEN as an obligation, but already treated beyond linearization: phase197 `BARRIER_D2_001_DEFECT_STABILITY_SPLITTING_AND_CONTINUATION_NO_GO.md` and `AUDIT_197_2.md` examine arbitrary non-linear/global defects and continuation paths.
**Precise audited label.** N_010 §3 treats linearization. The phase197 result is a **PROVED reduction**, not a universal impossibility: a bound vanishing at the actual datum retains the required sign there plus sign-free rigidity. Its audit corrects the factor2 of the weight metric and distinguishes Lipschitz sharpness from the concave-class assertion.
**Admissible directions.** Merely saying non-perturbative/non-local is NOT a new hypothesis. A renewed construction must supply an independent signed endpoint or path-remainder estimate beyond the already treated defect/continuation framework. REF-D alone does not close this obligation. Must escape [F], [void], [margin] in the declared class.

#### R5. (E_γ): twisted Chebyshev inequality at one frequency
**Statement.** limsup_T 𝓕_T(F_T)/‖F_T‖² ≤ m^♯(γ) for the concentrating packets at γ. Here m^♯ = Re ψ(5/4+iγ/2) − log π
(exact form, N_001; P46 prop:Egamma-exact). D ⇒ (E_γ) is PROVED (R186_050; P46 prop:wit-Egamma).
**Status.** OPEN. The packet limit equals m^♯(γ) exactly, so the inequality is critical at every γ (N_013).
**Dead sub-routes.** Weakening by a constant (E_γ,C) collapses to (E_γ) (N_013, CONDITIONAL); large sieve and VK are insufficient (R186_051);
centre γ=0 is exactly critical (L2_010); no F-uniform bound (N_001).
**Admissible directions.** An exponent-½ signed twisted ψ bound at frequency γ. Must escape: [zeros], [crit], [void]. R186_050 §4.3 and N_013
Prop 3.3 read (E_γ) as a zero-side statement, so a prime-side proof must avoid zero-location input.

#### R6. Lower half of the bilateral law
**Statement.** λ_A(T) ≥ L(T)(1−o(1)) with explicit L > 0 (Zhu Conj 12.1, primitive normalization; R186_039 BL). By P46 thm:wit-Tc(iv),
λ_A ≥ −ε(T) with ε → 0 already gives the target. In the stated asymptotic lower bound, any admissible L(T) must satisfy L(T) ≤ (1+o(1))4·10⁹ T exp(−15.449T) by P46 cor:margin1. The cited, unverified doubly exponential ceiling for λ_W is not a proved ceiling for λ_A.
**Status.** OPEN. Not excluded by W-fam (P46 rem:bar-fam). Beyond ½log5 no lower bound better than C₀ − A is known.
**Dead sub-routes.** Landau–Widom main term (predicts β_max > 1: NO-GO, R186_039 §2.3); L_Sh = exp(−cN_Sh log N_Sh) is not bilateral (ARGUED);
pattern fit 13.0e^{2T} (W-pat, NUMERICAL); f_t and M_m share the law up to a perturbation (R186_039 §3); bounded-range families (W-fam).
**Admissible directions.** An asymptotic in which the sign enters through the lower half, uniformly in T. Must escape: [fam], [pat], [det],
[margin] (the proved exponential ceiling for λ_A), [F] (M_m, f_t).

##### R9 — dead sub-route recorded in phase 212

- **Phase 212, enlarged system of squares with arithmetic selection or twisting at nodes or modes — NO-GO with class, PROVED (relative to GRAM §18.2 and to the holomorphy of z ↦ P_z of GLOBAL «Square-free scales»).** `ROUND_001_C.md`, Lemma 1, Theorem R, Corollary 2; check `REVIEW_001_LC.md` (modal-coefficient uniqueness lemma included there). In a single identity A_0 = Σ squares + nonnegative remainder over the carrier of integer scales (y = 0), each square is continuous in the graph norm and its coefficients in k are the integer values of a holomorphic function of polynomial growth in a half-plane; hence no nonzero square can vanish on a set of nodes or modes of divergent reciprocal sum, nor be the twist of a continuous functional by a function with a divergent level set of divergent complement (characters of modulus q ≥ 2, nonconstant Ramanujan sums, μ, μ², Λ, indicators of residue classes, of multiples or of fixed gcd). It generalizes, with the same instrument, GRAM §18.7 (finite support) and GLOBAL «Square-free scales» (square-free tail, discontinuity of S_sq); what is new is the class, not the tool. It does not exclude continuous squares with arithmetic index or weights in the dilation, twists without a divergent level set, remainders without manifest sign, nor objects by window or over 𝔸_M. It contributes no sign. The direction of R9 in formulation (S) remains open with a single modulus-of-continuity restriction (Remark 5).

##### B1. Hyperbolic polynomials, Gårding cones, real stability (Borcea–Brändén), MSS interlacing families — score 4
- Mechanism: a polynomial hyperbolic in direction e has a convex Gårding cone; stability is preserved by a classified
  set of linear operators (Borcea–Brändén); interlacing families give "some member beats the expected polynomial".
- Action: the index has the exact separability theorem (front E, Thm 1: D ⟺ positivity of 𝔞_T on Euler-product vectors
  ⊗_p v_p). The restriction F ↦ 𝔞_T(⊗_p v_p) is multi-affine/multilinear in the per-prime blocks — exactly the object
  Borcea–Brändén/MSS act on, and NOT one-variable real-rootedness (Jensen, closed) nor TP (closed). New reason vs.
  Lee–Yang/Rayleigh (front J): J used correlation inequalities in a ±1 gauge; here the variables are the prime blocks and
  the question is hyperbolicity of a mixed form, not ferromagnetism.
- Screen: a Borcea–Brändén preserver statement is a class statement → CG unless the preserver uses the window-wise
  vector (Λ(n))_{n<e^{2T}} exactly (cor:shape (a)). Clause 5: the FE enters through the archimedean block, which would
  be one more "variable"; that is the only place the coupling could be non-ζ(½+iτ). Risk: frustration Thm 1.3 may
  imply the multiaffine form is not stable → that itself is a clean NO-GO worth having.
- First theorem: decide whether P_T(z_2,…,z_P) := det or the symbol of 𝔞_T on ⊗_{p≤P} span{1, z_p·e_{log p}} is real
  stable for T = log 2, P = 2,3 (finite, pure algebra); either a stable-preserver structure or an explicit
  non-stability witness tied to the frustrated cycle (m, 2m).

##### B2. Bakry–Émery Γ₂ / curvature–dimension CD(K,N) on the Markov semigroup of front I — score 4
- Mechanism: Γ₂ ≥ KΓ gives spectral gap ≥ K (lower bound on the bottom), via a *quadratic* (not linear) functional of
  the jump measure J_T.
- Action: front I proved the form without polar term is Markov (λ₀ < λ_A ≤ λ₂) and that Markov/PF/max principle
  don't decide (O2 conserves them). Γ₂ is not in the index (grep: Bakry absent). Γ₂ of a jump process is bilinear in
  J_T: Γ₂(f) = ∫∫ J(dx)J(dy)(…), so it is non-linear in Λ (clause 1) and is not a cone condition (clause 2).
- Screen: must check whether O2 and (1+c)Λ preserve CD(K) — if yes, NO-GO by thm:shape(A) immediately (cheap screen).
  Rigidity Thm 3 (front I: FE-symmetric twists lose Markov for T ≥ T_E) hints curvature is FE-sensitive → clause 5.
- First theorem: compute the jump-measure Γ₂ for J_T at T = ½log3, and prove or refute CD(K,∞) with explicit K for
  Λ vs. the falsifiers O2, O4^ε, Beurling.

##### B3. Modular / conformal bootstrap (Hartman–Keller–Stoica, Mazáč analytic functionals, spinning bootstrap) — score 3
- Mechanism: unitarity (positive spectral density) + crossing/modular invariance ⇒ linear functionals with sign give
  bounds; crossing is an exact functional equation coupling light and heavy states.
- Action: the explicit formula is a crossing equation (primes ↔ zeros, FE as S-transform). Clause 5 asks exactly for a
  coupling of small primes with the FE not through ζ(½+iτ): crossing-kernel functionals (Mazáč–Paulos) are such a
  coupling. New vs. fronts L/N: those built *magic functions* (V1–V3) for sphere-packing LPs; HKS-type bounds use the
  *light-spectrum sparseness* hypothesis, which here is "comb supported on log n, n<e^{2T}" (a finite light spectrum).
- Screen: a functional valid for all positive light spectra is CG (B″) and dual-certificate class (D) — likely REF-D.
  Only escape: functionals that use integrality of light dimensions (log n) and conductor 1 jointly (cor:shape (b)).
- First theorem: write 𝔞_T on P_T as a crossing equation with "light sector" {log n: n<e^{2T}}; prove whether an HKS
  universality bound for the heavy sector holds for every comb (then NO-GO, index it) or needs Λ exactly.

##### B4. Proof mining (Kohlenbach) / reverse mathematics of the window statement — score 6 for a meta-result, 0 for sign
- Mechanism: logical metatheorems extract uniform rates from ∀∃ proofs; WP_T is Π⁰₁ for each rational T.
- Action: turns lem:shape-est(iv) ("no estimate carries the sign", ARGUED) into a PROVED statement for proofs in a
  declared formal system (e.g. a monotone functional interpretation would extract a margin ≥ explicit f(T), which
  contradicts thm:margin if f decays slower than e^{−15.449T}). Gives a sign-free but honest closure tool.
- Screen: not a sign carrier; it is a classifier of method classes (closure by impossibility
  within a declared class).
- First theorem: in WKL₀/ACA₀ with an "estimate" schema formalised, any proof of WP_T for all T ∈ [1,2] yields a
  computable margin bound m(T) ≥ g(T) of extractable form; with thm:margin, classify which g are excluded.

##### B5. Resurgence / exact WKB / Stokes constants of the window operator at large T — score 3
- Mechanism: transseries of the bottom eigenvalue; Stokes constants are sign-definite in many integrable problems;
  median resummation preserves reality.
- Action: λ_A(T) ≍ (bounded by) e^{−15.449T} is an exponentially small eigenvalue — the natural object of exact WKB
  (instanton splitting). Archimedean Γ-factor is resurgent (Stirling); prime atoms enter as discrete instantons at
  log n. Clause 5: Stokes data couple the Γ-factor (FE) with atoms log n directly, not through ζ(½+iτ). Not in index
  (WKB/resurg absent; L41 spheroidal asymptotics is only the prolate piece, covered).
- Screen: the leading instanton action is probably comb-generic; sign would sit in a Stokes constant depending on the
  exact vector (Λ(n)) — admissible in shape, unproven to exist.
- First theorem: for the two-atom model (n=2,3, T∈(½log3,½log5)), compute the transseries of the bottom of 𝔞_T and the
  first Stokes constant exactly; test its sign under O2/O4^ε.

## IV — `AUDIT_A.md`

### AUDIT  A — three arXiv papers (adversarial audit)
Sources: arxiv.org/abs pages fetched  (abstract level). Full PDFs were NOT read; every claim below is labelled from the abstract only.


#### 1. arXiv 2602.20313 — W. Michalowski, "On the Pólya Frequency Order of the de Bruijn–Newman Kernel: Certified Failure at Order Five" (v1 , v2 )
- **Statement (abstract):** K(u)=Φ(|u|) (dBN kernel) is not PF₅. Witness: one 5×5 Toeplitz minor det[K(u₀+(i−j)h)] at (u₀,h)=(0.01,0.05) is rigorously negative. PF₄ is left OPEN globally; locally positive at the tested configurations.
- **Method:** 80-digit outward-rounded interval arithmetic; theta-series truncation with proved tail bounds; cross-check by Leibniz expansion plus an independent interval determinant; mpmath ancillary scripts.
- **Correctness (as far as checkable, abstract level):** the claim is finite and falsifiable: one minor, one point, certified enclosure. The method is sound in kind. A small h=0.05 makes the minor nearly singular (Toeplitz minors scale like h^{20}·Wronskian), so the result rests entirely on the interval width. 80 digits is ample if the tail bounds are right. We did not re-run it. Label: **CITED (certified numerics, unrefereed)**.
- **What it implies:** Schoenberg: PF∞ ⇔ 1/𝓛K is Laguerre–Pólya type. PF₅ failure kills every route that needs Φ to be PF_k for k≥5 (PF∞/TP of the kernel, variation-diminishing of order ≥4 for convolution by Φ, Karlin-type sign-regularity of order ≥5). It does NOT touch: PF₄ or lower, Laguerre–Pólya properties of Ξ itself (Ξ in LP class is not equivalent to Φ being PF; Φ is not PF∞, so the de Bruijn/Pólya universal-factor routes run through the Fourier side and not through the kernel's TP), Turán/Jensen-polynomial routes (GORZ), or sign-regularity of Φ on restricted grids.
- **Corpus comparison:** 104_21 shows PF₂ failure for the *prime-exponent lattice law*, which is a different object, so this result is not redundant with it. 104_83 (Ξ Fourier gate) and R155_046/047 (Sturm/nodal, Karlin): this sharpens them by giving a certified ceiling of 4 on the kernel's TP order. R162_1701 §2.4 and R186_041 TP mentions: any step there that assumed TP/PF∞ of Φ is now dead. **Closes more routes: yes, at order ≥5 only.** ⚠ [etiqueta revisada: ver Parte VII.A / Parte VI]

#### 2. arXiv 2609.02882 — Y. Lamzouri, "A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of ζ are simple and on the critical line" (v1 , v2 )
- **Statement:** >67.25% of zeros are simple and on the line; ≥88.76% are simple or on the line.
- **Method:** this is NOT an inertia count. The abstract says it *replaces* the matrix (finite-compression/Sylvester) framework of Alpöge–Furman 2608.13637 with "a single Hilbert-space inequality" plus Montgomery's pair-correlation theorem.
- **Mis-attribution:** the task brief and 05_LITERATURE L52 describe it as "inertia counts on finite compressions". That is wrong for this paper. Only 2608.13637 uses the compression plus Sylvester.
- **Correctness:** it is a streamlined version of a known-to-be-verified result. Label CITED (unrefereed).
- **Relation to Paper 46 Theorem P / thm:index / R186_028:** no inertia number is produced, so it neither agrees with, sharpens, nor contradicts n₋ ≤ 5/7/8 or index one. It is a proportion statement (density), and a proportion is blind to finitely or infinitely many exceptional quartets of density zero. That gives it no purchase on row D, a ∀-test positivity statement. The Hilbert-space inequality is quadratic in a mollified test, which is the same structural position as R184_009 §2(b).

#### 3. arXiv 2609.15329 — A. Pearce-Crump, "Optimising Selberg's method for critical zeros"
- **Statement:** ≥7% of zeros on the line via Selberg's sign-change method (optimised Zhuravlev 1974): closed form for the reciprocal-square-root coefficients, plus PSD mollifiers.
- **Not an inertia paper either.** It is a sign-change counting method. The bound is weaker than Levinson–Conrey, Lamzouri, and Alpöge–Furman. Correctness: plausible, CITED.
- **Relation:** none to Theorem P or thm:index. The one transferable detail is a "PSD mollifier" optimisation, i.e. a positive-semidefinite constraint on mollifier coefficients. The corpus already covers that through the dual-certificate LP/SDP of Paper 46, so it adds nothing.

#### Alpöge–Furman 2608.13637 (context; already audited in R184_009 §2(b))
- Re-stated without the reasoning used in R184_009: on a finite compression, Sylvester inertia counts negative directions. That count is class-blind: the falsifier M_m shifts the index by 4m and the count cannot tell the difference without prior knowledge of the index. A density statement also cannot exclude a density-zero exceptional set, and DH is the separator.
- It is consistent with Theorem P: both bound n₋ of a finite compression from above. Theorem P is archimedean-only per window (n₋(A_∞|P_T) ≤ 5/7/8). AF bounds the off-line contribution on the zero side. Neither contradicts the other, and AF does not sharpen 5/7/8 because it gives no window-indexed count.

#### 1. L55 — Johns, LP slack κ*

**Statements (from 02-setting.tex).**
- Test class: 𝒯 = even, real functions analytic on |Im z| ≤ ½+δ with (1+|z|)²|F| bounded.
- Arch(F) = F(i/2)+F(−i/2)+∫F Ω_∞, where Ω_∞ is the digamma density. **The polar term is part of Arch.**
- Admissible pair: positive measures μ (zero side, even) and ν on [log2/2π, ∞) (prime side) with Arch(F) = ∫F dμ + π⁻¹∫F̂ dν.
- Cone: 𝒞 = {F ≥ 0, F̂ ≥ 0 on [log2/2π, ∞)}. Slack: κ* = inf{Arch(F) : F ∈ 𝒞, ∫F = 1}.
- Thm (duality) [PROVED in paper, standard; the proof route was checked and is sound]: 𝒦 ≠ ∅ ⟺ Arch ≥ 0 on 𝒞 ⟺ the same on Gaussian packets ⟺ κ* ≥ 0. Method: Carathéodory in finite-dimensional sections, a-priori bounds, Helly.
- Prop (floors) [PROVED]: κ* ≥ −1.3231. This is elementary.
- Certified: κ* ≤ 1.4291572·10⁻¹⁰⁶⁰, using Ξ²P_J(t²) with J = 111 prime powers. The certificates vanish at every zero. The proof is computer-assisted; the code was not rerun here (NUMERICAL for us).
- Unconditional lower bound: κ* ≥ −2.7112·10⁻³, from a certified admissible pair for a slightly larger conductor.
- Theorems B: uniqueness when μ is supported on the ordinates plus 0, or on the ordinates plus summable extra points with ν on the Bondarenko–Radchenko–Seip nodes, or when μ is integer-atomic.

**Correctness.** The parts read are correct and standard: a Delsarte/Odlyzko–Poitou–Serre-type LP. The only nontrivial claims are the numerical certificate and Part II, and neither was re-verified. I found no error in §2.

**Relation to Paper 46.**
- **No overlap in the object.**
  - Johns' κ* is a *linear* program on the whole line with a *fixed* prime gap log 2. It has no window T and no Tate/primitive constraints, and the polar term is inside Arch.
  - Paper 46 def:PD is a *quadratic* (eigenvalue) problem at every window T. The primal is μ = |F̂|²dτ/2π with μ̌ = 0 beyond 2T plus the two polar constraints. The dual consists of signed ν on {|u| ≥ 2T} and β ∈ ℝ².
- **Structural parallels:**
  - (i) Johns' duality theorem ↔ thm:D1 (strong duality, finitely atomic dual sequences). Same Carathéodory/compactness skeleton, different cone.
  - (ii) Johns' certificates Ξ²P_J, which vanish at every zero, ↔ thm:Z (a certificate equals the explicit formula, i.e. a zero-side sum). Johns' certificates are positive on ℝ and not flat-top, so they do not contradict finZ.
  - (iii) The band-limited slice of Johns' cone, with F̂ supported in the gap, is exactly the nonnegative band-limited functions. By Fejér–Riesz/Akhiezer these are the |Ĝ|², i.e. our class at 2T ≤ log 2 **without** the primitive constraints and **with** the polar term. So Johns' statement restricted to the gap is the *complete-form* (non-primitive) version of λ_A(T) ≥ 0 for T ≤ ½log2, which Paper 46 already proves.
- **κ vs κ_⋆: name clash only.** Our κ_⋆ (thm:kappa, sec:combs) is the density threshold for the smooth comb 2κe^{u/2}du to be positive at every window; κ_⋆ ≥ ¼|C₀| > 1. Johns' κ* ≈ 0 is the LP slack. They are not comparable.
- **Usable:**
  - (a) "Certify an admissible *primal* pair for a perturbed conductor to get an unconditional floor" is a primal-side method. Paper 46 has only dual certificates. The analogue would be a lower bound for λ_A via an explicit positive representing pair at a shifted archimedean datum.
  - (b) Hermite interpolation at prime powers as a certificate family. It can be compared with the lattice certificates thm:R / thm:latedge, which pay an O(1/M) edge cost; Johns' family has no window edge because it has no window.
  - Neither touches the sign at T > ½log5.

**Verdict:** parallel and not overlapping, with no error found. Interest: low–medium (tool (a)).

#### 3. L35 — Franchi Viceré, semilocal spectral descent: the flaw

The chain is Thm 1 (CCM 2025 Thm 1.1: σ_S(N,λ) self-adjoint for the inner product QW_λ^N − ε_N⟨·|·⟩, hence real "spectral zeros") → Thm 2 (QW_λ^N(g∗g♯) = Σ g̃(ρ_k) g̃(1−ρ̄_k) = Σ\|g̃(ρ_k)\|² ≥ 0) → Thm 3 (Fejér truncation g_N → g, giving QW_S(g) ≥ 0) → Thm 4 (S ↑ all places) → Weil.

**Flaw 1 (fatal, Thm 2). The ε_N-shift is dropped.**
- ε_N is *defined* as the least eigenvalue of QW_λ^N. So QW_λ^N − ε_N is PSD by definition, and the reality in Thm 1 is a property of that shifted form only.
- Reality of the zeros of the minimal-eigenvector transform does not give QW_λ^N ≥ 0. Indeed QW_λ^N ≥ ε_N, and the sign of ε_N is exactly the open question.
- The displayed "arithmetic–spectral identity" is a finite-dimensional form written as a sum over the spectral zeros of a different operator. Neither CCM §5 nor Connes 1999 Thm 4 contains it in that form. Connes' semilocal trace formula has a remainder, and that remainder is where the sign lives: our phase 183, E_S = Son + R_{S,T}, with n₋(R_{S,T}) = ∞ for T > ½log2 (R183_018 Thm 5.1, R183_019 Thm 4.1).
- So Thm 2 asserts as an identity precisely the step that the phase-183 Sonin NO-GO shows carries no sign.

**Flaw 2 (fatal, Thm 3/4). "QW_S ≥ 0 for each finite S" is false as stated.**
- Take S = {∞}. Then QW_S is the archimedean+polar form, and Paper 46 prop:archneg (PROVED) exhibits a negative vector from T = 0.4608. So a uniform-in-S positivity of semilocal forms is refuted by a single explicit vector. Eberwein §8.1–8.2 report the same numerically.
- Thm 3 also conflates S (places) with the cutoff λ (all primes ≤ λ² enter QW_λ). The "stabilization for λ > M/ε" is only the finite-support statement for fixed g, and it is true but carries no sign.
- In our terms, Theorem X (R186_046) shows that new primes must cancel σ at resolution π/T. The sign lives in the coupling and the complement, not in any S-local block (W-loc, R186_044 Thm 2). Descent "S finite ⟹ S = all" therefore has nothing to transport.

**Flaw 3 (minor).** The numerics (Mathematica, S = {2,3,5,∞}, 4 test functions, 30 zeros) are reported as verifying "Class A" theorems. A form evaluated with zeros on the line is non-negative by construction, so the check is circular.

**Verdict:** NO-GO. The precise failure point is Thm 2: the PSD of QW − ε_N is substituted for the PSD of QW. The failure falls under the phase-183 Sonin wall, prop:archneg, and W-loc.
