## IV — `AUDIT_LIU.md`

### Audit : L70 (Liu, "Certified Weil Positivity Beyond the Unit Window")

Read-only audit. Paper 46 not edited.

#### 1. Identification
- Title: "Certified Weil Positivity Beyond the Unit Window: Source-Exact Block-Schur and Tail-Compensation Bounds for the Riemann Zeta Function".
- Author: Vincent Liu (AI-Native Mathematical Research Lab, Taiwan). Manuscript date 14 Sep 2026, alphaXiv posting 15 Sep 2026.
- Location: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.weil-positivity-riemann-zeta-bounds (PDF read in full, 1392 text lines). No arXiv id found.
- Status: "preprint / manuscript under review" (Math. Comp. per the alphaXiv page). The paper itself says alphaXiv is not peer review and that "a public archival identifier and a finalized data/code license have not been supplied". The certificate is NOT publicly reproducible yet. The author declares AI tools (ChatGPT/Codex) as research support.
- Corpus: R186_027 (phase-186-toolbox, row 2) mentions it only for its method (block-Schur, Legendre, rank-two tail), not for its range. Master grid R162_2300 3A has the residual "S5 §5#14: web hit ... sin leer" (OPEN, "could move [compl] endpoint"). That residual is now resolved: it does move the endpoint, CITED.

#### 2. Setting and normalization (Liu §2, eq. (1))
- D_L = C_c^∞((−L,L);ℂ), H_L = L²(−L,L). "Half-width L" = support of f in (−L,L), so supp h_f ⊂ (−2L,2L) and the sum runs over log n < 2L.
- Q(f) = P(f) + (1/2π)∫A(t)|F_f(t)|²dt − Σ c_n H_f(log n), c_n = 2Λ(n)/√n, A(t) = Re ψ(1/4+it/2) − log π, P(f) = 2Re(F_f(i/2)·conj F_f(−i/2)). This is the COMPLETE form (pole term kept, no Tate/pole-vanishing constraint), arbitrary complex tests.
- Thm A: Q ≥ 2^−151‖f‖² on D_1. Thm B: Q ≥ 2^−49162‖f‖² on D_{17/16} (log 8 < 17/8 < log 9; all of 2,3,4,5,7,8 kept). Rigor: interval enclosures + exact integer Gram residual certificates on two 224×224 integer matrices + analytic complement/tail bounds (block-Schur).
- Obstruction theorem: a specified tail-dropping lower comparison has negative high-frequency limit once L > ½log 8 (concerns the comparison, not Q).

Matching with Paper 46: N_T = {n: log n < 2T}, v_n = 2Λ(n)/√n (v_2 = 2log2/√2 matches c_2), F(±i/2) are the Tate moments A, B, so P = 2Re(A B̄) and Q = W_T = 𝔞_T + 2Re(A B̄) on L²(I_T), I_T = [−T,T]. Hence **L = T**. Liu states his normalization agrees with CC21 (149)–(154) and with Zhu; Paper 46 already identifies Zhu's half-width 0.8 with T = 0.8 (main.tex 142, 302–304, 4605, 4656). Liu: the 17/16 window has autocorrelation support 17/8 (L70's "≈ log 8.4" is correct: e^{2.125} ≈ 8.37).
- Domain: Liu's bound is on C_c^∞, Paper 46's λ^W_T is on L²(I_T) (form domain). C_c^∞ is a form core (Liu cites CC23/Suzuki; Paper 46 has its own closure lemmas), so the bound passes to the bottom. Minor check, not a gap.

#### 3. Verdict
If Liu Thm B is correct: λ^W_T ≥ 2^−49162 for all 0 < T ≤ 17/16 (monotonicity, Paper 46 lem:monoT), and since λ^W_T ≤ λ^prim ≤ λ_A(T) (Paper 46 thm:A, rem:Kprim), also λ_A(T) > 0 on (0, 17/16]. 17/16 = 1.0625 > ½log5 = 0.8047; even Thm A (T = 1 > ½log 7 = 0.973) passes ½log5. **So Paper 46's "certified range up to ½log5" is superseded in range (not in constant) — label CITED (alphaXiv preprint, unrefereed, certificate not yet publicly archived).** Paper 46's own theorems (log5A/W) stay PROVED and keep much larger constants (2.5e-12, 1e-18 vs 2^−151 ≈ 3.5e-46).
Caveat: the constants 2^−151 and 2^−49162 come from a block-Schur with doubly exponential loss (consistent with Paper 46 prop:env / Zhu Thm 1.4); this is a range record, not a method toward all T. No effect on Gate/D mechanism; it changes the first-contact lower bound from ½log5 to 17/16 (CITED).

#### 4. Paper 46 sentences that become outdated (main.tex line numbers)
Rule: keep every PROVED statement; add the cited extension; do not replace ½log5 in statements proved in-paper.

(a) l.141–142 intro: "...and was certified by Zhu for $T\le0.8$ \cite[Thm.~1.2]{Zhu2026}."
→ "...was certified by Zhu for $T\le0.8$ \cite[Thm.~1.2]{Zhu2026}, and, in a preprint under review, by Liu for $T\le17/16$ with $\lamW\ge2^{-49162}$ \cite[Thm.~B]{Liu2026} (CITED; not used in any proof here)."

Question: *"we discarded many fronts — are we really sure of everything discarded?"*
Scope: `03-research/phase-193-creation-campaign/` (all CA_*_000 seed tables, CA_* memos, syntheses, adversarial reviews,
CAMPAIGN_LEDGER.md) and the phase 190–192 verdicts in this folder's README. Pen and paper; nothing re-developed.

#### 0. Strength scale and the base labels the kills rest on

Strength of a kill (weakest → strongest):
- **NUM** — rests on a NUMERICAL datum (finite M, finite T, perturbation tests).
- **CIRC** (CIRCULAR-RISK) — the killing clause itself is ARGUED / CONDITIONAL / OPEN in Paper 46 (list below).
- **1L** (ONE-LINE) — a pre-screen sentence, no development, only "✓" recorded.
- **ARG** (ARGUED) — written reasoning in a memo, no proof.
- **RD** (REF-D) — PROVED that the object *is* the target restated: **this is not a closure**, since a reformulation of D is
  a valid objective, attacked by its constructive tractability. An RD discard means "no progress by itself", never "impossible".
- **CIT** (PROVED-BY-CITATION) — rests on a PROVED Paper 46 lemma / falsifier (O1–O4, O6–O8, O13–O15; lem:shape-ident (B″);
  lem:shape-est (i)–(ii); thm:O; thm:sos; cor:Qp; cor:Tarch; σ_T(0)<0) whose hypotheses were checked to cover the seed.
- **THM** (PROVED-THEOREM) — a written, reviewed proof covering this exact construction.

Status of the clauses that kills invoke (grep-verified in Paper 46 main.tex, def:shape-ops l. 8328, thm:shape l. 8853,
lem:shape-* l. 8370–8527, lem:shape-est l. 8664):

| clause | status in Paper 46 | effect on kills that use it alone |
|---|---|---|
| O1, O2, O3, O4 (c large/small), O6, O7, O8, O13, O14, O15 falsifiers | PROVED | sound (CIT) |
| O4^ε, O5 | CONDITIONAL on κ_T ≠ 0 / c_{F⋆}(log n₀) ≠ 0 | CIRC |
| O10 Epstein | CITED for the complete form, ARGUED for the primitive bottom | CIRC for primitive-bottom kills |
| O11 Beurling | ARGUED (no window form of a Beurling system shown negative) | CIRC |
| O12 ζ_K | falsifier OPEN; (R)(10) is a standard-of-proof clause, not an impossibility | CIRC |
| (B′) "no estimate carries the sign" | lem:shape-est (i),(ii) PROVED, (iii) CONDITIONAL, **(iv) the reading ARGUED** | CIRC unless the seed's loss is shown > proved margin |
| (B″) identity valid for every comb | PROVED (lem:shape-ident) | sound |
| G1 "monoid-only sees nothing" | PROVED as isomorphism; excludes only via (R)(10) (O11 ARGUED, O12 OPEN) | CIRC |
| H0(b) "additive-only ⇒ shared by Epstein x²+5y²" | ARGUED (Γ(s), conductor 20) | CIRC |
| [crit] "precision M^{−3}" | NUMERICAL (EXP_005, phase 190); the PROVED version is the margin bound 4·10⁹Te^{−15.449T} | NUM unless restated via the proved margin |
| doubly exponential margin exp(−13e^{2T}) | **NOT PROVED** (README correction : conjectural law / NUMERICAL) | any kill using it is CIRC |

Seed vs idea column: **S** = kill covers the seed as formulated (a property set); a reformulation that adds a load-bearing
ζ-specific ingredient is not excluded (thm:shape(C) says every proof must contain one). **I** = kill covers the whole idea
(structural impossibility of the mechanism itself). **S/I** = mixed.

#### 2. Systematic findings

1. **REF-D is the single largest discard category (≈30 items) and it is not a closure.** Every RD verdict
   is PROVED as an equivalence, but reformulations of D are valid objectives in their own right. The campaign used "REF-D" as a
   stop. The correct label is "restatement — rank by constructive tractability". None of these was ranked by tractability.
2. **Kills resting on CIRC clauses** (O11 ARGUED, O12 OPEN, O10 primitive ARGUED, (B′)(iv) ARGUED, κ_T≠0 CONDITIONAL, H0(b)
   ARGUED, G1 via (R)(10)) account for ≈15 items. In most of them a PROVED falsifier (O2, O7, O15) or (B″) also applies, so the
   kill survives the downgrade. **The exceptions — killed by a CIRC clause alone — are J4′ (O11 only), H10/G10/G12-monoid (G1
   only), D4 Iwasawa ((R)(10)), G5 VOA (O10 primitive only), SPEC_A ((γ) used the unproved doubly-exponential scale).**
3. **The [crit] screen rests on NUMERICAL M^{−3}.** The proved substitute (margin ≤ 4·10⁹Te^{−15.449T}, lem:shape-est(i)) supports
   every [crit] kill against perturbative/constant-loss methods, but only through the ARGUED reading (iv). The kills are very likely
   right; their label is ARG, not PROVED.
4. **Almost all O-kills are seed-level (S).** thm:shape(C) guarantees a proof must contain a property destroyed by all
   modifications; a seed killed because it survives O7 is killed *as formulated*, and the idea escapes if a load-bearing ζ-specific
   ingredient is added. Idea-level (I) kills are few and solid: commutative collapse/Schur NO-GO (E), RP false for every atomic comb,
   frustration (no ferromagnetic gauge), Markov class via O2, magic function via thm:O, free independence of commuting elements,
   Pila–Wilkie vacuity, Golden–Thompson equality, closure of the Hardy cone.
5. **Independent adversarial checks confirmed every discard**, but several confirmations are one-line "✓" on one-line kills (F6–F15, G4–G11,
   E3, E10–E12, J8, K11–K12, L7–L10). Confirmation of a one-line kill is itself one-line.
6. **Labels that drifted upward**: index README phrase "NO-GO" for Lewis–Zagier (ARGUED), condensed MW-3 generic (ARGUED; PROVED only
   for three classes), Pila–Wilkie (ARGUED in index although near-immediate), SPEC_A (rests on the retracted scale). Recommend
   re-labelling in the README (not done here: audit only).

#### 3. Discards that deserve re-examination, ranked by plausibility of an escape

1. **CA_I_001 Cor 6 — the property set 𝖯⋆ = {(S⁺), pole residue, entire with FE and Γ_ℝ, Markov ∀T}.** The only object of the
   campaign not closed under any declared single modification (O14 OPEN). Discarded as "a separation, not an inequality ⇒ REF-D as
   route" — that step is ARGUED, and thm:shape(C) says exactly that a proof must use such a property. Escape: a deduction whose
   load-bearing line is 𝖯⋆ (first: settle O14's Markov status, then ask what Markov-∀T forces on λ_A). Highest priority.
2. **CA_L_002 prime-site LP / torus certificate (L5/L6).** Attained dual, slackness set = minimizer, exact for |X| ≤ 5 — the exact
   analogue of Viazovska's structure. Killed as RD + comb-generic (true for the LP as formulated). Escape: an LP whose constraint set
   contains a ζ-specific datum (FE/pole via the archimedean column) with |X| → ∞ controlled by the elliptope rank. RD ≠ impossible.
3. **D8 amplitude-exponent homotopy W(α).** One-line ARG kill; W(α) is defined for real α without zero-freeness, and W(k) ≥ 0 at
   integers is PROVED (CA_D_001). The real question — a convexity/interpolation in α between integer data and α = 0 — was never
   examined. Seed-level kill.
4. **CA_K_002 site independence (Arch ≥ Near on prime-sited tests) and (S)/(N) restatements.** RD, but they are the most concrete
   reformulations produced (finite matrices, explicit Chen-type shifts). They should be ranked by tractability, not
   closed.
5. **CA_A_001 residue: Mellin-in-y / Rankin–Selberg in w reaching ζ(½+iτ) on the unitary axis** and **CA_A_003 §4 metaplectic
   off-diagonal packet form** — both left OPEN in the ledger, never developed; CA_A_004 Salié/Kuznetsov OPEN-RESIDUE. ⚠ [label revised: see Part VII.A / Part VI]
6. **P191 SPEC_A.** Its main kill (γ) used the unproved doubly exponential scale; the remaining kills are RD (L* exact) and (θ).
   Re-run the (γ) check with the proved margin; the RD part then becomes a tractability question.
7. **C5/F3 condensed HM with archimedean (liquid) input** — explicitly ARGUED and uncovered by CA_F_001's three classes.
8. **G7/J5 total positivity of order ≤ 4** (PF₄ OPEN) and **CA_A_007 §4 rigged-space eigenvectors built from primes** — the
   memo itself names the escape.
9. **J4′, H10, G10/G12 (monoid form), G5, D4** — killed only by CIRC clauses; escape requires naming a property separating ζ from
   Beurling/ξ_K, which these seeds as formulated cannot do; low plausibility, but the kill is not a proof.
10. **CA_A_002 Lewis–Zagier** — ARGUED; low plausibility (Λ absent), verify ψ_s formula before relying on the NO-GO label.

#### 4. Overall statement of certainty

- **Certain (PROVED, idea-level):** about 15 structural NO-GOs (commutative collapse and Schur NO-GO, RP failure, frustration,
  Markov class, thm:O magic functions, Hardy-cone closure, Hecke multiplicativity, J(1)=∞, inversion false, classical HM class,
  site arithmetic information-free, identities valid for every comb). These close mechanisms, not just seeds.
- **Certain as formulated (PROVED / CITED, seed-level):** about 35 kills through PROVED falsifiers O1–O3, O6–O8, O15 or (B″). They do
  not exclude a reformulation that adds a load-bearing ζ-specific property.
- **Not closures:** about 30 REF-D verdicts. They are PROVED restatements and remain objectives in their own right.
- **Weak (one-line, ARGUED, CIRC, NUM):** about 25 kills. Most would survive a downgrade because a PROVED falsifier also applies, but
  ≈8 rest on a CIRC clause alone or on the unproved margin scale.
- **Honest summary:** the campaign's statement "0 admissible candidates" is reliable in the narrow sense that no seed *as formulated*
  passes the PROVED filters. The stronger reading "these areas are closed" is not established: roughly one third of the discards are
  REF-D (not closures), one quarter are one-line or argued, and the single best object found (𝖯⋆) was set aside by an ARGUED step.
  No discard was found to be wrong; several are under-proved or over-labelled.

## IV — `AUDIT_ZENODO_FRONTIER.md`

### Audit : Zenodo frontier items (survey S1 B1, B2, B3, B5, B8)

Read-only, adversarial audit. Paper 46 not edited. Sources were downloaded to a scratch directory, not the repo.

#### 0. Common conventions
Every item writes Weil's form in the logarithmic variable as Q(f) = 2|∫f cosh(x/2)|² − 2|∫f sinh(x/2)|² + (1/2π)∫a(t)|F_f(t)|²dt − 2Σ_{n<e^{2L}} Λ(n)n^{-1/2} Re∫f·conj f(x−log n), with a(t) = Re ψ(1/4+it/2) − log π. Note that 2|c|² − 2|s|² = 2Re(F(i/2)·conj F(−i/2)) = 2Re(A B̄). So Q = W_T = 𝔞_T + 2Re(AB̄), the complete form with the pole term kept, on L²(I_T), with **L = T** (the support half-width). This is the same matching as Liu (AUDIT_LIU §2).
- "Width log μ" (Mori) means e^{2L} = μ, that is **T = ½ log μ**. So "width log 15" is **T = ½log15 = 1.354025** (prime powers 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13). The answer to the question in the brief is yes.
- Mori V and Guo use the multiplicative window [λ⁻¹,λ] on L²(du/u). This is unitarily equivalent to L²([−log λ, log λ]), so T = log λ and μ = λ² = e^{2T}.
- Ziad uses odd functions with ∫u sinh(x/2) = 0. On odd functions ∫u cosh = 0 holds automatically, so this is exactly **the odd sector of Paper 46's primitive space P_T** (both Tate moments vanish), and λ₁ is the odd-sector primitive bottom.
- Domain: C² or C_c^∞ functions are a form core of the closed form (same remark as in the Liu audit), so the bounds pass to λ^W_T.

#### B1. Mori, "Weil positivity on the window of width log 15" (zenodo 23281236; code 23092422 v1.6.2 = github moriryota/prolate-weil-bounds certificate-VIII; data 23281176)
(a) Theorem O: Q(f) ≥ 2^{-2904}‖f‖² for every complex C² function f with supp f ⊂ [−½log15, ½log15]. In our notation: **λ^W_T ≥ 2^{-2904} at T = ½log15**. By lem:monoT this holds for all T ≤ ½log15. Since λ^W ≤ λ^P ≤ λ_A, it also gives λ_A > 0 there.
Proof chain:
- bounded comparison (Liu framework plus Mori papers VII/IX, i.e. the log 10 and log 12 papers, which were not audited here);
- weighted Schur bound ‖C_p‖ ≤ 66/16;
- out-of-band tail with C = log(Ω/2π) − 1/Ω − γ and Ω = 736;
- Legendre projection with N = 1664 (832 modes per parity);
- block elimination;
- the finite matrix inequality (2.2) certified in Arb by a congruence test.
(b) Rigor and reproducibility:
- The code and 1.8 GB of data are public (Apache/CC-BY), with SHA-pinned sources.
- Checker and proposer are separate programs, and there is an independent re-check. Seven mutation tests were rejected.
- Not refereed, not formalized.

**My independent recomputation (mpmath, no shared code):**
- c = ΩL = 996.5625
- −log₂ d(c) = 2900.286
- C = 0.1369944
- u₀E₀ = 0.136844 < C and u₁E₁ = 0.136341 < C
- Cδ ≥ 2^{-2904} holds
- max R_w on a 2·10⁵-point grid = 4.09133 ≤ 66/16 = 4.125 (paper: 4.0915 on 2304 Arb cells)

The author's scalars.py also passes (log₂(α+βb²) = −697.74 < −697).

Gap: the shipped independent_scalars.py fails because notes/0792_claude_lowmem_generator/scalar_mu15.json is missing from the release. This is minor.

**§B1-run (done , scratchpad).**
- Code: github v1.6.2 certificate-VIII.
- Data: 46 files fetched from github raw; all SHA-256 sums match; restore.py reports "all 24 data files restored and verified".
- Ran `check_certificate.py --bits 1280` (python-flint 0.9.0) in 283 s, 3.5 GB. Result: **PASS_EXTERNAL_CERTIFICATE**.
- λ_min(T) ≥ 2.3979369226737e−70 (even) and 3.9458005898258e−66 (odd), with ε_T = 4.79e−94. These are exactly the paper's Table 2.
- Independent entry check: A₀₀ (even) = γ − ⟨v₀, C_p v₀⟩ = 37/8 − Σ_{n<15} Λ(n)n^{-1/2}·2(2L−log n)/(2L) = 1.3127070815421376549595321292 by my own mpmath. It agrees with the packet's dyadic centre to 40 digits. This confirms the prime set (including 13) and the normalization.
- Not done: regenerating J (7800 s/parity); the analytic lemmas of papers VII/IX.

(c) Consistency with our data:
- Fuchs: 1−λ₄(c) ≈ (4√π 8⁴/4!) c^{9/2} e^{-2c}, with c = 2πμ.
- At μ = 15 this gives about 1.5e−70. Times Mori's Galerkin ratio of 4–5, that is about 7e−70.
- The certified finite margin is 2.40e−70 (even), the lowest eigenvalue of a Schur complement of M+V, which must be ≥ λ_min of the compressed form. **The orders of magnitude match.**
- The certificate does resolve levels about 10⁻⁷⁰. It does so with 3328-bit arithmetic, and all paid errors are < 2^{-300} ≈ 5e−91.
- The final constant 2^{-2904} ≈ 10^{-874} is the out-of-band δ ~ e^{-2ΩL}. It sits far below the true bottom, so there is no tension.
- Our NUMERICAL μ_even ≤ 2.5e−22 at T = 1 (BARRIER_Z_001, M = 64, not converged and still decreasing with M) is an upper bound. It is consistent with the Fuchs-model value of about 9e−30 at μ = e². Our Galerkin data simply do not resolve the bottom at T ≥ 1. This needs no correction, but it should be recorded: **the true bottom at T = 1 is plausibly ~1e−29**.
- **Margin plausible.**

Verdict: **VERIFIED (computational part)**. The certificate was reproduced, and the scalars and the A entry were checked independently. The analytic reduction of papers VII/IX (Prop 3.1, Lemma 3.2, block elimination) was not re-proved here. Label for Paper 46/index: **CITED** (unrefereed, AI-generated, but externally reproducible). λ^W_T ≥ 2^{-2904} for T ≤ ½log15.

#### B2. Mori, "Improved upper bounds for windowed Weil forms with exponential factor e^{-4πμ}" (zenodo 23363767, v3; concept 23175060)
(a) Theorem K, unconditional. With λ_min = λ^W_T and T = ½log μ:
- λ_min ≤ 3.50e24 μ^{9/2} log μ e^{-4πμ} for 50 ≤ μ ≤ 10⁴;
- λ_min ≤ 7.58e24 μ⁵(log μ)³ e^{-4πμ} for all μ ≥ 50.
Method: an explicit smoothed prolate test vector, with the zero sum bounded using RH verified up to 3·10¹² and a zero-free region. These are upper bounds only. Conjecture 1.2 is λ_min ≍ μ^{9/2}e^{-4πμ}. The earlier bound from the same series is 1.362e9 λ^{46} e^{-4πλ²} for μ ≥ 5 (cited by Guo).

(d) Comparison with ours. cor:margin1 is λ_A ≤ 4e9·T·e^{-15.449T}, which is **singly** exponential in T. Mori's bound is **doubly** exponential: exp(−4πe^{2T}).

| T | cor:margin1 | Mori 1.362e9 μ^{23}e^{-4πμ} (μ ≥ 5) | Mori Thm K value (proved only for μ ≥ 50) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 781 (vacuous) | 6e−12 | (2.7e−12) |
| ½log15 | 4.5 (vacuous) | 2e−46 | (2.6e−52) |
| 1.956 (μ = 50) | 5.9e−4 | 2e−225 | 8e−241 |
| 2.5 | 1.7e−7 | 1e−751 | 1e−775 |

cor:margin1 bounds λ_A, while Mori bounds λ^W ≤ λ_A, so the two are not directly comparable. Mori uses zero data (verified RH up to a height and a zero-free region); Paper 46 cor:margin1 removes one zero via the testfam family. Even so, as a ceiling on certificate methods **Mori's bound is overwhelmingly stronger** for λ^W, and it supersedes the "e^{-15.449T}" scale as the quantitative barrier for any complete-form certificate. prop:env (τ_env doubly exponential in T) is consistent with this: both say the resolution needed grows like exp(e^{2T}).

Verdict: **PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED**. The proof was not checked line by line; the bound is consistent with the B1 margin and with the Fuchs asymptotics. Recommended label: CITED.

#### B3. Guo Chen, "Prolate leakage and near-zero spectral clusters…" (zenodo 23297284)
(a) Theorem 1.1: for λ ≥ Λ_m, A_λ has ≥ m eigenvalues in [−δ_m, δ_m], δ_m ≲ λ^{4m+17/2}e^{-πλ²}, via the summation map E applied to prolates with f(0) = f̂(0) = 0. This is an exact residual identity (Thm 4.5) plus transfer and nondegeneracy.
The constants are astronomical: log Λ_m ≤ 700(4m+5)⁴. Theorem 1.8 (m = 1) needs λ ≥ 2^{15}/√(2π) for part (b), and λ ≥ 232 (T ≥ 5.4) for parts (d) and (e).
**This is vacuous at every window we work at (T ≤ 2).** Its value is structural: an unconditional NO-GO quantifier saying the near-kernel has growing multiplicity. Any lower-bound method must separate m clustered eigenvalues at scale e^{-πμ}. It is the multiplicity version of the CCM mechanism (L06/L39).

Verdict: **PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED** (classical ingredients; not checked line by line). Record in the index as a NO-GO quantifier, not as a route.

#### B5. Senke, window (−77/64, 77/64) (zenodo 22871384, v0.3)
The record is **Restricted**: no files are public. Only the description is available. It describes a cellwise Schur certificate plus a Binet tail plus a dyadic transfer, with prime powers 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11 and T = 1.203125.
Nothing can be checked. The window is also superseded in range by Mori ½log12 = 1.242 and ½log15 = 1.354.

Verdict: **UNVERIFIABLE (restricted)**. This is treated as PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED at most. Do not cite.

#### B8. Ziad, "Localized constrained Weil forms: near-degeneracy and a Davenport–Heilbronn first kernel" (zenodo 23145455)
(a) Zeta, odd primitive sector at T = ½log7: 0 < λ₁ < 5.0023e−19.
- The upper bound comes from an 80-mode Legendre witness: archimedean 0.2157094617577142245 against prime −0.2157094617577142240. Arb, ±3.8e−51.
- The lower bound comes from a 431-mode head plus an analytic tail (Schur).
- The coefficients are not published; the record contains only the PDF, and "no separate Git repository".
- The result is consistent with our μ_odd (3.8e−18 to 5.3e−20 at T = 1, not converged).

(e) DH witness: the form for F = Σa_n n^{-s} with a_n periodic mod 5 (0, 1, κ, −κ, −1), gamma factor Γ((s+1)/2)(5/π)^{(s+1)/2}, α = 3/4, coefficients b_n/√n from −F′/F. These coefficients are real but **not supported on prime powers** (for example b₆ = (1+κ²)log6 ≠ 0), and **there is no Euler product and no pole**.
- The constraint ⊥ sinh(x/2) is imposed artificially.
- Positivity holds for a ≤ ½log2: no shifts, and an analytic floor of 0.4289.
- The negative witness at a = 9/5: 140 sine modes, Rayleigh quotient −6.1690e−9 ± 4e−23 (archimedean 2.38352025058 against arithmetic up to n ≤ 36, −2.38352025675).
- **Admissibility:** the witness is exactly constrained, odd and supported in (−9/5, 9/5), so as a test function it lies in the odd part of our P_T with T = 9/5. But the form is **not** our W_T: archimedean kernel K_{3/4}, conductor 5, and non-prime-power coefficients. It is therefore a falsifier only for method classes that use nothing beyond the functional equation, a gamma factor and a Dirichlet series (no multiplicativity of the coefficients, no Euler product). It is not a datum about W_T.
- Its window 9/5 = 1.8 lies well beyond our working windows. The first-loss scale is bracketed only loosely: (½log2, 9/5).
- Plausibility: DH's first off-line zero is near 0.808 + 85.7i. The witness bandwidth is 140π/1.8 ≈ 244, enough to reach it. A 9-digit cancellation is of the kind expected near a first crossing. The result is plausible.

Verdict: **PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED** (not reproducible: coefficients and code are absent). Use: add to the index as falsifier test **F-DH**: "any proposed carrier/certificate method that does not use the Euler product must fail for DH at some a < 9/5". This complements the Beurling and cΛ falsifiers. This is consistent with the semiring principle (the sign must come from the (ℕ,+,·) structure).

#### Index actions
- B1: record the frontier datum (CITED pending human review). The certified first-contact lower bound moves from 17/16 (Liu) to ½log15 = 1.354. Route class: dual certificate / bounded comparison (KNOWN; no new mechanism for all T).
- B2: record the doubly exponential ceiling exp(−4πe^{2T}) as the quantitative barrier for complete-form certificates.
- B3: record as a NO-GO quantifier (multiplicity of the near-kernel).
- B5: UNVERIFIABLE, superseded.
- B8: record falsifier F-DH, with the caveat that its form is not W_T.

##### phase 159 / G1_B3_R2 — Iwasawa mechanism (main conjecture) as a source of prior positivity
- Files: G1_B3_R2.md (Theorem I, Props I1–I2, Cor I′, Lemma S′, Prop C_δ, Prop AP); withdraws W1 of G1_B3_R1.
- What was attempted: the prior positivity of the p-adic school: lattice `Z_p` Iwasawa invariant, acted on by a compact group; proof of whether the scaling flow of Q can act through some compact group. Also the Weil–Arakelov cohomology of Flach–Morin.
- Result according to the memo: «Dead end for the object on this angle». Theorem I PROVED (given CITED): Iwasawa positivity is compactness, it controls only p-adic absolute values; forcing the flow through a compact group gives Sz.-Nagy boundedness + almost periodicity, of strength [H]. Prop WA PROVED conditional on Conj. 2.3/4.1 of Flach–Morin. Lemma S′ (sharp multiplicity ceiling, corrects Rem 2.2 of R1). Prop C_δ: completeness problem named as equivalent.
- Why it failed: the flow `R_{>0}` of Q is annihilated by every compact arithmetic group; the compactness route is of strength [H].
- Reopening: a carrier with a non-compact amenable group («weakest step» clause, `HEURISTIC`/open).
- Closest in IDX: l.5115 «Hodge/twistor/Fargues–Fontaine/condensed polarizations | G8H-R160_S5 §2.3#21 G1_B3_R2/R3 | DEAD [integer-weight wall] | … Weil–Arakelov blind» (it does not name Iwasawa nor Theorem I); «Iwasawa» in IDX appears only through CA_C_004 (l.5853, another route: rationality of ζ(2k)/π^{2k}).

- Files: G2_B10_R2.md.

  `M(s)+M(1−s)`, the differential combination `ζ + λζ′` and shifts by `log n`.

    or as a positive combination of copies of it. It never adds positivity.

  falsifier, `L_2`.

- Files: G2_B6_R1.md (later rounds: G2_B6_R2 §4, G2_B6_R3 §2)
- What was attempted: to take universes of 100 randomly chosen zeros, see where the truncated certificate fails and deduce which
  infinite structure repairs it; to look for a «succession equation» that gives each window from Λ.
- Result according to the memo: RESTATEMENT (panel 5/5). Thm H (horizon H_*(w) ≥ 2e^{2A_T}; above it, the certificate
  survives deletion/insertion/sparse displacement), Cor H1 (random thinning survives with positive
  probability), Prop S (certificate ⟹ lower sampling inequality; second proof of finZ), Prop R: PROVED (conditional
  on a certificate). Below the horizon every zero is load-bearing (DIAGNOSTIC). L_seq = cor:RH(c), EQUIVALENT.
- Why it failed: the only law that fixes the configuration below the horizon is the explicit formula (thm:Z(i)); the
  horizon belongs to the proof, it is not intrinsic (P1, P4, P5).
- Reopening: none.
- Closest in IDX: l.3809 and l.4364 (thm:finZ, finite universes). The random probe, Thm H and Cor H1 do not appear.

  reality (otherwise the falsifier Ξ_a with the same counts); reality is [H]. Cor M4 PROVED unconditional: for the test
  of Lemma K the Λ(n), n<e^{2T}, satisfy a linear identity with the archimedean term to precision
  exp(−e^{(2−ε)T})‖F‖². Prop T″ PROVED (multisets compatible with [H] whose thinning has D⁻=0 a.s.); Prop T′
  PROVED conditional (bounded multiplicity). Lemma E′ (re-derivation). Theorem M = «plunge» of Slepian–Landau–Widom below
  the Shannon number + counting at the Nyquist height: CITED + PROVED, «new as an application, classical as analysis».
- Why it closes: density/reality dichotomy; dead_end.
- Reopening: the memo points out that a law that uses positions below X *and* something of Λ beyond the explicit formula lies
  outside the definition.

  literature are absent.

##### phase-166 — First contact as the kernel of a truncated Toeplitz operator (Makarov–Poltoratski route)
- Files: R166_301_TOEPLITZ_KERNEL.md
- What was attempted: read the contact as ker A_T ≠ 0 of the truncated Toeplitz operator on PW_T ≅ K_Θ, Θ = e^{2iTz}, symbol σ_T/2π plus a polar term of rank 2, and apply the scalar Toeplitz-kernel criteria of Makarov–Poltoratski (BM/MP); also sought a T₁ > ½log5 certified by an «argument budget» Σ_{n<e^{2T}} v_n.
- Result according to the memo: 1.1–1.3, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 PROVED; 2.1 PROVED-CITED (equivalence with a 2×2 matrix kernel of symbol [[Θ̄,0],[σ,Θ]]); 3.3 formula PROVED, non-additivity ARGUED; 4.3 ARGUED; 4.4 «NOT OBTAINED». Route DEAD, wall W-TK = E1 + sign blindness + truncation (audited in R166_190 round 8, «DEAD, wall W-TK, confirmed»).
- Why it failed: the truncated kernel is not a scalar kernel; the scalar criterion gives trivial kernel for every T (also past the contact of f_t); ker A_σ = ker A_{−σ} (blind to the sign); criteria stable under perturbations that move T_c (granularity).
- Positive tools of the memo (2A): triviality of the scalar kernel 2.2(b), invariance 3.1 under symbols with Fourier support outside (−2T,2T), formula of the quartet bump 3.3, sign blindness 4.1; 1D reformulation «contact ⟺ ker A^Θ_{σ_T} ≠ 0 under ⪰ 0».
- Written reopening: O166.301 (OPEN, low priority): 2×2 matrix theory of Makarov–Poltoratski for truncated Toeplitz operators with real symbol; it would still be blind to the sign; «Not recommended as a lead».
- Closest in the index: l.12792 (Makarov–Poltoratski only as literature: «PW-canonical systems: tool only»). «R166_301», «W-TK», «O166.301» and «truncated Toeplitz» do not appear. R164_101 (l.12498) records the reformulation «Toeplitz compression of −θ′ ⪰ 0», but not this route.

##### phase-186 — «Two regimes» conjecture: C ≤ 0 on the almost Sonin-orthogonal part (V_δ = {Son_S < δ})
- Files: `phase-186-toolbox/R186_101_AUDIT_018_AND_SONIN_ORTHOGONAL.md` §2.2–2.3 (original opened)
- What was attempted: prove that the remainder C = ∫c_h ε_S is ≤ 0 where the Sonin mass is small (s₀ = lowest eigenvector of Son_S), so that E_S = Son_S − C ≥ 0 there by sign.

##### phase-188 — Exponential moments of linear functionals + nets for random Poisson combs; independence route through disjoint-lag windows
- Files: `phase-188-closing-D/L2_BUILD_022_LARGE_DEVIATIONS_AND_ZETA_MATRIX.md`
- What was attempted: bound P(M ⪰ 0) for the random matrix of the span of embedded modes by means of the Laplace functional (Chernoff, (C1)/(C2)) of linear functionals and nets on the sphere; then, independence of Poisson functionals with disjoint lag supports.
- Result according to the memo: §2(c) NO-GO (PROVED): exponential moments of individual functionals plus nets give no P(M ⪰ 0) better than ½ + o(1). §3 reduction PROVED, construction OPEN (obstacle: Tate correction of two-bump tests). GOE-type rate exp(−cT²) only ARGUED. §4: in Poisson coordinates the fluctuation of the embedded-span matrix for the completed function is O(1) versus ≍T for a Poisson comb (ARGUED, with verified zero data; «super-regularity», label data/heuristic).
- Why it failed or what it closes: the union bound goes in the wrong direction; the decay demands independence among several functionals. (The obstacle of §3 was later removed in L2_023 Lemma L.)
- Written reopening: construct F_k ∈ P_T with random parts of disjoint lags (resolved later by L2_023).
- Closest match in the index: l.3845 / l.11752 «L2_021–023 random Poisson combs … NO-GO» (it names neither L2_022, nor the NO-GO of moments+nets, nor the «super-regular» reading marked heuristic).

##### phase-188 — Proposition 0: the «archimedean slack» is not invariant
- Files: `L2_BUILD_013_EULER_CONE.md` §0
- Statement: for every positive definite causal kernel k and c > 0, 𝔞_T = (1/2π)∫(m^♯ + c k̂)|F̂|² − 2⟨R^♯ + (c/2)k, c_F⟩; the value of the archimedean symbol at 0 can be made arbitrarily positive by moving a p.d. kernel into the remainder; only 𝔞_T is invariant. #### §3 MISSING POSITIVE RESULTS (d)

##### phase-209 — Mellin identity of the logarithmic arm (CONSTRUCTOR_002, Lemma 6)
- Files: `03-research/phase-209-nonlocal-kernel/CONSTRUCTOR_002.md` (Lemma 6, lines 164–182 of the original).
- Statement according to the memo: Cov_y(Σa_dX_d, log|N|) = Σ a_d q_y(d)[log d + L(d²y) − L(y)]. The weighted transform ∫_0^∞ y^{s/2−1}τ(y)L(y)dy = −2π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2)ζ′(s) holds for Re s > 1. The quotient by the Mellin transform of τ gives −ζ′/ζ(s). Label: PROVED. The memo warns that there is no transport to Re s = ½ nor a sign.
- Retracted or superseded in the stretch: no. AUDIT_002 accepts it («arm Cov exact»).
- Closest in the index: l.9415–9418 («Completeness gives observable log|N|, arm Cov(X_d,log|N|) exact but still without sign»). The covariance identity is recorded; the Mellin formula that gives −ζ′/ζ is not. Low importance: it is a link with the comb only in Re s > 1.

#### §2 MISSING ROUTES (c)

##### phase-209 — QRH quotient with principal target and diagonal of matching heights
- Files: 03-research/phase-209-nonlocal-kernel/QRH_PRINCIPAL_TARGET_QUOTIENT.md
- What was attempted: specialize the row quotient of the QRH source (7/8 manuscript, §§4.8, 7, 8, 10) to the target η=1 keeping the complex phase, with an exact identity (QGEN) via the primitive functional equation, original masks P_χ, root number ε_χ and primitive conductor; on the diagonal w=1−s̄ the last factor has modulus 1 and one obtains the bound (BDIAG) |L_orig(1−s̄,χ)/L_orig(s,χ)| ≪ (Nu)^ε Q^{a−1/2}(1+|t|)^{2a−1}; in addition it is examined whether the conjugate rows u↦u⁵ give an automatic average.
- Result according to the memo: «Exact identities conditional on the source functional equation; restricted diagonal bound. No new row-average estimate, no 4/5 theorem.»
- Why it failed: the real high integral has two independent heights; the kernels do not impose the diagonal; off it the two-point quotient L(1−w,χ̄*)/L(s,χ*) is not bounded by BDIAG; the diagonal bound costs (Nu)^{δ/2+ε}, the same power already published (no improvement); the involution u↦u⁵ changes the norm (Nu#=(Nu)^5 for squarefree u) and does not preserve weights; the conjugate phases only add up to 2·Re, without sign.
- Written reopening condition: an estimate of the average of the two-point quotient of QGEN is needed, with root number, conductor, masks, local corrections and height weights preserved.
- Closest in the index: «Phase209 — continuation of the QRH coherent mean» (l.9671–9681) and «QRH: focal reading» (l.9639–9652); neither mentions QGEN, the diagonal of heights or the conjugate rows. Grep «QRH_PRINCIPAL», «matching-height», «root number», «QGEN»: 0 matches.

##### phase-209 — specification of what would count as positive in the continuation O1
- Files: 03-research/phase-209-nonlocal-kernel/REVIEW_TARGETS_002.md
- What was attempted: review of the corpus (README and index 06_OPEN_RESIDUES R1, R4, R7–R9, W₂; P1_BBSTAR_001; D_CONSTRUCTION_001; R11_2_ORIGIN_001; CELL_001/AUDIT_207; R152_001) looking for an already available positive arithmetic+FE lemma; it fixes four requirements (domain 𝒱_b prior to the sign, exact identity with the FE, inequality B_Λ≥0 without using Q_T≥0 with a restriction that fails on the deleted-prime falsifier, oriented link), an early specificity test of b=Λ against b^{(p)} with defect Σ_{d|n}b^{(p)}(d)=log n−v_p(n)log p, and a list of non-constructive continuations (I+J, projections of J, Gram/Schur/Cholesky/2×2 minor without a new arithmetic relation, Gonek with indefinite weight, formal h⁰ count, sign that dies in the polar orthogonal).
- Result according to the memo: «OPEN; neither a candidate nor a new NO-GO». Finding: the corpus does not contain a positive arithmetic+FE lemma ready to be extracted by change of representation.
- Why it closes: it is not an impossibility; it is the observation that in the residues examined there is no independent positive inequality available.
- Reopening condition: the four data of §2 and the answer to the specificity question of §3.
- Closest in the index: block «Phase 209 — first round» (l.9395–9420, AUDIT_001) and «Phase 209 — second round» (l.9422–9467); they do not record the corpus finding nor the list of §4. Grep «REVIEW_TARGETS»: 0.

- Files: 03-research/phase-209-nonlocal-kernel/QRH_QUOTIENT_ABSOLUTE_MEAN.md

Fidelity correction (PROVED): with the fixed real character ξ of the source (non-principal at each prime of S, all unit classes), lim average ξ(u)R_u(s,w)=0 for both measures of rows, also with a finite product of factors H_{1,u}.

##### phase-211 — Malmquist-type density bound for three poles (scalar uncertainty cap)
- Files: `POWER_ARCH_TRIPLE_004.md`
- What was attempted: bound the archimedean energy on span{e^{−u_j y}}, n≤3, u_j≥a=31.5, by the maximal density Σu_j/[π(u_j²+τ²)] (rational Malmquist basis + Cauchy–Schwarz) and "fill in from low frequencies".
- Result according to the memo: PROVED the density bound; NUMERICAL that the resulting bound is −0.0506 (it does not give positivity); OPEN archimedean positivity of all triples ≥31.5.
- Why it failed: the scalar cap loses ≈0.051 at the worst triple; improving the quadrature does not resolve it. A spurious negative due to ill-conditioning was discarded and is NOT used as a falsifier.
- Written reopening: a collective inequality improving the cap by ≥0.051, or monotonicity of the smallest eigenenergy when separating rates.

#### §2 MISSING ROUTES (c)

##### phase-211 — Arch+polar transport when moving poles: general falsifier in dimension one and sector Pold≤0
- Files: POWER_POLAR_MOVEMENT_005.md (§§2–4; original opened at l.30–47)
- What was attempted: identity (F) Enew−Eold=[Covμ(m,R)+(r0−EμR)Pold]/EμR for the arch+polar quotient with fixed numerator when increasing poles. It is studied whether the quotient grows.
- Result according to the memo: PROVED. (i) Sector Pold≤0: the sign is transported (Enew≥Eold). (ii) FALSIFIED: "arch+polar increases when poles increase", already in order one with numerator 1, by E(2)−E(1)=4/5−π<0 (rates 1 and 2, outside the high range). (iii) Order one, u≥8: E'>0 PROVED. (iv) Positive derivative of order four at confluence 63/2 (only local). Global transport of order four: OPEN.
- Why it failed or what it closes: the polar term enters with sign opposite to Pold, because r0<R. Only the general monotonicity at small rates is closed. The range u≥63/2 is not refuted.
- Reopening condition written in the memo: §7, "dominate in (F) the loss (EμR−r0)Pold by the covariance when Pold>0, or prove directly a transport of a weaker sign".
- Closest that is in the index: l.7337 ("CONFLUENT_FOUR_005, POLAR_MOVEMENT_005 (local) … PROVED") and l.9888 ("Individual derivative ARCH+POLAR>1/420 … only LOCAL"). Neither records (i), (ii) or (iii). The high-order falsifier (HIGH_ORDER_PM_NOGO_007) is there (l.6480, l.7338, l.9893), but it is another case: n=2^17 in the high range.

##### phase-211 — Packets of the Tate family f_n=(D²−1/4)y^(n−1)e^(−uy): concentration, limit threshold and exact recurrence in n
- Files: POWER_PACKET_SCOPE_AUDIT_009.md
- What was attempted: (1) spectral concentration E_nτ²=u²/(2n)(1+O(1/n)), with ρ_n→1 locally uniform and Arch_n→C0. (2) Limit threshold C0+4, the same center E0 as R2/R5. (3) Exact recurrence p_(n+1)=w p_n/E_n[w], ρ_(n+1)−ρ_n=−∂_uρ_n/[2nuE_n(w)], Arch_(n+1)−Arch_n=Cov_n(m,w)/E_n(w)≤0, and the full formula for W_(n+1)−W_n. (4) Re-audit of POWER_BRIDGE_002 without defects.
- Result according to the memo: PROVED the concentration, the identities and the re-audit of the bridge. OPEN a finite arithmetic inequality, since W_(n+1)−W_n has no automatic sign. Arch decreases in n.
- Why it failed or what it closes: the limit threshold reproduces the already known E0. The local convergence of ρ_n does not allow interchanging the infinite sum of the comb. The step in n lacks a sign.
- Reopening condition written in the memo: "a one-sided inequality controlling this difference, or a renormalized ratio preserving non-negativity". Do not require W_n to grow.
- Closest that is in the index: l.9903 and l.7340 (`POWER_TATE_CHAIN_009`: "exact second difference…; convexity open, limit E0 already known, individual family not dense"). The file PACKET_SCOPE_AUDIT_009 is not named. Neither the recurrence in n nor the sign Arch_(n+1)≤Arch_n appears. It may be RECORDED-MERGED if one accepts that the TATE_CHAIN entry covers the same chain. It is reported here by strict rule.

- Files: POWER_GEOMETRIC_TRANSFER_015.md §7; POWER_MIXTURE_AUDIT_015.md §4 (and §2: hypothesis u>1)

#### §2 MISSING ROUTES (c)

##### phase-211 — Exact Schur complement on the archimedean spectral band and its Neumann expansion in the comb (ROUND_008_A)
- Files: 03-research/phase-211-sign-sandbox/ROUND_008_A.md (128 lines)
- What was attempted: split P_T into the band B_t = span{eigenvectors of Arch with α_l ≤ t}, threshold t ≥ π_+ = λ_max(Π) (sharp band of ROUND_005_E), and its complement C_t. In that partition Arch is block diagonal and the blocks are coupled only by the comb. Exact Schur complement S_T = D_b − Π_bb − Π_bc(Arch_c − Π_cc)^{−1}Π_cb, and Neumann expansion of the resolvent in the comb: S_T^{(K)} = D_b − Π_bb − Σ_{k≤K} T_k, polynomial of degree K+2 in v with only archimedean coefficients. It is the step requested by ROUND_006_B §5(iii).
- Result according to the memo: PROVED Thm 2.1 (exact reduction to the band: coercivity of the complement without conditions if t_c > π_+), Thm 3.1 (Neumann expansion with two-sided tail S_T − S_T^{(K)} = −Y*X^{K+1}(1−X)^{−1}Y, ε_K = max{r_+^{K+1}/(1−r_+), r_−^{K+1}/(1+r_−)}), Cor 3.2 ((a) λ_min(S^{(K)}) < 0 with K odd ⇒ λ_A < 0; (b) sufficient criterion of positivity with the tail; (c) necessary degree K+1 ≳ log(‖Y*Y‖/((1−r)λ_min S_T))/log(1/r)), Rem 3.3 (the truncation is not homogeneous in c, unlike the families of words of 6B). The announced numerical §4 ("if it rejects c = 1.01 with bounded degree") does not exist: the file ends at Rem. 3.3. No final verdict written.
- Why it failed or what it closes: the memo does not close it; the quantification of Cor 3.2(c) (degree ∝ log(1/λ_A)/log(1/r)) is the same wall that ROUND_008_D later measures on E_T. Class: Neumann truncations of bounded degree on the archimedean spectral band.
- Reopening condition written in the memo: none explicit (§4 remains undone).

#### §3 Missing or incomplete routes (c)

##### phase-211 GRAM §8.11 — shifting the half-plane in the functional calculus (A−a not accretive)
- Files: POWER_GRAM_SLICES_OBSTRUCTION.md l.1061.
- What was attempted: use the bound for contractions of §8.10 applied to the Cayley transform of A−a when the rates are ≥a.
- Result according to the memo: with f(r)=e^{−ar}−e^{−br}, b>a, Re⟨(A−a)f,f⟩=−a‖f‖²<0; "controlling a function only on Re u≥a does not authorize applying a bound for contractions to the Cayley transform of A−a". Moreover, an absolute dimension-free error bound does not by itself provide the relative compensation.
- Why it fails: A−a is not accretive in general.
- Reopening: not written (only "no such compensation has been constructed").
- Closest in the index: MI 10648 (§8.11) and MI 10644 (§8.10, "A=−D is accretive") — neither mentions the failure of the shift.

##### phase-211 GRAM §17 — bibliographic antecedent of RES-SOS (divisor graph / von Mangoldt chain)
- Files: l.1622.
- What was attempted: cross-check of the SOS (RES-SOS) with Keller–Pinchover–Pogorzelski (graph forms with potential, §4.2) and Alexeev et al. (chain P(q→q/m)=Λ(m)/log q, Ex. 2.4, §10.1): the weight ν_d(q)=I_{dq²}log q reproduces the conductances.
- Result according to the memo: general antecedent of the representation; subinvariance is not transferred; D_q>0 is proved separately; "adds neither sign nor a closing method".
- Why it matters: it is an external antecedent of the form of the identity; its absence may lead to claiming novelty or to relaunching the "criticality on graphs" route.
- Closest in the index: MI 10803–10805 (RES-SOS, antecedents only 019/209); grep "Keller", "Pinchover", "Alexeev" without relevant match (MI 13102 is another topic).

#### §4 Missing positive results/diagnostics (d)

##### GRAM §4.1 — covariance identity for ∂t∂s log A
- Statement (l.166–172): for t,s>0, q=t+s+2r, p=−Φ'/Φ, μ ∝ qΦ(t+r)Φ(s+r)dr: ∂t∂s log A = Cov_μ(p(t+r),p(s+r)) − Cov_μ(1/q, p(t+r)+p(s+r)) − (E_μ[1/q])². No label of its own (section PROVED); the memo warns that μ depends on both nodes and is not a Gram.
- Index: absent (MI 10614–10620 do not cite it). Not retracted.

##### GRAM §4.1 — second NUMERICAL diagnostic at the origin
- Statement (l.174–182): exact coefficients a_ij; with ten modes, 70 digits: A00≈0.010060677517939842554 and [t⁵s⁵]log A ≈ +1.904303578425…; "NUMERICAL, not certified"; it does not reproduce the quartic falsifier in theta; decision: real condition OPEN, do not start a table of orders.
- Index: only the first diagnostic is there (MI 10614 "A single real block of five nodes gave no numerical falsifier"); the second is absent (grep "1.9043", "Second diagnostic" without result).

##### GRAM §12 — "Gate history": test at the origin and mpmath diagnostics
- Statement (l.1263): if V''(0)>0, the test at the origin is 10V⁽⁴⁾(0)²−3V''(0)V⁽⁶⁾(0)≥0, not deducible from V'''>0; mpmath diagnostics (60 digits, 20 modes, r=0,¼,½,¾,1,3/2) favorable, NOT certified, not used. Superseded by the certificate of §12.1.
- Index: absent (MI 10759 only the certificate). Low importance.

#### §2 MISSING ROUTES (c)

##### phase-124 — Schur reduction of the Tate collar: the collar as a primitive–Tate cross block
- Files: P124_011_SCHUR_COLLAR_REDUCTION.md
- What was attempted: translate the Schur/Douglas block computation of D.190 to q_T = ⟨L_T F,G⟩ and J_+(F) = ⟨ρ_{+,T},F⟩, in order to control the collar by means of a Schur complement.
- Result according to the memo: «EXACT REDUCTION / COLLAR IS A CONCRETE CROSSBLOCK, NOT YET CONTROLLED». c=0 on a parity branch is equivalent to (6.2) vanishing. Schur/Douglas would prove it with positivity of the augmented primitive+Tate block, which is equivalent to the range condition ρ_{+,T} ∈ Ran L_T^{1/2}.
- Why it failed or what it closes: the positivity already proved (L_T ≥ 0 on primitives) does not include the augmented block. The reference energy bounds ρ before the shorting; at first contact the reference energy equals the load energy and the collar may fail to vanish. D.190 cannot be used as a free estimate.
- Reopening condition written in the memo: prove the concrete range/shorting statement for the column ρ_{+,T}, not a generic leakage bound nor the constant-one factorization of D.190 as a black box.
- Closest that is in the index: l.4672 / l.11915 (P124_013, Σ(T) = B − X*L^{-1}X ≥ 0, which uses this same Schur); l.4671 (P124_004-008). P124_011 does not appear.

##### phase-124 — Causal storage: the seam gate reduced to a scalar surplus
- Files: P124_012_CAUSAL_STORAGE_SCALAR_SEAM_GATE.md (original opened, ll.120–160)
- What was attempted: use the causal storage identity of phase 120 (half-line field 𝔥_F, output per prime cell E_{p,T}) to force the seam to vanish at first contact.
- Result according to the memo: «PROVED REDUCTION / NO SIGN». (3.2) proves K_T^seam 𝔥_F = 0 ⟺ 𝒞_T(F) = 0 ⟺ 𝒞_T(F) ≤ 0. The new goal is L_T F = 0, F ∈ 𝒫_T ⟹ 𝒞_T(F) ≤ 0. That sign is not proved.
- Why it failed or what it closes: the identity rewrites the transversal seam norm as a coherent surplus, but gives no upper sign bound. The completed square of phase 120 does not suffice either: it would prove a global square, not vanishing at equality.
- Reopening condition written in the memo: prove the one-sided scalar estimate (3.3) from the Euler source without supertrace. With (3.3), the first-cell rigidity of P121 would give F = 0.
- Closest that is in the index: l.4578 / l.4828 (Gate S, P122_028, constant flow); l.5069 (two-gate criterion). Neither the scalar reduction nor 𝒞_T is recorded.

##### III.3 Precise answers requested

- **Object.** Exact Schur complement of a_T=Arch−Π over the archimedean spectral band B_t (finite, of dimension
  N_Arch(t)), with t_c > π_+. In that partition Arch is block-diagonal and the coupling is only −Π_cb.
- **How the weights enter.** Π=Σ v_n S_{x_n} is linear in v. With the threshold t fixed, S_T=D_b−Π_bb−Σ_{k≥0}T_k, and T_k is a
  homogeneous polynomial of degree k+2 in (v_n) (Thm 3.1(iii), l.93–100). Altogether it is a power series in v
  convergent if r<1: degree 0 (D_b), degree 1 (−Π_bb) and degrees ≥2 (−T_k). The truncation S^{(K)} has degree K+2.
- **Is the leading term affine?** The part of degree ≤1, D_b−Π_bb, is affine in v. The first term of the Neumann
  series, T_0=Π_bc Arch_c^{−1}Π_cb=Y*Y, is quadratic. Hence, according to the memo's formulas, the series starts with an affine
  part followed by terms of degree ≥2, and its first properly Neumann term is not affine. There is a caveat that
  the memo does not develop: the band depends on v through π_+ if one takes t=π_+. The degree is defined only "for a fixed
  threshold t" (l.93).
- **Sign of the higher terms.** The memo does not give the sign of each T_k. It only asserts this: (1) Y*Y ⪯ (π²/t_c)·1_B
  (l.103), only an upper bound; (2) the tail after K odd is ⪰ 0 in the form Y*f_K(X)Y, and therefore S_T ⪯ S_T^{(K)}
  (l.104, l.114); (3) for all K, S_T ⪰ S_T^{(K)}−(r_+^{K+1}/(1−r_+))Y*Y. It says nothing about the sign of T_k for k ≥ 1
  separately.
- **What remains unwritten.** The numerical §4 announced in l.126 and the verdict. The value of r or of K* is not recorded for
  any window.
- **Nearby index entries.** P211-8D: l.6401 "NO-GO (finite-degree Neumann class) — REVIEW_005: ARGUED +
  NUMERICAL; Thm 2 CONDITIONAL on (H₋)", with reopening "Chebyshev resummation (same log(1/λ_A) wall) or signed
  resummation on V"; l.9796; l.878 "1.16 … ARGUED"; l.7317. P211-8E: l.6418 and l.9798 (margin law; does not treat this
  object). Reopening that the index assigns to this object: l.6149 (P211-6B) "exact Schur complement on a band; Neumann
  degree". It is exactly 8A, and the index does not record that it was done.

##### 114_a_56 — exact criterion of selective quotient
- Statement: the unital quotients of a moment block F_p^m are projections to coordinates F_p^S. They separate if and only if S meets the support of every code difference. The sharp RR is equivalent to κ(r,Q;p)·log p − log #I_r(Q) = o(t²).
- Label: Thm 2.1, unconditional per block.
- Index: only as a reopening condition (l.20647).

##### 114_a_84, a_85, a_86, a_87, a_99 — proved conditional criteria for prime regularity
- a_84 Thm 2.1: if the plane is tame and p cancels in the scalar monoid, then there is p-regularity in every arity. It is correct as a conditional theorem; a104 refutes the tameness of the signed plane.
- a_85 Prop 2.1 and Thm 3.1: the classes of E_cancel are the connected components of the sandwich graph. There is p-saturation if p-convexity and the lifting of split paths hold.
- a_86 Thm 1.1: S is componentwise convex if and only if every component of G∖S meets at most one component of G[S]. It is a proved graph theorem.
- a_87 Thm 2.1 and Cor 3.1: if the real residual embedding ρ=(ρ_u) into ℝ^(ℝ>0) is faithful, scalar p-regularity is obtained for every p. Gate: H7-REAL-RES plus H7-TAME-PLANE.
- a_99 Thm 3.1: TAME plus CONTEXT-RETRACT forbid every rigid even parity move.
- Index: the files appear at l.20658 only as “OPEN in most”; these criteria are not recorded.

##### 114_a_93 / a_94 — exact Smith form of the parity model
- Statement: the 6×4 incidence has Smith diag(1,1,1,2). The zero-fold differences have factors 1,1,2, with witness w and detector ω. An odd column brings the factors to 1.
- Label: PROVED in the model; the memo says explicitly that it is not Haran torsion.
- It is neutralized by a_95.
- Index: absent.

##### 114_d_101 / d_102 — maximal neutral relation and Fourier–Poisson complex
- d_101: canonical Euler–Gamma maximal neutral relation (graph of the unitary phase of the functional equation): neutral, maximal, translation-invariant and covariant under real reflection. Its infinitesimal Green form is the prime–Gamma normal connection (D.94).
- d_102: Z is a topological isomorphism of nuclear Fréchet spaces. The even cohomology is the Tate plane and the odd one is the Meyer quotient V. The nuclear Green form on V gives −B_nuc by pullback.
- Label: constructions proved; the sign remains open (REF-D).
- Index: the files appear at l.20689 only as failed mechanisms; the constructions do not.

##### 114_d_108 — numerical Hodge index theorem in the rules of row A
- Statement: with H=e_1+e_2, the primitive line is negative definite. It is the two-dimensional Hodge theorem on the quotient of rules.
- Label: PROVED.
- It does not transport to row D: it has rank two and vanishes on the primitive kernel.
- Index: absent.

##### 114_d_114 / d_115 / d_118 — OS, adelic Poisson and Doob identities
- d_114: the OS quotient of the rank-one Hankel contact reconstructs p^{−1/2}; its dilation gives the covariance p^{−|r−s|/2}. Chain Λ(p^{r+s})p^{−(r+s)/2} → p^{−1/2} → (log p)p^{−|r−s|/2}; the same mode by mode for Γ.
- d_115: the non-product positive functional on the additive adeles is self-dual, invariant under rational scaling and has as exact jets the two Tate functionals.
- d_118: the rank-two Doob transform separates Λ(n)/√n into the two rates Λ(n) and Λ(n)/n; the jets are the reciprocal ground states.
- Label: proved; none gives the sign.
- Index: absent (l.20689 lists the mechanisms, not these identities).

#### §2 ABSENT ROUTES (c)

##### phase 102 — Strong margin λ_n ≥ ½A_n via increment measure (second differences of Li) and Fejér kernels
- Files: 198, 200, 202, 203, 204, 205, 206, 259, 261, 264, 266, 271, 272, 273
- What was attempted: the strong margin (which with A0 closes A1) was rewritten as n∫F_n dν_g ≥ A_n, where ν_g is the Herglotz measure of g_m = λ_{m+1} − 2λ_m + λ_{m−1} (198, 200). Then a scale audit was done: bounded density (202), atom at ζ=1 (203), logarithmic density (204, 205). The Abel→Fejér Tauberian gap was also studied (206). There is a conditional closure theorem (259) with its finite-remainder schema (261, 264). Then come the Abel→Fejér defect reduction (266), the separation ν_g ≥ 0 ⇏ margin (271), the necessary localization (272) and the layer-cake form (273).
- Result according to the memo: gates «Closed as … gate/audit»; A1 «remains open». There are these explicit no-gos:
  - (198) the positivity of the second-difference Toeplitz matrices does not imply the margin («formal no-go», l.158–211);
  - (202) an absolutely continuous bounded density cannot give the margin («formal scale no-go for that regularity class»);
  - (203) an atom at 1 would force quadratic λ_n and a cubic pole in 𝓛, which is incompatible with the Euler–Gamma scale («eliminated»);
  - (206) the Abel logarithm does not imply the Fejér bound, because Fejér kernels have moving zeros;
  - (271) ν_g ≥ 0 gives global Li positivity but not the compact margin;
  - (272) every Fejér bound requires localized logarithmic mass near 1.
  - (259) is CONDITIONAL: positive measure + log density with a > ½ ⇒ strong margin.
- Why it failed: positivity, finite mass or bounded density do not give the scale n log n. The atomic shortcut is excluded. What is missing is a non-circular construction of ν_g with lower log density a ∈ (½,1].
- Written reopening condition: construct ν_g in a non-circular way with local log density a > ½ (or a direct Fejér bound, or anticoncentration); 264 fixes the explicit threshold.
- Closest in the index: l.4534 / l.11831 (G3F-phase-102/270,281,290,300,310,328 «Poisson/Fejér/Abel/real-ray transfers», DEAD) covers only the transfers, not the strong-margin route nor the no-gos 198/202/203/206/271/272. Also l.4517 (115,116 boundary measure, REF-D).

There follow the Laguerre correlation form of the high block (228), the single transform S_n(T) = Σ_{m≤e^T} Λ(m)m^{−1}L_{n−1}^{(1)}(log m) (229, 230), the summation by parts and the Mertens–Chebyshev identity (231, 234), and finally the Laguerre lobe blocks (298, 299).
- Result according to the memo: exact normal forms («Closed as … normal form»); A1 open. (329) adds a monotonicity no-go: the positivity of Λ and the monotonicity of ψ do not prove the lobe-oriented dominance.
- Why it failed: what remains is a signed prime–Laguerre correlation that does not follow from size bounds (221/223/232).
- Reopening condition: the oriented discrepancy inequality (299 (8) / 329 (6)).
- Closest in the index: l.4536 / l.11834 (313, term-by-term sign, DEAD) and l.4823. The monotonicity no-go of 329 and the chain of normal forms do not appear.

##### phase 102 — Cutoff transfer (fixed cutoff → moving cutoff T_n)
- Files: 233, 235, 237
- What was attempted: a fixed-cutoff generator for S_n(T) (233) and the exact derivative C_n′(T) = −E(e^T)e^{−T}L_{n−1}^{(2)}(T) (235). With it, the transfer between cutoffs turns out to be equivalent to a signed tail theorem (237).
- Result according to the memo: «Closed as … gate / equivalence». Positivity at fixed cutoff is not transferred without the sign of the integral, and symmetric bounds fall back to the bulk no-gos.
- Why it failed: there is no separate monotonicity principle.
- Closest in the index: nothing.

##### phase 102 — Margin–tail route (M_n + δ_n), quarter margin + nonpositive tail, zero phase and tail lobes
- Files: 236, 238, 239, 240, 244, 247, 248, 249, 254, 255, 274, 280, 320, 321, 322, 327 (and 245 as a dependency of the terminal threshold)
- What was attempted: the identity C_n(T_n) = M_n + δ_n, with a ladder of thresholds (κ_n − ρ_n ≥ ¼), the deficit ratio s_n ≥ d_n and the requirement of improvement over A0 (238–240, 244, 255). One variant uses quarter margin + R_n(T_n) ≤ 0 (247, 248). The tail sign was written by partition at Laguerre zeros (249), in phase form of the explicit formula (254) and in lobe/phase duality (274, 280). There is a one-sided envelope criterion per lobe with its certificate schema (320, 322) and an absolute cost of the final ray (327). The transfer between direct and tail lobes was also studied (321).
- Result according to the memo: sufficient gates. There are these no-gos:
  - (236) Li positivity / support on the line does not give compact A1 without additional margin;
  - (274) lobe and phase are the same functional, so they are not independent sources;
  - (321) ω_n′ = K_n is algebraic and nonpositive, so the lobe-to-lobe transfer is circular.
  - (224, 248) classify the strong margin and the quarter margin as of «strength [H]». By standing rule, this is read as REF-D.
- Closest in the index: l.4533 (250 symmetric tail, 241, 257) and l.4557 (258). The no-go 236, the duality 274, the transfer no-go 321, the criterion 320/322/327 and the audits 224/248 are missing.

- Result according to the memo: «no-go for finite-block Herglotz shortcuts». The counterexample g_0 = 1, g_{±(N+1)} = M > 1 has all blocks L ≤ N positive and the next one indefinite.

##### phase 102 — Abel→Fejér defect route by anticoncentration on the bad set (weighted Carleson, central floor, Euler–Gamma remainder)
- Files: 291, 292, 293, 296, 297, 312, 315, 316, 325
- What was attempted: the constant threshold d_α < 1 − α/2 (291), the Poisson-weighted anticoncentration on B_{n,τ} (292) and the geometry of the bad set (293: it contains windows of scale 1/n around every nontrivial n-th root). There follow the weighted Carleson version (296), the central floor and its compatibility (297, 316), the log kernel model, with numerical constant κ_α and optimization (312, 315), and the remainder certificate schema (325).
- Result according to the memo: gates and reductions. The log kernel alone leaves a positive margin (NUMERICAL calibration, 312/315). The obstruction is the Euler–Gamma remainder near the moving zeros. 297/316 «two-sided budget constraint, not a no-go».
- Closest in the index: l.4535 / l.11832 (294, 311, 314, DEAD). The route as such, its thresholds and its status (open, not dead) do not appear.

#### §3 ABSENT POSITIVE RESULTS (d)

##### 217 — Margin certificate at the base n=8
- Statement: λ_8 − ½A_8 > 0 by the rational interval verifier `omega7_point4_interval_verify.py`, extended to n=8 (l.71–123). Together with A0 at n=8 (|R_8(T_8)| ≤ ¼A_8) it gives C_8* > 0 (eq. 13–14) and, with small T_7, Γ_B > 0.
- Label of the memo: «Closed as a finite n=8 base margin certificate». The margin is certified by intervals; C_8* > 0 holds «provided A0 is instantiated for n=8 with its declared tail bound».
- Warning: the index (l.4926, l.612) records that 103_13 withdraws the numerical threshold and the certified range tied to A0. The part λ_8 − ½A_8 > 0 does not depend on A0; the part C_8* > 0 does. Nothing in this stretch retracts it. The index has only λ_1..λ_7 (l.2647).

##### 219 — Telescoping collapse of the Laguerre mixture
- Statement: with the weights w_{n,k} = ½(n(n+1)/(k(k+1)) − 1), the cumulative kernel on (T_j, T_{j+1}), j ≥ 8, collapses to −L_{n−1}^{(2)}. Two exceptional low-cutoff intervals remain.
- Label: «Closed as a mixed-kernel telescoping theorem». It replaces the no-go 218.

##### 212–213, 215, 220 — Coefficient of the terminal budget
- Statements:
  - 212: Γ_B = (1 + Δ_8*)/16 − (3/64)(A_8 − A_7), by exact telescoping of the archimedean series.
  - 213: 16Γ_B = I_7(T_7) − I_8(T_8), exact compact identity.
  - 215: with T_7 ≤ min(log 2, 1/130), C_8* ≥ 0 ⇒ Γ_B > 0.
  - 220: Γ_B > 25/64; the asymptotic terminal absorption is closed.
- Labels: «Closed as …» (identities / reduction). The effective threshold is not computed (245).

##### 208 — VK cutoff ratio
- Statement: for canonical VK A0 cutoffs, log((1+T_n)/(1+T_{n−1})) = O(1/n). Hence the terminal load is O(log n).
- Label: «Closed as a VK cutoff-ratio scale audit» (limited positive).

##### 260 — Exact constant of the Fejér log kernel
- Statement: ∫F_n L dm = H_{n−1} − (n−1)/n ≥ log n − 1. That is, B_L = 1 for all n ≥ 1.
- Label: «Closed as an exact analytic subcertificate».

##### 262 — Explicit archimedean upper bound
- Statement: λ_n^arch ≤ ½ n log n + 3n for n ≥ 2 (B_A = 3, N_A = 2; text of the plan, l.279).
- Label: «Closed as the explicit archimedean upper input».

##### 265 — Abel coefficient budget
- Statement: if ν_g ≥ 0 has lower local density aL near 1, then a ≤ 1. The viable window is ½ < a ≤ 1.
- Label: «Closed as an Abel coefficient budget».

##### 263 — Local-to-global patch for the log density
- Statement: a local log density with h ≥ 0 and ν_rem ≥ 0 gives the global Fejér bound, with an explicit constant depending on the arc.
- Label: «Closed as a local-to-global patch» (conditional lemma, proved).

##### 295 — Bounded density on the bad set
- Statement: if 0 ≤ h ≤ H, then ∫_E P_{1−1/n} h dm ≤ H for every measurable E. The logarithmic contribution vanishes.
- Label: «Closed as a bounded-density reduction». 296 confirms it (β_τ = 0).

##### 326 — Finite reduction for bounded lobes
- Statement: in each bounded tail lobe, the constant one-sided envelope of ψ(e^u) − e^u reduces to finitely many extremes at prime powers. Only the final ray remains infinite.
- Label: «Closed as the bounded-lobe finite reduction».

Secondary reusable identities, with no entry in the index (included in the files of §2):
- 198/203: 2λ_n = n g_0 + 2Σ(n−m)g_m.
- 271: 2λ_n = n∫F_n dν_g.
- 235: C_n′(T) = −E(e^T)e^{−T}L_{n−1}^{(2)}(T); C_n is continuous at the jumps.
- 237: C_n(V) − C_n(U) = −∫_U^V E e^{−t} L_{n−1}^{(2)}.
- 236/238: C_n(T_n) = λ_n − ¼A_n − R_n(T_n).
- 276: ½𝔔^{𝓒,T_n}(p_n,p_n) = C_n(T_n).

#### §2 ABSENT ROUTES (c)

##### phase-102 (discard) — Signed mechanisms for A1: local blocks of prime powers, finite-kernel factorization, Mellin coboundary, bordered Euler current
- Files: `102_A1_SIGNED_COMPENSATION_CANDIDATES.md`. It is the draft of `102_A1_SIGNED_COMPENSATION_MECHANISMS.md` of the live campaign.
- What was attempted: four mechanisms.
  - (A) Grouping prime powers into blocks of u = log m, with a one-sided bound per block.
  - (B) Writing C_n(T) + ¾λ_n^arch = ‖Q_{n,T}‖² + error with a finite symbol.
  - (C) A Mellin coboundary identity with respect to d log(π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2)ζ(s)), with the symmetry s ↦ 1−s.
  - (D) A quotient det H_n^border / det H_n^base of a bordered Hermitian form built from the Euler–Gamma data.
- Result according to the memo: «No candidate in this document proves A1 yet. The local and finite-symbol routes are eliminated as independent closures». (A) is left «eliminated as an independent route»; (B) is left «allowed only if the symbol positivity is proved independently». (C) and (D) are the survivors, «not yet proved».
- Why it failed or what it closes:
  - (A): the Laguerre derivative changes sign in the oscillatory region and prime powers have no local positivity law; the cancellation is global.
  - (B): with a chosen nonnegative symbol it is the Fejér–Riesz wall of Paper 36, hence circular.
- Reopening condition written in the memo: (B), if the positivity of the symbol is proved independently; (C) and (D), prove one of the two identities, «not to rename them».
- Closest in the index:
  - l.2877: «No local unit (prime, finite shell, Laguerre lobe, Fejér–Riesz, positive Gram, smoothing in n) survives», ARGUED, source OA.
  - l.2583: «global compensation law: involution, coboundary, functional identity, energy…», as a candidate class.
  - l.4574: bordered Euler current DEAD, but that entry comes from the later memo 119, not from this one.
  - l.23507: the Part VI report already records the live version (MECHANISMS) as absent.
  - No closure entry names this file or the discard of the finite symbol.

##### phase-102 (discard) — Zero-side discriminant for A1: class «finite signed fit + after-the-fact zero-side diagnosis»
- Files: `102_A1_ZERO_SIDE_DISCRIMINANT.md`. It is the draft of the homonymous file of the live campaign; it differs in 8 lines of wording.
- What was attempted: using λ_n = Σ_ρ(1 − w_ρ^n), with w_ρ = 1 − 1/ρ, as a diagnostic. An off-line quartet gives |w_ρ| > 1 and a term −2Re(w_ρ^n) of geometric size, which exceeds the archimedean growth O(n log n).
- Result according to the memo: «The off-line sensitivity control is formulated. It is not a proof of A1». It declares a class NO-GO: «finite signed fit + zero-side diagnosis after the fact … cannot close A1 … a valid falsification tool and not a proof». It leaves alive the form A1 + ¾λ^arch = 𝓔_n + 𝓑_n, with 𝓔_n, 𝓑_n ≥ 0 proved from the Euler product, the Gamma factor, the functional equation and the paired boundary.
- Why it failed or what it closes: the diagnostic detects the quartet but does not give the arithmetic inequality that excludes it.
- Reopening condition written in the memo: a signed identity or variational principle with 𝓔_n, 𝓑_n ≥ 0 proved independently.
- Closest in the index:
  - l.2603: planted quartet required by A1.
  - l.2065 and l.2254: the zero side does not decide the sign (P8 Thm C, B0).
  - l.23704: Part VI merges the live twin with l.2603.
  - The class NO-GO of this memo does not appear with its statement.

##### phase-77 — TRICOMI-LP: H_L = pure Tricomi + compact/decreasing arithmetic perturbation (route R2)
- Files: E77_7_TRICOMI_LP_AUTOPSY.md
- What was attempted: prove LP at the real point μ by discrete fundamental Tricomi asymptotics plus a compact perturbation.
- Result according to the memo: «refuted: pure Tricomi plus decaying arithmetic perturbation as R2»; «proved: exact nondecaying arithmetic coefficient (AT-1); the fixed-L arithmetic matrix is not a compact perturbation».
- Why it failed: the arithmetic diagonal coefficient V_n^arith is almost periodic and does not decay (tail RMS 1.34 up to n=4000); it does not refute LP, only the R2 proof.
- Reopening: «A new almost-periodic subordinacy theorem could in principle attack LP».
- Closest: l.2505 (literal LP), without mention of Tricomi.

##### phase-66 — Rank-one subcritical isolation and conditional closure theorem
- Files: MAXIMAL-CLOSURE-omega7.md §§1–5
- Statement: (i) HB is closed under locally uniform non-degenerate structural convergence; (ii) shorting of the positive pole preserves index 0 under finite Gram convergence; (iii) dominant rank-one trace does NOT imply primitive boundedness (counterexample a_P|e₀⟩⟨e₀| + b_P Q_V, b_P = o(a_P), b_P→∞); (iv) in a source core with decay a_φ > ½, Σ (log p)p^{−k/2}|φ̂(k log p)|² < ∞ uniformly: the only divergent direction is the pole line; the passage to the critical endpoint is exactly sup_P‖P_prim K_P P_prim‖<∞ (REF). Conditional theorem (1)–(4) ⇒ κ(Ξ)=0.
- Label: PROVED (i)–(iv); the critical endpoint OPEN.

##### phase-4-handoff/proofs — The archimedean de Branges space H(E_γ) as home of the semibounded realization (Days 1–10)
- Files: `B2-semiboundedness.md`, `B2.4a-de-branges-norm.md`, `B2.4a-closability.md`, `B2.4a-break-attempt.md`, `EF-identity-audit.md`, `closure-in-HEgamma.md`, `CLOS1-audit-and-RFB.md`, `space-correction-strip-hardy.md`, `Day10-kernel-audit.md`.
- What was attempted: to realize the Weil form 𝔱 in the de Branges space of the Gamma factor H(E_γ) (DB.1: Ω = 2 Re γ′/γ; DB.3 bounded evaluations off the axis), to prove closability (CLOS.1 by Kato's monotone convergence; CLOS.2 «[H] ⇒ 𝔱 closable»; CLOS.3 = (RFB)), and to reduce B‑2 to the de Branges chain condition.
- Result according to the memos: CLOS.1 PROVED (existence) with «closure = 𝔱_+» RETRACTED (Day 8, form core OPEN); Day 9: «H(E_γ) is trace-class — hence trivial — for the Weil form» (𝔱 bounded ⇒ CLOS correct but empty); Day 10: the trivialization depends on the normalization of E_γ, «neither Gamma normalization is Goldilocks … Gamma–de-Branges is wrong home ✅ both normalizations fail». EF‑id: «unconditional on the dense core»; survival under closure in H(E_γ) «OPEN». B2.3 («naive KLMN fails», Day 0) retracted on Day 5 for the same hard-cutoff error as BR.1.
- Why it failed: the exponential weight of the Gamma factor makes the form of finite trace (empty problem); the growing weight does not control evaluations; it holds for the family of Gamma normalizations of H(E).
- Reopening condition: «exact weight (flat vs log) … resolve via Bombieri/Lagarias» (Day 10, open); the home passes to the oversampled band Hardy space.
- Closest in the index: l.2996 (self-adjoint realization, EF‑id, R=Kρ, P=ρℓ, oversampled Hardy: PROVED); l.2147 (Fock retracted, truncation artifact); l.2142 (de Branges/structure function, Conrey–Li). No line records the trivialization of H(E_γ) or the exclusion of the Gamma normalizations.

#### §2 ABSENT ROUTES (c)

##### phase-12 — «Correct mechanism» chain carried up to the freezing transition and the moment problem (M12.8–M12.10)
- Files: M12.8-verdict-freezing-live-frontier.md, M12.9-verdict-moment-problem-candid-status.md, M12.10-the-meta-obstruction.md
- What was attempted: to extend M12.4–M12.7 to the supercritical regime of multiplicative chaos (β_c=1, m(β) measured) and identify it with the off-diagonal term of the moment problem (k≥3); M12.10 tries to close N7 and classifies the mechanisms of absence (positivity, counting/density, finite computation, statistics).
- Result according to the memo: M12.8 NUMERICAL (m(β) 1.00→0.08); M12.9 «mechanism-correct but HEURISTIC, not a rigorous reduction»; M12.10 with explicit correction: «not proven … a conceptual map of strategies, not a proof of impossibility» (ARGUED).
- Why it failed: the last link (control of extremes ⇒ absence) is the N7 gap «describe vs force»; the supercritical front is another open problem.
- Reopening written: supercritical/off-diagonal bound (CFKRS) with the machinery of ω classes.
- Closest: l.2223 «PL05 Part IX (M12.1–M12.7) … front remains in additive energy» and l.2753 «N7 … OPEN, heuristic». None names the freezing, the moment problem as a landing point, or the downgrade of M12.10.

##### phase-15 — Four direct attacks on the core of M3 (Attempts 1–4)
- Files: M3-genuine-attempts-on-the-core.md
- What was attempted: (1) 2×2 Hodge determinant in ⟨H,Γ⟩ (reverse Cauchy–Schwarz a²>2λ²V); (2) Bochner positivity of the sine kernel to sign the off-diagonal; (3) dBN flow + arithmetic; (4) tower of symmetric powers / Rankin–Selberg.
- Result according to the memo: all four «land on the irreducible core»; (2) gives only effectivity V≥0; (3) falls into N5; (4) controls Satake, an axis orthogonal to the zeros.
- Why it failed: every available source is lower-bound positivity (effectivity/Bochner/relaxation) or local functoriality.
- Reopening: uniform upper bound ⟨Γ,H⟩²>⟨H,H⟩⟨Γ,Γ⟩ not coming from effectivity, Bochner, relaxation or Satake.
- Closest: l.2740 «M3 arithmetic Hodge index … M3 REF». It does not name the four attempts.

##### phase-16 — Pillar 1/2 on the modular surface: the zeros as resonances (Re s=1/4), not L² eigenvectors; triage of routes
- Files: 01-pillar1-triage-three-routes.md, 02-pillar2-prototype-resonance-wall.md
- What was attempted: triage of three routes for the witness variety: C global prismatic (REJECTED), B δ/𝔽₁ (NOT TESTABLE: no cohomology constructed), A GL₂/Eisenstein (survives: poles of φ(s)=ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s) at s=ρ/2, verified); prototype of regularized Maass–Selberg pairing.
- Result according to the memo: the density −φ′/φ is the modular explicit formula (verified to 10⁻²⁵), indefinite and independent of the zeros, but the zeros are resonances outside the L² spectrum; open core = «realize the resonances as a Kreĭn space».
- Why it failed / what it closes: there is no Gram matrix on a discrete basis of zeros; afterwards closed by the theorem of 05.
- Closest: l.4584 (only the theorem of 05), l.3039/5084 (prismatic), l.11317 R9-19. Route B (δ/𝔽₁) «not testable» and the resonance wall do not appear.

##### phase-16 — Residual weight r_ρ=ξ(ρ−1)/(2ξ′(ρ)) as a Kreĭn sign
- Files: 03-residue-pairing-nontrivial.md
- What was attempted: to use the residue of the scattering determinant as the self-weight of each resonance and its sign as a detector of κ.
- Result according to the memo: |r_ρ|=O(1) (does not decay; nontrivial space, unlike the H(E_ξ) of phase 4) — NUMERICAL/proved by exact cancellation of factors; «self-refuted»: Re r(s₀)<0 for β=0.30…0.70, no sign change off the line.
- Why it failed: the sign of the residue is stable in β; it does not detect the off-line position.
- Reopening: bilinear pairing (Gamow vectors) sensitive to β — executed in 04 and closed.
- Closest: l.2736 (MSZ «FALSIFIED as a detector … Definite/non-diagonal»). The scalar residue and its falsification in β do not appear.

##### phase-16 — Lorentzian (Klein–Gordon) pairing of Eisenstein resonances
- Files: 06-hunt-indefinite-object.md
- What was attempted: (i) to split each resonance into components y^s / y^{1−s} with opposite signs; (ii) Klein–Gordon symplectic current on y=const.
- Result according to the memo: (i) Gram remains definite (+0/−12, 6 zeros); (ii) norm ∝ γ_ρ, blind to β (=20.0 for β=0.3 and 0.7). «Unified negative»: Petersson ∼(1−β) definite, bilinear Kreĭn ∼1/(1−β) definite, Klein–Gordon ∼γ blind to β. Principle: a geometry with a Hilbertian L² product does not house κ. NO-GO in the structures proved.
- Why it failed: the detector (β−½) is the evaluation off the axis, not a mass pairing nor a Cauchy surface pairing.
- Closest: l.4584 (Riemannian theorem of 05). The Lorentzian variant and the «unified negative» do not appear (the «Lorentz» entries of the IDX, l.1901/5163/5560, are other objects).

##### phase-16 — Self-adjoint realization / Weyl function m(z)=(1/i)ξ′/ξ(½+iz)
- Files: 09-self-adjoint-construction.md (and the identification of 07-pontryagin-the-indefinite-object.md)
- What was attempted: to construct the self-adjoint operator/canonical system whose m-function is ξ′/ξ; unconditional ingredients: residues +1 and Im m=0 on the axis; route (A) inverse from the measure (circular), route (B) via deficiency extension (phase 4, B-1/B-2).
- Result according to the memo: OPEN; the open step (reality of the poles/semiboundedness) reduces to the RFB / uniform pair correlation; 07: H(E_ξ) detects κ «by construction» (diagonal kernel K_w(w)<0 with one zero moved) — without new positivity.
- Closest: l.2742 «Herglotz of ξ′/ξ | F00 §016 | REF»; l.2741 Conrey–Li; l.2997/4812 RFB. The realization by m-function and its reduction to B-2/RFB do not appear as a route; 07 is only implicit.

##### phase-17 — Route-2 testbed: the real-structure scaffolding (X,j) is free and blind to γ
- Files: 03-route2-testbed.md (with 01-SURF-A-triage.md)
- What was attempted: to build (X,j) without zeros and see whether it reproduces the signature template (blocks (1,0)/(1,1), index = no. of quartets) and whether it derives the ordinates.
- Result according to the memo: PROVED that the scaffolding reproduces the template without zeros and is blind to γ (real, random or progression ordinates give the same): «SURF-A reduces to SURF-B»; producing T with spectrum {γ} is the classical spectral problem.
- Closest: l.4624 «Involution j(s)=1−s̄ … REF-D | Symmetry, not positivity» (covers 02/04). The collapse SURF-A→SURF-B and the blindness to γ do not appear.

##### phase-19 — Rate function of ω, B-smooth sums and tempered maximum
- Files: 02-omega-rate-freezing.md, 03-bsmooth-freezing.md, 04-random-mult-maximum.md
- What was attempted: freezing in the rate function of ω(n)/loglog n; exact B-smooth products ∏_{p≤B}(1+q/(p−1)); maximum of B-smooth Dirichlet polynomials with random signs.
