### 212-58 — Exact unitary identity of 212-57 (verified with its constant), item C6 of the complement and cell block
- Closest antecedent: 212-57 (C2-1); 212-52; 212-46; 212-56 (C6, K7); 212-51.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: the normalization of the unitary identity is verified, the low-frequency behavior and its renormalized stationary form are studied, C6 is examined, and the cell block is redone in an orthonormal basis with the three controls.
- Result: no candidate. Identity and constant PROVED; cell data NUMERICAL; explicit square of the cell block OPEN.
- (1.0) Identity verified (PROVED; checked to 25 digits at `T = ½` with the prime 2 on a non-even `F ∈ P_T`).
  - (A) For every `G` in the domain: `½∫log|κ||ĝ|²dκ = arch(G) − ⟨tG,G⟩`, with `g(x) = |x|^{−1/2}G(log|x|)`, `ĝ(κ) = ∫g e^{−2πiκx}dx` and `arch(G) = C_0‖G‖² + ∫_0^∞(c_G(0)−c_G(u))K(u)du`. There is no constant nor extra factor; this settles the normalization that 212-52 and 212-57 left unverified.
  - (B) `Σv_nc_F(log n) = ⟨t𝔅_XF, 𝔅_XF⟩ − ⟨tF,F⟩ − θ(X)‖F‖²` for `X ≥ e^{2T}`.
  - Therefore `a_T(F) = ½∫log|κ||ĝ_X(κ)|²dκ + ⟨tF,F⟩ + θ(X)‖F‖²`.
- (1a) Low frequency (PROVED; principal constant NUMERICAL to 10 digits).
  - With `A_X = Π_{p≤X}(√p − 1/√p)/log p`, the multiplier has a pole of order `π(X)` at the origin, and the first condition of `P_T` removes one order.
  - `ĝ_X(κ) ~ −2A_X(∫tFe^{t/2})(log 1/|κ|)^{π(X)−1}/(π(X)−1)!` as `κ → 0`; it is bounded and oscillating in `log|κ|` if `π(X) = 1`. «`ĝ_X(0) = 0`» is false.
  - The low-frequency mass `∫_{|κ|<1}log(1/|κ|)|ĝ_X|²` is finite and grows like `A_X²(2π(X)−1)!/((π(X)−1)!)²`.
  - The second condition is the linear moment `∫log|κ|ĝ_X(κ)dκ = 0`, which is not local at 0.
- (1b) Drift and stationary form (PROVED).
  - Adding a prime `p > e^{2T}` changes `½∫log|κ||ĝ|²` by exactly `−log p‖F‖²` (exact drift); increasing `X` worsens the cancellation.
  - Renormalized stationary form: with `R_X = τ_{−θ(X)}𝔅_X`, of symbol `Π_{p≤X}(1−p^{−1/2+iτ})/(1−p^{−1/2−iτ})`, and `h_X ↔ R_XF`, one has `a_T(F) = ½∫log|κ||ĥ_X|²dκ + ⟨tF,F⟩`.
  - Symmetrizing with the reflection `R`: `a_T(F) = ¼∫log|κ|(|ĥ_X[F]|² + |ĥ_X[RF]|²)dκ` for all `X ≥ e^{2T}`, with no change on adding primes above `e^{2T}`.
  - It is not a sum of nonnegative terms (`log|κ|` changes sign at 1): it is a reformulation, valid literally for `𝔅` with a factor at `16/5`.
  - The formal limit `X → ∞` does not commute with the form (ARGUED). The sharp logarithmic uncertainty inequality applied to `h_X` gives only `a_T ≥ C_0‖F‖² − comb`.
- (1c) NO-GO. `g_X` does not have compact support, so `ĝ_X` is not band-limited. The integer dilations preserve the sampling lattice of `ĝ_F` but undersample the dilated terms; integrality enters only as a closure property of the lattice.
- (2) C6.
  - PROVED: every symmetric kernel that vanishes on `P_T` is `Σ_{u∈{1,1/x}}(u⊗h_u + h_u⊗u)`.
  - `L = ∂_xx²∂_x` annihilates `1` and `1/x`, so `L_xL_{x′}` annihilates all those kernels, but not a nonzero density on a line `x′ = Nx`. With one or finitely many non-unimodular weights the excess atom density cannot be cancelled.
  - Loophole (PROVED that it exists): the continuous family `w_y(x) = x^{−1/2}ρ(y/x)` has constant integrated atom density with `|w_y|` nonconstant. But the averaged weight is homogeneous of degree `−1`, and the construction is a Mellin multiplier unless `μ` is not homogeneous with a null defect of rank `≤ 4` (OPEN, without object).
- (3) Cell block.
  - Normalization: `‖F‖² = Σa_j²`; the comb entries are `Λ(n)/n` on each side of the pattern `⌊j/n⌋ = i`.
  - `P_T` on cell functions supported in `x ≥ 1` is `Σa_j = 0` and `Σa_j log(1+1/j) = 0`.
  - The minima quoted in 212-46 are generalized eigenvalues in a non-orthonormal basis.
  - Rayleigh minima (NUMERICAL, orthonormal basis of `Σa = 0`) at `N = 3, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40`:
    - true weight: `0.2636, 0.0708, 0.0332, 0.0228, 0.0121, 0.0075, 0.0052`;
    - `1.1Λ`: `0.2852, 0.1669, 0.1247, 0.1003, 0.0616, 0.0366, 0.0198`;
    - `𝔅` (exact integration of `⟨1_i, D_{q^k}1_j⟩` over its prime powers): `0.2441, 0.0309, −0.0721, −0.1044, −0.2415, −0.4002, −0.4497`, first negative at `N = 10`;
    - archimedean part alone: `−0.44 … −2.11`.
  - The explicit cell matrix separates `𝔅` from `N = 10` and does not separate `1.1Λ` up to `N = 40`.
  - Admissible window for a multiplier `λ` of the comb (with true `Λ`): `[0.98513, 1.32872]`, `[0.99280, 1.25319]`, `[0.99578, 1.17257]`, `[0.99719, 1.15031]` at `N = 16, 24, 32, 40`.
  - `LDL^T` in the difference basis:
    - the pivots do not depend on `N`; the 39 pivots are positive for the true weight (the first twelve: `0.527188, 0.580257, 0.378695, 0.502973, 0.374499, 0.514056, 0.466511, 0.474895, 0.531468, 0.538900, 0.571396, 0.569659`; minimum `0.3745`);
    - first pivot in closed form `d_1 = −2γ − 2log π + 6log 3 + 10log 5 − 27log 2` (PROVED, 20 digits);
    - the later pivots are Schur complements of logarithms of small integers, with no recognizable pattern;
    - for `𝔅` pivot 9 is `−0.556`.
  - Representation by integer division (PROVED).
    - `(B_na)_j = a_{⌊j/n⌋}`, `B_mB_n = B_{mn}`, and `n^{−1/2}B_n` is isometric on ℓ²(j≥1), with a_0=0. In the compression to 1,…,N it is only a contraction: (B_n^(N))*B_n^(N)=diag(min(n,max(0,N−ni+1))). The truncated semigroup is preserved. `Z_1 = ΣB_n/n` is unipotent with inverse `Σμ(n)B_n/n`, and the comb is `−2⟨Z_1′Z_1^{−1}a, a⟩`.
    - For real `z ≥ 1`, `⌊⌊u⌋/z⌋ − ⌊u/z⌋ ∈ {0, −1}`, identically 0 if and only if `z` is an integer. It is an exact characterization of integrality, which fails for `16/5`.
    - It is an inequality of indices: it gives operator order only on monotone nonnegative sequences, while the vectors of `P_T` change sign.
    - The non-semigroup part of the archimedean matrix is indefinite (eigenvalues `−42.2 … +41.6` at `N = 24`) and does not commute with `B_2`.
- Reopening condition: an explicit square of the cell block (for example, a closed formula for the pivots of `LDL^T`) that uses the characterization `⌊⌊u⌋/z⌋ = ⌊u/z⌋ ⟺ z ∈ ℤ` and explains why it does not separate `1.1Λ`; or a non-homogeneous measure with null defect of rank `≤ 4` for C6.

### 212-51-rev — Correction to Theorem 2 of 212-51
- Closest antecedent: 212-51, case (ii), Theorem 2 (L31694); correction derived in 212-57 (C2-0, C2-1) and 212-58 (1.0).
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: Theorem 2 assumed that the same correlation coefficient multiplies the atom and the singularity `1/dist` on each quotient line. It is false: by the dilation rule for the finite part, `pf(1/|kz|) = k^{−1}[pf(1/|z|) + 2 log k·δ]`, the coefficients are `λS_0 − 2cS_1` for `δ` and `−cS_0` for `pf`, with `S_0 = Σ_k c_k/k` and `S_1 = Σ_k c_k log k/k`; they decouple.
- Result: PROVED (elementary correction). There exists an explicit family (coefficients of a unimodular Euler product) with the exact atoms `−Λ(N)` and no singularity off the diagonal. Theorems 1 and 3 of 212-51 do not change. Case (ii) of 212-51 ceases to be a NO-GO; it remains as an exact reformulation without sign mechanism.
- Why it does not close: the resulting identity is exact, has index density `log|κ|` of indefinite sign and also holds for `𝔅` (detail in 212-57 and 212-58).
- Reopening condition: that of 212-57 and 212-58.

### 212-59 — Cell form in `x = e^t`: closed form of the archimedean cell matrix, its structure and the pivots
- Closest antecedent: 212-42, 212-46, 212-56 (K7), 212-58 (3). Toeplitz + Hankel type: L2252, L3126, L4712, L6003 (NO-GO of the Toeplitz + Hankel class as a source of sign; detail L9166), L5828, L6583. The exact cell formula does not appear in the index.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: all entries in closed form and the structural decomposition.
- Result: closed form PROVED; no candidate; explicit square of the cell block OPEN.
  - Closed form (PROVED; checked against quadrature to `6e−30` for `i ≤ 8`, `j ≤ 13`). With `ψ(x) = x log x` and `h(n) = Δ²ψ(n) = (n+2)log(n+2) − 2(n+1)log(n+1) + n log n`: off the diagonal `A_ij = −½h(i+j) − ½h(|i−j|−1)`; on the diagonal `A_ii = −½h(2i) + δ_i`, `δ_i = −γ − log 2π + (i+1)log(i+1) − i log i`. Proof: the overlap length is a signed sum of four ramps; each is integrated against `1/(y²−1)` by partial fractions; the divergent terms cancel because the slopes sum to zero.
  - Structure (PROVED): `A = D − ½H − ½T`, `D = diag(δ_i)`, `H = [h(i+j)]` Hankel, `T = [h(|i−j|−1)]` Toeplitz with null diagonal. The fraction `1/(y+1)` (the half `1/(2cosh(u/2))` of the kernel) gives exactly the Hankel block; the fraction `1/(y−1)` (the half `1/(2sinh(u/2))`) gives the Toeplitz block and the diagonal.
  - `h(n) = ∫_0^∞e^{−nx}((1−e^{−x})/x)²dx` (PROVED): `H` is a Stieltjes moment matrix, `Σa_ia_jh(i+j) = ∫_0^∞|Σa_ie^{−ix}|²((1−e^{−x})/x)²dx ≥ 0`. The only positive structure of the archimedean block enters with a minus sign: `M = (D − ½T − C) − ½H`, and the positivity of `M` is strictly stronger than that of `D − ½T − C`.
  - NUMERICAL (`N = 40`, orthonormal basis of `Σa = 0`): `λ_min(D − ½T − C) = 0.01839`, `λ_min(M) = 0.00519`, `λ_min(−½H) = −0.278`, `λ_min(D − ½T) = −1.84`.
  - Negative Loewner/Pick proof: the off-diagonal part is of the form `f(i+j) + g(|i−j|)`, not a divided-difference matrix of `log` nor of `x log x`.
  - Conjugation by `Z_1 = ΣB_n/n` or its inverse (NUMERICAL): dense, it neither diagonalizes the comb nor cancels the diagonal logarithms; the cell pairing is not the Dirichlet one.
  - In the difference basis the comb touches the diagonal only at `k = 1` with `+log 2` (PROVED); the diagonal grows like `2 log k`.
  - Pivots: independence of `N` is trivial (nested leading blocks, PROVED); `d_k` for `k ≥ 2` are quotients of determinants of log-linear entries, so no log-linear closed form exists (ARGUED).
  - Tables (NUMERICAL): true weight, the 39 pivots positive, minimum `0.3745`; `𝔅`: first difference at `d_2`, first negative `d_9` (cells `≤ 10`), other negatives at 12 and 16; `λΛ`: first negative pivot `d_5` for `λ = 0.9`, `d_20` for `λ = 0.99`, `d_18` for `λ = 1.3`, none up to 39 for `λ = 1.1`; the archimedean part alone is negative at `k = 1`.
  - Reading: the cell block is a detector of a lower bound on the weight of the comb (the growth `δ_i ~ log i` must be cancelled) and takes a long time to see an excess.
- Why it does not close: there is no explicit square; the archimedean block is indefinite on the constraint space; there is no order between the pieces to exploit (`−½H` costs close to 70 % of the margin at `N = 40`). It is a closed form, not a mechanism; it must not be pursued as a Nehari/AAK-type source of sign (L6003, L9166).
- Reopening condition: a representation of the whole cell form in the Laplace variable of `H`, `∫_0^∞(…)q(x)dx` with `q = ((1−e^{−x})/x)²`, in which the comb enters through the exact geometric block sums `Σ_{j∈[ni,n(i+1))}e^{−jx}` (not computed); cross-check it against the Lambert/theta entries before any construction.

### 212-60 — Rigidity of `W_∞`: gap lemma and exclusion of mixtures of characters
- Closest antecedent (read in full): G2_B9_R3 (L5210, L12194), R160_M2_R1, ROUND_025_A, ROUND_025_B (L9847); entries 212-25 (L31323), 212-30-A (L31386) and their revisions A and B, 212-53 … 212-55. Conventions of 212-53-rev; `w ∈ W_∞ ⟺ ν_w ≥ 0`.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: Thm R′/N of G2_B9_R3 treat `Λ` plus a tempered perturbation and exclude only the proportional case; here a family with non-tempered difference is excluded, by means of the gap lemma, which is not in the antecedents.
- Result: Lemma 0 PROVED; Theorem 1: historical proof recorded outside the sandbox, not usable in this campaign; admissible proof pending. Proposition 2 PROVED except for a CITED oscillation theorem; rigidity OPEN.
  - Lemma 0 (PROVED, elementary): since the comb vanishes on `(−log 2, log 2)`, every `w ∈ W_∞` has there `ν̌_w = k_∞ + (2−α_w)cosh(u/2) − β_w u sinh(u/2)`; for `w, w′ ∈ W_∞`, `μ = ν_w − ν_{w′}` satisfies `μ̌ ∈ span{cosh(u/2), u sinh(u/2)}` on that interval: no `δ_0`, no derivatives of `δ_0`, no constant. Mean-value form: for `g ∈ C_c^∞`, `∫ĝ(τ/R)dν_w = ∫ĝ(τ/R)m(τ)dτ + 2π(2−α_w)∫g + O(R^{−2})`, `m(τ) = Re ψ(¼+iτ/2) − log π`: the mean density of `ν_w` is universal, `m/2π`.
  - Theorem 1 (historical proof outside the sandbox; admissible proof pending; functional equations, explicit formulas and Laplace transform of tempered distributions on the half-line CITED): for `χ` a real primitive character modulo `q > 1`, `v_{χ,n} = 2Λ(n)χ(n)/√n` and `w_t = (1−t)v + tv_χ`, `t ∈ (0,1]`, one has `w_t ∉ W_∞` (for `t ≤ ½`, `w_t ≥ 0`: the natural candidate for a second element); the same for finite convex combinations with combs of primitive characters of conductor `> 1` (the complex ones via `v_χ + v_χ̄`).
  - Proof: if `w_t ∈ W_∞`, the Laplace transform of the truncated comb, `(1−t)(−ζ′/ζ)(½+z) + t(−L′/L)(½+z,χ)`, is holomorphic on `Re z > 0` except at `z = ½`; a point of the divisor of `ζ·L(·,χ)` with real part `> ½` would give a residue `−[(1−t)m_ζ + tm_L] < 0` that cannot be cancelled; therefore, under the hypothesis, a statement of type [H] holds for `ζ·L(·,χ)` (used only inside this reduction to absurdity, never assumed). The explicit formulas then give the tempered representation `ν′ = 2π[(1−t)N_ζ + tN_χ] − t(log q)dτ` in the even case, and `−t[log q + π/cosh(πτ)]dτ` for the continuous part in the odd case (`Re ψ(¾+iy) − Re ψ(¼+iy) = π/cosh(2πy) > 0`), with `N_ζ, N_χ` positive locally finite atomic; by uniqueness (212-54) `ν = ν′`, negative on every interval without atoms: contradiction.
  - Mechanism: the conductor term is a `δ_0` in `u`, inside the gap that Lemma 0 forbids; this makes exact the deficit `(log q)c_F(0)` pointed out in 212-25 and ROUND_025_B §1.
  - Reservation: the proof goes through a statement of type [H] as an intermediate consequence of the hypothesis being refuted; no proof avoiding it was found.
  - Proposition 2 (PROVED except for a CITED oscillation theorem, not reverified in the source): if `w, w′ ∈ W_∞` have equal constants, `μ̌` vanishes on `(−log 2, log 2)`, the smoothings of `ν_w` and `ν_{w′}` by `|ĥ|²` with `h` supported in `(−½log 2, ½log 2)` coincide, and a `μ ≠ 0` must change sign with lower density `≥ log 2/π`; if `ν_w` is atomic, the negative part of `μ` sits at the atoms of `ν_w`; no contradiction follows.
- Why it does not close: nothing forces the constants `(α, β)` of two elements to coincide (Theorem C of 212-55 only confines them); a real tempered `μ` with `μ̌` supported on `±log N` outside the gap, null in the gap, and `ν_w + μ ≥ 0` is not excluded. Nothing here gives a sign for the form itself.
- Reopening condition: equality of the constants for any two elements, and then `μ = 0`; or a second element that is not of character type.

### 212-61 — Replacing the index density `log|κ|` of the exact identity (212-57, 212-58) by a positive measure modulo null kernels on `P_T`
- Closest antecedent: R186_008, semilocal scattering phase (L15805, L30733; cited in 212-57, L31873); R160_C8 (L15067); identity (A) of 212-58.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: the question is whether the indefinite density `log|κ|` can be replaced by a multiplier `m ≥ 0` with null defect on `P_T`, and an exact scale parameter is introduced.
- Result: identity and dilation constant PROVED; spectra NUMERICAL; existence of a positive index measure modulo null kernels on `P_T` OPEN.
  - Exact reformulation (PROVED; checked numerically to `3e−4` at `T = 0.5, 0.8, 1.0`): with `α(τ) = arg[Γ(½+iτ)cos(π(½+iτ)/2)]` (`α′ − log 2π = Re ψ(¼+iτ/2) − log π`), `β′(τ) = −2Σ_{p≤X}log p·Re[z/(1−z)]`, `z = p^{−1/2}e^{iτ log p}`, `X ≥ e^{2T}`, and the unitary map `F ↦ Ψ_F(v) = (2π)^{−1}∫e^{i(α+β)(τ)}F̂(τ)e^{iτv}dτ`, with `w = −v − log 2π = log κ`: `a_T(F) = ½[⟨wΨ_F, Ψ_F⟩ + ⟨wΨ_{RF}, Ψ_{RF}⟩]`. The form is the compression of the position operator `w` to the image of `L²(−T,T)`. It is not new as a reformulation.
  - An index measure `≥ 0` is a multiplier `m(w) ≥ 0`; the question is whether `⟨(m − w)Ψ, Ψ⟩` vanishes on the image of `P_T` modulo null kernels on `P_T`.
  - Scale parameter (PROVED, exact): for every `c`, `a_T = P_c − N_c + c‖F‖²`, with `P_c = ½Σ⟨(w−c)_+Ψ,Ψ⟩ ≥ 0`, `N_c = ½Σ⟨(c−w)_+Ψ,Ψ⟩ ≥ 0` (sum over `F` and `RF`); equivalently `a_T = P_c + ⟨min(w,c)Ψ,Ψ⟩`. When `c → −∞`, `N_c → 0` and `a_T = lim[P_c − |c|‖F‖²]`: the divergent counterterm is a multiple of the identity, of infinite rank; it cannot be absorbed with finitely many functionals, with null kernels on `P_T` (rank `≤ 4`) nor by changing `X` (which adds exactly `−log p‖F‖²`); the rank-two terms in `∫tFe^{±t/2}` are subdominant.
  - Spectra (NUMERICAL, smooth basis of dimension 8–12, precision near `3e−4`): floor of the form on the whole space `−1.948, −3.278, −4.249` and on `P_T` `0.0199, ~1e−6, 1.3e−7` at `T = 0.5, 0.8, 1.0`. On the whole space `N_c` is in practice of rank one, rising to two when `c → −∞` (ratio second/maximum eigenvalue `0.009–0.017` at `c = −6`, `0.14–0.19` at `c = 0`); its principal eigenvector lies in `span{e^{t/2}, e^{−t/2}}` with cosine `0.9991–0.99999` (cosine `≈ 0.74` with `span{te^{±t/2}}`): the negative low-frequency part is carried, to first order, by the two directions that `P_T` eliminates.
  - But `N_c` restricted to `P_T` has no finite effective rank (eigenvalues `0.65, 0.64, 0.59, 0.53` at `T = 1.0`, `c = 0`), and the generalized eigenvalue `N_c/(P_c + c)` on `P_T` has maximum `1.0000` at `T = 0.8, 1.0`: on `P_T` the sign is a balance among many directions.
  - Attempted obstruction (NO-GO): the almost null vector does not exclude a positive `m`, because its density has near zeros where `m` could concentrate (density ratios between `1e−8` and `1e11`).
- Why it does not close: there is neither a positive `m` with null defect on `P_T` nor an impossibility theorem; the question is an exact moment problem for the compression of a multiplication operator. The falsifiers were not run (there is no construction to test).
- Reopening condition: an operation that eliminates a full-rank identity counterterm, outside the class of finite-rank null kernels on `P_T`.

### 212-62 — Low-frequency side of the exact unitary identity: form by smooth integers, Poisson reference and exact subtraction
- Closest antecedent: R162_403, exact identity for the comb of `P`-smooth integers (L13978, L5447, L12436); R161_003, polar renormalized Müntz operator (L5085); 212-57 C2-1; 212-58 (1a)(1b); 212-61.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: `ĥ_X` is written as a sum over smooth integers and an explicit Poisson reference is subtracted. It has not been proved that this reference is the limit of the images as X grows; see the audit at the end of Part V.
- Notation: `f(x) = |x|^{−1/2}F(log|x|)` even, `Ju(κ) = |κ|^{−1}u(1/κ)`, `S_X = |ĥ_X[F]|² + |ĥ_X[RF]|²`, `X ≥ e^{2T}`.
- Result: identities PROVED; data by bands NUMERICAL; NO-GO as a mechanism.
  - (1) PROVED (orientation fixed numerically; `T = 0.5`, primes `{2,3}`: `0.707190` against `0.707170`): `ĥ_X(κ) = Σ_{k|P_X}μ(k)k^{−1}Σ_{m P_X-smooth}f̂(mκ/k)`, that is `h_X(x) = Σ_kμ(k)Σ_mm^{−1}f(kx/m)`: superposition of dilates of `f` by the quotients `k/m`, not only by integers.
  - (2) PROVED: over all the integers, `Σ_{m≥1}f̂(mκ) = |κ|^{−1}Σ_{j≥1}f(j/κ)` (uses `f̂(0) = 0`, first condition of `P_T`); the reference `ĥ_ref = Jf` is defined (denoted `ĥ_∞` in the original record, without a convergence theorem X→∞); a formal Möbius inversion does not prove that convergence. The reflected copy needs `∫f/|x| = 0`, the second condition: the two conditions are exactly the null Poisson corrections. `S_∞(κ) = |f(κ)|² + κ^{−2}|f(1/κ)|²`, supported on `e^{−T} ≤ |κ| ≤ e^{T}`, of mass `4‖F‖²` and with identically null logarithmic moment. Therefore, for every `λ > 0` and `X ≥ e^{2T}`: `a_T(F) = ¼∫log(|κ|/λ)(S_X − S_∞)dκ = −¼∫_0^∞N_X(λ)dλ/λ`, `N_X(λ) = ∫_{|κ|<λ}(S_X − S_∞)`. With the other orientation the symmetric form is worth twice the archimedean part, not zero.
  - (3) PROVED: since `∫S_X = 4‖F‖²`, the dependence on `λ` is trivial (a single identity; the partitions of 212-61 are regroupings of it); `a_T(F)/‖F‖²` is the mean of `log|κ|` under `S_X`: the sign says that the geometric mean frequency of the symmetrized `h_X` is at least 1, a value attained exactly by the Poisson image.
  - Three-band form with thresholds `e^{±T}`; NUMERICAL at `T = 0.5` (contribution / mass): primes `{2,3}`: low `−0.261 / 0.33`, middle `+0.001 / 0.68`, high `+0.967 / 0.99`; primes `{2,3,5,7}`: `−0.252 / 0.24`, `0.000 / 1.11`, `+0.918 / 0.63`. `N_X` changes sign near `λ = 1` (positive below, negative above): there is no stochastic dominance argument.
  - OPEN (formerly ARGUED): it has not been proved here that as `X` grows the mass approaches `S_∞`. The interpretation through mass escaping to 0 and to ∞ is conditional on an appropriate convergence theorem; it does not constitute evidence of such a limit.
  - (4) PROVED: `a_T(F) = −(γ+log 2π)‖F‖² − ⅛pf∬[h_Xh_X′ + h_X^Rh_X^{R}′]/|x−x′|`, and the same energy of `h_∞` is worth `(γ+log 2π)‖F‖²`: the form is minus one eighth of a difference of finite-part energies, without sign.
  - (5) WITHDRAWN under the identification of(2): the formula `ĥ_∞(0) = −4∫tFe^{t/2}` is false if `ĥ_∞=Jf`. That reference vanishes in a neighborhood of0. An explicit primitive test with strictly positive right-hand side is given in the audit at the end of Part V. The formula is not reassigned to another object.
  - (6) Falsifiers: the subtraction of `S_∞` is a universal zero, valid whatever the weight, so the identity holds literally for `𝔅` and for `1.1Λ`; the Poisson step is the only arithmetic one and enters only through that zero; the term that separates is the difference of combs, linear in the weight; the witness of `𝔅` was not run.
- Why it does not close: reformulation; there is no explicit cause for the high-frequency escape to dominate the low-frequency one.
- Reopening condition: an argument in which the Poisson limit enters otherwise than as a universal zero.

### 212-63 — The near-null vector of the form in the time, `x` and additive-frequency images; the near-null ladder
- Closest antecedent: none for these images; near-nullity as an object, 211 C11 (L1884, L7932, L11196); vector `X_T` (212-19-A, 212-20-B). Galerkin matrices of phase 211 (Dirichlet sine basis, 40 digits).
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: the bottom vector and the low modes are examined in the time, `x` and additive-frequency images.
- Result: NUMERICAL unless indicated; no identity.
  - Precision limit: the bottom eigenvalue is not converged in the basis (`T = 1.0`: `1.963e−23` with `N = 90`, `1.611e−23` with `N = 160`; `T = 0.8`: `5.974e−12`, `5.897e−12`), and the bottom vector moves by about `1e−4` in `L²` between the two bases: lowering the value by `Δλ` rotates it toward the next near-null mode by `≈ √(Δλ/gap)`. The minimizer is determined only to `≈ 1e−4`, and a functional of size `√floor` cannot be resolved this way.
  - Near-null ladder (structural finding): the near-null set is a ladder of modes, not a single vector. Bottom eigenvalues at `T = 1.0`, even sector `1.6e−23, 1.2e−17, 1.3e−12, 3.8e−8`, odd `9.1e−21, 3.5e−15, 1.9e−10, 3.8e−6`; at `T = 0.8`, even `5.9e−12, 5.7e−7, 3.1e−3`, odd `1.1e−9, 5.1e−5, 9.8e−2`; at `T = 0.6`, `7.4e−5` and `3.7e−3`. Successive ratios `1e2–1e3`; eight independent directions below `4e−6` at `T = 1.0`, increasing in number with `T`. Consequence: every exact identity `form = Σc_j|ℓ_j|²` needs near-null functionals on a subspace of growing dimension.
  - Time image: the bottom vector is even for all `T`; its profile converges as `T` grows (peak `≈ 1.71` at 0, sign changes at `±0.226` (`T = 0.8`), `±0.230` (`T = 1.0`)); it empties out near the edge, and its derivative at the edge scales like the square root of the floor: `F′(−T) = 42, 5.3, 3.0e−2, 3.8e−3, 3.3e−4, 2.1e−8` at `T = 0.5, 0.6, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 1.0` (log–log slope `≈ 0.45`). ARGUED: effect of the cost of a kink at the edge under the archimedean term, not an arithmetic one.
  - `x` image: the integer-dilation sums `Σ_mf(mx)`, `Σμ(m)f(mx)` of the bottom vector have size `≈ 1.1‖f‖` in the window: not small. PROVED (trivial): for `x ∈ (e^T/2, e^T)` only `m = 1` contributes, so the compression to the window of `Σ_mw(m)D_m` with `w(1) ≠ 0` has trivial kernel on `P_T`.
  - Additive frequency: `f̂*(0) = 0`; values at integer `κ` almost independent of `T` (`≈ 1.37, 0.43, −0.12`, then `1e−2…1e−3`); real zeros in `κ` stable in `T` at `0.33, 0.73, 1.195, 1.74, 2.46, 3.2, 4.0, 4.9, 5.9`: not at integers or at simple rationals; there is no vanishing on a lattice.
  - Non-negative least squares in the low spectral subspace with the functionals `f̂(κ)`, `κ ∈ [0.05, 12]`: relative residue `0.69` (even), `0.66` (odd) at `T = 0.8`; these functionals do not vanish on the bottom vector (`max |ℓ_κ(F*)|/√λ* = 5.8e5`).
  - The images `h_X/S_X` and `Ψ(w)` were not computed.
  - Falsifier (correction of working statements of 212-43 and later entries): with the own weight of `𝔅`, `2log 3.2/√3.2` at `log 3.2`, the form of `𝔅` is already negative at `T = 0.6` (`−1.25e−3` even, `−3.51e−2` odd) and at `T = 0.75` (`−0.215`, `−0.083`), that is, as soon as the atom 3.2 enters (`½log 3.2 = 0.5816`). `T ≥ ½log5 + 10⁻⁴` is only the range of the PROVED certificate, not the first window of failure. The bottom vector of `𝔅` at `T = 0.6` has overlap `0.996` with the bottom vector of the integers: `𝔅` breaks positivity inside the near-null ladder of the integers.
- Why it does not close: data, no identity.
- Reopening condition: take the whole near-null subspace as the data object.

### 212-64 — The floor as a function of the position of one atom, with the other atoms at the integers and the weights fixed
- Closest antecedent: not recorded before; weight window `(0.9Λ, 1.1Λ)` (212-58 (3), 212-59); near-null ladder (212-63); P211-22A (L9844, generalized integer systems in the form of `R` cells).
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: a single atom is moved in the full form, with weights fixed. Galerkin in double precision (Legendre basis 50–56), parity sectors.
- Result: NUMERICAL.
  - Atom 3 moved to `x`, atom 2 fixed, weight `2log x/√x` (the same image with the weight frozen at `v_3`): at `T = 0.60` the floor is `−1.4e−1, −4.6e−2, −1.4e−2, −4.3e−3` at `x = 2.50, 2.80, 2.90, 2.95`, `+6.7e−5` at `x = 3.00`, and `−8.5e−3, −1.9e−2, −3.6e−2` at `x = 3.05, 3.10, 3.20`: a sharp peak at the integer, positive only there.
  - By sector at `T = 0.60`: even floor `−1.44e−2, −1.9e−3, −4.0e−4, +6.7e−5, +3.8e−4, +5.5e−4, +6.1e−4, +3.2e−4, −5.4e−4` at `x = 2.90, 2.97, 2.99, 3.00, 3.01, 3.02, 3.03, 3.06, 3.10`; odd floor `+3.0e−2, +1.1e−2, +5.9e−3, +3.4e−3, +8.8e−4, −1.5e−3, −3.9e−3` at `x = 2.90, 2.97, 2.99, 3.00, 3.01, 3.02, 3.03`. The even sector excludes positions below `≈ 2.999`, the odd one those above `≈ 3.014`; both are non-negative only for `x ∈ [2.999, 3.014]`.
  - At `T = 0.65`: even `−1.3e−3, +2.3e−6, −9.3e−5` at `x = 2.99, 3.00, 3.01`; odd `+2.3e−3, +1.9e−4, −2.0e−3`: the admissible interval shrinks to about `[3.0000, 3.001]`.
  - Atom 4 moved (atoms 2, 3 fixed, weight `log 2`), `T = 0.72`: even `−1.1e−3, −5.4e−7, +9.5e−9, +4.9e−8, +1.0e−8, −8.4e−8` at `x = 3.96, 3.99, 4.00, 4.01, 4.04, 4.10`; odd `+8.9e−6, +4.6e−6, +1.3e−6, −3.2e−6, −3.1e−5` at `x = 3.96, 3.99, 4.00, 4.01, 4.04`. `T = 0.75`: even `−2.4e−4, +7.6e−10, −6.5e−8` at `x = 3.995, 4.000, 4.005`; odd `+1.9e−6, +9.4e−8, −1.4e−5` (values below `1e−8` are at the limit of double precision).
  - Reading: in each window, the set of positions of one atom with non-negative form is a short interval around the integer, bounded on one side by one parity sector and on the other by the other, and it narrows quickly as the window grows; it is the positional analogue of the weight window `(0.9Λ, 1.1Λ)`.
  - Mechanism (ARGUED): the derivative of the form with respect to position is the quadratic form `−v_nc_F′(log n)`, indefinite on the near-null ladder of 212-63, so that a displacement in any direction is negative on some near-null mode.
- Why it does not close: it is a rigidity statement (the integers are an isolated point of the positivity region in position), not a proof of positivity at the integers.
- Reopening condition: an exact statement of the pinching: a description of the near-null subspace on which the position-derivative forms of all the atoms are controlled simultaneously.

### 212-65 — Numerical search for a positive certificate in several images at once: `a_T(F) = Σ_p∫m_p|U_pF|²` with all `m_p ≥ 0` on `P_T`
- Closest antecedent: certificates in the `τ` image of phases 154–155, not converged (L18905–18918); logarithmic form in two images, R160_C8 (L15067); 212-51 (iv); 212-61. The combination in several images was not recorded.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: simultaneous non-negative weights are sought in four images: (a) time; (b) additive frequency `f̂(κ)`; (c) `𝔅_XF`; (d) `Ψ_F(w)`; the images in `x` reduce to (a) and (c).
- Result: NO-GO (NUMERICAL) for positive diagonal certificates in several images with few-parameter weights in (a)–(d); the unrestricted version is the canonical factorization and carries no information.
  - Controls (NUMERICAL): identity (A) of 212-58 to `7e−11`; `𝔅_X` unitary to `3e−11` and identity (B) to `2e−11`; identity `Ψ` of 212-61 to `1.3e−5`. A positive decomposition on `P_T` compresses to every Galerkin section with the same weights, so infeasibility on a section for a family of weights is an obstruction for that family.
  - Sections `d = 8…32`, `T = 0.5…0.8`: with non-negative few-parameter families (ramps, bands, hats; 9 or 17 nodes per image), the relative residue of the best non-negative fit at `T = 0.5` is `0.11, 0.080, 0.064, 0.046, 0.042` for `d = 8, 12, 16, 24, 32` with the four images; it does not improve with finer nodes and grows with `T` (`0.11, 0.17, 0.19, 0.27, 0.33` at `T = 0.5, 0.56, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8`, `d = 8`). There is no exact decomposition in these families.
  - Shape of the best fit: a single ramp `≈ log⁺|κ|` in additive frequency (threshold `0.1–0.2`, slope `1.05–1.2`) and a positive-part weight in the `Ψ` image; the `𝔅_X` and time images receive no weight. The fit is "each indefinite exact density replaced by its positive part" and it fails because the cancelling negative parts are not reproducible with positive weights.
  - Closed-form test `a_T ≟ c_1∫_{t>T}(t−T)|𝔅_XF|² + c_2∫(log κ − c)_+|f̂|² + c_3‖F‖²`: residue `27 %` (`T = 0.5`) and `34 %` (`T = 0.56`), full-rank and indefinite defect: refuted.
  - Large free dictionaries: the exact LP is unstable under the node layout and uses weights up to `1e9` where the densities vanish: resolution artifacts.
  - Falsifiers: `1.1Λ` and `𝔅` give the same residues as the integers in comparable windows, also where the form of `𝔅` is negative: the diagnostics are blind.
  - Additional data on `𝔅` (refines the correction of 212-63): for `T ≤ ½log3` the two forms coincide; in `(½log3, ½log 3.2)` the form of `𝔅` is that of the integers without the prime 3 and becomes negative near `T ≈ 0.567`, before the atom `16/5` enters (floors: integers `9.6e−4, 6.1e−4, 4.8e−4, 3.7e−4, 9e−5` and `𝔅` `9.6e−4, 8.2e−4, 8.2e−4, −6.6e−3, −0.035` at `T = 0.55, 0.56, 0.565, 0.57, 0.6`).
- Why it does not close: the cancelling negative parts in each exact density are not reproduced with positive few-parameter weights; unrestricted, the search is the canonical factorization.
- Reopening condition: none within this class.

### 212-66 — The floor `λ_A(T)` on a grid of windows: table, convergence and corrections to recorded values
- Closest antecedent: the five two-digit values used in 212-50 (from P211-27A), the fit of 212-50 (L31678), 212-63.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: two Galerkin bases: the Dirichlet sine one of phase 211 (which vanish at `±T` while the minimizer does not: algebraic convergence) and a new one in orthonormal Legendre polynomials (exact correlations, ball arithmetic, 70 digits; quadrature and precision checked to 12 digits; the only source of error is truncation at the basis size `N`).
- Result: NUMERICAL unless indicated; data, no law or closed form.
  - Convergence at `T = 0.8` (even sector): sines `N = 40…120`: `7.64, 6.63, 6.23, 5.99, 5.96, 5.94 e−12`; Legendre `N = 40…140`: `6.603, 5.858, 5.517, 5.410, 5.399, 5.372, 5.360, 5.344 e−12`, still decreasing. Best upper bound `λ_A(0.8) ≤ 5.344e−12`; estimated limit `5.30 ± 0.05 e−12`.
  - CORRECTIONS: the recorded value `6.2e−12` at `T = 0.8` is not converged (about 17 % high). Beyond `T ≈ 0.85` no basis converges (`T = 0.9`: `1.9e−16` with `N = 60`, `4.7e−17` with `N = 100`; `T = 0.95`: `8.5e−20`, `3.6e−20`; `T = 1.2`: `5.65e−37` with Legendre `N = 100` versus `2.6e−41` with sines `N = 90`). The recorded values `2.5e−23` (`T = 1.0`) and `2.6e−41` (`T = 1.2`) are upper bounds from non-converged bases, not data; the fit of 212-50 and the reading "size `≈ e^{−4πe^{2T}}`" rest on them and are not established.
  - PROVED (elementary, in Paper 46): `λ_A` is non-increasing in `T`. The grid with `N = 60` violates this near `T ≈ 1.03` and `1.2`, which confirms the lack of convergence there.
  - Table (`N = 60`; about 3 % for `T ≤ 0.85`; the minimum always in the even sector, the odd one `10–500` times larger): `T = 0.35`: `0.533`; `0.41`: `0.180`; `0.45`: `0.0661`; `0.49`: `0.0179`; `0.53`: `2.52e−3`; `0.55`: `9.21e−4`; `0.57`: `3.55e−4`; `0.61`: `3.56e−5`; `0.65`: `2.32e−6`; `0.69`: `1.31e−7`; `0.71`: `2.31e−8`; `0.75`: `7.55e−10`; `0.79`: `1.43e−11`; `0.81`: `1.90e−12`; `0.85`: `2.16e−14`.
  - Law for `T ≤ 0.85`: `log λ_A` is smooth in `T` at the grid resolution, with no resolvable kink at the entries of 3, 4, 5. With `X = e^{2T} ∈ [3, 5.5]`: `log λ = −9.93X + c` (rms `0.25`); `log λ = −13.7X + 15.6 log X + 17.2` (rms `0.064`); with fixed slope `−4π`: `10.8 log X + 19.1` (rms `0.098`). Slope and power are strongly correlated in this range; neither the exponent `4π` nor a prefactor is determined.
  - Entry of an atom: just after `T_n`, the measured `c_{F*}(log n)` exceeds the linear prediction `2hF*(T)F*(−T)` of the recorded entry formula (P211-24A, L9846) by factors `2.1, 2.4, 3.3, 6` for `n = 2, 3, 4, 5` with `h = 0.003`; `F*(±T)² ≈ 2.8λ, 7λ, 10λ` at the entries of 3, 4, 5. The composites (6, 10, 12) require `T > 0.9`: not done; classification by type of `n` OPEN.
  - Explicit test vectors (theta kernel `M = −K″ + ¼K` truncated at `k` terms, cut at `±T`, projected onto `P_T`): ratios `a_T(test)/λ_A = 1.8e2, 3.7e7, 6.7e18` for `k = 1` and `1.9e2, 2.8e6, 7.0e12` for `k = 3` at `T = 0.6, 0.8, 1.0`. Explicit vectors with abrupt cutoff are far from the floor; the floor is approximately the square of their Rayleigh quotient times a factor `e^{−O(X)}` (rough). No sequence of explicit tests converging to the floor was found; no smooth cutoff was tried.
  - Falsifiers: `𝔅` crosses zero in the odd sector at `T = 0.5658 ± 0.0001`, in the window where its comb is only `{2}` (the prime 3 enters for the integers at `0.5493` and `16/5` enters for `𝔅` only at `0.5816`); `1.1Λ` crosses zero in the even sector at `T ≈ 0.493`; `0.9Λ` at `T ≈ 0.645` (even sector).
- Why it does not close: data; neither law nor closed form.
- Reopening condition: an enriched basis (adapted to the edge) with `N ≥ 200` to reach `T > 0.9`.

### 212-67 — Explicit basis of the near-null ladder; the ladder reproduces the pinching in position
- Closest antecedent: 212-63, 212-64, 212-66; vector `X_T = Mχ_T − a·u_ev` (212-cotejo-margen L31144; 212-19-A; 212-20-B L31189); 212-21-A (L31199), 212-22-A (L31228); P211-17A (L9833, L6457), P211-18B (L9837, L6458).
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: an explicit family approximating the rungs of the ladder is given, and the admissible position interval of an atom is predicted with it.
- Result: NUMERICAL (data); no sign mechanism and no candidate identity.
  - (1) Family `M_J = span{Π_TM^{(j)}, 0 ≤ j < J}`, `M = −Φ″ + Φ/4`, `Φ` the Pólya kernel, `Π_T` the orthogonal projection onto `P_T` (`j` even → even sector, `j` odd → odd sector). At `T = 0.8`, `J = 8` (Galerkin `N = 90` sines, 60 digits), sines of the principal angles between `M_8` and the numerical ladder: even `k = 1`: `2.6e−4`; `k = 2`: `(2.2e−5, 1.1e−2)`; `k = 3`: `(1.5e−5, 2.2e−3, 0.15)`; odd `k = 1`: `1.0e−3`; `k = 2`: `(1.4e−4, 3.6e−2)`; `k = 3`: `(1.4e−4, 1.1e−2, 0.34)`. Each additional derivative adds about one rung.
  - Ritz values in `M_8`, `10–100` times above those of the ladder: even `1.0e−9, 2.3e−5, 2.6e−2` versus `5.97e−12, 6.02e−7, 3.3e−3`; odd `6.5e−8, 8.1e−4, 0.21` versus `1.08e−9, 5.3e−5, 0.106`. The orthogonal projection is not the right correction; a rung-by-rung generalization of `X_T` was not built. Caveat: `5.97e−12` at `T = 0.8` is with `N = 90` and is not the converged floor (212-66 gives `5.30 ± 0.05 e−12`).
  - (2) Pinching from the ladder: `D_n = −(v_n/n)∂_u c^{sym}(log n)` restricted to the 4 bottom modes per sector is indefinite. First-order prediction of the admissible interval of atom 3: `T = 0.60`: `[2.998, 3.0144]` (sweep of 212-64: `[2.999, 3.014]`); `T = 0.65`: `[2.99996, 3.0009]` (sweep: `[3.0000, 3.001]`). The even sector excludes positions below the integer, the odd one those above; endpoints `≈ n − λ_0^{even}/|D^{even}_{00}|` and `n + λ_0^{odd}/|D^{odd}_{00}|`. The 4-mode model agrees with the full linear model to 3 digits. The falsifier `𝔅` (`3 → 16/5`) lies `14–200` times beyond the crossings; for `𝔅` the family `M_J` stops being near-null because `v_{3.2}c_M(log 3.2) − v_3c_M(log 3)` is `O(1)`.
  - (3) Writing the Gram matrix of the form on the ladder as tail integrals and deciding its sign is P211-18B (NO-GO, "do not retry") together with P211-17A (Schur form on the survivor); 212-20-B, 212-21-A and 212-22-A already identify the vector with images of the radical on the full line. That part was not redone and remains closed.
  - (4) Not done: `T = 1.0, 1.2`; `k = 6, 8`; single-theta-term family; explicit complement/Schur block; atom 4.
- Why it does not close: data; the explicit basis gives no sign and the pinching is first-order.
- Do not retry: tail Gram matrix on the explicit ladder as the carrier of the sign (= P211-18B).
- Reopening condition: an explicit rung-by-rung correction (not the orthogonal projection) with Ritz values at the level of the ladder, or an exact statement of the pinching.

### 212-68 — Enriched solver for the floor of `a_T` on `P_T`; converged values up to `T = 0.8`; two-sided pinching of positions and of null weights
- Closest antecedent: 212-63, 212-64, 212-66, 212-67; linear entry formula of P211-24A (L9846).
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: a basis enriched at the singular points of the minimizer gives converged values up to `T = 0.8` and a grid up to `T = 0.93`.
- Result: NUMERICAL (data and tool); no sign mechanism.
  - (1) Diagnosis of the slow convergence: the bottom vector has jump-type singularities at the first-generation comb points `±(T − log n)`, of amplitude `~ √λ` (`F(±T)² ≈` a few times `λ`). With 40 global Legendre and graded local pieces only at the endpoints: `6.603e−12 → 6.451e−12`; adding pieces at `±(T − log n)`: `5.303e−12`; second generation `−0.04 %`; more layers `−0.004 %`. The smooth part requires a global degree growing like `~ e^{2T}` (`T = 1.0`: `N = 60`: `2.93e−22`; `100`: `1.53e−23`; `140`: `1.389e−23`).
  - (2) Solver: global Legendre (`N_g`) plus one-sided piecewise Legendre (degree `p_e`) in geometric layers at `±T` and at the comb points; the `1/u` part of `K` integrated exactly; ball arithmetic at 50–70 digits; generalized eigenvalue problem, exact parity sectors, exact `P_T`; residues `~ 1e−52`.
  - (3) Converged: `λ_A(0.8) = 5.2940(3)e−12` (sequence `5.30308, 5.29543, 5.29511, 5.29433, 5.29417 e−12`). Ladder at `0.8`: even `4.9858e−7, 2.7760e−3, 0.61585`; odd `9.755e−10, 4.6521e−5, 8.728e−2, 0.7834`. `T = 1.0` NOT converged: upper bound `1.327e−23` (even ladder `1.056e−17, 1.173e−12, 3.34e−8`; odd `7.84e−21, 3.15e−15, 1.65e−10`). Floors (even sector, always the minimum; odd floor `10–300` times larger): `T = 0.534`: `1.953e−3`; `0.564`: `4.702e−4`; `0.678`: `3.547e−7`; `0.708`: `2.689e−8`; `0.75`: `7.402e−10`; `0.80`: `5.294e−12`; `0.85`: `1.954e−14`; `0.891`: `1.588e−16` (precision 5 %); `0.911`: `1.148e−17`; `0.93`: `6.57e−19`. Monotone in `T`.
  - (4) Entries of 3, 4, 5, 6: slopes of `log λ` before/across/after: 3: `−53.2/−41.4/−47.8`; 4: `−84.8/−84.5/−88.7`; 5: `−94.8/−108.6/−105.9`; 6: `−119.4/−130.2/−137.2`. Kink versus curvature not separable with step `0.01`: OPEN. At 3 the slope softens after the entry, against the linear entry formula of P211-24A.
  - (5) Floor law (19 points, `X = e^{2T} ∈ [2.9, 6.2]`): `log λ = aX + b log X + c` with `a = −13.07 ± 0.23`, `b = 13.1 ± 1.0`; slope `−4π` compatible (`b = 10.90`), `−2π` excluded (rms `0.82`). Structured residues (sign pattern following the integer part of `X`); range too short. Not established.
  - (6) Two-sided pinching (Hellmann–Feynman slopes `dλ/dx = −v_nc_F′(log n)/n`, confirmed by direct sweeps): the even floor rises when the atom moves to the right, the odd one falls. Admissible `x − n`: `T = 0.75`: atom 3 `(−6.7e−9, +6.1e−7)`, atom 4 `(−1.8e−5, +8.8e−5)`; `T = 0.85`: atom 3 `(−1.4e−13, +6.0e−11)`, atom 4 `(−5.4e−11, +1.2e−9)`, atom 5 `(−6.1e−7, +2.85e−6)`.
  - (7) Null weight at non-atoms (`T = 0.93`): adding weight `ε` at `y`, `dλ/dε = −c_{F*}(log y)`, with opposite signs in the two sectors: `y = 6`: `c_even = +1.10e−13`, `c_odd = −1.43e−11`, admissible `ε` `(−1.5e−5, +6e−6)`; `y = 5.9`: `(−2.8e−6, +9.4e−7)`; `y = 6.1`: `(−1.1e−4, +4.9e−5)`. The null weight is pinched on both sides at 6, but equally at 5.9 and 6.1: nothing distinguishes the integer 6 in this test; tolerance `= λ/|c_{F*}(log y)|`.

- Why it does not close: data and tool; the pinching is local and first-order, and the null-weight test does not distinguish integers from non-integers.
- Reopening condition: converged `T ≥ 1.0` with `N_g ~ 200`; separation of kink and curvature at the entries; an exact statement of the two-sided pinching.

### 212-69 — First-order statement of the pinching in position; it is not a sign mechanism
- Closest antecedent: 212-64, 212-67 (2), 212-68 (6); P211-18B (L9837).
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: the first-order formula is proved and it is examined whether the pinching can carry the sign.
- Result: no candidate. First-order formula PROVED; data NUMERICAL; pinching as a sign mechanism NO-GO (circular).
  - (1) PROVED (standard perturbation of a simple eigenvalue): moving the atom `n` to `x` with the weight frozen, `dλ_s/dx` at `x = n` equals `−(v_n/n)c′_{F_s}(log n)`, with `F_s` the normalized bottom vector of sector `s`; predicted endpoint `x_s = n − λ_s/(dλ_s/dx)`.
  - (2) NUMERICAL: `n = 3`: `T = 0.6`, slopes `+0.0378` (even), `−0.256` (odd), interval `[2.99805, 3.0144]` (sweep of 212-64: `[2.999, 3.014]`); `T = 0.7`: `+0.0925`, `−0.188`, interval `[3 − 6.9e−7, 3 + 3.9e−5]`. `n = 4`: `T = 0.72`: `+8.8e−6`, `−3.5e−4`, `[4 − 1.2e−3, 4 + 4.3e−3]`; `T = 0.8`: `+1.6e−4`, `−2.6e−3`, `[4 − 3.8e−8, 4 + 4.2e−7]`.
  - `n = 2`: BOTH sectors negative: `T = 0.6`: `−0.81`, `−0.039`; `T = 0.7`: `−0.94`, `−0.27`; `T = 0.8`: `−1.02`, `−0.43`. First order excludes only positions above 2 (`2 + 9e−5`, `2 + 6.7e−8`, `2 + 5.8e−12`); the lower endpoint for atom 2 is second-order or from rung mixing, OPEN, not computed. Therefore "the two parity sectors pinch from opposite sides at every integer" is REFUTED at `n = 2`; the opposition at `n = 3, 4` reflects where `log 3`, `log 4` fall with respect to the sign changes of the bottom autocorrelation (ARGUED).
  - (3) NO-GO as a sign mechanism: the pinching presupposes `λ_s ≥ 0` (endpoints `n ∓ λ/|D|`). The same first-order formula holds for `𝔅` at its own positions and for `1.1Λ`, where `λ_s < 0` at `T = 0.6` and the interval is empty or inverted; the step that fails for the falsifiers is the input `λ_s ≥ 0` itself. No relation between even/odd floors and position derivatives forces non-negativity.
  - (4) Near-null vectors: the Pólya derivatives cut off and projected by `Π_T` have Ritz/ladder ratio for the bottom rung `≈ 10` (`T = 0.6`), `220` (`0.7`), `4.4e4` (`0.8`) in the even sector; `3.2, 55, 2.2e3` in the odd one, that is, they grow like `λ^{−1/2}`: the Ritz value is the tail Gram matrix (closed), and the true floor is of the order of its square. Euler–Lagrange: `χAF = λF + αe^{t/2} + βe^{−t/2}`; for `F = χM^{(j)}` the comb part of the residue is `Σ_n(v_n/2)χ[(1−χ)M^{(j)}](t ± log n)`, the exterior tail translated into the window, with jumps at `±(T − log n)` (coincides with 212-68). Candidate corrector family `X_j = Π_T[χM^{(j)} + Σ_nc_{n,j}χ((1−χ)M^{(j)})(· ± log n)]`: ARGUED, not validated (computations not concluded), OPEN.
- Why it does not close: the pinching is circular as a source of sign (it assumes the sign of the floor).
- Do not retry: the pinching (opposition of sectors in the position derivatives) as the carrier of the sign; "opposite pinching at every integer".
- Reopening condition: for the data part, validate the corrector family `X_j` with Ritz values at the level of the ladder; none for the pinching as a mechanism.

### 212-71 — Selection on the data of 212-63 … 212-70: five operations considered, none passes the four-point filter
- Closest antecedent: 212-63 … 212-70; antecedents by operation below.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: an attempt was made to convert the new data (ladder, pinching, converged floor, Euler–Lagrange equation) into a sign operation.
- Result: selection without a seed (it is not a new impossibility theorem).
  - (1) Flow identity in the window: `dλ/dT = −`(sum of squares of the edge and jump traces of the bottom vector), `λ(T) = λ(T′) + ∫` squares. Dies: it needs the terminal sign (the goal); it uses only the Euler–Lagrange system and monotonicity, both valid for `𝔅` and `1.1Λ`. Antecedents: L4680 (window variation / virial, DEAD), L5940, P211-24A (L9846), L1892 (induction on the window, repetition). The dilation variant is equivalent to moving all the atoms at once, that is, the pinching of 212-69 (circular).
  - (2) "floor `≈` (Ritz of cut-off Pólya vectors)`²`" read as `A_T ≈ G²` with `G` blind to the comb: canonical factorization / square-root barrier (L19971; R162_1402 Thm 3, L13965); with `G` the tail Gram matrix it is P211-18B (L9837); the rest carries the comb without sign.
  - (3) Product formula `λ_A(T) = Π` over entering integers of positive factors: ratios of determinants / Schur pivots, clause 4.6 W-det (L1129, L3918); induction on the window L1892; closure under products of Euler factors L1911, L11190.
  - (4) Mixing even and odd floors to cancel comb terms using the opposite signs of their autocorrelations: linear in `c_F`, classes K8/K10 of 212-56; does not distinguish 6 from 5.9/6.1 (212-68 (7)); does not account for atom 2 (212-69).
  - (5) Ladder as index count / spectral flow / Kreĭn between the two sectors: BARRIER_W_001 (L5809, L1901).
- Why it does not close (common cause): each use of the new data is first-order or variational in the window or in the positions (it needs the sign of an extremum), or is canonical factorization / tail Gram matrix, or is linear in `c_F`; none couples the Euler product to integrality in a nonlinear way; each identity holds for `𝔅` and `1.1Λ` until the sign of the extremum is used.
- Reopening condition: an exact solution, over all generations, of the Euler–Lagrange system whose singular coefficients at `±(T − log k)` are arithmetic in `Λ` (not given by the eigenvalue).

CORRECTION to 212-68: the "jump-type singularities" at `±(T − log n)` are vanishing singularities of type `l^{−5/2}`; the convergence gain from local pieces there is maintained.
  - (3) Generating identity (algebra PROVED; identification as parametrix ARGUED; formal sum): singular points `T − log q`, `q ∈ ℚ_{>0}` (two-sided words), `F̂_sing(τ) ~ b e^{iτT}P(τ)m(τ)/s_T(τ) = b e^{iτT}P(τ)Σ_j(c(τ)/m(τ))^j`, `c(τ) = Σ_n(v_n/2)(n^{iτ} + n^{−iτ})`; coefficient at `T − log q`: `b·Σ_jd_j(q)·profile_{3/2+j}`, `d_j(q) = Σ` over words `n_1^{±1}…n_j^{±1} = q` of `Π v_{n_i}/2`; the one-sided words give the coefficients of `(Σ(v_n/2)n^{−s})^j` truncated at `log k < 2T`. ### 212-75 — From cells to the full carrier: equivalence by density
- Antecedent: 212-42, 212-46, 212-59; smooth kernel of P46 (proof of thm:KEP2 and passage over C_c^∞ ∩ P_T). It is an auxiliary verification of the scope of the existing carrier, not a sign candidate nor a new reformulation proposed as an advance.
- Status: PROVED as an auxiliary equivalence of carriers, after independent review of normalization, domain, convergence and moments. It is not a sign mechanism and no paper is modified.
- Verified statement: if the exact unit-cell matrices are positive semidefinite at all sizes on the two constraints Σ a_j = 0 and Σ a_j log((j+1)/j) = 0, j ≥ 1, then the form is non-negative on all of P_T, for all T. The converse implication is obtained by applying global positivity to each cell test, whose logarithmic image has compact support and belongs to the form domain.
- Density detail. For smooth F with compact support interior to I_T, put f(x)=x^(-1/2)F(log x). Let E_h be the average over cells [jh,(j+1)h), h=1/q. The supports of E_h f stay in a fixed compact subset of (0,∞) and, for small h, inside (e^(-T),e^T). One has E_h f→f in L² and uniformly bounded total variation: each difference between adjacent averages is expressed as an average of f(x+h)−f(x), and the sum of their moduli is bounded by ∫|f'|. The L∞ norms are also uniformly bounded.
- Returning to t, F_h(t)=e^(t/2)E_h f(e^t) has fixed compact support, and L¹ norm and total variation uniformly bounded. For G_h=F_h−F one obtains |Ĝ_h(τ)|≤C min(1,|τ|^(-1)) and Ĝ_h(τ)→0 pointwise by L¹ convergence. Domination gives convergence in H^s for each 0<s<1/2, and hence in the norm with weight log(2+|τ|). The comb of a fixed window is a bounded operator; so the forms converge.
- Exact correction. Choose two smooth functions φ_1,φ_2 with small disjoint ordered supports inside the interval in x, so that the matrix of their moments (∫φ_i,∫φ_i/x) is invertible. This is achieved with non-negative bumps: their averages of 1/x belong to disjoint intervals. The moment matrix of E_h φ_i converges to it. Subtract from E_h f the combination of E_h φ_i whose coefficients solve the two moment errors. The coefficients tend to zero, the convergence in the form norm is preserved and both moments become exactly zero.
- Passage to unit cells. If f_h is the corrected approximant, define g_h(y)=sqrt(h) f_h(hy). It is constant on [j,j+1), with j≥1 for small h. Its moments are h^(-1/2)∫f_h and h^(1/2)∫f_h/x, both zero. Its logarithmic image is F_h(t+log h): a translation that preserves autocorrelation, norm and global form. Each translated test fits in some finite window. The hypothesis at all cell sizes would give a(F_h)≥0; the limit and the smooth kernel give the goal. This argument does not give a reduction to a fixed size.
- Falsifiers: density and translation work equally for any locally finite comb; they provide no sign and do not distinguish Λ. The arithmetic load remains entirely in the positivity of the matrices for all sizes. The reopening condition of 212-59 remains without an explicit positive identity.
- Specification for the review of 212-75: indices i,j∈{1,…,N}, matrix M_N=A_N−C_N, with A_N exactly that of 212-59 and C_N=Σ_{n=2}^N (Λ(n)/n)(B_{n,N}+B_{n,N}^*), where (B_{n,N})_{ji}=1 if ni≤j<n(i+1), and 0 otherwise. It is the matrix writing of the comb of 212-42/58, not a positive factorization. For complex vectors a* M_N a is used; the constraints are complex linear, Σa_j=Σa_j log((j+1)/j)=0. Do not confuse this subspace with the single-constraint one used in several numerical tables of 212-59.
- Points checked in the review: normalization of A_N and C_N against the continuous form; form domain of the step tests; uniform variation estimate after x=e^t; moment correction with interior support; translation step between windows; density of the primitive smooth kernel. The equivalence of carriers and the positivity, which is not proved here, are kept separate.

- Refinements from the review: for a_j=h^(-1)∫_[jh,(j+1)h) f, Var(E_h f)=Σ_j|a_j−a_(j−1)|≤h^(-1)∫|f(x)−f(x−h)|dx≤||f′||_1. After the logarithmic change, the Fourier majorant C min(1,|τ|^(-1)) implies H^s, s<1/2, by domination; it also applies to each corrector. To avoid ambiguity between windows, a(F) is defined on compact tests with the full comb: there are only finitely many non-null contacts, and enlarging the window does not change its value.
- Verification of the matrix: for i<j, A_ij=−(1/2)∫_i^(i+1)∫_j^(j+1)[1/(z−x)+1/(z+x)] dz dx, which gives the formula of 212-59 even for adjacent cells. The diagonal is −γ−log(4π)+log(2i+1)+2i log(1+1/(2i)). The overlap <e_i,D_n e_j>=n^(-1/2) 1_{ni≤j<n(i+1)} verifies C_N. A finite cell test has compact BV logarithmic image, hence belongs to the form domain; this proves the converse implication without an omitted smoothness hypothesis.
- Final result of the scope: equivalence of carriers verified, positivity of M_N OPEN. This verification does not provide the missing positive identity nor by itself enable a new Laplace construction.

The geometric blocks are already included above; the divisor identity does not identify the Hardy and radial pairings nor provide a positive grouping of the crossings. ### 212-77 — Local/global correction and scope of the limits of squares in 212-43/49
- Antecedents: 212-43, 212-49 (1), 212-51 (iv), 212-51-rev, 212-56 C3/C7; P46 lem:K/thm:A; P48 F4 and linear limits; R166_502 §1.
- Result after independent review: PROVED correction of the local/global scope. The Fourier transform of the extension by zero, C:L²(I_T)→L²(R), has kernel e^(iκt)/sqrt(2π), smooth and locally L², but C*C=I has a delta kernel. Therefore local L² does not ensure absence of atoms. The sentence of 212-49 was corrected: global HS with D bounded suffices, or explicit absence of atoms in C*C,D*C,C*D. For unbounded D, domains and control of the products are also needed.
- Scope of limits: the separation of diagonal and cross terms of a finite sum does not pass automatically to an infinite family by convergence of the total form. The extraction of d=Σ|a_g|² requires a separate legitimate limit and preserving the distributional decomposition. No impossibility is claimed for joint limits outside those hypotheses.
- Example already proved in P46: m(F)−C0||F||²=(1/2)∫_0^∞K(u)||F−V_uF||²du. Since K(u)~1/u at zero, the diagonal and the cross term expanded diverge separately for F≠0, although the joint square is finite on the form domain. This realizes only Arch−C0, not the complete form nor its sign.
- A finite limit of complete squares is distinguished from subtracting a divergent counterterm: positivity is not automatically preserved in the second operation.
- Selection status: no candidate. Infinite families and renormalizations had already been considered; the correction does not establish novelty. The audit of 212-43/49 refers to its text in the index: no separate primary memo was located in the routes examined, and no theorem stronger than the written hypotheses is certified.

### 212-73 — Compiled solver (C with Arb, piecewise orthonormal mesh graded at 0, `±T`, `±(T − log n)`); converged floor up to `T = 1.05`; kinks at the entries of 3, 4, 5; a residue pattern is withdrawn
- Closest antecedent: 212-66, 212-68, 212-72.
- What changes with respect to the antecedent: compiled solver with graded mesh; it replaces numbers of 212-68 where indicated and withdraws the residue pattern of 212-68 (5).
- Result: NUMERICAL (tool and data); no sign mechanism.
  - (1) Validation: the same basis of 212-68 at `T = 0.8` reproduces it to 15 digits; the new mesh gives `5.294257e−12` (consistent with `5.2940(3)e−12`); doubling the precision (60 versus 120 digits at `T = 1.0`; 70 versus 110 at `T = 1.2`) gives identical results. A midpoint precision error in Arb was found and corrected.
  - (2) Converged values. `λ_A(1.0) = 1.320(1)e−23` (sequence `1.6041, 1.32250, 1.32231, 1.321087, 1.321086, 1.320703 e−23`); even ladder `1.0530e−17, 1.1694e−12, 3.3374e−8`; odd `7.820e−21, 3.1402e−15, 1.6482e−10, 3.2346e−6`. `T = 0.90`: even `4.5002e−17, 1.12141e−11, 3.50732e−7, 2.44816e−3`; odd `1.50410e−14, 1.89815e−9, 2.57417e−5, 5.9497e−2`. `T = 0.95`: even `3.3937e−20, 1.62420e−14, 1.14548e−9, 1.41043e−5`; odd `1.55994e−17, 3.63211e−12, 1.19045e−7, 8.15989e−4`. `T = 1.05`: even `1.80462e−27, 2.48337e−21, 4.96230e−16, 2.72905e−11`; odd `1.29100e−24, 1.01280e−18, 9.47679e−14, 3.97162e−9`. `T = 1.10`: floor `3.34e−31`, only to a few percent. ONLY UPPER BOUNDS: `T = 1.15`: `2.07e−32`; `1.20`: `5.12e−36`; `1.25`: `2.79e−37` (the floor keeps dropping by large factors with the grading depth; the limitation is the resolution near `±T`, not the precision; `|F(±T)| ~ 1e−11` at `T = 1`).
  - (3) The even sector has the minimum for all `T ∈ [0.539, 1.25]`; `odd_0/even_0 = 334, 460, 592, 715` at `T = 0.90, 0.95, 1.00, 1.05`; the ratios between rungs grow with `T` (even `1/0`: `2.5e5 → 1.4e6`).
  - (4) Entries (secant slopes of `log λ` before/across/after, step down to `1e−4`): `n = 3`: even `−33.7/−34.2/−39.6`, odd `−66.0/−64.1/−54.7` (slope jump `≈ −6` even, `+11` odd); `n = 4`: even `−75.1/−73.6/−80.0`, odd `−83.5/−84.8/−77.7` (`≈ −5`, `+6`); `n = 5`: even `−95.1/…/−98.7`, odd `−116/…/−109` (`≈ −4`, `+7`); `n = 7` inconclusive (noise); `n = 8` sparse (even drop `≈ −15` suggested); the composite 6 is smooth at resolution `0.002`. The sign agrees with the edge formula `Δ(dλ/dT) = −2v_nF(T)F(−T)` (only indicative). Curvature prior to the entry: the even slope rises sharply below `T_n` (`n = 3`: `−52.6 → −33.7`; `n = 4`: `−92 → −75`; `n = 5`: `−122 → −95`), the odd one the other way round; independent of the mesh. This resolves the OPEN item (4) of 212-68 for `n = 3, 4, 5`: the kinks exist. Note: at `T = ½log(ab)` the interior singular points `T − log a` and `−T + log b` coincide for prime powers `a, b`, so the composites could carry features. Windows 9–12 not converged.
  - (5) Law: 71 converged points, `X = e^{2T} ∈ [2.94, 8.17]`: `log λ = aX + b log X + c`, `a = −13.2548`, `b = 13.7817`, `c = 17.698`, rms `0.085`. The residues do NOT follow the integer part of `X` (they oscillate `±0.1` within a unit interval; means by integer part `−0.089, +0.057, +0.002, −0.048, −0.030, +0.009, +0.061`): the pattern of 212-68 (5) is WITHDRAWN.
- Corrections: `λ_A(1.0)`: the bound `1.327e−23` of 212-68 is replaced by the converged value `1.320(1)e−23`; the fit of the law is replaced by that of (5); the residue pattern of 212-68 (5) is withdrawn; item (4) of 212-68 resolved for 3, 4, 5.
- Why it does not close: data and tool.
- Not done: converged values beyond `T ≈ 1.10`; windows 9–12; dense points at 6.
- Reopening condition: does not apply (tool); extending the convergence to `T > 1.1` requires more grading depth near `±T`.
