### 212-85 — Continuous Gaussian profile of C6: condition on the atoms

Status: PROVED for the declared class, with proof independently reviewed. Antecedents: 212-51, 212-58(2), 212-75 and the identification of the complete defect after 212-84. Not a sign candidate nor a closure of C6.

**Class.** Fix a,c>0 and w_y(x)=x^(-1/2)exp[−a(log y−log x)^2]. Let μ be positive with H(s)=∫exp[−2a(log y−s)^2]dμ(y) finite and C∞. Suppose justified the interchanges giving K_μ=A_μ K_0, A_μ(x,z)=∫w_y(x)w_y(z)dμ(y). K_0 is real symmetric and independent of y. Near each diagonal point, at s=(x+z)/2, r=z−x, its form is −c pf(1/|r|)+d(s)δ(r)+R_0(s,r), with d,R_0 smooth. Near z=Nx, N≥2 integer, off the diagonal, its form is b_N δ(z−Nx)+R_N, with b_N constant and R_N smooth; the singularities are locally isolated. Require |b_N|≤C N^M for finite constants C,M independent of N. These are hypotheses of this class, not properties attributed to every admissible object.

The target kernel has diagonal singular coefficient −1/2 in this convention, a smooth diagonal counterterm, and coefficient −Λ(N) against δ(z−Nx). It is required that D=A_μK_0−K_target vanish on all compact tests with ∫f dx=∫f dx/x=0, in all windows.

**Exact covariance.** Completing the square gives

    A_μ(x,z)=(xz)^(-1/2) exp[−(a/2)(log(x/z))^2] H((log x+log z)/2).

**Singularities and moments.** Put L=∂_x(x²∂_x). For φ∈C_c∞(0,∞), Lφ has both moments zero because L1=L(1/x)=0. By polarization and formal self-adjointness, the vanishing of D implies L_xL_zD=0 distributionally. No regularity of the functionals of a null kernel is presupposed.

Off r=0, near the diagonal, D=−g(s)/|r|+|r|B(s,r), plus a smooth remainder, where g(s)=cA_μ(s,s)−1/2 and B is smooth. Indeed, by symmetry and Taylor, A_μ(s−r/2,s+r/2)=A_μ(s,s)+r²B_0(s,r), with B_0 smooth; this also justifies the estimates of its derivatives. On applying L_xL_z, the term of order |r|^(-5) is −24s^4g(s)/|r|^5; the remaining ones have lower order. The counterterms supported on the diagonal do not intervene off it. It follows that g=0, hence H(log x)=x/(2c) and

    A_μ(x,z)=(2c)^(-1) exp[−(a/2)(log(x/z))^2].

Near z=Nx, the atomic coefficient of the defect is f_N(x)=b_N A_μ(x,Nx)+Λ(N). In L_xL_z[f_N(x)δ(z−Nx)], the normal derivative of order four of δ has leading coefficient x²z²N² f_N(x), evaluated on the line. The other terms have lower normal order or are smooth. Since x,z>0, it follows that f_N=0; the diagonal counterterms lie outside this neighborhood. Therefore

    b_N=−2c Λ(N) exp[(a/2)(log N)^2].

On N=2^k, its absolute value is 2c log2 exp[(a/2)k²(log2)^2], incompatible with C exp[Mk log2] for large k. No measure of the declared class satisfies the identity with polynomial growth of b_N.

**Scope.** It has not been proved that polynomial growth is obligatory for every construction: it was imposed explicitly. Bases of larger growth with compensated convergence, other profiles, data a_m or ν depending on y, nor measures without the declared regularity are excluded. A family with window-dependent width a tending to zero is not excluded either: the contradiction uses fixed a>0 and global polynomial growth. The discard does not separate cΛ either and contributes no sign to the form. There is no new certified window and no changes in papers.

- Selection after 212-85: profile φ_β(t)=sqrt(β/2)sech(βt), w_y(x)=y^(-1/2)φ_β(log(y/x)), μ(dy)=dy. REJECTED as a new sign seed after independent review: the change t=log y leads to the homogeneous average already identified in 212-58(2). The proposed correlation k_β(r)=βr/sinh(βr) allows polynomial atomic compensation b_N=−Λ(N)sinh(βlog N)/(βlog N), so 212-85 does not exclude this profile. No new construction was opened nor was the division K_0=(K_target+R)/k_β presented as a mechanism: a formula of its own for R null on P and the positivity of the resulting kernel remain pending. Pointwise division by a positive kernel does not preserve operator positivity. The identification of b_(p^k) with coefficients of differences of logs of Euler products does not supply that inequality. Reopening: explicit R plus sign operation; not a NO-GO of the sech profile nor of the general non-homogeneous case.

### 212-86 — Local tail rate by means of two singular-value bounds

Status: abstract lemma PROVED, independently reviewed; application CONDITIONAL on the external smoothing input. No global positivity. Internal antecedents: BUILD_083 (control of tails and need for uniform estimates), 212-22-B and precision of B2. Directed cross-check without this step localized; no claim of priority. Operational difference: combining the norm of a spectral tail with the singular-value decay of its localization, keeping the same operator, gives an explicit trace rate.

**Lemma.** Let A be bounded self-adjoint, E a spectral projection onto a negative part of its spectrum and N=−AE≥0 with ||N||≤κ. Let M be self-adjoint, ||M||≤1, and suppose s_j(MA)≤L j^(−m), m>1. Then T=MNM≥0 is trace class and

    Tr(T) ≤ [m/(m−1)] L^(1/m) κ^(1−1/m).

Proof: T=−(MA)EM, so s_j(T)≤s_j(MA), since EM is a contraction. Also s_j(T)≤||T||≤κ. The sum of min(κ,Lj^(−m)) is bounded by the integral from 0 to infinity of min(κ,Lx^(−m)); splitting it at x=(L/κ)^(1/m) gives the written constant. The cases κ=0 or L=0 are immediate. It is not assumed that M commutes with A or E.

**Delimited application.** Primary source: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.13129v1#S8, Lemma 8.9 and equation (66). The cited input is s_j(M_η A)≤C_m(R^c/j)^m for a smooth cutoff η. Its proof has not been independently audited. With N_n the negative spectral tail and κ_tail=||N_n||, the lemma gives

    Tr(M_η N_n M_η) ≤ [m/(m−1)] C_m^(1/m) R^c κ_tail^(1−1/m).

This supplies a rate for (66) under that input. For a cutoff 0≤χ≤1, take η=1 on its support, 0≤η≤1, with support of comparable size; χ≤η² allows dominating its localized trace without requiring smoothness of sqrt(χ). The dependence of C_m on scale and semilocal data is kept. A rate in n additionally requires a quantitative bound on κ_tail, not just its convergence to zero.

**Limit.** The result controls a localized tail; not the retained finite negative part, the uniform high-frequency density nor the Schur complement. The global sign hypothesis remains OPEN. This external form has not been automatically identified with a_T on P_T, nor are its constants transferred to Paper 46. No papers modified.

### 212-87 — Uniform negative tail on tests of fixed support

Status: PROVED as an abstract lemma, with complete proof independently reviewed. Semilocal application established in the following extension under CITED dependencies; no global sign. Antecedents: 212-86; uniform control pending from the primary source linked there. Difference: localization on intervals of fixed length with logarithmic constant in their CENTER, obtained from the kernel on the line and from approximation in Hilbert–Schmidt norm. The Cayley change with polynomial constants in the center is not used.

**Hypotheses and goal.** In L²(R,ds), let P be the Hardy projection with kernel (1/2)δ(s−t)+(1/(2πi))pv(1/(s−t)). Let v∈C²(R), |v|=1, and ℓ(s)=1+log(2+|s|). Suppose |v'(s)|≤Bℓ(s), |v''(s)|≤Bℓ(s)². Put A=M_v* P M_v−P. Let E be a spectral projection of A onto its negative spectrum, N=−AE≥0 and ||N||≤κ. For each fixed T it is intended to prove

    Tr(M_H N M_H*) ≤ C_(T,B) κ^(1/3) ∫ℓ(s)|H(s)|² ds,

for H the Fourier transform of f∈L² with support in [−T,T] and finite right-hand energy. The constants are not uniform in T nor in parameters affecting B. For a tail N_n with κ_n→0, the bound is uniform over all those f, not only over a finite family.

**1. Kernel and local bounds.** The δ term cancels, and A has kernel

    a(s,t)=[conjugate(v(s))v(t)−1]/[2πi(s−t)].

Take η_j(s)=η(s−j), 0≤η≤1, equal to1 on [0,1], supported in (−1,2). Let B_j=M_(η_j)A, G_j(s,t)=η_j(s)a(s,t) and ℓ_j=1+log(2+|j|). With constants independent of j,

    ||G_j||_(L²(ds dt))² ≤ Cℓ_j,
    ||∂_s G_j||_(L²(ds dt))² ≤ Cℓ_j³.                 (a)

Proof: near the diagonal, |s−t|≤1/ℓ_j, write the difference quotient as −conjugate(v(s))∫_0^1 v'(s+θ(t−s))dθ. Its size is O(ℓ_j) and its derivative in s is O(ℓ_j²), using v'' and v'. The intermediate points remain at bounded distance from j. Integrating the squares over width 1/ℓ_j gives O(ℓ_j) and O(ℓ_j³). Outside that strip, |a|≤C/|s−t| and |∂_s a|≤C[ℓ_j/|s−t|+1/|s−t|²]. The corresponding integrals from 1/ℓ_j to infinity give the same bounds. The derivatives of η_j have uniform constants and are covered by these limits. This proves (a) without differentiating v(t) in the far region.

**2. Singular values.** Use an interval of length5 containing the support of η_j in its interior, and project the variable s onto the Fourier modes of absolute index≤J. The approximant has rank r=2J+1 and, by Parseval and absence of boundary terms,

    ||B_j−Q_J B_j||_HS ≤ C J^(−1) ℓ_j^(3/2).

The quadratic tail of the singular values after rank r does not exceed the square of that error. By monotonicity, r s_(2r)(B_j)² is bounded by that tail. Adjusting indices and the first values (||B_j||≤1), one obtains

    s_q(B_j) ≤ C ℓ_j^(3/2) q^(−3/2), q≥1.          (b)

**3. Mass of the tail in each cell.** T_j=M_(η_j)N M_(η_j)≥0 has norm≤κ and T_j=−B_j E M_(η_j). Applying 212-86 to (b), with m=3/2, gives

    Tr(T_j) ≤ C ℓ_j κ^(1/3).                       (c)

The identity Tr(M_η N M_η)=||M_η N^(1/2)||_HS²=Tr(N^(1/2)M_(η²)N^(1/2)) allows dominating the projection of each cell by η_j². Thus the local measure ν_N(I)=Tr(N^(1/2)M_(1_I)N^(1/2)) is finite on bounded intervals by (c). It has density ρ_N(s)=Σ_l |(N^(1/2)e_l)(s)|² for an orthonormal basis: Tonelli and (c) justify the local representation and its independence of the basis. In particular,

    ∫_[j,j+1] ρ_N(s)ds ≤ C ℓ_j κ^(1/3).           (d)

No pointwise bound on ρ_N is claimed.

**4. From local mass to all tests of the fixed support.** Choose χ∈C_c∞ equal to1 on [−T,T], and ψ=χ̂/(2π) with the convention H(s)=∫f(t)e^(−ist)dt. Then ψ is Schwartz and H=H*ψ. Cauchy–Schwarz with weight |ψ| implies

    sup_[j,j+1]|H|² ≤ ||ψ||_1 ∫|H(y)|² sup_(s∈[j,j+1])|ψ(s−y)|dy.

The moderation of the logarithmic weight and the decay of ψ give

    Σ_j ℓ_j sup_[j,j+1]|H|² ≤ C_T ∫ℓ(y)|H(y)|²dy. (e)

Indeed, the sum of ℓ_j sup_[j,j+1]|ψ(s−y)| is ≤C_Tℓ(y), using ℓ_j≤Cℓ(y)(1+|j−y|) and any order of decay greater than3. Combining (d),(e) proves the announced bound. Since f has compact support and belongs to L², it also belongs to L¹; H and M_H are bounded. Finally Tr(M_H N M_H*)=∫|H|²ρ_N by Tonelli; the bound proves that this positive operator is trace class. No Gevrey norm nor Galerkin dimension is used.

**Application obligations (verified in the following extension, with CITED dependencies).** To apply it to the obligation H2′ of the source cited in 212-86, one must verify the exact unitary conjugation to A, the two global derivative bounds of v, the identification of M_H and the existence of the negative tail with κ_n→0. Even if fulfilled, only the tail is controlled: the retained negative block is not eliminated nor is the Schur complement signed. No uniform bound is claimed as the set of primes or the window grows. Papers untouched.

#### Application of 212-87 to the semilocal symbol — independently reviewed

Identification sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.13129v1#S8, equation (53) and §§8.1–8.3. The structure of the space and the compactness of the negative part, with absence of the negative intersection block, are taken CITED from lemmas 8.5–8.6; their independent audit is not claimed.

Put a=log t, D_a=M_(exp(ias)), P_t=D_a P D_a*, U=M_u. Then A_t=1−P_t−Phat_t=U*P_(1/t)U−P_t and

    D_a* A_t D_a = M_v* P M_v−P,    v(s)=exp(2ias)u(s).

It is multiplier algebra: P_(1/t)=D_(−a) P D_(−a)* and U commutes with D_a. Also M_H commutes with D_a, so the conjugation preserves the trace being estimated.

For a finite set S, u is the product of the archimedean factor u_∞(s)=π^(is)Γ(1/4−is/2)/Γ(1/4+is/2) and unimodular local factors rational in exp(is log p). For a factor u_p=(1−r exp(−is log p))/(1−r exp(is log p)), r=p^(−1/2), the logarithmic derivatives satisfy

    |u_p'/u_p| ≤ 2(log p)r/(1−r),
    |(u_p'/u_p)'| ≤ 2(log p)²r/(1−r)².

The same bounds hold for the inverse. The choice of the quotient depends on the local convention, without altering the regularity check.

For the gamma factor, use the classical series of https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.7.E6 and https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.15.E1. At z=1/4+ib, splitting the series of ψ into n≤ceil(|b|) and its complement proves |ψ(z)|≤C log(2+|b|): the short harmonic sum is logarithmic, the short sum of 1/(n+z) is bounded for |b|≥1, and the tail of the differences is ≤C(1+|b|)Σ_(n>|b|)(n+1)^(-2). The stretch |b|≤1 is compact without poles. Moreover |ψ'(z)|≤Σ_(n≥0)(n+1/4)^(-2), uniformly in b. Hence

    u_∞'/u_∞ = i[logπ−Re ψ(1/4+is/2)],
    |u_∞'/u_∞|≤Cℓ(s),    |(u_∞'/u_∞)'|≤C.

Summing the logarithmic derivatives of the factors and the phase exp(2ias) gives |v'|≤B_(S,t)ℓ and |v''|≤B_(S,t)ℓ². B_(S,t) is finite for fixed S,t; no uniformity is claimed when varying S,t.

With the CITED spectral properties, transport the tail N_n to the conjugated model and put κ_n=||N_n||→0. For every f with support in [λ^(-1),λ], H(s)=∫f(u)u^(is)du/u is the transform of a test of logarithmic support [−logλ,logλ]. The sign of the Fourier transform does not alter 212-87. One obtains

    Tr(θ(f)N_nθ(f)*) ≤ C_(S,t,λ) κ_n^(1/3) Λ_log(f),
    Λ_log(f)=(1/(2π))∫log(2+|s|)|H(s)|²ds.

The equivalence between ℓ and log(2+|s|), and the factor2π, only modify the constant. This is the estimate H2′ for fixed parameters, modulo the CITED geometric properties. It gives no uniform control as the primes increase, an explicit dimension without bound on κ_n, nor sign of the retained block. The complete link with the normalizations of a_T of Paper46 is not presupposed.

- Status of the extension 212-87: H2′ demonstrated by means of the abstract lemma under the semilocal identification and existence of the CITED spectral tail. Conjugation, derivatives and norm transfer independently reviewed. No independent audit of the external lemmas 8.5–8.6; no global positivity.

### 212-88 — Direct link of 212-87 with the form of Paper46

Status: PROVED with independently reviewed argument. It is an autonomous verification of the identity and of its domains, not a new source of sign nor a claim of novelty of the trace formula. Antecedents: 212-87 and its application, Paper46 eq:symbol/eq:form/eq:Aform, external identity cited in 212-86. Does not modify papers.

**Data.** F∈D_T, extended by zero outside (−T,T), H(s)=∫F(r)e^(isr)dr. S is a finite set of primes containing all primes≤exp(2T). For t>0, put

    v(s)=exp(2is log t) π^(is) Γ(1/4−is/2)/Γ(1/4+is/2)
          × Π_(p∈S) [(1−p^(−1/2)exp(−is log p))/(1−p^(−1/2)exp(is log p))],
    A_v=M_v* P M_v−P,
    P(s,z)=(1/2)δ(s−z)+(1/(2πi))pv(1/(s−z)).

All the following traces are in L²(R,ds). The factor2π is kept in the Plancherel formula. The positive sign of the chosen Fourier transform is compatible with the even symbol of Paper46. One has

    a_T(F)=2log t ||F||²+Tr(M_H A_v M_H*).                 (1)

The identity holds before imposing the moments. On P_T it also coincides with W_T because both moments are zero.

**Absolute trace control.** The bounds of 212-87 for s_j(M_η A_v) apply to both spectral parts: N_+=A_v E_+, N_−=−A_v E_−, with norm≤1. The sign does not affect the singular comparison, since M_η N_± M_η=±(M_η A_v)E_±M_η. By the same proof, Tr(M_H |A_v| M_H*)≤C_(T,S,t)∫ℓ(s)|H(s)|²ds. In particular M_H|A_v|^(1/2) is Hilbert–Schmidt and M_H A_v M_H* is trace class. Compactness of A_v nor of its negative part is used for this step.

**Diagonal of the kernel.** The kernel of A_v off the diagonal is [conjugate(v(s))v(z)−1]/[2πi(s−z)], with continuous extension to the diagonal and value −conjugate(v(s))v'(s)/(2πi). By explicit differentiation,

    conjugado(v(s))v'(s)
      =i[2log t−m(s)+2Σ_(p∈S,k≥1)(log p)p^(−k/2)cos(ks log p)],
    m(s)=Re ψ(1/4+is/2)−logπ.

The prime series here are absolutely convergent: S is finite and each tower is geometric. The derivatives of the gamma factor and the global bounds were verified in the extension of 212-87.

**Why the trace is the diagonal integral.** First take F smooth with compact support, then multiply H by a smooth compact cutoff χ_R in frequency. The resulting kernel is continuous, compact and zero near the edges of a larger interval. In the Fourier basis of that interval, the Fejér sums of its diagonal entries converge to the integral of the continuous diagonal. They also converge to the trace of the operator, since it is of trace class. To remove χ_R, 212-87 is not applied again to the truncated Fourier transform: the Hilbert–Schmidt factorization already established for M_H|A_v|^(1/2) is used. The cutoffs converge strongly and boundedly to the identity, so their compressions converge in trace norm. On the diagonal, domination by Cℓ(s)|H(s)|² is applied. One obtains

    Tr(M_H A_v M_H*)
      =(1/(2π))∫|H(s)|²[m(s)−2log t
        −2Σ_(p∈S,k≥1)(log p)p^(−k/2)cos(ks log p)]ds.     (2)

**Contacts and domain.** Plancherel turns each cosine into Re c_F(k log p). Since c_F is supported in [−2T,2T] and is continuous, the terms with k log p≥2T are zero, endpoints included. The remaining ones are exactly the contacts of Paper46; Σ_(p,k)2(log p)p^(−k/2)Re c_F(k log p)=Σ_(n∈N_T)2Λ(n)n^(−1/2)Re c_F(log n). Thus (2) is (1).

Finally, approximate F in the logarithmic form norm by compact smooth tests. The absolute trace control above makes both corresponding positive forms for A_v^± continuous, and hence so is their difference. The Paper46 side is continuous in that norm; the moment corrections can preserve P_T when needed. This extends (1) to all of D_T. For complex tests, Re c_F is kept at the contacts; no parity is needed.

**What remains.** The semilocal geometric description of the compact negative tail was CITED when this entry was obtained; the direct justification of 212-89 removes that dependence for the existence of a tail of norm tending to zero. H2′ of 212-87 thus controls an operator tail that appears exactly in a_T. Identity (1) does not eliminate the retained negative part nor give a Schur sign; no global sign follows from the tail tending to zero. The parameters S,t,T remain fixed in the estimate and no uniformity is claimed as the window grows.

### 212-89 — Direct justification of the negative compactness used in 212-87

Status: PROVED, with independent review of the argument. This is an audit and simplification of a dependency of 212-87–88, not a new sign construction nor a novelty claim for the compactness principle. Immediate antecedent: the external lemmas 8.5–8.6 cited in the application of 212-87. Difference: the necessary compactness is proved directly through the absolutely summable expansion of the finite Euler product; it is not required to exclude the negative intersection of the two projections. The link with the full form is the identity of 212-88 and the uniform estimate on tests of 212-87. The retained negative part remains without sign control.

**Physical model and normalizations.** Work in L²(R_+*,du/u). P_b multiplies by 1_(0,b], I g(u)=g(1/u), and Jg(x)=x^(−1/2)g(x) is unitary onto L²(R_+,dx). Let C be the unitary cosine transform with kernel 2cos(2πxy) and F_∞=J^(−1)CJ. For Mellin with positive exponent is, U_∞=I F_∞ has symbol

    u_∞(s)=π^(is) Γ(1/4−is/2)/Γ(1/4+is/2).

This identification is the classical Fourier–Mellin identity: integrating x^(z−1)cos(2πxy) gives Γ(z)cos(πz/2)(2πy)^(−z) for 0<Re z<1, first with regularization; the duplication and reflection identities give the quotient as written. No information about zeros of special functions is used.

**Local expansion in norm.** For r=p^(−1/2), z=exp(is log p),

    (1−rz^(−1))/(1−rz)
      =−rz^(−1)+(1−r²)Σ_(k≥0)r^k z^k,
    Σ |coefficients|=1+2r.

Therefore, for S finite, U_fin=Π_(p∈S)U_p has an expansion in operator norm

    U_fin=Σ_α c_α T_α,   Σ_α|c_α|<∞,
    T_α g(u)=g(exp(−α)u).

The multi-index of the product can be kept, without grouping coincident translations. Each T_α is unitary, its Mellin symbol is exp(isα), and T_α P_t=P_(t exp α)T_α.

**Compactness of the overlap.** Put U=U_∞U_fin and

    Γ=(1−P_(1/t))UP_t.

Since (1−P_(1/t))I=IP_t, the previous expansion gives

    Γ=Σ_α c_α I P_t F_∞ P_(t exp α)T_α.

Each summand without coefficient has norm≤1 and is Hilbert–Schmidt: under J, P_t F_∞ P_b has kernel 2cos(2πxy) on the rectangle (0,t]×(0,b], and HS norm≤2√(tb). For b=t exp α this bound is 2t exp(α/2), finite for each α. The summability of |c_α| proves convergence in operator norm of compact operators, hence Γ is compact. It is not claimed that the sum of the HS norms converges; that conclusion is not needed.

**From compact overlap to compact negative part.** Let P=P_t, Q=U*(1−P_(1/t))U, A=1−P−Q. Both P,Q are orthogonal projections and

    PQP=Γ*Γ,   (QP)*(QP)=PQP.

Thus QP is compact, by polar decomposition, and so is PQ. The algebraic computation gives A²−A=PQ+QP, compact. On the spectrum of A⊂[−1,1], define the bounded Borel function h(s)=(1−s)^(−1) if s<0, and h(s)=0 if s≥0. The functional calculus implies

    A_−=max(−A,0)=h(A)(A²−A).

Consequently A_− is compact. If Ran P∩Ran Q is nonzero, there A=−1; compactness implies that this intersection is finite-dimensional. It can be included entirely in the retained block. It is not necessary to prove that it is null.

**Exact consequence for 212-87.** Enumerating the positive eigenvalues of A_− with multiplicity and retaining the first n, the tail N_n satisfies κ_n=||N_n||→0. If there are only finitely many, take the tail zero once all are retained. The conjugation already verified to A_v transports this statement without altering norms or traces. Therefore the existence of the required tail in H2′ is established for the explicit symbol and fixed parameters, without using the external geometric lemmas. This update replaces the CITED character of that dependency in the extension of 212-87. It neither imports nor credits an external quantitative rate for κ_n.

**Limit of the result.** Compactness does not mean absence of negative eigenvalues. Neither this proof nor 212-87–88 shows that the retained block is dominated by the positive terms when the two moments of P_T are imposed. No global positivity, no uniformity as S,T grow, and no separation of falsifiers through compactness alone is obtained. Papers intact.

**Scope warning, independently reviewed.** A finite-rank spectral head does not necessarily induce a finite-rank form on the tests. Already for N_head=κ|e⟩⟨e| with κ>0 and ||e||_2=1,

    Tr(M_H N_head M_H*)=κ∫|H(s)|²|e(s)|²ds,
    Tr(M_H N_head M_H*)≤2Tκ||F||_2².

The second bound uses ||H||_∞≤√(2T)||F||_2 and proves that the expression is defined for all F∈L²([−T,T]), without additional logarithmic regularity. If F≠0, H is an entire function not identically zero; by the identity principle it cannot vanish on a real set of positive measure. Since |e|² is positive on a set of positive measure, the integral is strictly positive. The restriction to P_T∩D_T remains positive definite on an infinite-dimensional space; hence it has infinite rank. The two moments do not universally annihilate even an individual negative contribution. This observation prevents confusing the auxiliary spectral truncation with a finite reduction of the form; it does not exclude a compensation with the positive terms nor the independent finite reduction of Paper46. It is not presented as a new sign mechanism.

#### Quantitative corollary by reuse of R186_015

Status: PROVED, independent review. Exact antecedent: `03-research/phase-186-toolbox/R186_015_CHAIN_TWO_PRIMES.md`, §2, paragraph (Sp), already proves membership in all classes S_q with q>2 by interpolation between operator norm and HS norm, followed by a geometric sum over the monoid. It is not a new construction nor a new method. Here its consequence for the tail of 212-87 is made explicit in the normalizations of 212-89; the corpus results on comparison operators that do not belong to Schatten classes refer to other operators.

For each q>2, define the explicit constant

    C_q(S,t)=(2t)^(2/q) Π_(p∈S)
      [p^(−1/2−1/q)+(1−p^(−1))/(1−p^(−1/2+1/q))].

If B_α=I P_t F_∞ P_(t exp α)T_α, then

    ||B_α||_(S_q)^q ≤ ||B_α||^(q−2)||B_α||_HS²
                   ≤4t² exp α.

The expansion of 212-89 therefore converges in S_q, because

    Σ_α |c_α| exp(α/q)
      =Π_(p∈S)[p^(−1/2−1/q)
                  +(1−p^(−1))Σ_(k≥0)p^(k(−1/2+1/q))].

The exponent −1/2+1/q is strictly negative. The triangle inequality in S_q gives ||Γ||_(S_q)≤C_q. Since (QP)*(QP)=Γ*Γ, the nonzero singular values of QP and Γ coincide; hence ||QP||_(S_q)=||Γ||_(S_q). From A_−=h(A)(PQ+QP), ||h(A)||≤1 and the ideal property it follows that

    ||A_−||_(S_q)≤2C_q,
    κ_tail(n)≤min{1,2C_q(n+1)^(−1/q)}.

The second inequality is obtained by ordering the eigenvalues of A_− from largest to smallest and using (n+1)κ_tail(n)^q≤||A_−||_(S_q)^q; n counts the modes already retained, with multiplicity, including any negative intersection. In particular, n+1≥(2C_q/δ)^q suffices for κ_tail(n)≤δ.

Applying 212-87 yields, for fixed parameters S,t,T and every test in the form domain with support [−T,T],

    Tr(M_H N_tail(n) M_H*)
      ≤C_(T,B) (2C_q)^(1/3)(n+1)^(−1/(3q))
        ×∫ℓ(s)|H(s)|²ds.

The spectral constant C_q is written explicitly; C_(T,B) remains the constant of lemma 212-87, with no numerical evaluation here. The endpoint q=2, optimality of the rate, uniformity as S,t,T increase, and that the retained block induces a finite-rank form are not claimed. The bound only makes the disappearance of the tail quantitative; the domination of the full negative contribution remains OPEN.

#### Subsequent selection: scale variation and falsifier control

Independently reviewed selection, REJECTED as a new sign mechanism: letting t→0 to exploit ||A_−||≤2C_q(S,t)→0. Antecedents: identity 212-88; `03-research/phase-186-toolbox/R186_017_DICTIONARY_AND_C1_RESOLUTION.md`, D3/C1, where omitting the logarithmic term already produced an incorrect interpretation, and R186_018, which preserves the cancellation. The historical proof of R186_017 has the scale limitation indicated in its final note; here the identity of 212-88 itself is used.

Indeed, as t→0 the term 2log t ||F||² remains, negative and divergent for F≠0. The small norm of A_− does not control the difference between the positive contribution and that term. Nor can one pass from small norm to small trace by ignoring the dependence on t of C_(T,B). In the opposite direction, t→∞ and discarding the positive part only gives a_T(F)≥2log t ||F||²−Tr(M_H A_− M_H*), without a bound that compensates the second term. A new inequality for the complete balance is missing; the variation of the parameter alone does not provide it. Not every future construction using scales is excluded.

Scope control PROVED, reviewed: the hypotheses and auxiliary proofs of 212-87–89 remain valid for any finite set of real generators b>1, replacing p by b. The local quotients are unimodular, the expansion in translations and the product of C_q converge, and the logarithmic derivative gives contacts klog b with coefficients (log b)b^(−k/2). If there are coincidences of contacts the contributions are summed; neither unique factorization nor integrality was used. This includes the generators of the falsifier 𝔅 relevant to each window. Therefore this chain, without additional information, does not separate 𝔅. It is not a refutation of a future arithmetic compensation: it identifies that this compensation has not yet been constructed. There is no new lower bound for λ_A nor new sign result in this selection.

### 212-90 — Divisorial sampling defect with explicit gcd coefficients

Status: PROVED, with selection and proof independently reviewed. Antecedent: `03-research/phase-188-closing-D/N_BUILD_022_MATRIX_IDENTITY_FOR_X_M.md`, §3 and self-audit4; 212-expediente-near. The index of the remainder that remained ARGUED there is resolved. The difference is to keep all non-divisor factors and group them exactly; the defect is not identified with all of Near nor is a positive representation claimed. Connection with the objective: it specifies a remainder that the divisorial transport must compensate, without yet controlling its quadratic form nor the archimedean part.

**Normalization and carrier.** Fix M≥1, m,k∈{1,…,M}, R>0 and a profile c_0 supported in [−R,R]. Define oriented matrices

    K_mk=Σ_(n≥1) Λ(n)n^(−1/2)c_0(log(m/(kn))),
    L_mk=Σ_(n≥1) (log n)n^(−1/2)c_0(log(m/(kn))),
    (Z^(−1))_mj=1_(j|m) μ(m/j)(m/j)^(−1/2),
    D=K−Z^(−1)L.

These are the normalizations of the oriented convolution declared here. K is not simply identified with the full matrix of Paper46: factors of 2, symmetrizations or archimedean terms are neither omitted nor presupposed. All the sums contributing to an entry are finite, with n≤exp(R)m/k; in particular the cutoff n≤M is not imposed.

**Exact identity.** For g=gcd(m,n), put

    d_m(n)=Λ(n)−1_(g=1)log n−Λ(g),

with Λ(1)=0. Then

    D_mk=Σ_(n≥1) d_m(n)n^(−1/2)c_0(log(m/(kn))).       (1)

Indeed, writing a=m/j and then n=ab,

    (Z^(−1)L)_mk
      =Σ_(a|m,b≥1) μ(a)(log b)(ab)^(−1/2)
          c_0(log(m/(kab)))
      =Σ_(n≥1)n^(−1/2)c_0(log(m/(kn)))
          Σ_(a|gcd(m,n))μ(a)log(n/a).

For g=1 the inner sum is log n. For g>1, use Σ_(a|g)μ(a)=0 and Σ_(a|g)μ(a)log a=−Λ(g); the inner sum is Λ(g). This proves (1) by finite groupings.

**Sign of the coefficients, not of the matrix.** For all m,n≥1 one has d_m(n)≤0. If g=1, it reduces to Λ(n)≤log n. If g>1 and n=p^r, then g=p^s with s≥1, so that Λ(n)=Λ(g) and d_m(n)=0. If g>1 and n is not a prime power, Λ(n)=0 and d_m(n)=−Λ(g)≤0. The case n=1 gives zero. In particular:

- d_m(n)=0 whenever n divides m;
- d_m(p)=0 for every prime p and every m;
- d_m(4)=−log2 for m odd, and zero for m even.

The alternating Möbius sum of the defect thus has an arithmetic evaluation without alternations, although the values of the profile still keep their signs.

**Why the sign of the form is not deduced.** If c_0(u)=∫F(x)F(x+u)dx for a real, compact, primitive, nonzero test, then

    ∫exp(u/2)c_0(u)du
      =(∫exp(−x/2)F(x)dx)(∫exp(y/2)F(y)dy)=0.

But c_0 is continuous and c_0(0)=||F||²>0. Therefore it also takes negative values. The sign of d_m(n) does not determine the sign of the entries of (1) for these profiles; moreover D is not, by definition, self-adjoint, and not even negative entries of a symmetric matrix would suffice for negative semidefiniteness. No matrix comparison is obtained by replacing D with its Hermitian part.

**Falsifiers and limit.** Keeping the arithmetic Z and L fixed and replacing Λ by a weight w on the integers, the same computation gives d_m^w(n)=w(n)−1_(g=1)log n−Λ(g). For w=cΛ with c>1, already at n prime one gets d_m^w(n)=(c−1)log n>0, independently of m; the coefficient sign proved for Λ is not preserved. This is not a proof of separation of the full form: no PSD step has been constructed nor has a positive identity been contrasted with the whole battery. For non-integer generators the divisorial sampling as written is not transferred without justification. The joint compensation of the defect, the arithmetic remainder and the archimedean term remains OPEN. Papers intact.

#### Exact diagnosis: indefinite Hermitian part with a primitive profile

Status: PROVED, selection and proof independently reviewed. Immediate antecedent: the scope warning of 212-90. The sign of the defect D defined here is decided, without identifying it with all of Near nor repeating as proof the diagnosis of another operator.

Put a=log(8/7) and choose

    0<ε<min{a/3,log(7/6)−a}.

This interval is nonempty, since 8/7<7/6. Take φ∈C_c∞(0,ε) real nonzero, g=(1/4−∂²)φ and F(x)=g(x)+g(x−a). The function g is not zero: a compactly supported solution of g=0 would force φ to be a combination of exp(±x/2) and hence zero. Integration by parts proves ∫g(x)exp(±x/2)dx=0; translations preserve the vanishing of both moments, so F is primitive.

For c_0(u)=∫F(x)F(x+u)dx and R=a+ε, the support of c_0 is contained in [−R,R]. The separation of the two supports gives

    c_0(a)=c_0(−a)=||g||²>0.

Evaluate (1) at m=7,k=2. The integers that can contribute satisfy

    (7/2)exp(−R)≤n≤(7/2)exp(R).

Since a<R<log(7/6), the lower endpoint is greater than3 and the upper one less than49/12<5; n=4 belongs to the interval because R>a. It is the only admitted integer. Thus,

    D_72=−(log2)/2 ·||g||².

In the opposite direction, |log(2/(7n))|≥log(7/2)>R for all n≥1, hence D_27=0. On the diagonal entries R<log2 only allows n=1, whose coefficient is zero. Therefore D_22=D_77=0.

For any M≥7, the compression of (D+D*)/2 to the ordered coordinates (2,7) is

    [[0, −(log2)||g||²/4],
     [−(log2)||g||²/4, 0]],

with eigenvalues ±(log2)||g||²/4. Consequently the Hermitian part of D is indefinite for this primitive profile. The nonpositive arithmetic coefficients of 212-90 cannot be turned, without another operation, into a matrix contribution of fixed sign.

Scope: the profile satisfies exactly the two moments, but this residual matrix is not the full form of Paper46. No negative test for that form is obtained, nor a NO-GO for the joint compensation. The next obligation remains to control D together with Z^(−1)L and the archimedean term, preserving the cross terms.


#### Control by deletion of the comb

Scope check, independently reviewed; not a new archimedean theorem nor a new construction. Keep the matrices L and Z^(−1) of 212-90 fixed. For any weight 0≤w≤Λ,

    d_m^w(n)=d_m(n)+w(n)−Λ(n)≤0.

The coefficient sign survives every deletion, including w=0. The observed breakdown for 1.1Λ is not enough to turn that inequality into a global sign mechanism.

To check the failure of sufficiency while preserving the moments exactly, take φ∈C_c∞(−1,1) real nonzero, G_b(t)=φ(t/b) and F_b=(1/4−∂²)G_b, b≥1. Integration by parts gives ∫F_b(t)exp(±t/2)dt=0. Its transform is H_b(s)=(1/4+s²)b φ̂(bs). With the archimedean symbol m(s) of Paper46, Plancherel and ξ=bs give

    a_arch(F_b)/||F_b||²
      = [∫m(ξ/b)(1/4+ξ²/b²)²|φ̂(ξ)|²dξ]
        /[∫(1/4+ξ²/b²)²|φ̂(ξ)|²dξ]
      →m(0)<0.

The convergence is dominated: |m(s)|≤C log(2+|s|), while φ̂ is Schwartz; the limit denominator is (1/16)∫|φ̂|²>0. The digamma series already used in 212-87 implies ψ(1/4)<ψ(1)=−γ, hence m(0)=ψ(1/4)−logπ<0. Consequently, for b sufficiently large the deleted comb has negative form on a primitive test, although all its coefficients d_m^0(n) are nonpositive.

Result: the isolated arithmetic sign of 212-90 does not distinguish the true weight from all the controls. The exact identity is not altered nor is a compensation refuted that uses additional information from the true weight and from the remaining terms.


Final precision of the diagnosis, PROVED and independently reviewed: for real weights w(n), n≥2,

    [d_m^w(n)≤0 for all m≥1,n≥2]
       ⇔ [w(n)≤Λ(n) for all n≥2].

Necessity is obtained by taking m=n: d_n^w(n)=w(n)−Λ(n). Sufficiency uses d_m^w=d_m+w−Λ and d_m≤0. It does not require w≥0. For the block 1≤m,n≤M, with n≥2, the equivalence controls only 2≤n≤M, not the frequencies n>M that can contribute to an entry. The equalities d_n^w(n)=0 identify Λ, but do not prove positivity. Therefore the isolated coefficient inequality expresses exactly an upper bound on the weight: it provides no additional mechanism for the sign. The residual identity is kept as a tool; this inequality alone is not a candidate for the global proof.


### 212-91 — Coercive complement via the trace of the negative head

Status: PROVED as a corollary of 212-87–89, with selection and proof independently reviewed. Antecedents: rank warning of 212-89; finite reduction of Paper46; theorem8.14 of https://arxiv.org/html/2611.13129v1#S8.SS5. It is not presented as a new reduction of global positivity. The technical difference is to use directly the trace operator induced by the negative head, without a two-scale decomposition of pairs nor exclusion of the intersection of projections. A consequence of the already proved tail control is discharged; the sign on the full carrier remains OPEN.

**Statement.** For each T>0 and finite set S containing the primes of the window, there exists a finite-dimensional subspace E of P_T in L²(−T,T) such that

    a_T(F)≥(1/2)||F||²
    for all F∈D_T∩P_T∩E^⊥.

E is defined spectrally from a negative head of the auxiliary operator of 212-88; no certified algorithm for computing it is claimed, nor a uniform dimension as T,S vary.

**Comparison of norms.** With H(s)=∫F(x)exp(isx)dx, define

    L_log(F)=(1/(2π))∫log(2+|s|)|H(s)|²ds,
    C_arch=max{0,sup_s[log(2+|s|)−m(s)]},
    C_T=1+C_arch+2Σ_(2≤n<exp(2T))Λ(n)/√n.

C_arch is finite by the continuity and the logarithmic asymptote of the archimedean symbol of Paper46. The bound |c_F(log n)|≤||F||² and the formula for a_T prove

    L_log(F)≤a_T(F)+C_T||F||².                         (1)

Positivity of a_T is not presupposed in this comparison.

**Choice of the tail.** Fix t=exp(1) in 212-88 and write the negative part of A_v as N_head+N_tail, retaining n orthonormal eigenvectors e_j∈L²(ds) with eigenvalues κ_j>0. All the negative intersection directions are included if they exist. By 212-87 and 212-89 one can choose n finite so that

    q_tail(F)=Tr(M_H N_tail M_H*)≤ε L_log(F),
    ε=min{1,1/(2C_T)}.

The equivalence between the weight ℓ of 212-87 and log(2+|s|), and the factor2π, are absorbed in the choice of n. If the negative part is finite it suffices to retain it entirely; if it is null, n=0.

**The head induces a trace-class operator.** Put ρ(s)=Σ_(j≤n)κ_j|e_j(s)|² and define B:L²(−T,T)→L²(R,ds) by

    (BF)(s)=√ρ(s)∫_(−T)^T F(x)exp(isx)dx.

Its kernel is Hilbert–Schmidt, since

    ||B||_HS²=2T∫ρ(s)ds=2TΣ_(j≤n)κ_j.

Thus K=B*B is positive of trace class and q_head(F)=⟨KF,F⟩. This trace is not divided by2π: the e_j are normalized in L²(ds) and the declared transform H is used. Let K_prim be the compression of K to P_T. Its trace does not exceed that of K. Define E as the sum of its eigenspaces with eigenvalue greater than1/2. Then

    dim E≤4TΣ_(j≤n)κ_j,
    q_head(F)≤(1/2)||F||² for F∈P_T∩E^⊥.

This does not contradict the infinite rank of the head form: its spectrum above a threshold is retained, not its whole image.

**Absorption.** The identity212-88, the positivity of the contribution of A_v^+ and t=exp(1) give, for F∈D_T∩P_T∩E^⊥,

    a_T(F)≥2||F||²−q_head(F)−q_tail(F)
          ≥(3/2)||F||²−ε L_log(F).

By (1),

    (1+ε)a_T(F)≥(3/2−ε C_T)||F||²≥||F||².

Since ε≤1, the bound1/2 of the statement follows. All steps hold on the form domain by the trace controls of 212-87–88.

**Domain and limit.** E is defined in L²; it has not been assumed that its eigenvectors belong to D_T. No new Schur complement on those vectors is derived here. Coercivity of finite codimension likewise does not determine the sign of the removed part nor of its couplings, and does not by itself distinguish the falsifiers. A coercive complement has been constructed within this chain, not a positive identity on all of P_T. Papers intact.


#### Smooth substitution of the removed space: domain resolved

Status: PROVED, with independent review. It is an applicability check of 212-91, not a new positivity reduction. Antecedents: density with moment repair of 212-75; Schur of Paper46 and BUILD_083. The difference is that the approximation is controlled through the bounded operator K_prim, without assuming continuity of a_T for the L² norm.

Let r=dim E, e_1,…,e_r an orthonormal basis of E and L=||K_prim||. If r=0 take V={0}. Otherwise choose η∈(0,1) with Lη²≤1/4 and functions v_j∈C_c∞(−T,T)∩P_T such that

    Σ_(j=1)^r ||e_j−v_j||²≤η².

These approximations exist: first approximate each e_j by compact smooth functions in L², and then repair the two moments with two fixed bumps of invertible moment matrix. They can be chosen as translations, around two distinct centers, of one and the same small nonnegative bump; the moment rows have factors exp(±x/2), so that their determinant is not zero. The moments are continuous functionals on the L² of the window, so the repair tends to zero in L².

Put V=span{v_j}. The error bound implies

    ||Σ_j c_j v_j||≥(1−η)||c||_2,

hence dim V=r. If F⊥V, then

    ||P_EF||²=Σ_j|⟨F,e_j−v_j⟩|²≤η²||F||².

E is a spectral subspace of K_prim, so there are no cross terms between E and E^⊥ in q_head. For F∈P_T∩V^⊥,

    q_head(F)≤L||P_EF||²+(1/2)||(1−P_E)F||²
             ≤(1/2+Lη²)||F||²≤(3/4)||F||².

With the same tail and the same constant C_T of 212-91,

    a_T(F)≥(5/4)||F||²−ε L_log(F),
    (1+ε)a_T(F)≥(5/4−ε C_T)||F||²≥(3/4)||F||².

Thus, for all F∈D_T∩P_T∩V^⊥,

    a_T(F)≥(3/8)||F||²,
    dim V=dim E≤4TΣ_(j≤n)κ_j.

The generators of V belong to the operator domain: their extension by zero is smooth compact, their transform is Schwartz and the archimedean multiplier grows only logarithmically; the contacts of the window are a finite sum of bounded translations. The subsequent primitive projection is bounded. Therefore the domain question pointed out at the end of 212-91 is resolved by means of V, without claiming additional regularity for the original eigenvectors of E.

This allows applying the already existing Schur reduction to V and its complement, but it does not supply the sign of the Schur complement nor of its couplings. Nor does it numerically certify the chosen generators. It is not presented as a new positive window nor as a global proof.


### 212-92 — Correction of the quantitative bounds of the Schur complement of Paper46

Status: audit PROVED, independently reviewed. Source: `04-papers/46-row-d-sign-radial-intersection-form/main.tex`, theorem `thm:coer-schur`, equation `eq:coer-sandwich` and its proof. The paper is not modified. The exact identity of completion of squares and the sign equivalences are kept; the quantitative sandwich as written must not be used without the following correction. This audit does not prove global positivity nor does it by itself invalidate independent certificates.

**Localized problem.** In the orthogonal decomposition F=v+e, with v in the coercive complement and e in the finite space, the proved identity is

    a(v+e)=a(v+Ke)+s(e),   a(w)≥c||w||² in the complement,
    c>0,   λ_S=min_(||e||=1)s(e).

The paper writes min(c,λ_S)/(1+||K||)²≤λ_A≤min(c,λ_S). There are two errors in the inferences used:

- Taking e=0 compares λ_A with the actual infimum of the coercive block, not with a lower bound c for that infimum.
- Taking v=−Ke gives the quotient s(e)/(||e||²+||Ke||²). If s(e)<0, increasing the denominator increases the quotient; λ_A≤λ_S is not deduced. Neither is the negative lower bound as written deduced from that upper bound.

**Counterexamples to the abstract sandwich.** For a(v+e)=(v+e)²−e² on orthogonal R², c=1, K=1 and λ_S=−1. The matrix is [[1,1],[1,0]], with λ_A=(1−√5)/2. It contradicts both λ_A≤−1 and λ_A≥−1/4. For a(v+e)=v²+10e², K=0 and the valid lower bound c=1/2, one has λ_A=1>c. The examples refute the general inferences of the proof; they are not negative tests of the form of Paper46.

**Correct bounds.** For the nonzero finite space, put k=||K|| and d_*=inf_(w≠0)a(w)/||w||² over the complement. Always λ_A≤d_* and, for any e≠0,

    λ_A≤s(e)/(||e||²+||Ke||²).                        (1)

If λ_S≥0,

    min(c,λ_S)/(1+k)²≤λ_A≤λ_S.                        (2)

The lower bound follows from a(v+e)≥c||v+Ke||²+λ_S||e||² and

    ||v||²+||e||²≤(1+k)²(||v+Ke||²+||e||²).

The upper bound uses (1) with a minimal eigenvector of s. It can be combined with λ_A≤d_*; d_* is not replaced by c.

If λ_S<0,

    λ_S≤λ_A≤λ_S/(1+k²)<0.                            (3)

For the first inequality it suffices that a(v+e)≥λ_S||e||²≥λ_S(||v||²+||e||²). For the second take in (1) a unit minimal eigenvector e_0; since ||Ke_0||≤k and λ_S<0,

    λ_A≤λ_S/(1+||Ke_0||²)≤λ_S/(1+k²).

These bounds correctly separate the two signs.

**Preserved equivalences.** The identity, without using the incorrect sandwich, proves a≥0 if and only if s≥0: one direction is obtained by putting v=−Ke and the other by using the positivity of the coercive block. In finite dimension, s positive definite gives λ_A>0 by (2); if λ_S=0, (1) and nonnegativity give λ_A=0; if λ_S<0, (3) gives λ_A<0. Hence the equivalences of (iii), used as a reduction of the objective, remain valid.

**Scope for 212-91.** The coercivity 1/2, its smooth version3/8 and their absorption proofs do not use `eq:coer-sandwich`; they do not change. Nor has the sign of the pending Schur complement been obtained. The quantitative fix is recorded for a future revision of the paper authorized by the rules of the repository; the paper remains intact.


#### Examined dependencies of the correction 212-92

Independently reviewed audit, limited to the following passages; not a complete recertification of the paper nor an exhaustive search of all its consequences.

- In `rem:coer-honest`, the comparison λ_A≤λ_S≤(1+||K||)²λ_A requires **0≤λ_S≤c**, not only λ_S≤c. The upper condition already appears there; the lower one needs to be made explicit.
- In the open problem (L2), the comparisons with λ_S likewise do not hold without separating signs. The final positive ceiling for λ_S survives trivially when λ_S<0 and, when 0≤λ_S<c, through (2) of 212-92 together with the positive ceiling for λ_A. It is not justified by that argument without the condition λ_S<c in the positive case. No uniform bound for ||K|| is introduced.
- `rem:inertiatower` uses the identity of completion of squares and the compactness of the resolvent, not the questioned sandwich.
- The examined proofs of `thm:log5A` and `thm:log5W` refer to `prop:lowercert`. The latter uses the coercive high block, the inertia congruence and a Gram majorant for the Schur term; it does not use `eq:coer-sandwich`.
- BUILD_083, (84)–(85), derives the positive bound in the physical norm by an explicit norm inequality, without the invalid inference. (136)–(137), strict monotonicity and its consequence under global nonnegativity, uses compactness and translations, without that sandwich.

No dependence on the erroneous formula was found in those examined proofs. This check does not re-run certificates nor vouch for parts of the corpus that were not inspected. The correction does not supply the sign of the pending global Schur complement. Papers intact.


### Selection after 212-92 — Dilation versus average of rational translations

REJECTED at selection, independently reviewed; without construction nor computations. Antecedents: 212-42 (affine semigroup and projections by cells), 212-43 (obligation to match the contacts of the square). Proposed object, with extension by zero in R_+:

    D_n f(x)=√n f(nx),   T_h f(x)=f(x+h),
    V_n f=D_n f−n^(−1)Σ_(r=0)^(n−1)T_(r/n)f,
    Q(f)=Σ_n b_n||V_n f||²,   b_n≥0.

The formal difference with respect to a conditional expectation by cells is the average of translations inside the same square. No identity with the objective form nor with its archimedean compensator was written. The cross terms between dilation and translation with r>0 produce affine contacts with nonzero intercept; the cross terms between translations have slope one and do not provide an explicit cancellation of those contacts. The contacts of the objective pass through the origin, while the archimedean kernel is smooth off the diagonal. The moment restrictions do not automatically eliminate these singularities.

The candidate does not pass the filter for lack of an explicit compensator of those cross terms and of a signed remainder, not because of a general impossibility of using affine operators. No new barrier is derived nor is the objective form altered to accommodate the square. Reopening: write the complete cancellation and its sign, preserving the two moments and the normalization of the form.


Repair by phases of the affine candidate, elementary identity independently reviewed. For a finite sum of indices and

    V_(n,θ)f=D_n f−(1/n)Σ_(r=0)^(n−1)exp(irθ)T_(r/n)f,

the orthogonality of the phases gives exactly

    ∫_0^(2π)||V_(n,θ)f||²dθ/(2π)
      =||f||²−(2/n)Re⟨D_n f,f⟩
        +(1/n²)Σ_(r=0)^(n−1)||T_(r/n)f||².

D_n is unitary on L²(R_+,dx), while ||T_hf||²=∫_h^∞|f(x)|²dx. Therefore the diagonal potential is d_n(x)=1+n^(−2)Σ_r1_[r/n,∞)(x)≥0. The operation does cancel the additional affine contacts. To match the original contacts in the normalization f(x)=x^(−1/2)F(log x), one needs b_n=√nΛ(n)≥0 for the n of the window. Then the sum of squares reproduces the comb together with a potential d=Σ_nb_nd_n≥0, and the identity with the full form leaves as remainder a_arch(F)−∫d(x)|f(x)|²dx. That remainder is negative on the negative archimedean primitive tests constructed in the deletion control of 212-90, for sufficiently large windows.

Result: the algebraic repair works, but this candidate returns to the diagonal obstacle of 212-43; it does not provide a global nonnegative remainder. It is not necessary to discard every affine construction nor other averages in order to reject this concrete formula. There is no new bound for λ_A.


### Cross-check of the link between 212-90 and 212-91

Independent review: there is no established identity that directly converts the divisorial defect of 212-90 into the head operator or into its Schur complement. An explicit obstacle to the identification is checked by means of the same translated profile; additional transports with compensators are not excluded.

Fix a window containing all the translations considered and a single head operator of 212-91. For F_m(t)=F_0(t−log m), with F_0 primitive, the translations are primitive and

    q_head(Σ_m c_m F_m)
      =∫ρ_head(s)|H_0(s)|²|Σ_m c_m exp(is log m)|²ds.

The entries of this Gram matrix depend only on the quotient of indices. The primitive compression does not change these pairings. In contrast, for the explicit profile of the diagnosis of 212-90,

    D_(7,2)=−(log2)||g||²/2,   D_(14,4)=0,
    7/2=14/4.

In both entries the support admits only n=4; the change comes from gcd(7,4)=1 versus gcd(14,4)=2. Thus, D is not that stationary compression. Its one-sided character and the indefiniteness of its Hermitian part are other differences that do not disappear by sharing the same arithmetic weights.

The trace identity212-88 represents the full form, but does not separately identify all these components. For another link one needs to write the transport and the identity of pairings preserving norm, moments and complementary terms. The cross-check produces neither a candidate nor a new sign bound.


### 212-93 — Exact elimination of the sampling defect by divisible enlargement

Status: PROVED as an algebraic corollary of 212-90, with independent review. Antecedents: N_BUILD_022 §3 and its sampling defect; exact formula of 212-90; «Factorial extension before resonance» of `03-research/phase-211-sign-sandbox/POWER_GLOBAL_ROUTE_REVIEW.md`. Introducing divisibility by means of a common multiple is not a new tool; the difference with respect to that earlier extension is the concrete defect that is eliminated, not a global sign mechanism.

**Data and operation.** Fix M≥1 and a profile c_0 supported in [−R,R], R>0. Use K_M,L_M,Z_M^(−1),D_M of 212-90, with the same complete sums in the frequency n. Choose

    N=ceil(exp(R)M),   q=lcm(1,2,…,N),
    J:R^M→R^(qM),   J e_m=e_(qm).

Then

    J* K_(qM) J=K_M,
    J* D_(qM) J=0,
    K_M=J* Z_(qM)^(−1) L_(qM) J.                    (1)

**Proof.** The entries of K depend on m/k: replacing (m,k) by (qm,qk) leaves log(m/(kn)) unchanged, which proves the first equality. In an entry with those indices, the support only allows n≤exp(R)m/k≤exp(R)M≤N. By construction n divides q and therefore qm. The formula of 212-90 gives d_(qm)(n)=0 for all those frequencies; this proves the second equality. Compressing K_(qM)=Z_(qM)^(−1)L_(qM)+D_(qM) proves the third. All the sums involved are finite.

**Why the defect changes.** The intermediate indices j of the product Z_(qM)^(−1)L_(qM) include divisors of qm that are not multiples of q. They must be kept. It is not claimed that

    J*Z_(qM)^(−1)L_(qM)J
      =(J*Z_(qM)^(−1)J)(J*L_(qM)J),

since that separate compression would again lose the intermediate indices. Nor has a factorization been found in the original carrier of size M. The size qM can be enormous and it is not proposed to compute it by brute force.

**Arithmetic scope and limit.** Keeping the logarithmic Z and L fixed and replacing Λ by w on the integers, the compressed defect has coefficients w(n)−Λ(n) at the visible frequencies; therefore its vanishing is not a generic property of any comb. For non-integer generators this simultaneous divisibility is not available in the declared carrier. This only controls the exactness of the representation, not the sign of its remainder nor the complete battery of falsifiers.

The conclusion is that this sampling defect can be eliminated by enlarging the carrier; it is not a universal impossibility of relating the contacts by means of divisors. The product Z_(qM)^(−1)L_(qM) is not a positive Gram matrix, nor is it signed by (1). The compensation with the archimedean term remains unconstructed. D is not identified with all of Near, global positivity is not proved and no papers are modified.


#### Transfer of 212-93 to the full form and to the physical Gram matrix

Identity and normalizations independently reviewed. Let F_0 be real, smooth, compact and primitive, c_0 its autocorrelation and F_m(t)=F_0(t−log m). Define G_mk=⟨F_k,F_m⟩ and (B_arch)_mk=a_arch(F_k,F_m). For the oriented contacts K of 212-90, the matrix of the full form on this family is

    A_M=B_arch−(K_M+K_M^T).

The two orientations reproduce exactly the factor2Λ(n)/√n. With the data of212-93,

    A_M=B_arch−(C+C*),   C=J*Z_(qM)^(−1)L_(qM)J.

The enlarged family satisfies F_(qm)(t)=F_m(t−log q). This common translation preserves G, B_arch and the full form. It multiplies the two moments by q^(±1/2), preserving their vanishing; after recentering, the width of the window is the same. J is a Euclidean isometry between coordinate spaces, but the physical norm of Σc_mF_m is c*Gc, not necessarily c*c.

The elimination of the defect is thus also verified as a rewriting of the full form on this family. There is still no inequality comparing B_arch with C+C*. Möbius inversion and the logarithmic weights, without an additional operation, do not prove that comparison. No new sign construction is selected from the factorization alone; future explicit compensations are not excluded.


### 212-94 — Correction of the algebra of cell projections of 212-42

Status: REFUTATION of the indicated claims for the declared carrier, with independent review. No paper is modified. The distinction is maintained between averages over cells and other families, such as projections onto periodic frequencies, which might satisfy another algebra.

For q a positive integer, let E_q be the orthogonal projection in L²(R_+,dx) onto functions constant on each cell [j/q,(j+1)/q), j≥0; it is the average over that cell. These are the conditional expectations declared in 212-42.

**The gcd law is false.** With u=1_[0,1/3),

    E_2E_3u=(2/3)1_[0,1/2),
    E_1u=(1/3)1_[0,1).

Therefore E_2E_3≠E_1. The law E_mE_n=E_gcd(m,n) does not hold for these projections when the lattices are not nested. If m divides n, E_mE_n=E_nE_m=E_m is preserved by inclusion of the subspaces.

**The Möbius sum is not positive.** Define P_6=E_6−E_3−E_2+E_1 and h=1_[0,1/2)−1_[1/2,1). One has E_6h=E_2h=h, E_1h=0 and E_3h takes the values1,0,−1 on the three thirds. Thus,

    ⟨h,P_6h⟩=−||E_3h||²=−2/3.

In particular P_6 is not a positive orthogonal projection.

**Counterexample preserving the two physical moments.** Let h_1(x)=h(x−1), h_2(x)=h(x−2), extended by zero, and

    a=log(9/8),   b=log(25/24),   f=b h_1−a h_2.

Each h_i has integral zero, while ∫h_1(x)dx/x=a and ∫h_2(x)dx/x=b. Hence ∫f(x)dx=∫f(x)dx/x=0. The operators E_1,E_2,E_3,E_6 separately preserve the unit cells [1,2) and [2,3), and therefore

    ⟨f,P_6f⟩=−(2/3)(a²+b²)<0.

With F(t)=exp(t/2)f(exp t), these are exactly the two moments of P_T. For T>log3, F has compact support interior to (−T,T) and belongs to the form domain: it is of bounded variation, so that its transform decays as O((1+|s|)^(−1)), sufficient for the logarithmic energy. The negativity here concerns P_6, not a_T.

**What is withdrawn and what remains.** For this carrier, the following are withdrawn: the gcd law, the positivity/orthogonality of P_n, the identification of ||P_nf||² with Σ_(d|n)μ(n/d)||E_df||², and the conclusion of positivity of combinations with nonnegative weights based on them. The correct equality for that sum is with ⟨f,P_nf⟩, with no predetermined sign. The identity Σ_(d|N)P_d=E_N remains a purely algebraic Möbius inversion.

Object2 of 212-42 keeps its argument: if E=E_1 and the means of f over all unit cells are zero, integrating D_n f over [j,j+1) sums the zero means of the n whole cells that make up [nj,n(j+1)). Hence ED_n(I−E)=0 for n integer. The present correction does not automatically invalidate that invariance, the cell reduction of 212-75 nor the later certificates; it does not constitute an exhaustive audit of all their dependencies.

#### Precision on 212-93: universal divisibility criterion without powers

Status: PROVED as an algebraic corollary of 212-90, independently checked. Same identity and same sign problem; no new candidate. For an integer N≥4, define q_N=Π_(p≤N/2)p. For a positive integer q one has

    d_(qm)(n)=0 for all m≥1 and 2≤n≤N
        if and only if q_N divides q.

Sufficiency: every prime divisor of a composite n≤N is ≤N/2. If n=p^r, r≥2, the gcd(qm,n) contains p, and Λ(gcd)=Λ(n). If n has at least two distinct primes, the gcd also contains them and both values of Λ are zero. In both cases 212-90 gives d=0; for n prime d=0 with no restriction. Necessity: take m=1. The case n=4 forces 2|q. For each odd prime p≤N/2, n=2p forces p|q: otherwise the gcd would be 2 and d_q(2p)=−log2. This proves the criterion. For N≤3 q=1 suffices.

In 212-93, with N=ceil(exp(R)M), lcm(1,…,N) can therefore be replaced by q_N (or 1 when N≤3). All the visible coefficients vanish and what remains is

    K_M=J*Z_(q_N M)^(-1)L_(q_N M)J,
    𝔸_M=B_arch,M−(C_M+C_M*).

The proof no longer asserts that each visible n divides q_N m; it uses the gcd criterion directly. The intermediate indices of the product are kept. q_N is minimal by divisibility for the UNIVERSAL vanishing of coefficients as stated, not necessarily for a particular profile or compression. No sign, positivity of the factors or complexity estimate is deduced. The comparison with B_arch remains OPEN.

#### Explicit image of 212-57/58 via Ramanujan and grouped Poisson

Status: PROVED in the declared smooth kernel, independently checked. It is an explicit form of the existing operator, not a sign candidate nor a claim of conceptual novelty. Antecedents: 212-57/58 (Blaschke product and logarithmic index identity), INV_H_001 §2 A1–A2 (Ramanujan on the linear comb), R161_001 (Müntz–Poisson) and CORRECTION_RESIDUE_BALANCE_031 (do not omit weighted pairings by block cancellation). The directed query did not locate this exact combined formula; exclusions of the other carriers are not automatically transferred.

**Data.** F real in C_c^∞(−T,T) with both moments zero. Put g_0(x)=|x|^(−1/2)F(log|x|), extended by 0 at 0, and h=ĝ_0 with Fourier exp(−2πiκx). Then g_0 is even, smooth, compactly supported and zero near 0; h is Schwartz and h(0)=∫g_0=2∫F(t)exp(t/2)dt=0. The other moment is ∫_(0,∞)g_0(x)dx/x=0 and is kept as an additional constraint, without attributing to it an undemonstrated cancellation.

Let S be a finite set of primes, q=Π_(p∈S)p and U_pF(t)=F(t−log p). Define

    B_S=Π_(p∈S)(U_p−p^(−1/2)I)(I−p^(−1/2)U_p)^(-1)
       =Σ_(n S-smooth)b_n U_n,
    g_S(x)=|x|^(−1/2)(B_SF)(log|x|).

Here n S-smooth means that all its prime factors lie in S; U_n is the translation by log n. The product is that of 212-57/58 with this explicit convention. Define c_q(n)=Σ_(a mod q,(a,q)=1)exp(2πian/q), with c_1(n)=1.

**Exact coefficients.** For a prime, b_1=−p^(−1/2) and b_(p^k)=(1−p^(-1))p^(−(k−1)/2), k≥1. Thus sqrt(n)b_n=c_q(n)/sqrt(q) for n S-smooth, by the multiplicative formula c_p(n)=p−1 if p|n and −1 otherwise. Outside those n, b_n=0. Consequently,

    ĝ_S(κ)=q^(−1/2)Σ_(n S-smooth)c_q(n)h(nκ),   κ≠0.       (I)

For each factor Σ|b_(p^k)|=1+2/sqrt(p); the finite product gives Σ|b_n|<∞. The expansion converges in operators on L², since n^(−1/2)g_0(x/n) is a unitary dilation. Its Fourier transform is sqrt(n)h(nκ). At κ≠0, (I) converges absolutely and locally uniformly away from 0 by |c_q(n)|≤φ(q) and the Schwartz decay, identifying a representative of the L² transform.

**Poisson with justified grouping.** The identity

    1_(n S-smooth)=Σ_(d|n,(d,q)=1)μ(d)

allows us to write the sum of (I) as Σ_(d,q)=1 μ(d)Σ_(k≥1)c_q(k)h(dkκ), since c_q(dk)=c_q(k) if (d,q)=1. For κ≠0 the double sum is absolutely convergent: it is dominated by φ(q)Σ_(n≥1)τ(n)|h(nκ)|, where τ(n) counts divisors. For y>0, twisted Poisson, parity and h(0)=0 give

    2Σ_(k≥1)c_q(k)h(ky)
      =y^(-1)Σ_(a mod q,(a,q)=1)Σ_(m∈Z)g_0((m+a/q)/y).

Therefore, for κ>0,

    ĝ_S(κ)=1/(2sqrt(q)κ) Σ_(d,q)=1 [μ(d)/d]
                 Σ_(a mod q,(a,q)=1)Σ_(m∈Z)
                    g_0((m+a/q)/(dκ)).                  (II)

Each inner sum in m is finite. The outer sum in d converges absolutely AFTER grouping the inner samples, by its equality with the previous Fourier series. Absolute convergence of all the individual physical samples is not claimed, nor is it allowed to omit their cancellations. The extension to κ<0 uses parity.

**Scope for the sign.** If S contains the primes of the window, (I)–(II) describe exactly the image that appears in the identity of 212-58. That identity is not replaced by a sum of positive samples. The representation uses one moment to eliminate h(0), but does not prove that the second controls the integral with log|κ|. Nor does it authorize interchanging an increasing limit in S with that integral. A signed comparison of the contributions |κ|<1 and |κ|>1 is missing; no new bound for λ_A is obtained and the OPEN status of the global proof is not altered.


**Additional image restriction: multiplicative periodization.** For the same data and each p∈S,

    Σ_(j∈Z)g_S(p^j x)=0,   x>0.                         (III)

Independently checked proof. In the positive variable x, g_S(x)=Σ_n b_n n^(-1/2)g_0(x/n), and Σ_n|b_n|n^(-1/2)<∞. If the positive support of g_0 lies in [A,B], 0<A<B, the number of j for which p^j x/n belongs to [A,B] is bounded uniformly in x,n. Hence the absolute convergence of the double series of the periodization. Isolating the factor p and rearranging: each dilation by p^k has the same periodization, and its total coefficient is

    −1/sqrt(p)+(p−1)/sqrt(p) Σ_(k≥1)p^(-k)=0.

This proves (III). The same summability preserves L¹(dx/x); no pointwise asymptotic of the tail is required. (III) is a direct consequence of the Blaschke factor, not a new source of sign. Its proof also holds for real bases greater than 1, with multi-index expansions if there are multiplicative relations. Hence (III) alone does not separate Beurling. The specifically integer part of (I)–(II) remains the representation by rational residues and Poisson; a positive comparison combining both pieces of information has not yet been constructed.


#### Stationary version: coprime samples and legitimate cutoff by denominators

Status: identities and scope of convergence PROVED, independently checked. Corollary of the explicit image above and of 212-58(1b), not a new sign candidate. Additional conceptual antecedent: ROUND_025_B of phase 211, §2, and the grouping by quotients of phase 199; there another operator with harmonic cutoffs is treated, so its conclusions are not automatically transferred.

With q=Π_(p∈S)p, put R_SF(t)=(B_SF)(t+log q), h_S(x)=|x|^(-1/2)(R_SF)(log|x|). Then h_S(x)=sqrt(q)g_S(qx) and ĥ_S(κ)=q^(-1/2)ĝ_S(κ/q). Substituting in (II), and writing ell=qm+a, gives for κ>0

    ĥ_S(κ)=1/(2κ) Σ_(d≥1,(d,q)=1) μ(d)/d
                       Σ_(ell∈Z,(ell,q)=1)g_0(ell/(dκ))
           =1/κ Σ_(d≥1,(d,q)=1) μ(d)/d
                       Σ_(ell≥1,(ell,q)=1)g_0(ell/(dκ)).       (IV)

The second equality uses parity. The inner grouping by d is kept: the series of these blocks converges absolutely. q no longer appears in the scale of the samples, only in coprimality. If S contains all the primes ≤X, every positive integer coprime to q, except 1, is >X. This does not attribute a sign to the blocks.

**Absolute divergence before grouping.** For g_0 nonzero there is an interval [A_1,B_1]⊂(0,∞) where |g_0|≥c>0. Fix κ>0. For each sufficiently large prime d not dividing q, the interval [dκA_1,dκB_1] contains at least c_1 d integers coprime to q, with c_1>0 fixed: it suffices to count each of the φ(q) admissible classes, with bounded error. Since |μ(d)|=1, the sum of absolute values of the samples of that block, multiplied by 1/(κd), is ≥c c_1/κ. There are infinitely many such primes. Hence the double sum of absolute values in (IV) diverges. It is not permitted to regroup freely all the terms by reduced fractions.

**Exact cutoff.** For D a positive integer, define H_D using the second sum of (IV) with d≤D. All the sums are finite, because g_0 has compact support away from 0. With

    M_r(y)=Σ_(k≤y,(k,r)=1) μ(k)/k,

the grouping ell/d=a/b, (a,b)=1, is legitimate and gives

    H_D(κ)=1/κ Σ_(b≤D,(b,q)=1) [μ(b)/b] M_(bq)(D/b)
                         Σ_(a≥1,(a,bq)=1)g_0(a/(bκ)).       (V)

Indeed, write d=kb and ell=ka. If b has a square divisor, μ(kb)=0; if it is squarefree, only (k,b)=1 contributes and μ(kb)=μ(k)μ(b). Coprimality with q requires (a,bq)=1 and (k,bq)=1. The upper limit k≤D/b keeps exactly the factor M_(bq)(D/b).

For κ in any compact subset of (0,∞), H_D→ĥ_S locally uniformly: one returns to the expression via h=ĝ_0 and uses its Schwartz decay to dominate the tails in d,k. This does NOT assert convergence in L² with weight |logκ|. One cannot replace M_(bq)(D/b) by a limit for each b and then sum in a,b, nor insert H_D into the energy of 212-58 and pass to the limit without another argument. The cutoffs and cross terms remain; (IV)–(V) do not prove a positive comparison between the regions κ<1 and κ>1.


#### Passage to the energy by truncation of coefficients of the finite product

Status: PROVED, independently checked. Regularity precision for the same representation 212-58 and its earlier image; no new sign construction. The truncation is changed: this one keeps the S-smooth coefficients n≤L of the unitary product, not the denominators d≤D of (IV)–(V). It is not identified with the Schatten argument of 212-86.

Fix S finite, q=Π_(p∈S)p, h=ĝ_0 and b_n as before. For a>0, U_a h(κ)=sqrt(a)h(aκ). The stationary image is

    ĥ_S=Σ_n b_n U_(n/q)h,
    Htilde_L=Σ_(n≤L)b_n U_(n/q)h.

Define ||h||_W²=∫R(1+|log|κ||)|h(κ)|²dκ. The declared smooth h belongs to W. Changing variable u=aκ and using

    1+|log|u/a||≤(1+|log a|)(1+|log|u||)

proves ||U_a h||_W≤sqrt(1+|log a|)||h||_W.

For 0<δ<1/2, put r_p=p^(-1/2) and

    f_p(δ)=r_p+(1−r_p²)p^δ/(1−r_p p^δ),
    P_δ=Π_(p∈S)f_p(δ)=Σ_n|b_n|n^δ,
    f_p'(δ)=(1−r_p²)p^δ log p/(1−r_p p^δ)².

The products and their derivatives are finite; P_δ'=Σ_n|b_n|n^δ log n. These equalities come from the geometric series of each factor, absolutely convergent because δ<1/2. For L≥1, the inequality n^(−δ)≤L^(−δ) on the tail and sqrt(1+|log(n/q)|)≤1+log q+log n give

    t_L:=||ĥ_S−Htilde_L||_W
      ≤L^(−δ)[(1+log q)P_δ+P_δ']||h||_W.                (VI)

The series thus converges absolutely in W and its limit coincides with the L² image already identified. For Q(H)=(1/2)∫log|κ||H(κ)|²dκ, Cauchy–Schwarz with the weight W gives

    |Q(Htilde_L)−Q(ĥ_S)|
      ≤(1/2)t_L(2||ĥ_S||_W+t_L).                        (VII)

One can also bound ||ĥ_S||_W by [(1+log q)P_0+P_0']||h||_W. Therefore the constant of (VII) can be written entirely in terms of explicit data of the finite product and of the test.

**Scope.** It is justified to evaluate the stationary energy as a limit of these finite expressions, keeping all the cross terms. It has not been proved that Q(Htilde_L) is nonnegative; in 212-58 the unsymmetrized identity also keeps the term ⟨tF,F⟩. No convergence in W of the cutoff H_D by denominators is obtained, nor uniformity as S grows, nor a comparison of masses giving the sign. The geometric summability argument does not by itself distinguish the falsifiers. The global question remains OPEN.


#### One-sided passage to the sign for the cutoff by denominators

Status: PROVED as a limit-passage lemma, independently checked. The cutoff H_D of (IV)–(V) is audited; no new sign candidate and no proof of convergence in W is presented. Immediate antecedent: the two previous entries, which separated local convergence of this cutoff and W-convergence of the cutoff by coefficients.

With the same smooth data, q fixed and h=ĝ_0, Poisson gives exactly, for κ>0,

    H_D(κ)=q^(-1) Σ_(d≤D,(d,q)=1) μ(d)
                         Σ_(k≥1)c_q(k)h(dkκ/q).          (VIII)

The prefactor is 1/q, not 2/q: the physical sum over all integers is twice the sum over the positives. H_D and ĥ_S are extended by parity.

Fix N>1 and C_N=sup_(u>0) u^N|h(u)|<∞. Write Z_N=Σ_(k≥1)k^(-N), merely a convergent constant. Using |c_q(k)|≤φ(q), one obtains, for κ≥1,

    |H_D(κ)|, |ĥ_S(κ)| ≤ K κ^(-N),
    |H_D(κ)−ĥ_S(κ)| ≤ E D^(1−N) κ^(-N),
    K=φ(q)q^(N−1) C_N Z_N²,
    E=φ(q)q^(N−1) C_N Z_N/(N−1).

The second bound uses Σ_(d>D)d^(-N)≤D^(1−N)/(N−1). For

    Q_+(H)=(1/2)∫_(|κ|≥1)log|κ| |H(κ)|²dκ,
    Q_−(H)=(1/2)∫_(|κ|<1)(−log|κ|)|H(κ)|²dκ,

one deduces, by parity and ∫_1^∞logκ κ^(-2N)dκ=(2N−1)^(-2),

    |Q_+(H_D)−Q_+(ĥ_S)|
       ≤2KE D^(1−N)/(2N−1)².                            (IX)

Each H_D belongs to W: if the positive support of g_0 is contained in [A,B], it vanishes for 0<κ<1/(DB), is smooth on positive compacts and has decay of any order at infinity by (VIII). The exact image belongs to W by the earlier coefficient-truncation result. Pointwise convergence away from zero and Fatou give

    Q_−(ĥ_S)≤liminf_D Q_−(H_D).

Together with (IX), this proves the one-sided inequality

    Q(ĥ_S)≥limsup_D Q(H_D),   Q=Q_+−Q_−.                (X)

Convergence of the negative parts is not required. A possible concentration of negative energy near κ=0 has a favorable direction for transferring a lower bound.

**Exact conditional connection.** If S contains the primes of the window, the stationary identity of 212-58 is a_T(F)=Q(ĥ_S)+⟨tF,F⟩. Therefore it would suffice to prove, for each primitive smooth test F, along a sequence D_j→∞,

    Q(H_(D_j))+⟨tF,F⟩≥−ε_j(F),   ε_j(F)→0.             (XI)

No uniformity in F is needed for this pointwise step; extending afterwards to the full carrier requires the density in the norm of the form already established. One can also apply (X) to F and to its reflection and average, eliminating the term ⟨tF,F⟩. (XI) remains OPEN: no sign has been proved for the cutoffs, nor that this sufficient condition is necessary. The lemma resolves the direction of the limit passage, not the control of the cross terms nor the global positivity. No papers are modified.


#### Audit of criterion (XI): translation and asymptotic norm conservation

Status: PROVED, independently checked; auxiliary consequences of the previous criterion, not a new candidate. Antecedents: (VIII)–(XI) and 212-62, which already distinguishes conservation of mass and control of its logarithmic moment. Mass control is not presented as a sign mechanism.

Put F_a(t)=F(t−a), q,D fixed, and E_D(F)=Q(H_D[F])+∫t|F(t)|²dt. Both vanishing exponential moments are preserved by translation. Directly from (VIII),

    H_D[F_a](κ)=e^(a/2)H_D[F](e^aκ),
    E_D(F_a)=E_D(F)+a(||F||²−||H_D[F]||²/2).             (XII)

The second identity uses Q(e^(a/2)H(e^a·))=Q(H)−(a/2)||H||². The exact image has norm²=2||F||² by the physical change and unitarity. For a finite cutoff that equality has not been established: IF the norm defect of (XII) is nonzero for a test, the energy of that same cutoff cannot be nonnegative under all its translations. It is not claimed that the defect is always nonzero. The observation is with q,D fixed and all translations, not a refutation of (XI), nor a counterexample to the form in a fixed window.

An additional consequence of (XI) is that norm conservation does not constitute an independent obligation. More generally, if D_j→∞ and E_(D_j)(F) is bounded below, (IX) implies Q_−(H_(D_j))≤C for some constant C≥0. For 0<η<1,

    ∫_(|κ|<η)|H_(D_j)(κ)|²dκ≤2C/|logη|.

The tail at infinity is uniformly small by the bound K|κ|^(−N). On compacts away from zero there is uniform convergence. Dividing the line into these three regions, and using that the exact image belongs to L², proves

    H_(D_j)→ĥ_S strongly in L²,
    ||H_(D_j)||²→2||F||².                               (XIII)

Thus the translation defect of (XII) tends to zero along any sequence satisfying the proposed lower bound. Convergence in W is not deduced: the logarithmic weight may preserve negative energy concentrated near zero even though its L² mass tends to zero. Nor is the lower bound required in (XI) obtained. The global problem remains OPEN.


#### Selection of rational pairs and divergent diagonal in the energy of H_D

**Selection: no new mechanism.** Cross-check with ROUND_025_B §2 of phase 211, the classes by quotients of phase 199, the table of pairs/Farey of Paper 48, the grid, the crossword and RULES_AVOID. The current operator has a different cutoff, d≤D, and coefficients μ(b)M_(bq)(D/b)/b; this does not authorize transferring the old NO-GOs. However, expanding in pairs of samples and grouping by reduced quotients does not by itself provide an operation that proves (XI). The selection of positivity by rational groups or local factors is rejected in that formulation, after independent check; collective compensations with another explicit operation are not excluded.

**Current integration obstacle: PROVED, independently checked.** Even for D finite, the expansion of the energy in individual samples is not absolutely summable. Take the term d=1, present with coefficient 1 for all D≥1, and define, for κ>0,

    v_ell(κ)=κ^(-1)g_0(ell/κ),   (ell,q)=1,

with even extension. If the positive support of g_0 lies in [A,B] and ell>B, the support of v_ell lies in |κ|>1. Put

    I_0=∫_0^∞|g_0(x)|²dx>0,
    I_1=∫_0^∞log x |g_0(x)|²dx.

Parity and x=ell/κ give exactly

    Q_+(v_ell)=(I_0 log ell−I_1)/ell.                   (XIV)

The sum of (XIV) over ell coprime to q diverges to +∞: the progression ell=1+jq suffices. On the other hand Q_+(H_D)<∞ by (IX). Therefore the double series of pairings of the individual samples has no absolute convergence after integrating: already its positive diagonal diverges. That there are finitely many samples at each κ for D fixed does not imply that there are finitely many samples when running over the whole integral.

This computation identifies an indispensable cancellation between cross terms for the current operator. It does not allow separating diagonal and remainder as two finite quantities; nor does it exclude grouping before integrating, using an additional common cutoff and keeping it to the end, or designing a collective compensation. It does not refute the original form nor (XI). The global lower bound remains OPEN.


#### Regularization by compensated cells of the cutoff H_D

Status: PROVED, independently checked; auxiliary repair of the interchange that fails in (XIV), not a new sign candidate. Antecedents: (IV), (VIII)–(XIV); elementary quadrature by cells. RULES_AVOID §U1 already prevents attributing a universal sign to a linear quadrature residue. Here only convergence is proved, without assigning a sign to the residue or claiming conceptual novelty.

Let A_q={a:1≤a≤q,(a,q)=1}, φ=φ(q). For y>0 and j≥0 define

    R_j(y)=y^(-1)[Σ_(a∈A_q)g_0((qj+a)/y)
              −(φ/q)∫_(qj)^(q(j+1))g_0(u/y)du].        (XV)

Extend each R_j by parity. The first primitivity condition gives ∫_0^∞g_0(x)dx=0. For each y, the compensating integrals add up to y∫g_0=0, and the samples run exactly over the positive integers coprime to q. Therefore,

    H_D(κ)=Σ_(d≤D,(d,q)=1)μ(d)Σ_(j≥0)R_j(dκ).          (XVI)

The initial equality is pointwise, with only finitely many nonzero blocks for each κ≠0. A stronger convergence is justified next.

If supp(g_0) on the positive half-line is contained in [A,B], then, for j≥1,

    supp(R_j)∩(0,∞) ⊂ [qj/B,q(j+1)/A],
    |R_j(y)|≤φ q ||g_0'||_∞ y^(-2).

The second bound is obtained by comparing each sample with the cell average and using the mean value theorem. On the interval of support y is comparable to j, with constants depending on A,B,q. Its length is O(j). Consequently,

    ||R_j||_W≤C j^(-3/2)sqrt(1+log j),   j≥1,          (XVII)

for W=L²((1+|log|κ||)dκ). The series of these norms converges. The block R_0 has positive support contained in [1/B,q/A]: below 1/B all the samples vanish and the cell integral includes the whole support of g_0, whose integral is zero; above q/A there is neither a sample nor a nonzero integral. Hence R_0 also belongs to W.

For q>1 there is an improvement: the involution a↦q−a on A_q gives Σa=φ q/2. The discrete rule and the integral have the same mass and first moment in each cell. Taylor around q(j+1/2) eliminates the linear term and proves

    |R_j(y)|≤(φ q²/4)||g_0''||_∞ y^(-3),
    ||R_j||_W≤C' j^(-5/2)sqrt(1+log j),   j≥1.         (XVIII)

The constant 1/4 is a valid majorant; the improvement is not needed for convergence.

Finally,

    ||R_j(d·)||_W≤d^(-1/2)sqrt(1+log d)||R_j||_W.

As D is fixed, (XVI) converges absolutely in W. Define B_log(u,v)=(1/2)∫log|κ| u(κ)conj(v(κ))dκ. The bound |B_log(u,v)|≤(1/2)||u||_W||v||_W justifies

    Q(H_D)=Σ_(d,e≤D;(d,q)=(e,q)=1) μ(d)μ(e)
                 Σ_(j,k≥0)B_log(R_j(d·),R_k(e·)),       (XIX)

with absolute convergence of the whole series of pairings. For real data all the terms are real; for complex data the Hermitian expression is kept.

**Scope.** The compensation inside each cell resolves the divergence of the expansion in individual samples, without altering H_D. No sign has been proved for the blocks or for their crossings. The bounds depend on D when summing dilations; uniformity in D is not claimed, nor the inequality (XI). The second primitivity condition has not been used in this regularization. It does not by itself constitute a mechanism separating the falsifiers nor a proof of global positivity.


**Audit of the local sign of (XV): convexity is not enough.** PROVED, independently checked. For q>1, define L_q(f)=Σ_(a∈A_q)f(a)−[φ(q)/q]∫_0^q f(x)dx. The equality of mass and first moment implies, for f∈C²([0,q]),

    L_q(f)=∫_0^q K_q(s)f''(s)ds,
    K_q(s)=Σ_(a∈A_q)(a−s)_+−φ(q)(q−s)²/(2q).

This is obtained by inserting f(x)=f(0)+xf'(0)+∫_0^q(x−s)_+f''(s)ds. For q=6, A_q={1,5}, one has K_6(s)=−s²/6 on [0,1], while K_6(3)=1/2. A smooth, nonnegative, nonzero function f'' supported in (0,1) produces L_6(f)<0; another supported sufficiently near 3 produces L_6(f)>0. Integrating twice one obtains in both cases smooth convex functions.

Therefore, not even the restriction to convex profiles imposes a uniform sign on this local quadrature rule in either direction. It is a concrete limitation of the current compensated block, not a new candidate nor an obstruction to the sign of its joint energy.
