At fixed rate 63/2 a verified square of a zero dominates the whole tail by |F(±δ+iγ)|≤|γ|⁻ᴺ, independently of k. Splice with POWER017 and 204. Intermediate region OPEN; it is not a sign for general numerators of that degree.

213-206-A. [Criterion of eventual sign by dyadic rays](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_206_A.md). An off-line zero forces W_(q l,p l)<0 infinitely often for some fixed pair q=2^j,p>0. Strict comparison with the maximum over the critical half-axis, separation of pairs and two neighboring slopes to avoid resonance. Eventual sign ray by ray without uniformity in the slope would suffice. OPEN for arbitrary slopes.

213-207-A. [Diagonal k=N and exact detection intervals](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_207_A.md). With variable rate u, the limsup of the N-th root of the normalized moment is max |−4u²z²/(u²−z²)²|. Each displaced zero δ generates an interval of rates of length 2|δ|; eventual sign or subexponential growth over rational rates suffices. Bound for u≤G−1 by Z2, eventual sign up to G−1000. No global closure.

213-208-A. [Arithmetic cutoff of the diagonal and exact displacement](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_208_A.md). A centered sum of Λ(n)−1 up to X_N=M_1(u)^(2N) preserves the moments of 207 up to O_u(1). The superunit growth recovers the maximal horizontal displacement by means of sup_u u√(Q−1)/Q. No new bound on the true displacement.

213-209-A. [Lone primes and profile of a verified zero](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_209_A.md). At the cutoff of 208, b_N=−2Σ_{p≤X_N}(log p)c_N(log p)/√p+o(1). Squares o(1) by PNT and L¹ control of Fourier; profile −m(u)exp(−x²) at rate u exp(x/√N) in the verified zone. The bound for every rate remains OPEN.

213-210-A. [A quadratic sequence over primes measures the relative displacement](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_210_A.md). For E_N=∫₃ᴺ|A_N(u)|²du/u⁴ the limit E_N^(1/(2N))=1+sup(δ/γ)² exists (in the limit N→∞). Under RH E_N→0; if it fails there is exponential growth on the whole tail. The prime bound on a subsequence remains OPEN.

213-211-A. [Diagonal distribution of criterion 210](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_211_A.md). Antecedent of separation of pairs in 162/167. For the weights of 210 one obtains the joint law du/u⁴ · y exp(−y²/2)dy/(2π) with y=u log p/√N and limit mass 1/(162π). The upper bound between distinct primes remains OPEN.
The same memo proves a local falsifier: truncating at log p≤Y√N/u produces unbounded sums in [3,4] even retaining a diagonal fraction as close to one as desired; the tail must cancel the boundary contribution.

213-212-A. [Threshold of the prime cutoff at linear scale](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_212_A.md). Improves the cutoff at fixed rate of 208 and specifies where shortening it produces spurious exponential growths even in [3,4]. Boundary profile by contour and PNT; two bounded shifts, with exception of the intermediate critical slope. The bound on the complete sum remains OPEN.

213-213-A. [Centered critical cutoff versus the same uncentered cutoff](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_213_A.md). Subtracting the continuous density makes it possible to remove an additional κ√N in log X with error o(1); at the same scale the raw error grows in two phases at most at least exp(ακ√N)/√N. Two consecutive increments moreover resolve the exceptional slope of 212. Antecedents 208, 212 and R161_078; the interior centered sum remains OPEN.

213-214-A. [Frequency of log u in the energy of 210](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_214_A.md). Exact beta factorization of the Mellin transform of b_N and exponential concentration at |t|/(2N)≈max|δ/γ|. All fixed-frequency averages decay even outside RH; the band o(N) does not detect the exponential growth. The sign remains OPEN.
Uniform L² comparison with the transform of the finite prime sum of 210: if there is an off-line zero, the same band concentrates its exponential growth.

213-215-A. [A band of width one at frequency √N measures the extreme angle](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_215_A.md). For J_N=||B_N|| on [√N,√N+1], log(1+J_N)/√N→Θ. Under RH J_N→0; outside RH J_N is comparable to exp(Θ√N)/√N on the whole tail. The floor comes from a finite Gram of the extreme frequencies. The arithmetic bound for a quadratic with cosine and sinc remains.
Discrete variant: limsup log(1+|B_(k²)(k)|)/k=Θ; outside RH the floor occurs on a set of integers of positive lower density, by the common phase of the coefficients that coincide modulo 2π.

213-216-A. [Absolute cost after integrating each prime in the rate](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_216_A.md). At frequency t=o(N), the total prime variation has N-th root M_(1/2)(3)>1, even performing first the complete oscillatory integral. For N=k² the rates u≥√k log(2k) are indeed discardable by absolute estimate at scale k. The intermediate signed bound remains OPEN.

213-217-A. [A linear sample without exceptional orders](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_217_A.md). The weight u^(−√k+ik−1) in the sum of 210 selects the smallest modulus among the zeros of extreme angle. Outside RH, log|C_k|=Θk−√k log r₀−log k+O(1) on the whole tail; under RH C_k→0. Subexponential bound on a subsequence suffices. The bound from primes is still missing.

213-218-A. [Signed cancellation across p=exp(k/3)](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_218_A.md). In the sample 217 the primes up to that cutoff produce an explicit complex term of modulus comparable to exp(k/6)3^(−√k)/k^(3/2) for all large k, even integrating the oscillation in u. The complement cancels it with relative error o(1). PNT gives the principal term, without resolving the precision exp(o(k)).

213-219-A. [Inversion of the centered prime blocks](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_219_A.md). Uniform subexponential control at all the endpoints of each cell of 218 is equivalent by Stieltjes inversion and geometric sum to the classical criterion of von Koch. A positive perturbation on the same primes exactly preserves the mass and the complex moment of each complete cell but alters its interior profile at order x^β. Antecedents R166_802 and 213-167; do not retry the classical estimate as a new mechanism.

213-220-A. [Sign excursions of the prime sample](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_220_A.md). For fixed threshold λ>0, the positive and negative frequencies on every progression and blocks H≫√M with H/√M→∞ balance unconditionally. Each frequency is zero under RH and tends to 1/2 if RH fails. Improves the infinitude of signs of 207 for a specific sample, without giving the arithmetic estimate that selects a branch.

213-221-A. [Exact scheduling of the complex sample under prime perturbations](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_221_A.md). Three intervals over the same primes make it possible to preserve the mass and prescribe C_k on a subsequence, with positive weights 1+o(1) and change of count O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) for every ε. Real three-by-three inversion by two independent boundary profiles. Obstruction for stability arguments, without asserting any change for ζ.

213-222-A. [Quantitative stability of the prime sample](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_222_A.md). A count difference √x exp((A+o(1))(log x)^(2/3)) costs at most 4A^(3/2)/(9√3) in the exponent per k of ΔC_k; if A=0 it preserves the subsequence criterion. Gives a necessary floor for the perturbations of 221. Neither optimality nor the ceiling for θ(x)−x is proved.

213-223-A. [Optimal stability constant over the primes](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_223_A.md). A contour with height of order k^(−1/2) and two integrations by parts make it possible to reach exactly 4A^(3/2)/(9√3) in the limsup by means of positive weights that preserve the mass of each block. Closes the question of optimality of 222, without proving the sign of the authentic form.

213-224-A. [Stable linear orders for the prime sample](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_224_A.md). At N=jk the rate is max(0,Θ−d_j), d_j∼1/(4j), and is invariant under count differences O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)). Every fixed j admits the stability that failed at N=k². An unbounded set of j suffices, even using only counts of primes between consecutive squares. The arithmetic ceiling for arbitrary j remains OPEN.

213-225-A. [Model of integer moments in logarithmic cells](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_225_A.md). At orders N=jk the rates of 224 are preserved using O_j(k²/log k) rounded moments in O_j(k) cells. Substitution error exp(o(k)) without inverting the interior counts. Storage bound after precomputation; the cancellation of the real moments remains OPEN.

213-226-A. [Obstruction to controlling only low moments per cell](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_226_A.md). At linear order j=1, positive weights that coincide exactly with the first M_n→∞ moments of each cell can produce upper rate log M_(1/2)(3), against zero for the authentic sample. Orthogonal projection in the empirical prime measure. M_n grows without prefixed rate; the necessity of the quantitative threshold of 225 remains OPEN.

213-227-A. [Optimal exponent of a subset of primes without modifying their weights](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_227_A.md). For θ_S(x)∼x^β, 1/2<β<1, the maximal upper rate of the sample over S is j log M_(β−1/2)(3). It is attained with a single subset of regular count. At j=1 the two parts of the partition can grow exponentially even if the total has rate zero. Removing θ_S(x)=O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) does preserve the rates.

213-228-A. [The absolute displacement as the rate of a quadratic mean of accumulated deficits](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_228_A.md). Translated Gaussian window and Cauchy weight of scale 1/2 give exactly the kernel (1/max(x,y)+1/(xy))/2. The single arithmetic average V_N satisfies log(V_N)/(2N)→sup|Re ρ−1/2|², without requiring that the supremum be attained. The subexponential ceiling over the primes is missing.

213-229-A. [Ordinary quadratic mean in every band of powers](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_229_A.md). Removing the Gaussian of 228 by Stieltjes inversion and comparison of scales gives log(1+∫_(X^α)^X (ψ(x)−x)²dx/x²)/log X→2 sup|Re ρ−1/2|, for every fixed α in (0,1). A subsequence with ceiling X^o(1) would suffice; it remains OPEN. No bibliographic novelty is claimed.

213-230-A. [Detection in any band of fixed ratio](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_230_A.md). On [X,cX] with c>1 fixed, the logarithmic rate of 1+∫(ψ−x)²dx/x² is exactly 2B. Ingham density makes it possible to isolate any right zero by convolution on arbitrarily short logarithmic support. A subsequence of dyadic bands with ceiling X^o(1) would suffice; it remains to prove it.

213-231-A. [Interior primes and best line in a shrinking relative band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_231_A.md). With log(1/h)=o(log log X) and 0<h≤1, the quadratic minimum of the local count of simple primes over [X,X exp h] against free lines, integrated with dx/X², has exponent 2B (with 1 added). It is obtained by quantifying the variation of the annihilator and eliminating two additional exponents. The exact quadratic is given by differences of consecutive primes; bounding it on a subsequence is missing.

213-232-A. [Gaps versus accumulated positions of the primes](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_232_A.md). Unconditionally the minimum of 231 differs from the fit at midpoints by O_ε(X^(−1/8+ε)). A jump identity of R³ converts the line of endpoints into a sum over primes of position errors with respect to the rank, plus O(L log²X/X²). Only the ceiling for the sum of ranks on a subsequence is missing.

213-233-A. [Modular directions of the primes and parity obstruction](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_233_A.md). On [q,2q], q prime, the exact mean of the centered rank error over multipliers a is asymptotic to log(q)/12, and the frequencies above √q cost O(log q) for all a. The direction a=1 preserves the global criterion. For a=b⁻¹ and b even V_a≳q/b² is proved uniformly; the average does not transfer the ceiling to the true direction.

213-234-A. [Empty arcs for all small inverses](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_234_A.md). For a=b⁻¹ there are b−φ(b) empty arcs of length 1/b: V_a≥M²[b−φ(b)]/(12qb³). Rules out the crude transfer also for odd inverses of subpower size. For b prime fixed V_a/q→1/(12b²). On correcting each arc by its mass and mean there remains exactly V₁ plus a nonnegative variance between classes after normalizing.

213-235-A. [Detection by the first η log q additive frequencies](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_235_A.md). On all the intervals [q,2q], the maximum of the first η log q true prime sums, normalized by √q and with 1 added, has exponent exactly B for each fixed η>0. Regularization by convolution of boxes of the filter of 230. A simultaneous ceiling q^(1/2+o(1)) in that band over a subsequence would suffice; it remains OPEN.

213-236-A. [A fixed cosine over moving intervals](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_236_A.md). The average X⁻²∫_X^(Xe^h) F(x)²dx, with F the first cosine component of the primes of (x,2x], has exponent 2B for the h of 231. Its multiplier does not vanish at the possible right zeros. Landau and the control between integers prove that if RH fails there are nevertheless infinitely many pointwise samples O(log n); the required estimate is over a window.

213-237-A. [Unconditional good windows of length X^(2/3)](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_237_A.md). The first verified ordinate dominates in modulus the bias of the squares for the cosine of 236 (verify_237.py). There are excursions of both signs of size 0.24√x and integer crossings O(log x) without hypothesis. On a subsequence of windows of length X^(2/3) the normalized energy costs O(log² X) even under failure of RH; the larger window of 236 is missing.

213-238-A. [Longer good windows by cancellation of increments](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_238_A.md). With L=X^(2/3)exp(κ(log X/log log X)^(1/3)) for some κ>0, the energy of F tends to zero at the crossings of 237, and the local fit error of 231 tends to zero for all X. The short-interval PNT of Thorner–Zaman is used. It is not a fixed increase of the exponent nor is the detecting window obtained.

213-239-A. [One and the same fit of growing degree at two scales of length X^(1−o(1))](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_239_A.md). Fixed smooth prime kernel with multiplier without zeros on the right, m≈t/(log t log log t), t=log X. At h=t^(−o(1)) the quadratic residual preserves exponent 2B; at h=t^(−log log t) the same residual is ≤exp(−t+o(t)) at every start by Taylor. This bound is not transferred to the raw cosine nor to the detecting scale.

213-240-A. [Exact transition of the energy after the polynomial fit](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_240_A.md). A new compact kernel of summable boxes gives exponent 2 max(B−λ,0) when log(1/h)∼λ log t log log t, also in the regime of ratio tending to zero. Finite isolation by density and almost exponential spectral tail. Constructing subsequences of low energy for λ↓0 is missing.

213-241-A. [Discrete test of primes without fit or principal term](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_241_A.md). 2r+1 logarithmic samples and binomial differences that exactly kill the mean. The maximum of r+1 normalized residuals has exponent max(B−λ,0). Simultaneous control of the block on a subsequence at λ=0 is missing.
For λ=0 one adjacent difference per node suffices, or the oscillation of the rescaled count on the mesh. The loss by telescoping is subexponential.

213-242-A. [Sparse good nodes and order statistic](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_242_A.md). Among N≈t² adjacent differences the n-th smallest, n≈t/log²t, already detects B. Real interpolation at arbitrary positions and discrete isolation. To close it suffices a fraction of nodes tending to zero on a subsequence; its existence remains OPEN.

213-243-A. [One good node at detecting scale and blocks at stationary points](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_243_A.md). Iterating the variable step of the normalized count produces an exact return if B>0. Rolle and PNT construct complete good blocks of physical length X^(3/4)exp(κ√log X). In the larger mesh of 242 only one node is guaranteed, against the approximately t/log²t required.

213-244-A. [Fixed limit of small nodes with attained supremum](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_244_A.md). For the prime count of 242–243, a unique extreme pair allows at most one small node per block even without spectral gap. An infinite extreme line admits a finite ceiling by density and isolation by derivatives. Arithmetic abundance of nodes remains to be proved and the supremum without maximum remains to be covered.

213-245-A. [Two increments of an average over the past](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_245_A.md). Positive gamma average of the prime count; each small rational slope uses three evaluations. The existence of two small adjacent increments per slope is equivalent to RH even without attained supremum. The selection by rates comes from 143/206. The simultaneous arithmetic estimate is missing.

213-246-A. [Two positive readings for 9/500≤c<1/4](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_246_A.md). The bias of the squares gives equivalent H(1/2)δ exp(t/2)/4 for both differences at every start using Z2. Under RH it holds for every fixed c. Conversely eventual sign of one reading for each rational 0<c<9/500 suffices. Control of slopes near zero is missing.

213-247-A. [Linear barycenter at prime endpoints](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_247_A.md). RH is equivalent to the barycenter of p<q with weight (q−p)log p exceeding or equaling q/3 at every sufficiently large prime q. Quadratic weight, minimum at endpoints by concavity of x²C(x), conditional margin by 092. verify_247.py certifies [3,99991]. The eventual arithmetic comparison remains OPEN.

213-248-A. [Positive barycenter for 3≤x≤10^20](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_248_A.md). Exact separation of even exponents by means of von Mangoldt, positive partial trace and two-sided tail by Z3. Margin >0.035√x from 10^7 and certificate of prime endpoints on the initial stretch. The window T of the Weil form is not enlarged.

213-249-A. [Positive radius even when erasing new primes](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_249_A.md). There are unconditional blocks of length 0.41 p^(3/4) at arbitrarily large primes. The maximal subsequential exponent of the radius computed on freezing the primes is (1+Θ)/2; the arithmetic ceiling 3/4 would suffice. Propagation at all primes is not obtained.

213-250-A. [Long blocks with arbitrary partial erasure](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_250_A.md). For 3/4<a<1 there are authentic blocks of length p^a that tolerate p^(3/2−a−ε) erasures. Maximal tolerance exponent min(a,1+Θ−a), with asymptotic constant under RH. The uniform ceiling of erasures to close the sign is missing.
The choice of worst effect in the whole block is exactly the prefix of the next m primes. The proof reduces the search of subsets to a single artificial gap.

213-251-A. [Inversion of the barycenter by sparse erasures](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_251_A.md). At 99991 the exact minimum cost is 30 primes. A single set of erasures of mass O(√x) forces both signs, preserves relative density one in intervals with many primes and alters arbitrarily little the Euler factor in Re s≥1/2. The stability already indexed in R163_102 is used; the boundary logarithmic derivative does change.

213-252-A. [Oscillating editing with divisor intact in Re s>1/3](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_252_A.md). Multiplicities 0,1,2 at true primes produce −√x cos(x^(1/24))+o(√x) in the barycenter. The ratio of products is holomorphic and without zeros in Re s>1/3, even at 1/2. The contour control used in 247 distinguishes this modification from ζ; it is not a failure of the sign at the genuine primes.

213-253-A. [All logarithmic moments of the barycenter at anchors up to 9·10^24](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_253_A.md). Simultaneous strict positivity of (−1)^n(KP)^(n)(s) for n≥0, 1/2<s≤G². Full formula over x in s>1, continuation below. Unbounded anchors are missing; gamma concentration would then recover the pointwise sign.

213-254-A. [Exact boundary and first negative order](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_254_A.md). For the barycenter of 253 all moments are positive up to the first tangent disc, endpoint included; beyond it both signs occur. At distance δ above a finite boundary the first negative order lies between c/δ and C/δ, even with ties. It remains to prove that there is no finite boundary.

213-255-A. [A binomial row of the barycenter up to order 2^G](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_255_A.md). b_n=(−Δ)^n F(2)>0 for n≤2^(3·10^12) by the beta product and Z2–Z3. Eventual positivity of this single row is equivalent to RH by continuation of a Dirichlet series. It has not been proved for unbounded orders.

213-256-A. [Budget of 1/3 for positive prime summands](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_256_A.md). Adding 255 produces positive rational weights. Under RH no finite cutoff exceeds 1/3; outside RH there are excesses at infinitely many N already with p≤N^(3/2). Budget proved unconditionally up to N=2^G. Its uniform control is missing.

213-257-A. [Positive budget only on x<p≤2x](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_257_A.md). Non-negative cosine weight with shift 1/2. The count stays below its integral with margin >0.009√x on [10^12,10^38]. The eventual sign is equivalent to the global one. verify_257.py certifies the spectral margin using the first 20 pairs and the residual trace.

213-258-A. [Optimal cost of a carry in one octave](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_258_A.md). At most 1/(2 log 2) of the mass of any binomial carry can fall in [x,2x], with equality in the symmetric split. The adaptive positive majorizations of the weight of 257 lose at least (2 log 2−1)xh. To use factorials one must control and subtract exterior mass.

213-259-A. [Signed carries: approximation of the octave and cost](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_259_A.md). The uniform split and a Möbius inverse reproduce the weight exactly on y≥v, with leakage only below the cutoff. For total variation B, the error exponent −1+o(1) is equivalent to RH; there is an unconditional approximation with error O(exp(−c√log B)). Reaching the critical cost unconditionally is missing.

213-260-A. [Concentration of the real factorization of the binomials](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_260_A.md). For n≤Kx and both sides of the split increasing, at most the asymptotic fraction 1/(2 log 2) falls on prime powers of [x,2x]. Avoiding the loss with positive coefficients requires a budget Ω(x/log x), an order attained by the individual binomials p over 1. The root bound of 257 is still to be obtained.

213-261-A. [Exact integer binomials with controlled cost](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_261_A.md). Cyclic averaging converts the floor coefficients into signed integer carries up to 2x. The optimum lies between one third and twice the explicit variation Σ|S_j−S_(j+1)|. Reaching x^(1/2+ε) at all integers is equivalent to RH; that bound has not been obtained without hypotheses.

213-262-A. [Adjustment on prime powers only and mass calibration](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_262_A.md). A scalar equality of entropies replaces the equations at non-prime-power integers while keeping the equivalence between root cost and RH. The combination 6,3,2 repairs the mass without touching the atoms. verify_262.py certifies uncalibrated optima at x=16,32,64; the unconditional calibrated rate is not known.

213-263-A. [Decreasing price of the mass correction](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_263_A.md). The optimal yield R_N of null relations on the prime powers tends to infinity and is ≤log(N+1). Unconditional proof by duality, additivity and the logarithmic term of Stirling. The error that must be corrected remains to be controlled; the improvement alone does not change a power exponent.

213-264-A. [Explicit mass correction with yield log log N](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_264_A.md). Two rational families have identical values at prime powers and net mass (1/2)log T+O(1) with variation ≤7.5+o(1). It follows that liminf R_N/log log N≥1/15; the size of the arithmetic error that needs to be corrected remains open.

213-265-A. [Root correction for simple primes in a binomial](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_265_A.md). For n^(16/19+δ)≤k≤n/2 the mass of proper powers is uniformly equivalent to |ζ(1/2)|(√k+√(n−k)−√n), without RH. For each fixed k there is a positive density of rows without any of these contributions. The errors after growing signed combinations remain to be controlled.

213-266-A. [Differences of rows with a common endpoint](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_266_A.md). In translation density, the centered variance of Y_(k+h)−Y_k depends only on h and is equivalent to ζ(3/2)√h log(h)/(2π). For signed zero-sum families a quadratic bound in terms of the diameter of the lengths is obtained. Compatibility with the prescribed atoms of 262 remains open.

213-267-A. [Exact octave with a fixed binomial endpoint](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_267_A.md). Variation O(1), weighted absolute error O(y³/x²) up to y≤x and hence O(√x) up to x^(5/6). A fixed strip of primes immediately below the octave still costs ≫x in absolute value.

213-268-A. [Necessary separation of the binomial endpoints](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_268_A.md). Exact adjustment on primes alone already forces Σ_n(x^(1/6+ε)+2x−n)V_n ≫ x. With a single endpoint 2x the cost exceeds the root budget; it also exceeds it for endpoints restricted to distance ≤x^(1/2−η) from 2x.

213-269-A. [Sparse endpoints sufficient for the calibrated adjustment](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_269_A.md). Every row of smaller side k is reproduced at cost ≤4s_b(k) using only endpoints N and N−b^i. It preserves each carry and the entropy exactly. With base two the additional cost is logarithmic; with growing base an arbitrarily slow number of endpoints tending to infinity suffices, at subpower loss.

213-270-A. [Optimal cost of universal compression to r+1 endpoints](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_270_A.md). The best worst-case cost to reproduce a row at all moduli is Θ_r(N^(1/r)), for each fixed r≥1. Sinusoidal certificate by boxes and ceiling by digits. The conclusion does not impose that cost on the specific arithmetic weight.

213-271-A. [Exact repair of all chains of small primes](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_271_A.md). One interpolates only at primes p>√N. The full calibrated cost is equivalent, up to absolute constants, to the initial cost plus the variation of the errors on the remaining chains and a corrected scalar defect. Errors uniformly bounded there cost O(√N) including the additional calibration.

213-272-A. [Exact calibrated adjustment at all large moduli](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_272_A.md). Truncating the inversion of 261, balancing at U and calibrating with the central row of endpoint U reproduces all m>U with exact entropy and cost O((x/U)log²N). With U=⌊√N⌋ only the control of the repair of the lower chains remains.

213-273-A. [Calibrated interpolation on both sides of a band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_273_A.md). A smoothed inversion with two discrete moments allows simultaneous adjustment of all m>√N and all prime powers q≤N^(1/3) with exact mass and cost O(√N log³N). The intermediate band of prime powers remains.

213-274-A. [Band of ratio O(log²N) in the calibrated adjustment](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_274_A.md). Reusing the convolution of 047 as a fixed weight with Mellin transform without zeros on the right, the binomial adjustment at root cost and exact mass leaves open only the prime powers between √N/(C log²N) and √N. It does not extend to the cosine of 257.

213-275-A. [A common weight and a signed scalar in the band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_275_A.md). The compressed and smoothed cosine preserves in the same octave an asymptotic one-sided margin ≥0.028 under RH and the interpolation of 274. For the constructed adjustment, a root lower bound with arbitrary loss for the signed sum Λ(q)R(q) in the band suffices; there is no need to repair each atom.

213-276-A. [Absolute floor on the primes of the band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_276_A.md). For the adjustment of 275, Σ_(Y<p≤U)log(p)|R(p)| ≫ N^(3/4)/log N. The first zero forces a continuous moment and the quadratic interpolation transfers it to prime samples. The signed bound remains open.

213-277-A. [Quantitative balance of both signs in the band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_277_A.md). The signed integral is already O(√N log³N). Over primes or all prime powers, |E|/ΣΛ|R| ≪ exp(−c(log U/log log U)^(1/3)) unconditionally; the absolute one-sided root bound remains open.

213-278-A. [Controlled divisors and reduction to short cofactors](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_278_A.md). After expanding Λ, the joint contribution of d≤√N/(C' log⁴N) is O(√N log⁵N) unconditionally. A signed sum of μ(d)log d with O(log⁴N) cofactors remains; the absolute one-sided bound is missing.

213-279-A. [Exact exponent of the absolute mass in the band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_279_A.md). The limit log A/log x is (1+sup Reρ)/2, also when summing only over primes. For RH the exponent ceiling 3/4 on the absolute prime mass along any unbounded subsequence suffices. That ceiling remains open.

213-280-A. [Prefixed sampling of the exponent in the band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_280_A.md). O(log²N log log N) integer or prime samples of the profile determine its maximum up to O(log N) and negligible error. Its limit exponent is Θ/2. It suffices to control that set at scale x^(1/4+o(1)) along a subsequence.

213-281-A. [Root diagonal for samples and calibrations](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_281_A.md). The two moments are rewritten with Möbius coefficients supported on d≥x/U and square-summable O(U). The diagonal of the Gram matrix of all samples is O(√N log⁹N); for the sign a one-sided ceiling of that exponent for the distinct pairs along a subsequence suffices.

213-282-A. [Pairs with a large common divisor in the Gram matrix](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_282_A.md). The pairs with gcd≥H together cost O((V²/H)log^C N), V=x/U. For H=V exp(−√log(2N)) they stay within the root budget, even with the infinite calibration tails. The signed upper bound for gcd<H is missing.

213-283-A. [Cancellation of the tails at crossing scales](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_283_A.md). The smoothed deficit of Λ crosses zero at unbounded scales L; at x=2L² two convolution identities eliminate exactly the calibration tails of all samples. The pending matrix uses only d,e in √N up to logarithmic factors, and its large-gcd part costs root per absolute sum.

213-284-A. [Auxiliary crossings with bounded logarithmic gaps](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_284_A.md). Every large [X,CX] contains a root of Jφ(L)−L for some fixed unquantified constant. This allows choosing L after fixing x and applying the finite reduction of 283 at all scales. The correlation with small gcd remains open.

213-285-A. [Möbius oscillation in bands of ratio tending to one](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_285_A.md). For log(1/h)=o(log log X), the maximum D of the increments from X to Xe^h satisfies log(1+D²/X)/log X→2Θ−1. A subsequence with a root ceiling suffices. Poles of 1/ζ are isolated with multiplicity and contour control.

213-286-A. [Favorable short bands and falsifier of the assembly](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_286_A.md). The external maximal theorem gives excursion ≤√X/log^A X in almost every interval of length √X log^B X. A multiplicative function with |f|=μ² preserves those savings in progressions but has excursion ≥X^(3/4−o(1)) in every long band of 285; the jump needs additional information specific to μ.

213-287-A. [One orientation of the Möbius increments suffices](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_287_A.md). For C(X)→∞ with log C=o(log X), each maximum of rises or falls of M on [X,XC(X)] has normalized exponent 2Θ−1. An exterior pole forces excursions of both signs in every band of a fixed ratio depending on the pole. The one-sided root bound along a subsequence is missing.

213-288-A. [Parity majorant and first negative collision](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_288_A.md). For κ≤√3 the triangular average over complementary divisors gives Q≥μ, with total excess O(√N/log log N). For √3<κ<2 there are infinitely many pointwise counterexamples. The sum of the majorant itself remains without a root bound.

213-289-A. [Repaired widening and semiprime barrier](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_289_A.md). The correction uses only cofactors m<κ². For κ=(log N)^(3/4)/log log N it gives a majorant with total excess O(√N); with κ=N^α, 0<α≤1/4, the semiprimes force excess ≫κ√N/log²N in every repair that only increases Q. The one-sided sum of the majorant remains open.

213-290-A. [Congruences separating nearby divisors and rank barrier](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_290_A.md). A multiplicative mark modulo P with valuation parity allows κ≤√3 P with excess O(√N/log log N), uniform in P. In the class of Gram masks, the semiprimes force excess ≫κ√N/(r log²N) if κ≫r log N. The signed sum of the majorant remains open.

213-291-A. [Oscillation of the trivial character and elimination after integrating](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_291_A.md). For each t∈[1,2] the trivial summatory function has excursions of both signs ≫x/√log x. After integrating and renormalizing, both trivial characters can be removed at the units with total root error up to logarithmic factors. The non-principal average remains.

213-292-A. [Multiplicity obstruction and non-principal autoconvolution](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_292_A.md). For a fixed character modulo 3 and generic t, a termwise root bound for a_t additionally requires excluding exterior zeros of odd order of its L. The autoconvolution eliminates that obligation; for RH a root ceiling of the positive part of its summatory functions averaged over 1≤t≤2 suffices.

213-293-A. [Frontier of discardable cofactors in the autoconvolution](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_293_A.md). For y=(log x)^A and cofactor above y at most x^δ, the masses of each sign of b_t have exponent 1−(1−δ)/A, uniform in t. The region δ≤1−A/2 can be removed at root cost. The larger cofactors remain to be controlled.

213-294-A. [Signed cancellation between the large prime and its complement](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_294_A.md). For b_t and fixed 1/2≤α<1, the block P⁺(n)>x^α equals −2 B_t''(1)x/log³x+O(x/log⁴x) and the complement has the opposite term; B_t''(1)>0 uniformly. The balance at root precision is missing.

213-295-A. [Adapted cut with a block already below root](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_295_A.md). For every large x and 1≤t≤2 there is y between √(x/48) and √(x/2) with |Σ_(P⁺(n)≤y,n≤x)b_t(n)| ≪√x/log x. Opposite signs at the endpoints by the two large primes; K_t(48)<−1/25 certified. The block with some prime larger than the cut is missing.

213-296-A. [Two monotone cuts of the block and its complement](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_296_A.md). Each jump at √(x/25)≤p≤√(x/8) lies between constants times u_p√x/log x. The global sign is equivalent to an x^o(1) ceiling for the weighted number of primes between the two crossings in the unfavorable orientation, averaged in t. Logarithmic savings of every order are proved for the distance, still insufficient.

213-297-A. [Optimal cost of discretizing the adapted cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_297_A.md). For D cuts common to all frequencies in I, the minimum mean absolute error of the smooth block is comparable to x/(D log²x) up to D equal to the number of primes in the stretch. Transversality certificate and construction by groups of primes. It does not control the global balance.

213-298-A. [Frequencies where the smooth block vanishes exactly](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_298_A.md). The zeros in frequency for prime cuts cover a fixed band with radius O(log x/√x). At them it suffices to bound the positive part of the complement with cell weights; the integrated sampling error is O_A(√x/log^A x). The arithmetic estimate of those values is missing.

213-299-A. [A fixed frequency and the exact order that detects a zero](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_299_A.md). At t=0 the coefficients of order 2k see only integers with at most k prime factors of extended character +1, with multiplicity. The one-sided ceilings per row are equivalent to the global sign without uniformity in k. For multiplicities r of ζ and m of L the first pole appears at k=max(0,m−r+1). No new root ceiling.

213-300-A. [Positive inversion of the first row at dyadic scales](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_300_A.md). When the prime 2 is separated, the odd discrepancy between classes modulo 3 and its normalized decay are averages with positive weights of the full summatory function at future dilations. Both identities are proved without assuming the root ceiling.

213-301-A. [Families of square parts with positive excess](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_301_A.md). For kernels e=hpa with p≈x^δ and optional factors in a fixed set, the signed odd contribution is asymptotic to a nonzero constant times x^((1+δ)/2); each optional prime multiplies the constant by (√ℓ−2)²/(ℓ+4). h=5 gives positive excess. The polylogarithmic kernels fit within the root budget.

213-302-A. [Uniform sign when the frequency tends to zero](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_302_A.md). The full block with prime >x^α is negative even in the transition t² log x≈1. The profile is 2(bv−3a)²+6a²; at t=0 the magnitude becomes x/log⁵x. The complement has the opposite term.

213-303-A. [Macroscopic cut with constant absolute error](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_303_A.md). A quantile of inert primes near x/3 leaves |R₀|≤4; in a fixed band near zero the cofactor jumps ≤3 give |R_t|≤18. The necessary one-sided ceiling remains in the complementary block.

213-304-A. [Infinitely many crossings of the first-row profile](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_304_A.md). A factorization into quotients of L and ζ gives real zeros at all points 1/n. By Landau and Rolle, J(z) changes sign arbitrarily far out. There exist cuts y=o(x) with block error x^o(1), without a rate for y/x or a bound for the complement.

213-305-A. [Barrier to transporting a balanced cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_305_A.md). For y≥√x, if x/y≥exp(K(log log x)²), the block preserves the negative equivalent of 302. Under the one-sided ceiling of the first row, every balanced cut there would have x/y≤(log x)^(8+o(1)). The crossings of 304 lack that rate.

213-306-A. [Converse of the logarithmic cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_306_A.md). RH is equivalent to the eventually negative sign of the block with p>x/(log x)^k for each frequency and k=4+1/n. An exterior pole forces oscillation of the effective block at generic frequency via the Mellin transform of the moving expansion. The unconditional eventual sign remains open.

213-307-A. [The critical cut k=4 changes sign unconditionally](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_307_A.md). For almost every frequency and 0<k≤4, the block with prime >x/(log x)^k is Ω±(x(log x)^(−1−k/2)log log x). At k=4 a known zero on the line suffices to overcome the term of order x/log³x. The equivalence of 306 requires k>4.

213-308-A. [Quantitative crossings beyond the fourth power](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_308_A.md). For almost every frequency there are infinitely many scales with √x≤y and x/y≥C_t(log x)^4(log log x)^2 where the block costs O(√x). The double complex pole still exceeds the real contribution upon choosing the constant of the cut. No crossing proved at a fixed power 4+ε.

213-309-A. [Means of the balance with sifted divisors](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_309_A.md). The discrete average with weights τ(n) of the balance B_t(x/n) satisfies an absolute root ceiling, uniformly after excluding any set of primes up to (log x)^(2+o(1)). Each prime also admits a partial weight reduction. The ceiling is not obtained for the isolated sample n=1.

213-310-A. [Optimal subpower gap per norm for positive means](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_310_A.md). The square of a sum of divisors eliminates all indices 2≤n≤D and preserves the root ceiling for D=x^o(1). The absolute cost D^(2−2σ+o(1)) is optimal in exponent for any positive weight of the form τ*h with that gap, by the products of two primes.

213-311-A. [Trimming the two ends of the sifted mean](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_311_A.md). For D=x^o(1), the distribution W_D(cx)/W_D(x)≈c allows removing the tail of small arguments with error x^o(1). In row zero all arguments below V(x)→∞ can be removed; the previous gap excludes those larger than x/D except the principal sample. The floor of the intermediate arguments remains.

213-312-A. [Sign of the sifted mean in decreasing relative windows](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_312_A.md). With fixed sieve D and generic frequency, the local average of the balance S_D at width x/(log x)^A is asymptotic to −c√x/log^(3/2)x. The sieve preserves the sign of the real coefficient by a Bernoulli representation. The sign of the isolated B_t remains open.

213-313-A. [Negative mean with growing gap and positive filter](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_313_A.md). For D=exp((log x)^θ), 0<θ<1/2, additional positive weights at dilations larger than D suppress both oscillatory points. The local average of the modified sifted mean has negative sign with a magnitude floor √x/log^(3/2)x. Isolating B_t is missing.

213-314-A. [Simultaneous negativity for all divisor coefficients](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_314_A.md). A common filter gives a negative definite matrix of dimension D=⌊exp((log x)^θ)⌋, θ<1/2, with uniform floor in max norm. The orthogonalization of valuation indicators includes prime powers. It is the matrix of the smoothed mean, not the global Weil form.

213-315-A. [Unavoidable mass of both signs for the whole divisor space](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_315_A.md). Normalizing λ₁=1, the minimum of h_λ(1) is 1/G_D≳1/log²(2D). Each orientation of the balance contributes in modulus ≫_{V,t} x log x/log²(2D) even above any fixed trimming V at generic frequency. Isolating B_t requires signed compensation.

213-316-A. [Signed cancellation up to power arguments](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_316_A.md). Three dilations with q>D preserve the principal sample and the initial gap, and eliminate with root error all arguments smaller than x^(77/285) uniformly in frequency. It uses the classical error of Huxley for τ. The integrated floor of the intermediate interval with signed weights remains.

213-317-A. [Cut at √x by convolutions of order one](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_317_A.md). The sequence c_t=b_t*1 maintains the integrated criterion and admits an elementary trimming up to √x by residues of divisions. For the original B_t, the trimming holds with two ordinary intermediate balances, B_t and C_t. At t=0 the coefficients of C are powers of −3 according to the inert primes of exponent one. The smoothed criterion of 049 was cross-checked.

213-318-A. [Cut at two thirds in quadratic mean](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_318_A.md). Averaging H≈X^(1/6) endpoints and grouping rational frequencies of residues allows removing arguments smaller than X^(2/3) with root mean-square error for C_t. The one-sided dyadic criterion is still equivalent to the global sign; the intermediate balance remains.

213-319-A. [Cut of arbitrary power for the local observation](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_319_A.md). With relative width x^(−δ/2), the smooth tail n≥2x^δ is removed with savings of every order and a one-sided criterion remains on D<n<2x^δ. The null moments of the local weight preserve the poles in Re s>1/2. There is no equivalent pointwise estimate of the error for the unsmoothed summatory function.

213-320-A. [Polylogarithmic band with positive local averages](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_320_A.md). For C_t the integrated floor of a sum over log X<n<O((log X)³), observed in relative windows O(1/log X), suffices. The exact recombination of the uniforms of 047 preserves the pole detector. The floor remains open.

213-321-A. [Contraction test for the short operator](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_321_A.md). In 1/2<σ<1 its vertical mean-square norm tends to zero but the supremum grows at least like N^(1−σ)/log N. At a fixed critical zero the multiplier is −1 with error of every logarithmic order. This rules out induction by uniform contraction without spectral control of the input.

213-322-A. [Contraction of the multiplier with its observation filter](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_322_A.md). For D=exp(√log X) the supremum is controlled at all heights in a strip of width ≍1/√log D next to 1. Uniform convergence to zero on each fixed line σ>1/2 of the critical stretch is equivalent to RH. The band of indices is now subpower and not polylogarithmic.

213-323-A. [Contraction at verified height with polylogarithmic band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_323_A.md). Explicit Taylor weights preserve the gap and approximate 1/ζ uniformly in interior rectangles with zero-free continuation discs. Using Z2 they reach G−2, with no improvement of the verified height nor control of growing heights.

213-324-A. [Localization of the symbol around the critical zeros](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_324_A.md). A smooth average of Taylor orders contracts up to the line at verified height outside discs of radius O_G(1/log log X). The profile inside the disc depends explicitly on the multiplicity and equals −1 at the center. No increase of the height nor of the support T.

213-325-A. [Extremal abscissa by an energy of nearby pairs](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_325_A.md). The exponential growth of a positive scalar sum of Möbius pairs with |log(n/d)|<exp(−√m) determines Θ exactly. The diagonal costs O(m^(−1/2)); the subexponential upper bound for the signed sum of distinct pairs is missing. No finite verification as hypothesis.

213-326-A. [Exact threshold of the count by moduli for nearby pairs](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_326_A.md). With width exp(−am), the absolute mass has rate max(1,2exp(−a/2)); at a≥log 4 it reaches the budget unconditionally. The signed ceilings for a=1/j remain equivalent to RH. Cancellation at the wider widths is missing.

213-327-A. [Asymptotic balance of the two Möbius orientations](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_327_A.md). In 0<a<log 4, Matomäki–Radziwiłł applied to the kernel gives E_m=o(P_m) and an explicit principal constant for P_m. Both masses of opposite sign are equivalent to P_m/2. Exponential savings are still missing; a fixed one in the absolute rate would already imply Θ<1.

213-328-A. [Dominance of the diagonal in widened critical windows](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_328_A.md). For h=4^(−m)m^b, 0≤b<1/50, one gets E_m[h]∼Δ_m. At fixed a below log 4, E_m/P_m≪m^(−1/50)log m is proved by means of the quantitative short-interval theorem. The exponential gain remains pending.

213-329-A. [Arbitrary savings in powers of m and complete critical window at polynomial scale](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_329_A.md). The central length exceeds Y^(1/6+ε), so the scalar maximal estimate for μ gives E_m/P_m≪_A m^(−A) for fixed a below log 4 and E_m∼Δ_m at h=4^(−m)m^b for each fixed b. The exponential obligation persists.

213-330-A. [Countermodel with identical Möbius signs](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_330_A.md). An arbitrarily small multiplicative perturbation at the primes, null on an arbitrary initial table, preserves support, signs and all polynomial savings of 329. A new real pole forces exponential rate >1 in any prescribed subcritical window. It rules out the abstract jump between both bounds.

Extension of 213-330-A. The defect D=1*f of the same countermodel accumulates C_P X^(1−δ)/(1−δ) with error O(X^σ) for (1−δ)/2<σ<1−δ and P fixed. Its constant only decreases like e^(−γ)/log P. For μ the defect is exactly zero outside 1; transferring that identity to the pair energy is missing.

213-331-A. [Trimming by common divisor in the energy of nearby pairs](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_331_A.md). The distinct pairs with gcd>G cost in modulus O(h binom(2m,m)/G). At subcritical scale the gcd>exp((log 4−a)m) are removed at the cost of the diagonal. All multiples of the same reduced quotient contribute with identical sign; the pending saving must mix distinct quotients.

213-332-A. [The whole absolute rate already appears in the coprime pairs](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_332_A.md). Elementary sieve in (n,d−n) with both lengths growing. At 0<a<log 4, even the class gcd=1 has absolute rate 2 exp(−a/2). The trimming of 331 alone cannot reduce it to the ceiling one.

213-333-A. [Simultaneous cancellation in classes of exact gcd](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_333_A.md). The sum of the absolute values of the signed off-diagonal contributions of all classes preserves the saving of every power of 329. Inversion over the common divisors, maximum over progressions and tail of 331. In particular the masses of both signs are asymptotically equal within the coprime pairs of 332.

213-334-A. [The separation by gcd preserves the rate that detects the zeros](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_334_A.md). For subexponential widths, the sum of moduli per class of exact gcd, diagonal included, has the same rate 1/(3/2−Θ) as the full energy. At h=exp(−m/j) the ceiling one for all those variations is equivalent to RH. The unconditional estimate of that ceiling remains pending.

213-335-A. [Threshold of the weights at the common divisor](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_335_A.md). Weighting the full classes by q^κ introduces a minimal rate 1/(1−κ/2) even under RH (0<κ<1); the first multiple of each prime is isolated in the Gram matrix. At subexponential widths the exact rate is the maximum with 1/(3/2−Θ). Weights q^o(1) greater than or equal to one preserve the original rate.

213-336-A. [Exact off-diagonal cost with weights up to the gcd](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_336_A.md). For 0≤κ≤1, the off-diagonal absolute rate with weight q^κ is 2 exp(−a/2) up to a=2 and a exp(1−a) afterwards. The barrier of 335 disappears at a≥log 4 upon removing the diagonal. For κ<1 the signed saving of every power of 333 is preserved, including the subcritical regime.

213-337-A. [Local Möbius mean without Taylor weights](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_337_A.md). At h=X^(−δ), the exponent of the dyadic second moment of the smoothed local sum tends to 2Θ as δ tends to zero. The ceiling Xh times X^ε for δ=1/j is equivalent to RH. The inverse step recovers Dirichlet blocks by Taylor inversion of the average; the unconditional estimate is missing.

213-338-A. [Two copies of the same Möbius block in the local mean](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_338_A.md). Subtracting 2S(x/2) eliminates the integral of the small combs and preserves the relevant poles. The criterion 337 reduces, with error O_B(X^(−B)), to the convolution square of a single block of μ near the root, plus the explicit sum in k. Antecedent of balanced factors in 049; estimate of the block pending.

213-339-A. [Resonance of two copies with individual cancellation](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_339_A.md). Real coefficients with signs over the squarefree numbers of a subblock and savings of a power in all their partial sums produce second moment ≫(hX)² in 338. A shared logarithmic phase at height c/h survives the smoothing. Counterexample to the generic bound for blocks, not to that of μ.

213-340-A. [An isolated rectangle with μ already requires RH](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_340_A.md). The target local bound for the two copies of μ restricted to the same interval (1.05√X,1.1√X] is equivalent to RH. Even a single fixed Mellin coefficient of the pulse recovers the obligation of Mertens; the converse uses Perron and Plancherel. Do not treat the separate estimation of rectangles as a weaker step.

213-341-A. [Small reduced quotients below the pointwise budget](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_341_A.md). In the short version of 338 all pairs with height of the reduced quotient ≤X^(δ/4) can be removed simultaneously, diagonal included. Their contribution is o(√(Xh)) uniformly in x for 0<δ≤1/10. The alternation in k over the density of coprime squarefree numbers is used; the directions of larger height remain.

213-342-A. [Second dilation that annihilates the density per quotient](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_342_A.md). The equivalent criterion with A_h(x)−2A_h(x/4) allows removing, at pointwise cost o(√(Xh)), all quotients of height ≤X^ρ for ρ<1/6−7δ/6, in particular X^(1/12) for each δ=1/j, j≥16. The cuts are scaled to the middle and the density term vanishes exactly for each k,r,s.

213-343-A. [The residue of large quotients of a rectangle still detects RH](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_343_A.md). At frequency zero, after the second subtraction and the elimination of heights ≤X^(1/6+δ/3), estimating that single rectangle at all scales is still equivalent to RH. The recurrence for the square of the Möbius sum recovers Mertens. For the second moment the equivalence with cut X^(1/8) is proved.

213-344-A. [Explicit compensation of the isolated rectangle by its own rows](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_344_A.md). In 338 every row with √X≤d≤2√X vanishes by inversion before the trimming; after trimming, the sum of moduli of their balances is O_B(X^(−B)). It includes all the rows of the rectangle equivalent to RH of 340. The simultaneous pruning by height of 342 remains valid with the scaled limits. The lower rows remain pending.

213-345-A. [Liouville balance in a band of surviving rows](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_345_A.md). In an explicit band of complete rows the inversion leaves exactly λ(n) times the number of balanced squarefree factorizations. After combining the two scales, only the odd products already cost in modulus ≍hX per center for δ<1/4. The signed balance remains open.

213-346-A. [Two compensations between bands at fixed odd product](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_346_A.md). In the band of 345 the fraction of odd mass entirely cancelled by having non-squarefree product tends to 1−∏_{p>2}(1−1/(p+1)²). At squarefree products, exchanging the factors 17 and 19 additionally proves a mass ≫hX of surplus multiplicities that cancels the complement. No new bound for the residue μ.

213-347-A. [A family of distinct products with opposite signs](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_347_A.md). Two odd factors a,b≈X^(1/3) with μ(a)=−μ(b) and distance ≤X^(1/12) pair coprime multiples in the full observable. At each center their mass is ≥X^(2/3−δ−o(1)) and their balance O(X^(5/12)) for δ≤1/16. Coverage of the rest and control of overlaps when combining families are missing.

213-348-A. [Disjoint pairing of a positive fraction in each window](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_348_A.md). Base factors with opposite signs and a single reserved prime among ≍log X scales give mass ≫H with total balance O(X^(7/16)log X)=o(√H), uniformly in the center for δ≤1/16. It surpasses the decreasing coverage of 347. The complement still lacks the necessary bound.

213-349-A. [Pairing in cells with sparse residue](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_349_A.md). A single mesh pairs mass ≫H at every center and all but O_A(H/log^A X) outside centers of proportion O_A(log^(−A)X). Pointwise balance of the pairs O(X^(9/20))=o(√H). It suffices to control the residual imbalances per cell in the second moment; the exceptional centers are not discarded.

213-350-A. [Almost total pairing without exceptional centers](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_350_A.md). In cells X^(2/3), the equidistribution of signs allows balancing the number and the first moment by deleting O_A(J/log^A X) samples. At each center the residual mass is O_A(H/log^A X) and the balance of the paired set O(1+X^(4/3)/H)=o(√H). The signed estimate of the residue persists.

213-351-A. [Residues at prescribed primes and cross criterion without diagonal](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_351_A.md). The deletions of 350 can be confined to qp and 2qp for each q=1 or odd prime ≤log^B X. Two choices give disjoint supports and approximate the same pulse with pointwise error o(√H). The upper bound of their cross correlation suffices; the selected subcollections still depend on μ.

213-352-A. [Counterproof for decorrelation by disjoint prime carriers](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_352_A.md). A sparse modification of signs at multiples of 1155 preserves all coefficients with up to three distinct primes and the cell estimates of 350. On the same carriers of 351 the correlation reaches H^(2−o(1)) in dyadic blocks. The model is not multiplicative and delimits the use of the disjunction.

213-353-A. [Contraction of prime powers in the critical local norm](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_353_A.md). In the exact identity μ log=−μ*Λ, the powers of exponent ≥2 cost at most (1/2+o(1)) of the normalized envelope after dividing by log X. Uniform absorption in 0<h≤1; the criterion remains in the signed term of simple primes. This remains open.

213-354-A. [Opposite means according to the primes of the cofactor](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_354_A.md). In the term of simple primes of 353, the y-smooth cofactors and their complement have means equivalent to ±e^(−γ)X(1−e^(−h))/log y, with log y=log X/(20 log log X). The compensation is unconditional for the linear mean; the second moment of the set is missing.

213-355-A. [Compensation of the smooth cofactors and their complement at each center](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_355_A.md). For h=X^(−δ), 0<δ≤1/16, both sectors of 354 are ±x(1−e^(−h))∏_{p≤y}(1−1/p)+O_A(H/log^A X) uniformly. The large smooth tail is detected by an intermediate divisor below H. Carrying the error to root scale remains pending.

213-356-A. [Optimal threshold for removing cofactors with large smooth divisor](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_356_A.md). With y=log^A X, 1<A≤2, the cofactors with squarefree y-smooth divisor ≥H^(A/2) cost in modulus O_ε(√H X^ε) for H≥1. A construction with products of primes proves that reducing that exponent exceeds the root in modulus already at h=1. The signed remainder remains open.

213-357-A. [Criterion with cofactors without any small prime](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_357_A.md). In 353 the term of simple primes with cofactor free of primes ≤y(X) suffices, for a single stepped threshold comparable to log²X. Exact reconstruction by Euler products, with depth bounded above X^κ. The signed bound of the sifted sector remains open.

213-358-A. [Reconstruction without cost per number of changes of the sieve](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_358_A.md). For every increasing sieve with Euler product X^o(1) at each σ>1/2 the bound of the single sifted observable at the corresponding scale suffices. The sequence of corrections is unique once the initial divisor and the total are fixed, with multiplicity ≤2^ω(D). It admits log^(2+o(1)) X without steps and additional sets of sparse primes.

213-359-A. [Criterion with the whole product free of small primes](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_359_A.md). The root bound suffices for the pairs pm without any prime ≤z in the full product, uniformly in log²Y≤z≤4log²Y. The small exterior primes are absorbed before inverting; the tail of long dilations pays its Euler cost. Signed bound of the remaining sector open.

213-360-A. [A linear measurement at fixed width for the sifted product](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_360_A.md). The pointwise root bound for a single fixed triangular window and the cuts of 359 suffices. The identity u w=ν*w keeps the logarithmic weight within the same observable at bounded cost; the multiplier W does not lose poles in Re s>1/2. Scalar bound pending.

213-361-A. [Amplification of the oscillation floor by the prime cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_361_A.md). For fixed z, each critical zero of multiplicity m forces both signs of Q_w at size √x(log x)^m with constant proportional to |E_z(ρ)|. The logarithm of that factor has asymptotic extremes ±√z/(|1−ρ|log z). The order of limits does not decide the moving cut of 360.

213-362-A. [Frequencies above log²x at cost below root](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_362_A.md). A causal weight with W(s)=exp(−√(1+s)) preserves the absorption of 360 and allows truncating the Mellin integral of the sifted product at |t|≤log²x with uniform absolute error O(x^(1−1/√2)log³x). The cancellation at growing heights within the band remains.

213-363-A. [Gaussian window with height √(2 log x)](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_363_A.md). A differential equation for the bilateral pulse and two envelopes preserve the doubly sifted criterion. In the new weight the Mellin tail beyond √(2 log x) costs O(log²x) uniformly. The interior root ceiling remains open.

213-364-A. [Diffusive Gaussian and exact parabolic region with moving sieve](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_364_A.md). For variance a log x and critical tilted weight, the uniform root bound is equivalent to excluding the zeros with β>1/2 and Re(ρ+a(ρ−1/2)²/2)>1/2. It holds at all scales if a≥1/((3·10¹²)²−1/4) by known verification. The family a→0 remains open.

213-365-A. [An exact moving cut and a single inequality](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_365_A.md). For z=(log x)², the parabolic exclusion of 364 is equivalent to Q_a(x)≤√x exp(2log x/loglog x) eventually. A forbidden zero forces both excursions in every sufficiently distant multiplicative block; the amplitudes are controlled without freezing the cut. The family a→0 remains.

213-366-A. [Positive bias and sign criterion without barrier](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_366_A.md). The real critical point s₀=1/2+(log 2+o(1))/log z produces an explicit positive principal term in Q_a under the parabolic exclusion, even with poles on its boundary. By 365, eventual positivity alone is equivalent to that exclusion. Sign proved in the verified range of a; a→0 is missing.

213-367-A. [A Gaussian of fixed width and only its sign](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_367_A.md). Eventual positivity of the fixed pulse exp(u/2)φ₁(u) for all log²x≤z≤4log²x is equivalent to RH. Under RH the Euler product damps the intermediate frequencies and leaves the saddle positive; conversely the Gaussian convolution transmits the sign to the diffusive pulses and contradicts the negative excursions. Unconditional sign of the fixed pulse open.

213-368-A. [A parity comparison at exact cut and fixed variance](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_368_A.md). RH is equivalent to the eventual negativity of the pulse of μ over numbers free of primes ≤(log x)², with weight exp(u/2)φ₁(u). No prime label nor corridor in the hypothesis: positive inversion extends the inequality and the diffusive average detects any exterior zero. The arithmetic inequality remains open.

213-369-A. [Unconditional odd dominance with growing number of layers](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_369_A.md). For the fixed pulse of 368, S^*(x;z)<0 uniformly in 2≤log x/log z≤(log x)^(1/4). The continuous model by number of primes has density ρ′(t)=−ρ(t−1)/t; a quantitative comparison by cells preserves the sign for the integers. Reaching z=(log x)² is missing.

213-370-A. [Unconditional saddle up to cuts exp(C(log log x)²)](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_370_A.md). PROVED, with [independent review](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/AUDIT_370_PHASE.md): S^*<0 and Q^*>0 uniformly in C(log log x)²≤log z≤(log x)^(3/4), with C an absolute sufficiently large constant. Antecedent: conditional saddle of 367 and layers of 369; difference: saddle α→1 inside the classical free region and phase loss at log p∈[log z−1/(1−α),log z]. What works: Euler damping and integration by parts of the PNT error; the cut z=(log x)² remains out of reach. Reopening: control the saddle outside that region or an arithmetic sign identity.

213, calibration of 366–368. [Saddle for z=(log x)^A at fixed A](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/SADDLE_FIXED_POWER_CALIBRATION.md). Abscissa 1−1/A+(log A+o(1))/log z and cost of the shift in a zero-free strip.

213-371-A. [Vinogradov–Korobov cut for the pulses of 370](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_371_A.md). PROVED, deduction and primary references independently reviewed in the file. Antecedent370; application of Ford's free region and of the PNT remainder for θ of Johnston–Yang to the phase audit: with h=log log x it suffices that log z≥C h^(5/3)(log h)^(1/3) up to the upper end of370, preserving S*<0 andQ*>0. What works: the contour margin and the oscillatory error exp(−ch); the target log z=2h remains out of reach. Reopening: an estimate of a different order or an arithmetic sign mechanism, not improving constants.

213-372-A. [Excursion exponents at the exact cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_372_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed in the file: if Θ>1/2, the positive and negative parts of the fixed pulse at z=(log x)² have limsup exponent Θ. Antecedents365/368; transfer of a one-sided ceiling by unique leaves and exponential moment of the diffusion, with exponentially small Gaussian tail. It works without reaching the supremum nor assuming simplicity; a one-sided arithmetic ceiling of exponent1/2+o(1) remains pending.

213-373-A. [Width of parity exceptions](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_373_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: if Θ>1/2 there are logarithmic intervals of length ≥exp(−ηv) of both signs at the exact cut. Antecedents368/372; derivative bound inside a cell and choice of the long side, valid even at a jump and forΘ=1. RH is equivalent to finiteness of both ∫S_+(x)x^(−3/2)dx and the measure of {S>0} with weight x^(ε−1), for each fixed ε>0. An arithmetic estimate of that measure remains open; divergence of the logarithmic measure is not deduced.

213-374-A. [Absolute cost of the layers at the exact cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_374_A.md). PROVED, packing and roundings independently reviewed: for k≥c log x/log log x, 0<c<1/2, the mass has limsup exponent1−c even when restricting one parity. The tail with c tending to1/2 costs at most x^(1/2+o(1)). Nearest antecedents293/356 (same binomial floor), here with logarithmic packing and primes above the cut; no exact internal antecedent was found. Removing it preserves the one-sided ceilings of exponent>1/2, not the pointwise sign; the cancellation of the remaining layers remains.

213-375-A. [Growing prefix with favorable sign](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_375_A.md). PROVED, multiplicities, tails and uniformity independently reviewed: at z=(log x)² the mass of k+1 factors exceeds twice that of k for1≤k≤c√log log x. Antecedent374; construction mqr per cofactor, multiplicity≤k(k+1) and gain≳h/k². The entire odd prefix is negative at the same scale. It can be omitted in a majorant, but the cancellation in the intermediate range up to374 remains open.

213-376-A. [Marking by log p/log n at the exact cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_376_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: k M_(k+1)≥(1−o(1))h M_k for k≤2h, h=log log x. Antecedent375; the prime moment J is preserved and a multiplicity is recovered by Σlog p/log n=1, with exclusions and tail uniform. The favorable odd prefix reaches(1−ε)h; the intermediate block remains and the guarantee is lost on exceeding k/h=1.

213-377-A. [The intermediate block necessarily compensates the prefix](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_377_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: at the exact cut its balance is positive≫x/log x at every large scale and recovers−P_j with relative error O(exp(−c log x/log log x)). Antecedents374–376 and classical free contour; complete bound S≪x exp(−c log x/log log x), without power saving. Paying that block alone at root level after omitting the favorable prefix is ruled out; reopening requires preserving its compensation or another grouping.

213-378-A. [Layer floors at every scale and multiplicity moments](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_378_A.md).
