Its multiplier ζ(1−ρ) also annihilates every exterior mode by the functional equation; the regularization is not an invertible detector of the sign.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: Z(Y)=O_δ(Y^(−1/2+δ)) withoutRH for0<δ<1/2. Trapezoidal correction−F(NY)/(2sqrt N), uniform Euler–Maclaurin and functional cancellation allow shifting without poles up to Re z=δ. Antecedents co-Poisson106.28(3)–(5),106.26(5a)–(6) and mirror199; application to the weight of073, not a new detection nor bound of the old carrier. All modes of zeros, also exterior ones, are annihilated, so it does not recoverF.

Extension 213-073-A. In Z at most the term −4(1−2^(1/6))Q(0)/√Y survives; the rest is O_A(Y^(−A)) for every fixed A. The trivial zeros of ζ(4z) and ζ(6z) cancel the other gamma poles. There is no need to assume RH nor to decide whether Q(0) vanishes.

Extension 213-073-A. For the original weight Q(0)>0 by monotonicity of the tilted mean and Arb bound reproducible at 128 bits. Thus Z(Y) is strictly positive for all sufficiently large Y, with explicit positive limit of √Y Z(Y). The regularization preserves this term of the weight and eliminates the modes of the zeros.

Extension 213-073-A. First variation by translation of the nodes of Z: B(Y)=Σn^(−3/2)V(nY), V=(Y∂Y−1/2)F. Absolutely convergent Möbius inversion by PNT and integration toward infinity recover F. A bilateral ceiling for B is equivalent to the sign. The bound of Z₀ does not control that variation.

Extension 213-073-A. Z_(−1/2)=√2 Z(Y/2)−Z(Y) is eventually positive; on omitting its first node exactly √2 F(Y/2) is subtracted. The mean over −1≤h≤0 is zero, so that at every large scale displacements of negative sign appear. Extending the entire sign to all translations is discarded; a floor for the incomplete half-lattice already requires the original ceiling.

Extension 213-073-A. Uniformly in 0≤θ≤1, Z_(−1+θ)(Y)/√Y=F(θY)/√(θY)+O(exp(−c√log Y)), with zero extension at θ=0. The logarithmic integral of the profile is zero by 072. Thus the normalized extremes converge to constants of opposite signs attained in the profile, and the first node explains the excursions of scale √Y.

Extension 213-073-A. The first-harmonic cosine average over a cell of translations has a constant bilateral ceiling exactly under RH. The identity with the cosine transform of F(v)/√v and the inversion against the Poisson kernel give the converse. The arithmetic ceiling for that coefficient is missing.

Cross-link 213-073, first harmonic and inversion. 2√Y A(Y)=Σ μ(k)S(Y/k), S(t)=√t Z(t), with S(t)→C₀>0 to every order and S(t)=O(t²) at zero. For k≤Y^(1−ε) there remains exactly C₀ M(⌊Y^(1−ε)⌋) up to superpolynomial error. It is a localization of the pending cancellation; no root ceiling for the set.

Extension 213-073-A. Ŝ(2n+1)=0 for n≥0 by the reciprocal gamma factor; S has both signs arbitrarily close to zero and there it is O_N(t^N). There remain C₀M(⌊Y^(1−ε)⌋) and the block Y^(1−ε)<k≤Y^(1+ε) with error O_A(Y^(−A)), even summing moduli in the high tail. Cancellations in the block and with the prefix are missing.

Cross-link 213-060/073/074. PROVED, independently reviewed: a one-sided ceiling of the finite balance prefix plus block at Y=j^d for any fixed d>0 already implies RH. The first interpolation excludes a strip and improves the bound of the second derivative for the next one; b passes to max(1/2,b−1/d). Iterated Landau preserves orientation without initial lower bound. No uniformity in d nor proof of the arithmetic ceiling of the samples.

Cross-link 213-073/074. PROVED, independently reviewed: the one-sided ceiling Σ_(j≤N)D(j^d)≤C_d N^(1+d/2) for a fixed d>0 suffices. Euler–Maclaurin leaves an integer difference and the change of scale is D̂((w−1)/d)/d; the poles pass to 1+dρ and Landau is applied to the accumulated prefixes. It requires no ceiling per sample; the accumulated estimate is not proved. Partial antecedents 038/060/074 and Euler–Maclaurin of 159; no exact duplicate of the accumulated criterion found.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: in square samples the zero of ζ(4z) at z=−1/2 gives ∫[S(u²)−C₀]du=0. For K=⌊N^(2−ε)⌋ the contribution k≤K to the signed average is C₀(N+1/2)M(K)+c_*+O_B(N^(−B)); Poisson and two fast tails. The average leaves intact the need for compensation with the remaining cofactors.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: two averages at N and ⌊N/2⌋ with the same cut K and quotient of corrected lengths cancel the term M(K) exactly. By positive iteration a ceiling O(N²) exclusively on N^(2−ε)<k≤N^(2+ε) suffices. On a subinterval k≈N² an absolute cost ≫N³ is proved, so that the estimate demands signed cancellation of a factor at least N.

Cross-link 213-073, continuous profile of the central block. PROVED, independently reviewed: the signed error on replacing the two square averages by their integrals is o(N²) without RH using M(x)=o(x), also for the logarithmic derivative of D. The remaining multiplier is (1−4^(−s))/(1+2s), nonzero for Re s>1/2. The discretization is discarded as the source of the pending saving.

Cross-check 213-049/073 and NO-GO of class 104_93. In the bilinear reduction of the weight L, the two terms with small factors have superpolynomially small absolute cost by Poisson. The diagonal costs O(√X) and has asymptotics with error O(X^(1/4)); ∫T=0 forces both signs of the kernel. The signed sum over distinct pairs remains, without reopening the factorization as a new mechanism.

Cross-link 213-059/060/073. In the contrast B(X)−2B(X/4) the density vanishes for each reduced ratio a/b. The aggregate cost for ratios with reduced product ≤X^η is o(√X) for η<1/3 by the uniform count of coprime squarefree numbers. Application to the new representative of a known technique; crossings of large reduced product remain.

Improvement 213-060/073. PROVED, independently reviewed: the ζ(4w) inherited in Q cancels exactly the denominator of the count of squarefree numbers at each ratio, including its possible poles at quarters of zeros. The contrast eliminates ζ(2w) at 1/2; the other positive poles are removable. With δ>η/2 the omitted cut in g costs less than any inverse power. For the same contrast every r≤X^η with η<1/2 is removed at cost o(√X), improving the previous 1/3. Direct antecedent 060, «What happens on a slope», which gets closer to root for another representative; it is not a new mechanism nor does it include η=1/2.

Extension 213-060/073. PROVED, independently reviewed: an additional difference eliminates the pole −1/2 of the common factor of the ratios. For r≤X^(1−ε) and r p_min(r)²≥X^(1+ε) there is a scale jump between d=1 and the corrections d>1: superpolynomially small cost even for some ratios r>√X. It gives no uniform threshold by size.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: for 0<α<1/4, boxes of ratios p/q with p≈X^α and q≈X^(1−3α) isolate the correction d=p, with uniform balance −f(X/(p³q)). Boxes of both signs reach ≫X^(1−2α)/(log X)². The decomposition into independent boxes fails at root scale even after summing with sign inside each box.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: in the whole band q=X^(1−3α±κ) of the resonance p³q, with X^α≤p≤2X^α, the oriented balance is asymptotic to 3f̂′(1)X^(1−2α)/(8α(1−3α)² log³X), strictly negative. PNT expansion with vanishing first moment and sign certified by Q′(1)>0. It is a one-sided sign of a band, without control of the complement.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: for p≈X^α fixed in scale and β_h=1−(2h+1)α>hα, the band p^(2h+1)q has sign (−1)^h and explicit asymptotic magnitude of order X^(1−2hα)/log³X. In every admissible finite initial family the first negative band absorbs the positive ones. No uniform control in α, h nor of the remaining families.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: with p≈X^α, 0<α<1/2, summing all oriented ratios p/q, q prime larger than p, gives positive balance ∼−f̂′(1)log(2)X/[α(1−α)² log³X]. All d>1 together admit power saving relative to X. The complement has the opposite equivalent by PNT; the cancellation down to root is open.

Cross-link 213-069/073. PROVED, independently reviewed: Σ_(p≈X^α)|row_p(B₁)|≪X^(α+(1−α)σ) for each small σ>0 and α<1/2. The positive contribution of q>p of size X/log³X is compensated down to o(√X) within the same rows upon including the rest of the denominators. The factorization of 069 is used after justifying the cut; it does not control critical rows.

Cross-link 213-069/073. PROVED, independently reviewed: for 0<a<1/2<b<1, all complete rows with prime numerator between X^a and X^b cost in moduli ∼(2√X/log X)∫|K(1/v²)|dv. K̂ is entire; the shifted periodic coefficients isolate X/p² with aggregate error o(√X/log X). The factor 2 comes from log(√X)=log X/2 and the cut is uniform if b+2κ<1. The root transition costs o(√X); it does not include composite numerators.

Cross-link 213-069/072/073. PROVED, independently reviewed: with semiprime numerator pq, p≈X^α, q≈X^(1−2α), the complete row isolates K(X/(p²q)) with sign +. A box of those rows costs ≫X^(1−α)/log²X in moduli. The widened band has negative signed balance ∼K̂''(1)X^(1−α)/(2α(1−2α)³log⁴X), without additional factorial in the second moment. The extension to all composites of the bound by moduli of prime rows is refuted.

Cross-link 213-069/070/073. PROVED, independently reviewed: in X^0.49≤m≤√(X log X) the complete rows with all primes ≥X^(1/L), L=⌊log log X/10⌋, cost o(√X) in moduli, without fixing ω(m). Each row costs O(2^(3L)) with uniform geometric tail and Chebyshev–Mertens counts O(ML/log X) numerators; the logarithmic exponent is −1/2+3log(2)/10<0. It does not include the part with small factors nor all supercritical numerators.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: in the transition up to √(X log X), admitting an arbitrary small prime keeps the cost of rows o(√X) on summing geometrically all its powers, with uniform majorant min(1,u²). Also h−1 intermediate primes fit under the explicit budget (h−1)θ<1/2−3log(2)/10. This elementary argument does not cover two fixed small primes simultaneously.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: the transition rows with primes in E fixed or ≥y cost o(√X) for the original B₁. The simple imaginary poles of distinct primes are separated polynomially by Matveev, §2, Theorem 2.1/Corollary 2.3 (primary reference verified), allowing absolute summation of the residues and shifting up to Re w=−1. The majorant min(1,t²) preserves the uniform count. It includes the case 6n; no uniformity for growing E.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: the weight of 047 gives decay exp(−c√height) and quantitative Matveev allows cost exp(CP log⁴(2P)) simultaneous for all subsets of primes ≤P. The sum of residues has logarithm O(Alog A+Aloglog(2P)), A=O(Plog²(2P)). With P=√log log X the cost is (log X)^o(1), absorbed by the fixed transition margin, without fixing the small primes beforehand. The intermediate strip P<p<y remains excluded; no numerical threshold for X.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED the cost of poles ≤exp(C(2+log b)²log(4+2log b)) for the divisors of b. The exception of a completely arbitrary prime remains OPEN in the intermediate interval: K_J has only the majorant min(1,u²), and summing its powers may cost 1+log_+(u)/log ℓ. The corrected extremes are reviewed below; the unrestricted arithmetic conclusion is not declared false.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: in all critical rows simultaneously, the local sector with each exponent ≥2 costs O(√X) in moduli of terms and o(√X) with sign. Unique decomposition n=b²h with h of exponents ≥4 (c₃=0), sign μ(b), absolute convergence in h and coprime Möbius PNT for b uniform at the variable endpoints of the interval. The sector with some exponent one remains; it is not a bound of moduli of entire rows.

Extension 213-073-A. PROVED, independently reviewed: in all critical rows, the sector with product of primes of exponent one ≤exp(c√log X) costs O(√X exp(−c′√log X)) with sign. Uniform coprime inversion in Q=ah≤X^0.11, quantitative PNT in b, tail h>X^0.1 with saving X^(−1/80) and choice of small c. It is not an absolute bound nor does it cover linear products of size a power of X.

213-073-A. [Corrected scope of the additional prime](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: with H=log log X and log b≤H^ν (0<ν<1/2), cost o(√X) for log ℓ≤H^κ (0<κ<1/2), incorporating it in J, or log ℓ≥(log X)^(1−θ) (0<θ<1/2−3log(2)/10), paying (log X)^θ. Counts and constants preserve the logarithmic margin. The intermediate interval remains pending.

213-073-A. [Pairwise budget for the largest prime](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: the stretch log ℓ≤H^κ reaches κ<1−ν. The exponent contains only pairs of distinct primes: O(B(B+D)), without D², and there are O(B+D) poles per unit interval. The cost exp(CB(B+D)log(2+B+D)) is exp(o(H)); counts and weights preserve the saving. Refinement of the same argument, without endpoint κ=1−ν nor closure of the intermediate interval.

213-073-A. [Average over phase intervals](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for log b≤H^ν, ν<1/2, finite periodic sum before moduli and absolutely summable residues. Brun–Titchmarsh lowers the lower limit of the large endpoint to (log X)^4; intervals of length ≥√P. Primary source Montgomery–Vaughan1973, Theorem2, (1.12), verified. Reciprocal average exp(o(H)), without cancellation between ℓ.

213-073-A. [Integer count in phase intervals](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: between exp(αH) and exp(4H) the discrete cost N/P is summed geometrically and exp((max(0,1−α)+o(1))H) remains. The margin λ=1/2−3log(2)/10 absorbs it for α>1−λ. It does not include equality nor prove an arithmetic obstruction below.

213-073-A. [Average of the number of large vectors](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: the marking weighted by (√L)^ω replaces 2^(3L) by exp(o(H)) after summing rows; a single factor w and Euler ∏(1+w/p). exp(−H) is recovered from the marking. Every additional prime is controlled under m≤√X/(log X)^ε, ε>0 fixed; for ℓ≥(log X)^α, α>1/2 suffices in the complete strip. log b≤H^ν is preserved; no equality cases.

213-073-A. [Crossing of √X with free additional prime](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for ν<1/3 and max(1/2,2ν)<κ<1−ν, all sizes of ℓ are covered up to m=√X exp(ηH^κ), 0<η<1, log b≤H^ν. The term N/P₀ and the marking leave −(1−η)H^κ; the losses O(H^(2ν)log H+√Hlog H) are smaller. No endpoints nor elimination of the budget of b.

213-073-A. [Common exceptional list up to the complete ceiling](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for log b≤H^ν, 0<ν<1/2, the pending additional prime is reduced to an explicit list common to all b, of size exp(O(H/log H)) and reciprocal mass ≤exp(−H^κ+O(H^ν+log H)), ν<κ<1−ν. Outside it, δ^(−1) and N/U leave margin −H/log H that dominates the losses. The contribution of the list is not estimated nor is it proved to be empty.

213-073-A. [Uniqueness of the resonant prime](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: eliminating log ℓ forces a form in log p,log q smaller than the Matveev separation for distinct primes; for the same prime an integer of modulus<1 remains. Each ℓ has a unique prime witness and reduced ratio. The characters exp(±iπj/3) retain only classes 6ℤ±1, with numerator and denominator coprime to six. The remainder costs C/δ uniformly; the retained sum remains open.

213-073-A. [Payment for the integer difference of powers](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: in exceptional pairs, with ratio a/d and g=|ℓ^d−p^a|, ℓ^(d−1)/g≤exp((1/2−ε)H), 0<ε<1/2, are absorbed. The weight 1/ℓ gains exactly one power; all multiples are paid with the absolute sum of residues, without extra multiplicity. It includes d=1; denominators ≥5 remain without sufficient bound of g.

213-073-A. [Separation in a class of numerators](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: among the unpaid pairs there are at most two candidates per p,d,a mod d for ε fixed in (0,1/4). The absolute approximation is uniform in d, and scaling by an integer power of p forces separation. Summing d classes up to d≪H^(4+ν) gives O(exp(H^ν)H^(8+2ν)) pairs, with logarithm ≤H^ν+O(log H). Their weighted cost remains pending.

213-073-A. [Asymptotic extinction for fixed p and d](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for ε,p,d fixed, the unpaid condition gives |p^(r/d)−ℓ/p^t|<q^(−1−c). Ridout with S={p} and p-adic factor q⁻¹ makes those fractions finite; specialized formulation cross-checked in Bugeaud2011, p37, (2.2). Simultaneous extinction for every fixed finite catalog, without uniformity for growing catalogs nor effective threshold.

213-073-A. [Separation exponent independent of X](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: the minimum between length and geometric bound, after the weight 1/ℓ, pays |ℓ^d−p^a|≥ℓ^(d−2+σ), 0<σ<1 fixed. The crossing ℓ=exp(H/(2−σ)) gives relative saving exp(−σH/(2(2−σ))+o(H)); all remaining factors are exp(o(H)). At σ=0 the maximization gives no strict saving, with no arithmetic conclusion about the survivors.

213-073-A. [Exact threshold for high-frequency denominators](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: if d/log p≥H^β, max(1,4ν)<β<2, reserving an exponential mean of each residue extracts exp(−c₂√(d/log p)) without changing the order of the gamma budget. It recovers σ=0 and even allows separation g≥ℓ^(d−2)exp(−c₁√(d/log p)). The geometric mean cancels the marking and leaves dominant frequency saving; it does not cover low frequency nor remove the budget of b.

213-073-A. [Obstruction to the critical separation without cut](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for each prime pair p<ℓ there are reduced exponents coprime to six with |ℓ^d−p^a|/ℓ^(d−2)→0. Two unimodular convergents give coordinates1 mod6 and gcd≤6, preserving the units on reducing and d→∞. It refutes only the universal gap without cut; it does not contradict Ridout with d fixed nor construct survivors of the list X/height.

213-073-A. [Uniqueness on gathering all scales](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_073_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: A≤H≤A^(1/κ) puts all witnesses in a polynomial budget in A. For large ℓ and given p at most one ratio enters, a convergent by Legendre; the next denominator exceeds ℓ^(1/3)−d. If κ>2ν, Matveev also makes p unique between scales. It does not estimate the single possible contribution.

213-195-A. [Persistent detection by subblocks](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: if the reciprocal mass above each fixed threshold diverges, minimal rates R_j→∞ with mass in [S,S+1/R_j] are selected. A negative physical test forces negative margin in all late blocks, even after omitting bounded reciprocal mass. Corollary of 087/195 and of the confluent antecedent014; it does not construct the required subsequence of floors.

213-195-A. [Two directions per exterior quartet](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: Cardinal values of ξ and physical cut justify 2k negative directions for k distinct quartets, with persistence in subblocks and criterion by second eigenvalue. Direct antecedent phase21, Theorem21-A.1; the independence step previously objected to in V.2 is completed here, without a new counting principle.

213-195-A. [Amplification by opposite translations](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: Preserving the cardinal values and reducing their norms forces λ_(2k)→−∞ in every family of divergent tails. Order R, cut and recovery; a fixed finite floor of λ₂ along a subsequence suffices for the sign. Antecedent R162_504 concerns another form without polar; the floor remains pending.

213-195-A. [Simultaneous physical rate for 2k directions](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: R=(1−η)T and uniform cut leave liminf log(1+(−λ_(2k))_+)/(2T)≥b. The error is summed over cardinal values zero/one, without spurious growth of the strip. First liminf, then η↓0; no rate in the index of blocks.

213-195-A. [Exact rates for finite exterior divisor](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: Conditional on exactly k quartets, the rates are b₁,b₁,…,b_k,b_k and λ_(2k+1)≥0; eventual index2k. Two continuous evaluation differences per quartet, codimension and form kernel justify min-max.

213-195-A. [Finite-rank model with bounded additive error](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: Conditional on the finite exterior catalog, 0≤λ_i(W_T)−β_i(B_T)≤C for i≤2k. Scaled Gram of endpoints uniformly nondegenerate; bounded positive critical contribution only in V_T. Weil extends to truncated exponentials by mollification in logarithmic domain. It does not localize unknown quartets.

213-195-A. [Negative product without oscillating phases](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for finite exterior catalog, the relative Gram comparison controls the pencils even with distinct rates. The normalized negative product tends to det(C)∏μ_j, without phases; the additive error O(1) is relative o(1). For one quartet the constant is μ²γ²/[4b²(b²+γ²)] with exp(−4bT).

213-195-A. [Second eigenvalue of the centered prime band](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: in N=ceil(T³) complete Dirichlet modes, the positive part of the second largest eigenvalue of K has rate Δ with normalization1/(2T), without finite catalog. 117/119/121 extend to both parities; two cardinals smoothed by Gevrey have tail H¹ exp(−cT^(4/3)) that absorbs the physical cost. The comparison transfers two directions; the subsequential arithmetic ceiling is missing.

213-195-A. [Band by halves and minors of order two](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for a>1/2, K=[[0,C],[C,0]] with prefactor2/T and divided differences, diagonal −F′. Central cut before separating and convolving preserves two directions and the rate of s₂(C). The maximal2×2 minor relative to M=max|C_ij| satisfies s₂/N≤L≤Ns₂ and detects Δ in rate. The arithmetic bound is missing; no matrix monotonicity assumed.

213-195-A. [Linear certificate for relative minors](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: the adjacent and diagonal secants give global M. If D<M/2, s₂≥3M/8; in the other branch the residue satisfies the identity of two determinants and s₂≤2N³E, E≤2Ns₂. The weights of C are polynomial and preserve the rate Δ. O(N) operations on already sampled F,F′; neither their cost of obtention nor the arithmetic sign is bounded.

213-195-A. [Cross matrix of all primes without reference integral](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: one moment per half annihilates exp(T)hhᵗ exactly. The operator −∂²+1/4, cut with four derivatives and moment correction with positive first sine preserve two directions in rangeP⊕P. The centered low band is an error of lower rate; s₂(PBP) detects Δ with positive prime weights, without finite catalog. Its subsequential arithmetic ceiling is missing.

213-195-A. [Smallest eigenvalue of the raw prime block](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: the odd reflection gives pattern1,−1,−1,1 and W negative. On(v,−v), K has quotient −⟨Cv,v⟩/||v||², forcing C and B negative with rate Δ; v⊥h annihilates the density. The positive density and ||C|| give the ceiling without compression. Criterion of primes only, without projection nor subtraction in the statement; its arithmetic bound is missing.

213-195-A. [Uniform floor for small divisors of the raw block](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: in Λ=−(μ log)*1, the d≤D contribute e^T c_D hhᵗ with c_D→1>0 and error O((1+N/T)√Dlog(2D)). Quadrature without jumps, ordinary convergence by PNT and (1/ζ)'(1)=1 verified. Subexponential floor for logD=o(T), D→∞, bilateral on h⊥. Outside h⊥ removing the positive principal term only preserves sufficiency; the tail d>D remains open.

213-195-A. [Edge localization and divisors up to X^(1−ε)](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for support(0,θT), θ<ε, the error has exponent(1−θ)/2−r(ε−θ)<0 and principal term zero by the moment. Witnesses in exterior bands keep W≤−c, normH^r exponentially small and interior combs negligible. The odd crossing enters with +2; a uniform subexponential floor for the tail m<X^ε suffices. Sufficiency, without estimate of that tail.

213-195-A. [Cofactors up to T^16](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: theta and the successive annihilations preserve double exponential tails in the cardinals. Support margin and fixed bump give G_L(v)≤Ce^(−bR). Poisson of order floorT costs(C_Lr³)^r; with D/Y=T⁻⁸ it leaves logerror≤T−5rlogT+O_L(r+logT). Sufficient criterion of uniform Gevrey floor for the tail m<T^16; the tail d almost X is not estimated.

213-195-A. [A single Möbius form for all cofactors](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: the tail is Σ_(m<T^16)m^(−1/2)Q_T(S_(log m/2)v), with moment multiplied by m^(−1/4), Gevrey norm invariant and support<12logT. Under RH the partial summation includes the edge M(D)f(D), uniformly bounded by the same budget. The uniform subexponential floor is equivalent to the sign; a root Mertens bound to prove it would be circular. No new cancellation of μ is proved.

213-195-A. [Semiprime obstruction with a fixed factor](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: in Q_T, prime q and zero-moment test fixed with M₁≠0 give sector d=qp∼−(2log q/q)M₁²√X/(log(X/q))³. Sign μ(qp)=+1, second moment2M₁² and Jacobian1/q verified. PNT error O_(q,w)(√Xexp(−c√logX)) smaller than the logarithmic remainder. It refutes only floors by sectors; not the total nor a bound uniform in growing q.

213-195-A. [Compensation between a cofactor up to X^δ and its complement](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: for w and δ<1/2 fixed, p≈X/h>h makes the representation unique and the PNT error uniform √X/h·poly(logX)e^(−cδ√logX). Abel with A(t)→−1 gives −J(logX), then principal −2M₁²√X/log³X and the opposite in the complement. The fixed total costs √Xe^(−c′√logX), without uniformity in the class nor sufficient scale for the sign.

213-195-A. [Common compensator of squares for variable functions](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: in support(0,8logT), zero moment, the sectors are −P_X and +P_X with error O_δ(√Xe^(−cδ√logX)||w||²H¹), uniform in w. Abel gives A_V≤−1/2 on t≤ε_δ/√V; absolutely interchangeable Laplace produces the same P_X≥0. The support avoids D; it is not extended without proof to12logT nor reaches the sign scale.

213-195-A. [Edge obstruction of the compensator](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: cut x<0 after centering at8logT gives Q_S∼−J₀√X/(T⁸logX), with J₀=±1 in the two tests. Bumps and norms verified; m=floor(T^16e^(−4)) realizes the discrete translation with errorO(T⁻¹⁶). It refutes extending that PSD compensator and error to support12logT; not the case8logT nor the totalQ_T.

213-195-A. [Edge obstruction to corrections of fixed rank](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: symmetric J changes sign under reflection; J(g_i,g_j′)=+δ_ij and g_i±g_i′ give ±2I. Support and discrete translation preserve the tests; polarization gives n directions per sign at scale√X/(T⁸V). A corrector of fixed rank has kernel in the space of the sign opposite to the approximant, leaving error of that scale. No uniformity in n nor NO-GO for growing rank or the total.

213-195-A. [Compensator after gathering the cofactors](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: Poisson for K has integral zero and pays the tail with exp(−2TlogT). The continued transform is ζ(1−t)M_v(t)², removable pole and value0 at t=0. Since A_V and ζ(1−t) are negative, gathered S has positive compensator; truncated K has polynomial C¹ boundssufficient for uniform PNT in G_L². Error still exponential in T; no individual sign is assigned to the translates.

213-195-A. [Moments and sign of the gathered complement](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: initial moment j gives opposite principal terms ±√X(2j−1)!M_j²/((j!)²log^(2j)X). TotalΛ has density0 and smaller PNT error. In v_j=e^(u/2)φ^(j), the monomial Gram with dt/t gives an r-plane of complement≤−c_r√Xlog^(−2r)X||v||²H¹, uniform on its sphere. It discards separate floors and exclusions of fixed dimension, without uniformity in r nor failure of the total.

213-195-A. [Loss of sensitivity on paying the compensator](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: P*≤exp(o(T)) and normL²≤1 give RMS e^(−T/2+o(T)) at t≈V^(−1/2). Taylor and Legendre cost respectively e^(−T/3+o(T)) and e^(T/6+o(T)), giving |M_T(z)|≤e^(−T/3+o_z(T)). The extreme amplification does not recover fixed evaluation for |Rew|<1/3; only an obstacle to paying P* in isolation.

213-195-A. [Optimality of the exponent 1/3 for isolated evaluation](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: binomial differences and modulated bump preserve anL² floor by Fourier atπn. After normalizing, P*≤exp(o(T)) and log|M_T(z)|=−T/3+o(T), for z≠0 fixed. Gevrey costs≤e^(C√n) and does not change the rate. Isolated optimality, without conclusion on global sign.

213-195-A. [Packets by cofactor of the product](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: extending the divisors before separating pays the complete aggregate by quadrature. In n=pr, p>√X unique, the packet r≤X^δ has coefficient−Λ(r) and balance−M₁²((1−δ)⁻²−1)√X/log²X; the exterior gives+M₁²(1−δ)⁻². Constants verified by Abel. The packets are not transported separately to the original cut d>D.

213-195-A. [Prime cut at √X and comparable strip](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: fixed test gives−3,+4 in unitsM₁²√X/log²X. The double PNT uses dp/logp and dr; the exact logarithm and the second moment2M₁² give+4. Error√Xe^(−c√V); proper powersO(X^(1/4)polyV). Distinct semiprimes produce the comparable; extended packets, without control of the global remainder.

213-195-A. [Pointwise cancellation in the comparable strip](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: Frullani gives+exp(Rt)/t and the interior−ΣΛ(r)r^(t−1). Abel, including edgesE(0)=−C, leaves1/t−C+O(t+e^(−c√V)) on t≤c₁/√V. B=8logT only adds absorbable powers in the uniform PNTH¹; V−R−B=V/2 pays the tail. Extended representation, without separate transport to the original cut nor sufficient sign scale.

213-195-A. [Exact closure of the partition by √X](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). PROVED, independently reviewed: complementary coefficientΛ(n_s) cancels the mixed products pointwise. Both sectors reconstructΛ; SUBTRACTING the powers returns the primes. Proper powers=(∫v)²/2+O(e^(−c√V)||v||²H¹), uniform in width4logT: squares by θ with error without√X, exponents≥3 by poly(T)X^(−1/6). The prime sum remains open; no new autonomous separation.

213-195-A. [Fixed autoconvolution test with square bias](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). In a fixed proportional prime band, a generic zero-moment Gevrey test gives B_X≤−1/16 eventually under RH and excursions of both signs if it fails. The −1/8 comes from the squares. Antecedents 104/115. PROVED, independently reviewed: generic choice outside countable sets, contour at a−1 and bias−1/8; eventual equivalence, without arithmetic proof of the ceiling.

213-195-A. [Explicit eight-box test](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). Piecewise polynomial weight supported on [0,16], known transform without exterior zeros, sum of moduli on the axis <1/32. The eventual prime ceiling −1/16 is equivalent to the global sign. Without generic selection of parameters. PROVED, independently reviewed: prefactor2⁸·7!, k∈C⁴ and decayτ⁻⁶; budget202/(4·9⁴)<1/32. Only annihilated critical zeros are omitted, never exterior ones.

213-195-A. [Unconditional interval of the eight-box test](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). With Z1–Z3 one obtains B_X<−1/16 for all 200≤log X≤230 by inversion of powers and explicit control of the tail |γ|>3·10¹². PROVED, independently reviewed: constant65536 verified and ALL additional errors together<1/1000 (principal high tail<0.000279). Scale of a single test; no new global data window.

213-195-A. [Moving test at all scales and loss of detection](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). For m=ceil(log X/8) boxes per factor, the prime sum is −1/8+O(X^(−1/20)) unconditionally. PROVED, independently reviewed: norms uniform in m, reserve of eight factors and tail of powersO(V³e⁻ⱽ⁄¹²) give the errorX⁻¹⁄²⁰. The filter also suppresses every possible exterior zero; the global ceiling for a fixed test is not deduced.

213-195-A. [Sublinear smoothing by blocks that preserves detection](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). Order m_l→∞, m_l=o(2^l), frozen on 2^l≤log X<2^(l+1). Under RH the sum tends to −1/8; if it fails, in each late block it has excursions of both signs for every exponent η<Δ. PROVED, independently reviewed: localizer115 with rates, maximizer and fixed gap; sum of coefficients uniformly bounded and selected coefficient≥exp(−o(2^l)). Only the frozen order is prolonged; strict margin absorbs O(1). No extension to variable orders within the block.

213-195-A. [Slope threshold in short windows](../03-research/phase-213-new-constructions/ROUND_195_A.md). Order m=ceil(αH) fixed in H≤log X≤H+2√H. The critical slope is max Re z/(−2log|U(z)|) over right exterior zeros; the test converges to −1/8 above it and has both signs without bound below it and even at positive equality. PROVED, independently reviewed: uniform reserve of eight factors, fixed gap and bounded rounding; ties reduce to the largest b and a finite Gram controls all phases. At F=0 the displacement+√H contributes exp(B√H). All slopes give equivalence, without arithmetic estimate of the threshold.

- Phase 213, ROUND_195_A, «Fixed frequency per block and single slope 1/8». Modulation before the polar derivative. A fixed rational frequency would exponentially detect any suitably tuned exterior zero. Under RH there is a bound per frequency. Argument in the note; the direct subexponential bound over primes is pending. Antecedents: the average of 115 and the unmodulated threshold of 195_A.

- ROUND_195_A, «Arithmetic cut above the root»: in the modulated test of slope 1/8 the part d≤exp(0.55H) of Λ=−(μ log)*1 decreases exponentially for each fixed frequency, using fourth-order quadrature and the exact exponential moment of the boxes. PROVED, independently checked: full integral zero, Euler–Maclaurin on all of R even if the support drops below 1, factor d³exp(−7V/2) and sum D⁴logD. The box moment gives c=0.0367056117…>0 uniformly in the window. Antecedent: small divisors of the raw block; bound for the long stretch pending.
- ROUND_195_A, upper end: absolute exponential bound for any subfamily of pairs dl≥exp(0.98H) of the modulated test, by tilting of the boxes. Together with the lower cut there remains the arithmetic problem d>exp(0.55H), dl<exp(0.98H), l<exp(0.43H). PROVED, independently checked: tilted Young and absolute sum of pairs give rate 0.7−log20/4<−0.048; margin −0.04H uniform. Remove the small divisor before cutting the product. No new window T.
- ROUND_195_A, bilinear reduction of the modulated test: the two null moments and the quadrature eliminate both Vaughan type-I terms with exponential error. What remains is a sum with r,q between exp(0.275H) and exp(0.705H), rq<exp(0.98H), coefficients A_Y(r)Λ(q). PROVED, independently checked: exact identity and signs, logarithmic integral null because L_k(1/2)=L_k′(1/2)=0, and triple tail ≤√X·poly(V) absorbed by tilting. Does not recur as a sign proof by sieve; the type-II estimate remains open.
- ROUND_195_A, asymmetric cut a=δ₁: cofactor coefficient exactly −1 and stretch n≤exp(0.55H) absolutely exponentially small. Gathering all cofactors reproduces 1*Λ=log; inverting this sum coincides with the renewal d_125 (already recorded). Discarded as an autonomous route; the symmetric correlation remains pending.
- ROUND_195_A, semiprimes of the moving symmetric remainder at zero frequency: explicit positive main term of rate 1/2+log(1−1/e)/4, compensated by the complement. Antecedents 066/067 and prime cut with fixed test in 195_A. PROVED, independently checked: ordered pairs without factor 1/2, uniform double PNT preserving U(1/2)^{2m}, absolutely small negative atom and dominated expectation give the constant (1−.275−ν/4)⁻². The linear slope does not suppress the cancellation between sectors; reach τ=0.
- ROUND_195_A, centering of the long factor Λ: in the symmetric reduction for any fixed τ one can subtract dq on q>Y with exponential error. PROVED, independently checked: positive edge √Y·Dh, identity A_Y=δ₁−μ≤Y*1 and remaining moment give error with factor exp(−7V/2)Y⁸U(−7/2)^{2m}. Cut after centering. Pending: estimate the remaining prime discrepancy.
- ROUND_195_A, response of the centered remainder to q^{s−1}dq: exact multiplier 1−ζ(s)M_Y(s) plus exponential error in the sum. The constant density is eliminated, but each power associated with a zero passes with multiplier 1 whatever the polynomial. PROVED, independently checked: contour at a−3 with eight boxes gives integrability t⁻⁷⁄² and error with the same c>0; pole at 1 removable and unique residue w=s. Individual response, without interchange of the error with an infinite sum of zeros. Do not pursue attenuation by changing only that polynomial.
- Update 213-193-A. The certificate verify_193.py passes the fifteen checks with T=5539/2000=2.7695 and the other original constants. Floor of the full form exp(−85000000001) by inclusion of supports under the same inputs Z1–Z3. Extension by margin already available.
- 213-193-A, norm barrier at fixed G: the constant test gives ||C||>26.349 for U≥3.3 with only q≤700, while log(R/(2π))<25.506 since 2R<H. verify_193_barrier.py reproduces both bounds. With variable G this comparison requires at least double-exponential growth in U. Sign of the form outside the certified window OPEN.

What is specific to 193 is the certified finite threshold U≥3.3 for the current verifier. Do not reopen that separation as a new route.
- ROUND_193_A, positive and negative parts of the symbol over a fixed datum: both integrals have the same equivalent of order exp(U), with explicit constant weighted by (1+4τ²)^(−1/2); their difference is already constant. PROVED, independently checked: amplitude 4 and mean 1/π, tails by logarithmic domain and signed difference constant. Quantification for a fixed profile of the P46 obstacle prop:negtrace/thm:nolocal, distinct from the essential edge of 081; no uniformity over moving profiles.
- ROUND_193_A, negative-mass criterion with a single fixed triangular profile for the compensated symbol of 121: subexponential growth in V=2U is equivalent to RH; under RH the mass is O((1+V)³). PROVED, independently checked: demodulating in V recovers exactly the causal convolution; Re(zK)>0 prevents hiding right-hand zeros. Polar rational and Fourier factors verified. Does not imply sign for the fixed datum; direct arithmetic bound on the negative mass pending.
- ROUND_193_A, unconditional trimming of the centered criterion with fixed profile: boxes of radii 1/[j(1+log j)²] preserve the causal mean without zeros; the mass outside 2⌈V⌉(1+log⌈V⌉)² decreases exponentially. PROVED, independently checked: fixed support, uniform limit of densities, K without zeros and tail 4^{1−N}/τ². An interior estimate suffices, still open.
- 213-193-A, mesh audit of the centered criterion: alternating sum of discrepancies reconstructs 2J(V) by periodization; in a bound by discrete negative masses k=0 already requires Landau's one-sided criterion (104/106/107). PROVED, independently checked: factor 2 from the two aliases of the edge, exponential tails and O(V²log²V) samples. Discard that sampling as a simplification of the global proof. Earlier geometry P46 thm:nyq.
- ROUND_193_A, continuous edge 0≤τ≤π/V: outside RH the exponentially weighted near-maxima of |d_V(0)| force a negative exponential contribution integrated over an interval of length π/(3V), by Stieltjes parts. Under RH the integral is O((1+V)²). PROVED, independently checked: selection of near-maxima valid with jumps, uniform error 2π|D(V)|/(εV), and lower bound π|D(V)|/(12V). Equivalence with RH, not a new arithmetic bound; the integral of the atom 0 is not inferred.
- ROUND_193_A, quantitative inversion of the band 0≤τ≤π/V by polynomial records: for each p>1, I(V)=O(V^{p−1}) ⇔ D(V)=O(V^p), which implies ψ(x)−x=O(√x(log x)^p). The margin in π depends on π∫s^p sin(πs)ds<1. Does not prove any of those estimates for the primes. Review pending.
- 213-193-A, adjustment of the rate under RH: the primitive of the normalized error of ψ is O(1) by absolutely summable residues. One recovers D(V)=O(V²) and I(V)=O(V); the linear rate is equivalent to RH. Use of integrated explicit formula, antecedent 092/103. Unconditional direction pending.
- 213-193-A, proper powers in the band 0≤u≤π: unconditional uniform expansion V sinc(u)+C_*+O(V^{-2}) for the symbol, grouping all even exponents and summing the odd ones ≥3. Omitting proper powers only changes I(V) by O(1); after their explicit correction, error O(V^{-3}). The discrepancy of simple primes persists.
- 213-193-A, compression of the simple primes in [j²,(j+1)²): only the complete counts intervene except for O(V) in the symbol and O(1) in the mass. An additional error ≤1 per cell costs O(V) in mass and preserves the linear criterion. PROVED, independently checked: uniform derivative, Chebyshev by blocks and final cell by integer count. Antecedent: count stability 224. Joint bound of the excesses still open.
- 213-193-A, exact Legendre sieve between squares: for all d≤j the rounding telescopes between cells and costs O(V²) in symbol, O(V) in mass. The short density, the li term and the contributions of d>j with their signs persist. PROVED, independently checked: floors with j²−1 and Abel per divisor with variation O(logd/d); the short main term is not removed. Related antecedent 195_A (smooth quadrature).
- 213-193-A, long sieve roundings by largest prime: up to A log(2p) fixed cofactors per p, of arbitrary size, jointly cost O(A V) in mass. Includes pairs of neighboring primes with product of scale j². PROVED, independently checked: single stretch [p,min(J−1,d−1)] and unique largest prime; cost independent of the size of the cofactor. Does not control the complete collection of cofactors nor their density terms.
- 213-193-A, first complete sieve by increasing primorial: k=⌊log₂ j⌋, all 2^k divisors and their product density give joint error O(V²) in symbol, O(V) in mass. Cost O(ℓ) when activating the layer of the ℓ-th prime. PROVED, independently checked: single activation at 2^ℓ and 2^{ℓ−1} divisors per layer. R_j=N_j+B_j exactly; substitution only in weighted sum with error O(V) in mass. B_j is neither small nor can be discarded by sign; its joint compensation remains.
- 213-193-A, first sieve plus simultaneous squarefree condition: count of squarefree survivors replaceable by density β_Q in the sum with error O(1) in symbol, using the unconditional Mertens saving and uniform control of the product up to p_k. PROVED, independently checked: convolutive tail d>√x includes d>x, Rankin gives saving exp(−ck/logk), and Abel by block leaves a summable series. O(1) aggregate, not per cell. Only composite survivors of distinct primes and their density to be compensated remain.
- 213-193-A, logarithmic marks of surviving composites: simultaneously all factors p≤exp(k^{1/3}) of block k give density β_Q Σ log p/(p+1) with weighted error O(1) global. log Z_k=o(√k) is allowed. PROVED, independently checked: added modulus pQ with absolute factor O(1), error by blocks summable when logZ=o(√k). The large marks persist; a mixed composite is not entirely eliminated.
- 213-193-A, X^δ cut of marks: error O_δ(exp(δV/2)) in symbol; at u=0 each cut removes asymptotic fraction δ of the composite weight. The cut exp(k^{1/3}) removed a fraction tending to zero. PROVED, independently checked: uniform PNT/Mertens at x/p≥X^{1−δ} and Σlogp/√p≤C√Z. For fixed exponential precision O(1/δ) marks per integer remain; a rate O(δ) is needed for the remaining balance.
- 213-193-A, semiprimes r_k p with r_k the first prime outside Q: their two-sided centered error at zero frequency over all partial cuts of the block has a subpolynomial bound if and only if RH. The rescaled intervals overlap and reconstruct the prime discrepancy. PROVED, independently checked: exact identity for P and coverage 2a_k≤a_{k+1}<4a_k, with polynomial losses. Do not demand cofactor-by-cofactor cancellation as a route to a proof.
- 213-193-A, two cofactors at common cut r=p_{k+1}, s=r p_{k+2}: even their centered sum or difference with a subpolynomial two-sided bound over all cuts is equivalent to RH; recurrence with total amplification exp(o(k)). The exact cancellation upon aligning the prime changes the cuts. PROVED, independently checked: translated arguments under the previous maximum, product of amplifications exp(o(k)) and complete cuts. Collective packets of comparable weight are not excluded.
- 213-193-A, two consecutive surviving primes at common cut: subpolynomial two-sided bound for the sum or difference over all partial cuts ⇔ RH. The exact overlap of the blocks equals the delay of the dilation; iterating short increments only costs a polynomial in the block index. PROVED, independently checked: step h=1/(2r_{K+1}), coverage by exact overlap and double loss O(1+K/h), only polynomial. Signs fixed within the block; jumps and endpoints included. Case of comparable weights, without extrapolating to the complete packet.
- 213-193-A, collective inversion at common cut: if Σ|c_s|(r/s)^(1/2+η)≤1 eventually for every η>0, the two-sided bound of the packet is equivalent to RH even with growing cardinality. Proof by maximum of normalized increments. The complete packet of unit weight violates the hypothesis already with two neighboring secondary cofactors. Audit pending.

At a zero the main term is 0 including m=1 and −1 when excluding it. PROVED, independently checked: uniform tail for all t≥Y, continuation to σ=1/2 by absolutely convergent integral. Control of the complete discrepancy and of the long remainder is missing; antecedent: diagnosis by power 195_A.

Right side by uniform tail in ρ, left by finite parts. PROVED, independently checked: error constant Cδ(1+|ρ|), summable multiplicities with W, left without continuing 1/ζ(2s). Result for the centered packet up to X^δ, not for the unsmoothed arithmetic total.

The total packet has controlled density; excluding m=1 the prime discrepancy reappears in full. Smoothed H_Q has rate ≤0 at Y=X; removing m=1 subtracts the prime discrepancy, with no consequence for the global sign.

By Cauchy in the integer parameter z. PROVED, independently checked: growth exp(CΓ(R√k+R²)), R=k^{1/4} and denominator (R−1)^{D+1} give the rate; residue −ν and lifted contour positively oriented. - 213-193-A, moving radius around a hypothetical zero of multiplicity ν: for r=exp(−λD/ν) the interpolated normalized period tends to −ν if λ<1 and to zero if λ>1, with error ≤exp(−D(λ−1−log λ)+o(D)). PROVED, independently checked: circle of the parameter R=1/λ and residues F(0)−ΣcF fix rate and sign. Edge λ=1 resolved below. Diagnosis of the resolution of the selector, without proof of the sign.
- Update 213-193-A: endpoint λ=1 resolved for the equispaced nodes and M=log(2k). The normalized period at r=exp(−D/ν) retains −ν with error ≤exp(−D/(20M²)) eventually. PROVED, independently checked: circle centered at the mean, first moment zero and second exact leave −D/(12M²); errors Oρ(√k+logM) absorbed. Reach: prescribed nodes and schedule, not variable critical scales.

- Cross-check 213-193-A, interpolated radii against the local model: A_z=(s−ρ)^{νz} reproduces exactly F_loc(z)=−exp(−λDz)(exp(2πiνz)−1)/(2πiz), both regimes and λ=1. PROVED, independently checked: monodromy/resolution behavior, without arithmetic discrimination or new restriction on zeros; control of the real cuts pending.
- 213-193-A, enlargement of the sieve to z=(log X)^{6/5} using the Vinogradov–Korobov saving in Mertens. Integer composites with a factor in (p_k,z] are removed, with weighted error O(1) global. In complete blocks at zero frequency they represent asymptotically 1/6 of the previous composite weight. PROVED, independently checked: Vinogradov–Korobov Mertens verified in Lee–Leong 2208.06141; cost of the product = o(B(L)) at 6/5 and Rankin tail paid. No bound for the remaining balance.
- 213-195-A, primorial κ(log X)² with fixed Gevrey detector test: all squarefree survivors sum to O(exp(−c log X/log log X)) in signed weight by polar cancellation and shift of ζ(s)/ζ(2s). The eventual floor 1/16 on the remaining composites is equivalent to the global sign. With fixed positive profile, the asymptotic half of the composite weight of the first sieve remains. PROVED, independently checked: classical region for ζ(2s), polynomial derivative and small κ pay for the product. Correct double residue and half only for smooth positive weight. Does not extend to the sharp cut.
- Explicit variant of 213-195-A: convolution of the eight boxes with uniforms [0,j^{-2}] gives the decay exp(−c√|t|) required for the sieve and preserves the detection of every right-hand zero and the bias of squares. PROVED, independently checked: locally convergent product, zeros only imaginary, Gevrey 2 and critical budget preserved.
- 213-195-A, smooth sieve κV²: distinct semiprimes have negative main term −K''(1/2)√X/(2V²), composites with at least three factors have opposite positive main term, both unconditional by PNT and the two null moments. The balance at constant scale is not resolved. PROVED, independently checked: Mertens after two derivatives gives error O(V⁻³), with z frozen; full PNT leaves total o(√X/V²). Does not control constant scale. Antecedents 066 and earlier symmetric sector of 195.
- 213-195-A, unconditional positivity of the composite balance with multiplier 2^{ω−1}−1 in the original smooth detector: explicit positive main term K''(1/2)b_z√X/2, absolute error exp(−cV/log V). Difference of nodes 2 and 1 cancels primes exactly. Unit weight still open because k changes sign. Audit pending.
- 213-195-A, sensitivity of the unit weight: w±=1±exp(−(ω(n)−1)V^{1/3}) are uniformly close to 1 but give opposite signs with explicit main terms. In the semiprimes a variation of order V²/√X changes the sum at order one. Prevents transferring the constant floor by mere uniform convergence of the weights. Audit pending.
- 213-195-A, explicit detectors with polar zero of any fixed order m: preserve bias and exterior detection, and negative semiprime force of order √X/(log X)^{2m} with explicit coefficient. PROVED, independently checked: shifts (δ_h−qδ₀)/(1−q), critical reserve and coefficient −K^{(2m)}/(2m) correct. Not extrapolated to variable order.
- 213-195-A, continuous model of semiprimes at variable order: exact representation as a negative integral of a square. If m→∞ and V₀=V−2(m−1)h≥εV, log|model|=V₀/2+o(V). Raising the order without losing effective scale does not suppress the continuous term. PROVED, independently checked: tilt q^N and Frullani produce exp(V₀/2); floor on [1/h,2/h] and ceiling by variation give the rate. No automatic extrapolation to the discrete prime error.
- 213-195-A, discrete semiprimes: C₂,m/M_m→1 uniformly in 4≤2m≤(log X)^{1/4}, hence negative sign in that growing range. A moving cut log p=V/(2m) controls the Mertens error after differentiating and the representation by positive measure avoids losing the moments. PROVED, independently checked: comparator H₀≥0, relative Mertens error O(n/V), physical variation coefficients O(1) and floor √Xexp(−CnlogV). PNT error absorbed uniformly since V^{3/8}≫V^{1/4}logV. Not yet uniform detection nor sign of the total.
- 213-195-A, global criterion for the detector of growing polar order itself: freezing 2m≤H^{1/4} on H≤log X<2H preserves sieve κV², bias and detection in each block by 115. In these same tests the real semiprime sector is negative. PROVED, independently checked: physical expansion of norm <1.05 preserves sieve and squares; b≤0 costs O(1) by copies, b>0 has uniform sum and floor exp(−o(H)) for 115. Does not assert the limit −1/8 under RH. Floor of the joint balance still open.
- 213-195-A, distinct triples in smooth sieve κV²: C₃=(K''(1/2)/2)√X/V² [1−log(V/log z)+o(1)], negative. Therefore C_{≥4} has positive main term +(K''/2)√X log(V/log z)/V², without constant term in that normalization. The sign of C₄ alone and the global floor are not asserted. PROVED, independently checked: conditional densities and factor 1/6 correct, repetitions o(√X/V²), constant 1 preserved. Fixed profile.
- 213-195-A, sign of ALL sectors of fixed cardinality d≥2 in the smooth sieve κV²: main term −K''√X log(V/log z)^{d−2}/[2V²(d−2)!]. Recurrence of densities and discrete control for fixed d. PROVED, independently checked: recurrence f_d′ and simplex with slack, small repetitions at the correct logarithmic scale. The positive compensation escapes every fixed truncation; limited uniform extension recorded later.

- Phase 213, ROUND_195_A, extension of the multiplicity computation. PROVED, independently checked: uniform argument up to ⌊(loglogX)^(1/3)⌋; simplex constants (Cd)^{Cd}, low exp(−c√h) and diagonal with factor 1/(2j!) leave relative error o(1). The total balance remains open.

- Phase 213, ROUND_195_A, localization of compensation. Counting the four factorizations per prime places a positive balance between any fixed D ≥3 and ⌈6 log log X/log 4⌉. The absolute tail is O(√X/log² X), insufficient for the constant floor.

- 213-195-A, extreme tail of the fixed detector. Refinement of the exponent cost of 374 by Σ(p/z)^(-s) with fixed large s: d≥V/(log z+δ) costs O(exp(−cV/log z)) in absolute value, sufficient to preserve the constant-floor criterion. PROVED, independently checked: Rankin/Stirling gives the announced coefficient with log(1+t/h)=o(1), endpoints and summation uniform. Fixed profile and eventual margin, without exact arithmetic maximum nor control of the intermediate balance. 374 is an antecedent of the mechanism, not of the budget o(1).

- 213-195-A, absolute withdrawal frontier at d≥V/(log z+a). Threshold F(a)=2+½ log κ+log a+a/2: exponentially small tail below and exponentially large absolute mass along a sequence above. PROVED, independently checked: optimization s=1+1/a, concentration at exact mean and collisions O(1/logZ), factor d! and cells O(d). Margin ε ensures cut κV² after choosing V. Tilted packing of 374; equality and signed balance open.

- 213-195-A, joint cancellation of divisibility patterns. For r≤ηV/log V arbitrary blocks of small primes, sum of moduli of the balances of all nonempty patterns ≪exp(−cV/log V), by uniform sieve and inversion over subsets. PROVED, independently checked: uniform product per subset, inversion kills the primes and cost 3^r−1. The empty pattern retains the global problem.

- 213-195-A, balances B_q at multiples of q within the sector without small primes. With κ adjusted to ε one obtains Σ_{1<q≤X^(1−ε)}|B_q|² ≪ exp(−c_ε V/log V), by the exact local factor and the harmonic norm. PROVED, independently checked: exact local factor, complete derivative without simple pole and saving ελV after extracting q⁻¹⁄². Limit for representations of the unit weight with coefficients of small norm.

- 213-195-A, unconditional obstruction to reconstructing the unit weight by proper divisors. Pairs of primes in an interval proportional to √X force norm ≥c X^(1/4)/√log X for exactness; below that scale the absolute cost of the error is ≫√X/log X at each sign of the kernel. PROVED, independently checked: exact mean 2Σb_p/N, weights V/√X and N² pairs. Covers absent coefficients and both signs; does not exclude signed compensation of the error.

- 213-195-A, rings of semiprimes by frozen separation of logarithms. Every 0≤α<β<1 gives explicit positive main term proportional to G(β)−G(α), G(t)=4t/(1−t²)²; the outer edge carries the total negative sign. PROVED, independently checked: density log((r+b)/(r−b)), curvature 4br/(r²−b²)² and PNT of exponential edges. With separation relative to log(pq) the main term disappears; no uniformity as β→1.

- 213-195-A, interior positivity at every fixed multiplicity d≥2. Polytopes frozen in the deviations (log p_i−log n/d)/log X, separated from the edge, have favorable main term by strict convexity of Σ_i Π_{j≠i}1/t_j when translating the logarithms. PROVED, independently checked: Jacobian V^{d−1}, without factor d or d!, convex section of an interval and telescoping PNT with edges. H_P″>0 and remainder O_P(√X/V³); frozen scale V essential. Total sum of each fixed d adverse; edge and uniformity remain.

- 213-195-A, comparison at the real edge of the sieve. The fixed band z<p≤exp(C)z has positive semiprime balance ∼K″C√X/V³; moving its endpoint by the factor exp((log n−V)/2) gives negative balance ∼−K″√X/(8(log z+C)²). PROVED, independently checked: fixed curvature 2C/V³ and moving 1/(4g²), uniform reciprocal PNT and sign by complement. Detects an effect of the cut that prevents attributing the deficit to the size of the prime by itself.

- 213-195-A, uniform positivity by largest prime in the composite detector. Without multiplicity limit, every fiber n=mq whose cut q>P⁺(m) lets the complete support enter is positive with uniform equivalent. The only fibers able to contribute a loss have the two largest primes in ratio ≤exp(width of the support). PROVED, independently checked: normalization √X/m exact, integral K″a/l³ and relative error bounded by (1+l)poly(l)e⁻ᶜ√l. Extends small cofactor up to l=log(X/m)≥logz+O(1). Endpoints k(A)=k(B)=0; does not estimate the comparison with cut fibers nor the joint floor.

- 213-195-A, balance of the two largest primes with arbitrary cofactor m. Formula uniform in ω(m) on compact bands of H/L, H=log max(z,P⁺(m)), L=log(X/m); favorable sign even after restoring the trimmed groups in one band, adverse in another. PROVED, independently checked: density (1+a/r)log((r−H)/H), curvature and normalization √X/m correct; PNT error absorbed using V=L+a. Examples of both signs uniform, without floor of the aggregate.

- 213-195-A, contact of the two free primes with the edge 2H. Positive jump of the derivative of the density at 2H; w=J″ converts the jump into (1+a/(2H))J(L−2H)/H. Sign of the complete fiber uniform where J has positive floor, including the regime H/L→1/2. PROVED, independently checked: jump of F′ positive, without δ′, and w=J″ produces J(θ) with sign +. PNT error uniform by V=a+2H+O(1); positivity only where J has floor. Joint remainder open.

- 213-195-A, aggregate mass of contacts of the three largest primes with residual cofactor t≤X^δ, δ<1/4. Positive balance ≍√X/(log X log z) by uniform count of the contact prime and harmonic mass of t. The complement has opposite main term; difference at constant precision open. PROVED, independently checked: P>t because δ<1/4, weight √X/(tPV), mass P≈1/V and harmonic mass ≈V/logz by Bernoulli 1/(p+1)+Markov.

- 213-195-A, quantified local compensation by cofactor t≤X^(1/5) and three largest primes with log p_i>8log(X/t)/25. Aggregate balance positive ≍√X/(V log z) after including an adverse band of the same order. Positive curvature of the integral over the simplex of three factors. PROVED, independently checked: Jacobian y², factor 1/6 and (y²D)″≥D. The adverse subband has Σ1/p₁≈1 and is of equal order; no global floor.

- 213-195-A, transition at x=3 for the complete subtotal over free primes >exp(log(X/t)/x), t≤X^(1/5). Collective sign negative immediately to the left and positive immediately to the right for fixed x, with modulus ≍√X/(V log z), including all multiplicities allowed by the cut. PROVED, independently checked: triple jump (α+3)/6 and lateral curvatures −1/4,+1/4. Single cofactor; excludes exact x=3.

- 213-195-A ↔ 213-392-A. The Buchstab oscillation was already present in 392. Corollary for the composite detector: intervals of both signs arbitrarily late with g=ω′ and g′ of the same sign force the simultaneous sign of [(R+α)ω]″ for all weights α≥0 of the cofactor. The discrete subtotal changes sign between arbitrarily late fixed cuts. Avoid extrapolation from x=3. PROVED, independently checked: mean value gives g,g′ of the same sign; density (R+α)ω and δ<1/(1+x) guarantee transfer and single cofactor. No uniformity as x→∞.

- 213-195-A, second cut Y=bz with 2e√κ(√b−1)<1. Subtotal of composites with zero or one prime >Y positive ∼K″log(b)√X/V³, without limiting multiplicity; incomplete fibers cost o(1) in modulus by finite Euler product. PROVED, independently checked: Rankin coefficient 2e√κ(√b−1), incomplete o(1), mass Σlogm/m→logb; complete tail only small relative to the main term.

- 213-195-A, sum of moduli of ALL balances by exact small part m up to Y≤κ₀V², without block budget. Factorization m^(−s)A_Y and Euler sum over m on the contour: total cost exponentially small. The gain with a prime >Y is canceled within the same class m>1 at precision o(1); the empty pattern retains the problem. PROVED, independently checked: Σm⁻σ Euler product and derivatives ≤Y·mass, both costs absorbed with κ₀ small. U_m=P_m+E_m+D_m and Rankin give ℓ¹ cancellation within each m>1, with no additional credit for m=1.

- 213-195-A, barrier of unit classes when raising Y=κV². For κ>1/(4e²) the classes of a single visible term force sum of moduli exponentially large along a sequence; for lower κ the entirely smooth mass is exponentially small. PROVED, independently checked: Bernoulli odds e^η/√p, cost exp((1−η+o1)V/h), slack θ<1 and unit classes. Equality resolved below; optimal range of ℓ¹ for all classes remains open.

- 213-195-A, critical case κ=1/(4e²) of the smooth barrier. Rankin expansion and tilted Bernoulli with exact mean give limsup (log³Y/V)log(1+absolute smooth mass)=2; unit classes of either sign on subsequences. Closes the equality for that obstruction, not for the global balance. PROVED, independently checked: quadratic expansion 4−2b+b²/2, exact mean with b=2+O(1/H), var≤VH and slack H⁻⁴≫V⁻¹⁄³. Preserves constant 2 after the shift; no signed limit.

- 213-195-A, collective sign of the products with all their primes in (ακV²,κV²], 0≤α<1 fixed. Smooth local limit by Fourier for tilted Bernoulli: signed subtotal positive with equivalent at every large scale; at the critical smooth edge log S∼2V/log³Y. Includes bands with positive lower cut. Complement open. PROVED, independently checked: central Gaussian CF, phase by sinc up to h⁴ and normalized Gevrey tail exp(−ch²). Critical gives signed growth at every scale and implies limit 2 also for absolute mass.

- 213-195-A, exact large part r with primes >Y. Fibers with log(X/r)≥(log Y)^10 positive simultaneously by local limit with error smaller than the moving double zero of the kernel. Every possible loss remains in fibers where the part in (αY,Y] has logarithm ≤(log Y)^10+O(1). PROVED, independently checked: normalized error O(h/√D)+o(h⁻²)=o(β²), β≥c logh/h; controls the moving double zero. No sign of the remaining edge.

- 213-195-A, counterexample to extending individual positivity to every growing W. At each scale there are large prime parts with fibers of opposite signs for W=(1/(4log(1/α))+o(1))log²Y. Isolated layers of growing multiplicity, two exact moments and PNT to realize the primes. PROVED, independently checked: exact second moment, support Oh and derivative CMV give radii ch⁻³ independent of M; PNT realizes both primes at every scale.

- 213-195-A, collective resolution of the isolated strip W≍log²Y. Large prime parts of mixed signs give explicit positive balance and ratio balance/absolute mass O(log⁴Y/V³). With admissible Y, the large composite parts of the same strip cancel it with exponentially small error. PROVED, independently checked: sum by largest prime gives P_j, modulus by PNT against |F| gives A_j, and ℓ¹ by small part cancels in detector αY; no residual global credit.

- 213-195-A, smooth cut in W for strips of overlapping multiplicities. Uniform residue formula at precision o(1) depending only on the m at bounded distance from the edge; sum of errors in modulus and exact cancellation of complementary residues. The complete cut leaves the prime detector pending. PROVED, independently checked: uniform Gevrey norm by translation, double pole without simple and residue (V−u)/m exact. Complements cancel for each m; m=1 retains primes. Do not substitute χ by a sharp indicator.

- 213-193-A, limitation of the local certificate as a global path. All checks reproduced at T=2.7695. For U≥3.4 no Schur weight of the current comparison can give archimedean margin to R≤3·10¹²: the quotient over the constant exceeds 28.77 against a ceiling of 26.90. Not an obstruction to the Weil sign.

- Cross 213-193-A / 213-081-A. The necessary ceiling 28.77 at U=3.4 persists with both polar moments exactly null, also when demanding interior smoothness. Application of the finite-codimension theorem already recorded in 081. Do not retry the route of rescuing the separate floor by imposing more finite moments.

- 213-195-A / 115, sampling of the fixed prime detector at O(H⁴) scales per block H≤log X≤2H. Poisson for modulated Gaussians plus Gevrey tail controls aliasing exponentially; an unbounded sequence of blocks with all samples favorable suffices for RH. PROVED, independently checked: Poisson per mode, Gevrey tail from H³ and discrete Gaussian tails; error O(exp(−cH^{3/2})). No proof of the sampled sign; 115 continuous antecedent, no literal duplicate located.

- 213-195-A, persistence of excursions of the prime detector on intervals of length c/H² in each block under failure of RH. Gaussian mass of both signs comparable and L¹ variation controlled by H². Allows free-position samples in O(H³ log H) cells; the arithmetic estimate is missing. PROVED, independently checked: Fourier cut R=C₁H² gives ||g′||₁≤CH²||g||₁, both masses and components including endpoints. Free samples in EVERY cell, not one point per block. Earlier Bernstein tools in R167_102, a different object.

- 213-195-A / 115, threshold of the unmodulated Gaussian average of the prime detector: c_*=sup 2b/(γ²−b²) over right-hand zeros. For c>c_* the average at variance cV tends to −1/8, for 0<c<c_* it has exponential excursions. Z2 already gives the favorable average with c=2/G². Pending step: control at arbitrarily small relative variances. PROVED, independent check: absolute interchange, Gaussian tails and injectivity of the exponent. Same parabolic map as 364/365 and average of 115; specialization to the fixed detector, no new spectral exclusion.

- 213-195-A, exact translation of the Gaussian average to a second moment of log p+u for the measure (log p)/p with positive weights. In the resolved regime the relative deficit is exponential in V; the mere Gaussian limit and the positive covariance of G1_B10_R3 do not give the ceiling. PROVED, independent check: completing the square and two integrations by parts; Z→∫J. Relative deficit s²exp(−V/2−s²/8)/(8∫J); no advance of window.

- 213-195-A, variance centered at the real arithmetic mean. A first-derivative detector controls the square of the displacement of the mean and preserves the threshold c_* of the sign. Equivalence with spatial log-concavity of Z at t=V+cV/2, variance frozen; it remains to prove it arithmetically for c↓0. PROVED, independent check: detector k₁ and f<d₀ make the mean correction relatively exponentially small in both sequences of excursions.

- 213-195-A, endpoint c_*>0 of the Gaussian prime average. The bias of squares dominates all critical coefficients by Z2–Z3, giving eventual ceiling <−1/16 at equality. At variance c_*V−log V a single dominant pair reappears and both signs unbounded. No improvement of c_* nor of T. PROVED, independent check: total spectral tail <1/64; maximum γ²−b² selects a single pair when reducing the variance by logV, with uniform tails.

- 213-195-A, Gaussian prime contrast without boxes or derivatives. Σ_p(log p)/√p g_s(V−log p) against exp(V/2+s²/8), s²=cV. At the endpoint c=c_*>0 the integer coefficients per zero dominate the bias 1/2, with limsup of the excess ≥1/2, unlike the test with boxes. Arithmetic ceiling for c↓0 missing. PROVED, independent check: contour up to Re w=−1, squares 1/2 and critical integer coefficient ≥1. At the endpoint limsup≥1/2 and liminf≤−3/2; favorable ceiling only for c>c_*.

- 213-195-A, cost of the positive sieve in the Gaussian prime average. At the cut y=exp(θ₀V) the excess of composites is Θ(V^(−3/2)), with explicit equivalent and threshold θ₀→1/2 when lowering c. Allows replacing primes >y by integers without small divisors at precision o(1); the arithmetic comparison remains open. PROVED, independent check: semiprime density log(1+v/H), exact factor 1/(H a²), tails and squares relatively negligible even F<0. At constant θ₀ [θ₀√(2πc)a₀²]⁻¹; no new arithmetic ceiling.

- 213-195-A, cross-check with the already indexed Selberg/Vaughan NO-GO. In the Gaussian comparison at level D=y=X^θ₀ the best quadratic main term is asymptotically (1+c/2)/θ₀ times the target; the ratio tends to two when lowering c. Do not retry optimization of coefficients at that level with errors paid in modulus. PROVED, independent check: exact diagonalization and minimizer 1/G(D), G(D)=logD+O(1), truncated Gaussian integral with mean (1+c/2)V. Scope: main term plus remainder in modulus; does not exclude signed compensation.

- 213-195-A, saturation by the complete primorial. Even the exact coprimality indicator, when using its period average, has main term of ratio R(c)→2e^(−γ_E)>1. Its real signed remainder is (1−R(c)+o(1)) times the target integral. Discards raising D as a remedy for small c; control at constant scale open. PROVED, independent check: exact minimum φ(P_y)/P_y, R(c)=e⁻γ_E(1+c/2)/θ₀, Q_c/I→1 and removal of primes ≤y by tilted tail. Eventual negative remainder if R(c)>1; only relative precision, not constant.

- 213-195-A, adaptive adjustment of y by density of the primorial. For c≤10⁻³ the first drop of δ_y below 1/((1+c/2)V) allows replacing Q_c−I by the balance of the zero class minus the exact mean over all translations, with exponential absolute error. The fractional excess of the minimal cut disappears; order between zero class and mean open. PROVED, independent check: jump ≤1/y, exact mean by counting/Tonelli, unimodal quadrature and both tails absolutely exponential. The sign between zero class and mean is not deduced from the calibration.

- 213-195-A, localization of the discrepancy of the primorial calibrated by reduced denominator. The non-constant absolute Fourier mass with q≤X^0.9 is O(exp(−V/3)) uniform in translation for 0<c≤10⁻³. The sign depends on composite denominators larger than X^0.9. PROVED, independent check: exact Ramanujan expansion, ℓ¹ norm of Δ²⁰f≤||f⁽²⁰⁾||₁ and absolute sums in b,q; exponent −.409875 before the polynomial factor. No control of the sign of the large denominators.

- 213-195-A, variance of translations of the calibrated primorial ≥const·√V. Energy of denominators dp₁p₂ isolated by orthogonality on the mesh p₁p₂ and removal of small resonances. Discards global approximation o(1) in quadratic norm to the mean; gives no sign at a=0. PROVED, independent check: E≍V³ᐟ², tail ℓ¹≤e⁻V, exact orthogonality N<p₁p₂ and removal of nonzero frequencies q′≤X^.56; constant pair masses and G(X^.01)≍V.

- 213-195-A, signed evaluation in the zero class of the conductors of the variance. The family dp₁p₂ with 1<d≤X^.01 turns out exponentially small after summing the phases within each q; the pairs alone give explicit negative main term and formula at absolute precision by means of the finite sum. PROVED, independent check: local Ramanujan identity, total tail ≤e⁻·⁶⁹V and residual frequencies ≤X^.56. Pairs without d: negative limit −½log²(.55/.54) after dividing by I; for absolute precision keep the finite sum.

- 213-195-A, elimination at all orders of the upper block B=[X^.54,y]. For q=dΠ_{p∈S}p with d≤X^.32 and S⊆B arbitrary, T_q is computed with joint ℓ¹ error O(X^(−1/3)), preserving the exact main terms of d=1. What remains are conductors whose product outside B exceeds X^.32. PROVED, independent check: uniform absolute products over S, tail tilted by n^(2/V) and sum d≤X^.32; normalized linear formula and unique conductors dp≤X^.9. Without loss 2^|B|.

- 213-195-A, simultaneous reduction of ALL the coefficients T_q to internal subproducts X^.94<a≤X^1.07 and cofactors n/a≤X^.13. Cost identity Σ_{a|q|P}δ_y/φ(q)=1/a; joint error in moduli O(X^(−1/3)). Summing over q recovers Möbius, with no sign proved for the central stretch. PROVED, independent check: exact identity 1/a, small error a of exponent −.509875 and positive tail Στ(n)f(n)=O(e⁻V). Without loss by number of conductors nor order of factors.

- 213-195-A, sign of the quadrature H_a−F₀ per central divisor. The tilt λ=1/2+(log a−V)/(cV) gives dominant term log(a)ζ(λ) after subtracting the integral; opposite signs on (−4,−2) and (−2,1), uniformly on compacta. PROVED, independent check: normalized inversion and polar residue, remainder O_c(1) uniform and change scale X^(1−5c/2). The correlation with μ(a) persists; neither λ=−2 nor the balance at constant precision is decided.

- 213-195-A, signed Möbius cancellation of all subproducts of primes ≤V^(2/5) in the central band λ∈[1/4,3/4]. Uniform equivalent E(a)Π(1−p^(−λ)) negative before multiplying by μ(a); quantified saving and exterior parity open. PROVED, independent check: inversion with D_z and complete derivative, uniform complex quotient by zlogz=o(s), Gaussian domination and PNT saving. Relative precision within each class; exterior μ(a) uncontrolled.

- 213-195-A, displaced saddle in the signed Möbius sum: z=(εV/log V)^(4/3), λ∈[1/4,3/4]. The equation s²(u−λ)+(log P)′(u)=0 preserves curvature and allows a uniform equivalent even when the linear phase is not negligible. Relative saving of scale exp(−const·V/log²V) at the endpoint λ=1/4; the exterior parity remains open. PROVED, independent check: existence/uniqueness with B≥s²/2, global majorant e^(−Bτ²/2), uniform cubic remainder and Jacobian s/√B. Do not extend without controlling curvature or exterior parity.

- 213-195-A, existence threshold of the real saddle at z=(κV/log V)^(1/(1−λ)). Subcritical there is a positive saddle; supercritical it disappears for κ>c(1−λ)²/e. At equality the correction log log V/log V maintains sufficient curvature for the equivalent. Do not extrapolate the proof to the exponential cut y. PROVED, independent check: constant cb²/e, negative correction −loglogV/logV and B/(cV)~√(2loglogV/logV); cubic remainder still o(1). Supercritical nonexistence includes all u>0.

- 213-195-A, exponential cut z=X^.16 without real saddle. In groups with exterior part a∈[X^.94,X^1.07] the complete sifting leaves f(a)−δ_z F₀/a with summed absolute error O(e^(−V)). Sign positive central and negative exterior with respect to log a=(1+c/2)V at scale s√log V. Restriction after grouping, exterior parity and small a pending. PROVED, independent check: joint tail with τ(n) and exponent −3.90V, prefactor ≍√V and error smaller than the negative base ≥e⁻·⁵⁸V. At most six exterior factors; reach of grouping preserved.

- 213-195-A, exterior sign resolved in .995≤log a/V≤1.005 at cut z=X^.16. Sum of μ(a)U(a) over all multiplicities ≤−I/50. Integer Darboux certificate verify_195_outer_parity.py for alternating convolutions of 2 to 6 primes, executed with PASS. PROVED, independent audit with PASS reproduction: integer cells and roundings correct, uniform ordered PNT and margin −.1+.07<−.02. Global balance open; the conclusion is of order I.

- 213-195-A, complete elimination of ω(a)≥7 at cut z=X^.16. Signed credit measured at precision O(e^(−V)) by finite product and six symmetric functions, between 0 and I/100. Smaller than the loss I/50 of the central strip; the determining compensation lies among the exterior orders ≤6. PROVED, independent check: real tail with τ(n) of exponent −6.08V, sign of the Taylor bracket and constant 7·1.3⁷/7!<.008715. Comparison with center and exhaustiveness correct; total at constant scale open.

- 213-195-A, conceptual audit of the six exterior profiles. Continuous convolutions summed exactly give exp_*(h−b), calibrated total O(exp(−εV)); for c=2/G² the real discrete total tends to −1/2. The integer half is lost even with exact continuous profiles. Do not scale density certificates to close the constant margin alone. PROVED, independent check: local Fubini of exp_*, identity rB and bound B≤1/H, absolutely exponential tails. Exact discrete references indispensable; not a bound on sectoral errors.

- 213-195-A, arithmetic frequency of failures: over n dyadic integers and c∈(0,.001), the NON-normalized average in c of the indicators of prime excess tends exactly to c_*/2. Generic dominant pair, irrational rotation and dominated convergence. A liminf of zero would suffice; that bound is not available. PROVED, independent check: countable exceptional rates and resonances, density 1/2 a.e. subcritical, continuity/measurability and DCT without uniformity. Transfer to the calibrated cut valid; factor 1/C not present.

- 213-195-A, density in c at ONE single scale and dichotomy of crossings. Positive length→c_*/2 without averaging in V. Jensen gives O_ε(V) zeros in [ε,.001]; outside RH there are ≫V sign changes in a fixed band at every large scale; under RH eventually none on any compact. Sublinear arithmetic bound pending. PROVED, independent check: finite maximum and uniform gaps by stretches; linear phase in c without irrationality hypothesis. Jensen disc with Re(1/c)>0 and central floor −1/2 gives O_ε(V) with multiplicities.

- 213-195-A, counterexample to the sublinear count by positivity and PNT in fixed progressions.
