A subset of integers constructed by rounding in reduced classes reproduces the bias −1/2 and ≫V crossings in a band of c under 2/G². Compatible with any finite prime prefix, without the multiplicative identity of the primes. PROVED, independent check: increments <1 per candidate, polylog error in all fixed APs, Gaussian integration by parts o(1) and three exact Gaussians. Preserves finite prefix, not multiplicative structure.

- 213-195-A, proof of the divisor identity over the perturbation of integer atoms. After including squares, centering and convolving with 1, the artificial pair is left with residue ζ(ρ)/2. Under failure of RH it can disappear from the Gaussian check of the defect while persisting in the crossing count. Explicit cross with the inversion NO-GO 1*(Λ−b); the pointwise identity is not reproduced. PROVED, independent check: squares cancel real residue −1/2, ζL_E+ζ′ cancels double pole 1, factor (s−1) kills the simple one. Gaussian remainder exponential if ζ(ρ)=0; conditional alternative, not a pointwise identity.

- 213-195-A, classification of the artificial residue against the entire hierarchy of divisors of phase-200/D_CONSTRUCTION_001. At a hypothetical right-hand zero of multiplicity m, all defects are regular exactly for r=0,−1,...,−m; outside that set the first pole occurs at order m+1. A single integer set with r=−m passes every centered Gaussian check of fixed order and preserves the crossings. Conditional on the zero, without uniformity in the order nor pointwise identity. Local proof in ROUND_195_A.

- 213-195-A, square of the pointwise divisor defect. In integer subsets with finitely many atoms divisible by each prime, quadratic mean with liminf zero characterizes exactly the primes. Argument by disjoint pairs (n,pn). A falsifier of all signed orders with any prefix admits explicit lower bound (1−1/p)(log p)²/(2p) for that energy. The aligned oscillating example remains conditional on the right-hand zero; the characterization is unconditional. Transfer to the sign missing.

- 213-195-A, uniform instability from the quadratic energy of the defect. Blocks of semiprimes lp added to the primes give RMS energy ≤ε in ALL prefixes but exceed the Gaussian ceiling by ≳_c I/V^(5/2) at arbitrarily high scales, for each fixed c. PNT in fixed APs and prescribed prefix preserved. Unconditional; prevents transfer by uniform continuity, does not decide the case of energy exactly zero.

- 213-195-A, optimal constant of one-sided stability. Under additions and RMS energy ≤ε, sup_E(Q_E−Q_P)∼ε² I/[(1+c/2)√(2πc)V^(3/2)]. The diagonal in multiples gives a summable budget, saturable by semiprimes 2p at the maximum of the weight. For each fixed E there is little-o at that scale. Control relative to the real prime count; sign of Q_P−I open.

- 213-195-A, deterministic sweep with a single rational width c_n=C(n−N+1)/N per integer of the block N=2^j. Frequency of excesses of the prime ceiling → c_*/(2C). Quadratic curvature and geometric differences avoid sampling resonances. Reduces the integral in width to an explicit sequence; o(N) excesses along a subsequence remains open.
  The same exact frequency holds over M consecutive integers from any N→∞, with M→∞ arbitrarily slowly and c_j=C(j+1)/M. The curvature depends only on M; the start disappears when differentiating the phase twice.

- 213-195-A, contrast with the sweep at consecutive centers. For every finite list of widths there is a set of integer centers with bounded gaps where the whole list falls below the ceiling by at least 1/4, even in ties and threshold. Therefore ever denser meshes can be chosen with zero excesses at centers selected a posteriori, unconditionally. Classical returns ES-12/104 applied to the single-center protocol; no uniformity in the size of the mesh.
  For the uniform mesh of m points the lower density of favorable integer centers is ≥exp(−O_C(√m log²(2m))); two coordinates per spectral pair suffice for all the points of the mesh.

- 213-195-A, positive sign of the exponential integral of the prime deficit I−Q_c at every rate λ>1/2+c/8. Moreover the mean with V gamma(k+1,rate .6) tends unconditionally to +1/2 with error O_c((15/16)^k). The continuation of the prime series leaves as nearest pole that of the squares. These means with growing centers can hide subcritical excesses; they give no bound on their frequency. Recurrence antecedent of the previous item: 091-A, resumed in 102-A.

- 213-195-A, positivity of ALL the integer moments of the Gaussian deficit of the primes for λ₀<λ≤3/2+9c/8. The first trivial zero dominates the absolute cost of the nontrivial ones in the derivatives of G=1/(s−1)+ζ′/ζ on 1<s≤2. Positive local composition with the root of the Gaussian resolvent. Includes the intermediate orders of the rate .6. Antecedent 253–255 for KP, a different observable. Does not enlarge T.

- 213-195-A, counterexample at order 400 to positivity of all the moments of the raw deficit at all rates: λ=400/log 2, every 0<c≤.001, p=2 suffices. For real centers V=log p, the last violation by the centered atom only reaches [log(1/c)+log log(1/c)−log(4π)]/2+o(1) when lowering c. The eventual condition at fixed c avoids this local obstacle.
  At the same rate .6 with all moments positive, a finite section of its Hankel matrix is indefinite by polynomial density and the previous negative test. The minimal degree is not identified nor is the bridge matrix of P46 addressed.

- 213-195-A, displaced-moment forms of the raw deficit at rate .6. Unconditional uniform positivity with degree ≤k/150 and quotient →1/2. Under RH it holds for each fixed slope B in degree ≤Bk. Outside RH, in widths with a unique winner, the Laguerre projection of 1−cos(ωV) produces a negative direction for every large k if B>ω²/(.6−f)². Distinguishes the tail and eliminates the false negative of the prime 2 in this regime. Arbitrary unconditional slopes open.

- 213-195-A, unconditional extension of the degree to 10¹² k for the displaced form of the Gaussian deficit, by oscillatory integration of each mode and Z2. For a subcritical winner, projection of the damped test exp(−tV)sin(ωV/2) gives a negative direction for any B>(√(1+(ω/(.6−f))²)−1)/2, linear in frequency. These are sufficient bounds, not the exact frontier nor an extension of T.

- 213-195-A, amplification of an adverse direction to ≥ηk negative eigenvalues of the displaced-moment matrix, for every large k with unique subcritical winner and B above the sufficient threshold. Two-dimensional mesh of damped exponentials, control by rows and Laguerre projection with uniform exponential tail. For the sign, inertia o(k) along some subsequence for each B,c suffices; the arithmetic bound is open.

- 213-195-A, dilation-commutator bound for the trace of each harmonic in the Laguerre space of degrees ≤Bk: O(1) when summing ≍k entries. In the normalization by the winning rate, the mean traces of the scaled deficit and of its modulus tend to 0 and 4m/π respectively even with linear negative inertia. Do not confuse compressing the parts with taking the parts of the matrix.

- 213-195-A, exact second-order transition in the compression of a Laguerre harmonic: norm HS²/k with integral limit of arcsine laws, by conjugation of the number operator and tridiagonal paths. In winner normalization, slope B₀=(√(1+(ω/a)²)−1)/2 exact for density of negative eigenvalues with fixed margin; at B=B₀ that density still vanishes. Does not assert zero inertia of small eigenvalues nor a new window T.

- 213-195-A, square of the prime deficit at physical scale: diagonal √V/(2√(πc))+o(1) and distinct pairs at additive distance ≤H with mass O_c(H/√V), 1≤H≤√V, by upper sieve. Up to H=o(√V) can be eliminated at absolute precision o(1). It suffices to bound above the remaining balance averaged on intervals of length one along some subsequence for each rational c; cancellation of far pairs pending.

- 213-195-A, arithmetic floor of the CENTERED local balance at distance H=λV for triangular kernel. By integrality of the number of primes in each interval and PNT only after averaging, liminf E_H/√V≥{λ}(1−{λ})/(2λ√(πc)) for noninteger λ; at integer λ there remains liminf E_H≥1/(2π). In the supercritical band the complementary compensation must be negative of order at least √V for noninteger λ. Does not close the complete balance.

- 213-195-A, two-sided order E_{λV}≍√V of the centered triangular energy for every fixed λ>0, integers included. The sieve discards neighbors of p and of p+H in short bands; isolated jumps leave quadratic mass on disjoint intervals. At supercritical widths the complement compensates with −Θ(√V) for any fixed multiple of the mean spacing. Does not determine the global subcritical balance.

- 213-195-A, dyadic localization of the far balance: a subcritical winner of rate f forces in each unit stretch of centers a positive contiguous additive covariance ≥const·exp(2fV)/V, at dyadic length H between exp(2fV−O(log V)) and exp((2+5c/4−2f)V+O(log V)). O(V) scales are queried. Upper arithmetic control missing; sufficient condition, no converse proved for individual covariances.

- 213-195-A, converse of the covariance criterion: conditional Selberg under RH, passage from relative to additive increments and Gaussian partition give E_H(v)≪_c(1+v)^4 simultaneously in H≥1. Hence the subexponential positive maximum on the dyadic scales of 195 along subsequences is equivalent to the global sign. The arithmetic side without RH remains to be proved.

- 213-195-A, exact rate of the edge energy for H=X=2^n, v=log X: limsup log(1+B_X)/log X=2Θ−1, at ONE fixed width even supercritical. The right-hand extremes in [X/4,X] with nonpositive start suffice. Dyadic partition and Mellin recover P−1/(s−1). Localized variant of the classical Chebyshev criterion, without unconditional subpolynomial bound nor criterion by mere subsequence.
  Identical exponent for the variance of the prefixes in [X/4,X]: by two copies it uses exclusively interior intervals and eliminates all datum of the primes prior to X/4.
  Audit of direct antecedent: 231-A already controls the unweighted affine fit in each block. Locally inverting h by parts costs O(log X) in the normalized energy; its theorem improves the two limsup to ordinary limits. A subsequence suffices. Do not pursue as an independent method.

- 213-195-A, audit of transfer to the confluent POWER blocks: 21-A.1 and density of the Cauchy fractions give limit index two per distinct quartet. Under finite defect all late determinants are positive and the negative fraction tends to zero even with nonzero defect. Do not transfer the density criterion of the Gaussian family to POWER. Index ≤1 at unbounded sizes would indeed suffice, without proved bound.

- 213-195-A, localized inertia of the displaced jets of the normalized POWER kernel. At fixed width d equal to the number of distinct zeros with |u²−λ²|<R, the late index counts exactly the interior right-hand zeros, whatever the tail. Finite Vandermonde plus exponential separation. Differs from the fixed start of GRAM §19.10; refines 21-A.1, does not prove control at every width. The normalization is carried out before displacing.

- 213-195-A, first partial cut of a quartet in normalized POWER displaced jets: under failure there exists rational u and fixed odd width r+1, r=number of interior nodes on the axis, with lower density ≥1/4 of determinants of each sign. Interior vanishing and a single Schur pivot leave a dominant cosine. Scalar criterion by density, without independent arithmetic bound. Complements the inertia of complete groups and the antecedent 21-A.1.

- 213-195-A, comparison T_n=D_nD_{n+2}−D_{n+1}² of three displaced determinants. At the partial witness width under failure of RH, T_n<0 eventually without phase exception; under RH, T_n≥0 at all orders. Unconditionally T_n>0 eventually at widths d≤N−2 of a safe cut of N distinct critical nodes, by the two largest Cauchy–Binet products. Antecedents Turán 046/055; no bound at every width nor effective start.

- 213-195-A, odd POWER block separated into two Hankel matrices by a↔1/a. For M_n(t)=Σm w(tw)^n, w=(t−λ²)^−1, alternating differences strictly positive for all n≥0,t>0, orders j≤10⁹, by the heat trace of the centered zeros and Z2. All j at one t is equivalent to RH by Hausdorff; antecedent of the finite wall phase-101/033/037. Does not imply general PSD of the sectors.

- 213-195-A, Hausdorff POWER differences. Each row with n,t fixed ends positive with equivalent Γ(n+1/2)j^(−n−1/2)log j/(4π√t). At t=1 the binomial variation of every diagonal n+j=N recovers exactly at root N the supremum of √(1+4(Re λ)²/|1−λ²|²) by a Fourier test; under failure the negative mass grows exponentially on every large diagonal. Control by rows insufficient and collective subexponential bound open.

- 213-195-A, uniform positive strip of POWER differences at t=1: there exist δ,J with A(n,j)>0 for all j≥J and n≤δ√j. Moving-saddle equivalent when n→∞ and n=o(√j), with principal contribution of ordinates |γ|≈√(j/(n+1)) in width √j/(n+1)→∞. Z2 is not required; the upper indices and the control of mass on complete diagonals remain.

- 213-195-A, positive sector of the Hausdorff POWER table at t=1: for all large N and n/N≥1/(1+(G−40)²), G=3·10¹², A(n,N−n)>0 uniformly by binomial comparison with an ordinate in [G−40,G−20] certified by Z2–Z3. Under failure, at a smaller rational slope there exists a window of fixed length containing exponentially weighted negative mass on every large diagonal. Small positive slopes remain open.

- 213-195-A, cross-check with 207: 4^K t A(K−1,K;t)=b_K(√t) exactly; each interior entry of the table is a positive mean of the same packet at order K≥max(n+1,j), with random beta scale. Do not reopen the diagonal as a distinct mechanism. Unconditional pointwise bound at every t>0 for max(n+1,j)≤⌊πG/2⌋ by direct phase control in Z2.

- 213-195-A, uniform scale: b_{10¹⁸}(u)>0 for all u>0, by concentration with quantitative cells and Z2–Z3. The beta mean implies A(n,j;t)>0 for all t>0, max(n+1,j)≤10¹⁸. Also b_K(u)>0 for K≥10¹⁸, u≥10⁴√K. Cross-check 205 (rows/cones at fixed rate) and 207–210 (same central family). The unverified fixed scale at unbounded orders remains open.

- 213-195-A, quantitative transfer of the square of 10¹⁸ to squares of polynomials with real coefficients in both Hankel sectors. For 2m≤N and certified tilted data: L(P²)≥(1+ε)L(P)²/L(1)−εL(P₂), ε=m/(N−m), P₂ carries Bernstein coefficients squared. The constant is optimal with only finite exchangeability, by an urn of fixed composition. PSD is not proved without a corrector.
- 213-195-A, refinement of the Kneser corrector. For the composition law q_k the loss of degree one is identified exactly by hypergeometric regression and the dispersion of the conditional means is retained. The residual loss is bounded by (m)_3/(N−m)_3 for m≥3. The uniform comparison for ξ remains open.
- 213-195-A, internal falsifier of the truncated hypergeometric comparison. With t=γ₁², tilt h=1000 and P=(1−2x)² its lower bound is negative for ALL admissible elevation degrees. Explicit loss of Johnson's degree two, stable under the real spectral tail of ξ. Discard the truncated sufficient criterion.
- 213-195-A, exact sign of L((1−2x)^{2d}) at t=γ₁², h=1000, uniformity of reach for every integer d≥0. A term of height G+√(dt) pays the whole adverse tail. Includes the counterexample to the truncated bound and does not certify linear combinations.
- 213-195-A, consecutive complete blocks R^d,...,R^{d+m}. For each fixed t,h,m there is definite positivity for every sufficiently large shift d, by matrix convergence in y=dx to gamma moments of shape h+1/2 and rate 4, using Z3. Includes all real coefficients; threshold without uniformity in the dimension.
- 213-195-A, sufficient threshold of sublinear width in translated blocks. For t=1,h=0, PSD along a subsequence with m=⌈10^(−24)d/log d⌉ is equivalent to RH under Z2/Z3: interpolation at the nodes up to d/(log d)^4 and a power that suppresses the tail isolate any nonreal pair. The implication is proved; the positive estimate at that width is open.
- 213-195-A, strict positivity with growing width m=⌊log d/(32 log log d)⌋ at t=1,h=0. Uniform comparison with projection of the zeros onto the axis, using Markov for the floor and damping in the tail. The width sufficient to detect every exterior zero remains asymptotically much larger.
- 213-195-A, quantitative improvement of the projection of translated blocks. For each positive α<1/13, m=⌊d^α⌋ admits definite positivity eventually at t=1,h=0. Local Markov with exponential normalization and tail estimate by Chebyshev. The scale d/log d remains open.
- 213-195-A, exact conditional threshold for a nonempty finite set of exceptions. At t=1, m≈c d/log d, eventual positive sign for c<b*/2 by interpolation at separated critical ordinates, indefinite for c>b*/2 by isolation, b*=min exterior −log|R|. Every width o(d/log d) is compatible with finite exceptions.
- 213-195-A, edge and inertia of the blocks of width ⌊cd/log d⌋. For finite exceptions the eventual negative index counts exactly distinct pairs with −log|R|<2c; ties are absorbed in the positive definite part. For infinitely many exceptions the index diverges for every c>0. The unconditional estimate of that index remains open.
- 213-195-A, exact exponential size of the negative part in monomial basis x. For visible finite exceptions, log D_d/d→−2b*, and for infinitely many →0. At the sufficient width, by Z2 it suffices to establish an additive error exp(−10^(−24)d+o(d)) in Euclidean norm of coefficients along a subsequence. Estimate open.
- 213-195-A, unconditional bound of the defect at ALL monomial widths, even ℓ². The norm error when truncating at k is ≤C((k+1)/(2ed))^(k+1). With the positive block k=⌊d^α⌋, 0<α<1/13, the defect is ≤exp(−(1−α+o(1))d^α log d). Passing to linear exponent in d at the sufficient width is missing.
- 213-195-A, stable transfer by spectral interpolation. D_{d,∞}≤Ck³D_{d,k}+exp(−2k log k+2k log log k+O(k)) uniformly in d. For k≈cd/log d, the remainder is exp(−2cd+o(d)), preserving the sufficient error exp(−cd+o(d)). The estimate of the block itself is missing.
- 213-195-A, falsifier from finite data plus precision at every algebraic order. Two model spectra with integer multiplicities, identical prescribed initial moments in finite number by adjustment of heights (Vandermonde), difference O(exp(−ηd)) uniform in width and opposite sign in the PSD/indefinite sense. Does not impose the arithmetic identity of ξ.
- 213-195-A, DUPLICATE of 213-412-A, with I(U)=D(U)/2. The rectangular formula and the unconditional bound appear in 213-413-A. Primitive of the logarithmic defect between orbits and projection to equal ordinates. U times the integral tends to 2Σa² (infinity included); obtained by second difference and triangular weight. Arithmetic control of the projection missing. A nontrivial finite surgery does not preserve the Dirichlet decay in both models with the same archimedean factors.
- 213-195-A, conditional adversarial proof of arithmetic sampling: starting from ξ under RH, finite surgery above G introduces an exterior orbit preserving ξ′/ξ exactly on any prescribed finite list of real abscissae >1, by independence of rational kernels and adjustment of ordinates. The genuine Euler values are preserved there, not the series as an analytic identity.
- 213-195-A, explicit arithmetic matrix by Taylor of (ξ′/ξ)(1/2+√(1−v))/√(1−v). Cut of the von Mangoldt series at exp(40d) gives operator error O(exp(−2d)) for all m≤d. The precision of the cut suffices for the sign criterion; the spectral inequality of the truncated matrices remains open.
  Verified antecedent: POWER_CONFLUENT_BRIDGE_014 §7 already has cut exp(40N/u) with exponential precision. Cauchy's formula specifies the translated coordinates; the truncation mechanism is already covered.
- 213-195-A, the pole alone forces liminf log X/d≥4log(5/3) in the raw Euler cut. In the translated blocks the factor 1−3x/4 annihilates it exactly and preserves detection by isolation and its exponential tolerance. Antecedents of polar elimination P46 and necessary cuts POWER 014. Estimate of the remainder open.
- 213-195-A, low-frequency obstruction after annihilating the pole. At Q=x every cut X≤exp(C√d) gives value ≤−c₀/√d finally for each fixed C, while the exact form is O(d^(−2)). The local transform is a positive Gaussian in log n/√d. For exponential precision one needs log X/√d→∞.
  Antecedents: 211-A and 212-A (cut at Gaussian scale), POWER 014 §9 (falsifier without pole). Here the zero phase forces the adverse sign for every sufficiently large d.
- 213-195-A, carrier [R(1−x)]^d and polar annihilation: preserves detection at the decisive width and tolerance; the archimedean part minus the single term n=2 has floor −O(exp(−10^(−13)d)) uniform for m≤d. The net contribution of the remaining prime terms is pending; it is not a two-sided approximation by the fixed cut.
- 213-195-A, in the carrier with central suppression, ALL p^k with k≥3 are absorbed in the archimedean half with error O(exp(−10^(−22)d)) uniform in m≤d. As a sufficient condition it remains to control primes and squares against the remaining half. Absolute convergence is not attributed to those two sectors.
- 213-195-A, NO-GO for splitting the archimedean term in halves and demanding the decisive floor of A/2−S₁−S₂. Interpolating test in a gap of the spectrum: it annihilates the complete form up to exponential tail, while A/2−S₃ retains positive mass ≫d^(−2) before normalizing. After normalizing, the defect exceeds the required tolerance. Control all the pieces jointly.
- 213-195-A, transfer of tolerance in coefficient norm for numerators with real roots: the defect over all squares is ≤4^m times that over real-rooted squares, by positive expansion and Jensen mean. At width m≈cd/log d no exponential rate is lost. Antecedent R160_X_C1 R2 for the physical minimum; the arithmetic sign remains open.
- 213-195-A, double-displacement criterion at t=1: with j=⌊d/log log d⌋ fixed in the weight x^(2j)H^(2d)V² the decisive floor over numerators of free degree ≤⌈log d⌉ suffices. Isolation up to height √log d and exponential suppression of the tail. Increases the total degree and changes the weight; does not inherit the positivity of the block at fixed h.
- 213-195-A, 2×2 criterion at rational slopes 0<α<4/G² for the carrier without pole. A dominant exterior pair forces S₀S₂−S₁² negative for every large d at some fixed slope, without residual oscillation. Specialization of domination in slopes and Prony determinants; trades a sequence of blocks for a family of slopes. Arithmetic inequality open.
- 213-195-A, strict sign of the 2×2 block for every fixed slope α≥(3+1000/G)/G² and d sufficiently large: two verified nodes give a rank-two floor above the exterior rate. From the criterion 0<α<4/G² the lower band down to zero remains pending. Does not enlarge T.
- 213-195-A, localization in height for the 2×2 block. At the saddle slope α(u), u=1/(1+U²), it suffices that the zeros in [U−1000,U+1000] lie on the line to obtain eventual positive sign; the exterior ones outside that band lose rate against two local ordinates. Does not require verifying the whole head nor certify new bands.
- 213-195-A, unconditional control in mean over unverified heights: the positive excess of spectral rate over the real saddle, scaled by U⁴, has mean O(1/log²T) on [T,2T]. Taylor gives the profile 6[δ²−(g−U)²] and Selberg (413) controls the third moment. Does not imply pointwise sign.
- 213-195-A, falsifier of passing from local rate excess to sign of the determinant. Models with E(U)=0 on a fixed interval and determinant eventually negative throughout it. For a pair separated by δ the change is detected at scale log(1/δ)/log(L/L₂), where L/L₂ is the previous discrete gap. Does not imply failure of sign for ξ.
- 213-195-A, quantitative DUPLICATION for the aggregation by envelope of slopes: when optimizing in α the advantage per node lies between L and L^5 with L=|x|+|1−x| of the variation of the Bernstein diagonals already indexed. Discard as an independent route based only on rates; does not identify finite arithmetic sums.
- 213-195-A, asymptotics of D_X for fixed Euler cut: normalized by d²/B^(4d) it tends to a positive constant by h_X(U)². Any nonzero sign of the density gives a determinant eventually positive; at a simple zero it is negative. The order of limits with X fixed does not verify the global criterion.
- 213-195-A, sign law of the determinant at moving cut log X=λ√d. Normalized profile proportional to cos²θ/(2κ)−λ²/(4κ²); for λ>√(2κ) the cut is negative for every large d, even at slopes of fully verified sign. Scalar Gaussian antecedent 211-A; do not extrapolate to growing λ.
- 213-195-A, sharp cut compensated by X^(1−s)/(s−1): cancels the Gaussian/PNT main term of the determinant at log X≈λ√d. A single prime leaves a matrix jump ≥const B^(2d)log p/(d√p), by the two sine/cosine phases. Prevents uniform exponential relative precision in X even after continuous correction. Does not decide sign.
- 213-195-A, unconditional positivity of the complete 2×2 matrix as j→∞, j=o(√d). In the centered and rescaled basis one obtains the Gaussian Gram of 1,−2y by local count Z3. The limiting variance is strict; the fixed unverified positive slopes remain.
- 213-195-A, frontier j=⌊λ√d⌋: for each fixed λ>0 the COMPLETE 2×2 block is positive definite for density one of d. Local projected floor on two intervals, stability against small horizontal displacements and exclusion by Selberg density (413). No uniform sign at the exceptional d nor at fixed slopes.
- 213-195-A, exact classification of the sublinear regime of the 2×2 determinant. Eventual sign for every sequence j→∞, j/d→0 is equivalent to finiteness of the exterior orbits; it is also equivalent to eventual uniform positive definiteness in some cone 0≤j≤εd. A finite exception remains invisible. For global closure keep specific positive slopes or growing dimension.
- 213-195-A, link of the sublinear band with the barrier C_B already recorded in R162_2501. If Σ_orb m a²<∞, the coefficient w³(A−P′/P) tends to 4Σ_orb m a² by the representation of 412, while ζ′/ζ=O(2^(−w)). The missing projected coefficient is identified; Euler alone does not estimate it.
- 213-195-A, proof of compatibility with window P46: for a fixed slope, every factor of the spectral modulus of the 2×2 block has at most C_α |I|/√d of its L² mass in I, uniformly in phase and direction of the plane. Restricting to a fixed certified window loses almost the entire norm. Does not exclude a new control of cross terms between windows.
- 213-195-A, crossings between two copies of a fixed compact primitive pulse of sinc product, without exterior zeros. Absolute subexponential bound only at h=n^(1/4) is equivalent to RH: Gevrey interpolation with k≈2h/log h and Laplace residues. The small window controls the diagonal terms; the arithmetic floor on the crossings remains open.
- 213-195-A, explicit primitive pulse of radius <2.59 with quadratic bias 1/2 and absolute critical contribution <.000083. On the mesh V=n^(1/4) it would suffice that |B(V)+1/2|≤.001 for the sum over ordinary primes. Explicit antecedents of eight boxes and mesh H^(−3) in this same round; the arithmetic inequality remains open.
- 213-195-A, strict positivity of the complete form in span(f,T_h f) for ALL separations 0<h≤10⁶ of the explicit pulse of radius <2.59. Two zeros with quotient certified by Arb give simultaneous margin and the Gevrey boxes suppress the exterior ones up to that distance. Not a window extension for arbitrary functions.
- 213-195-A, complete form strictly positive for three equispaced copies f,T_h f,T_{2h}f up to diameter 10⁶. Arb certificate for 15 ratios of gaps among four zeros; interpolation in three phases and divided-difference basis near h=0. Extension of dimension, not of general window.
- 213-195-A, lattice t_n=nh+1/n detects every isolated finite exterior front for any h>0, even with exact alias: zeros of finite order of exponential sums per class and Cesàro quadratic mean. Together with positivity in all sublinear sequences of the 2×2 it separates the infinite and finite cases. Antecedents of step selection 089–090.
- 213-195-A, primitive pulse of support [−2,2] by autocorrelated exponential boxes: |arg F(z)²|<.48 on the divisor. On any fixed lattice nh, the coefficients coinciding in phase do not cancel, and an attained exterior supremum is detected with its exact exponent at positive lower density, without gap hypothesis or finiteness of the front. Arithmetic bound and case of unattained supremum pending.
- 213-195-A, averaged crossings with n uniform boxes: exact rate R_h=max exp(h Re z)|sinh z/z|; log R_h/h recovers the supremal abscissa even if not attained. Z2 certifies R_h<.55 for integer velocities 2 to 56 and negative limit bias of the prime average at every scale. Does not resolve unbounded velocities.
- 213-195-A, unconditional definite positivity in span(f,T_t(μ^{*n}*f)) for every large n and |t|≤51n. After normalizing by the first ordinate there remains strict margin of the second on the fixed diagonal. The physical diameter can grow without limit; for a global criterion unbounded velocities are required, not just unbounded separations.
- 213-195-A, positive compact average ν by trace of a 2×2 matrix, radius one. Sign of the mixed plane for every large n and |t|≤(2G−5√G)n with G=3·10¹²; the fixed kernel preserves detection. A uniform comparison over the whole strip by moduli of any symmetric average of radius one has barrier h≤πG by harmonic measure. Does not enlarge general T.
- 213-195-A, optimal principal constant 2 in the velocity barrier of the compact average. Three lines after g=G without ζ give exterior sup |J(1/2+ig)|≥exp(−G)J(1/2), whence h<2G for the uniform margin. Tuned positive kernel certifies the plane up to h=2G−4G^(1/3), within 57700 of the limit for the verified G.
- 213-195-A, criterion of periodic separations with gaps: for fixed h an absolute subexponential ceiling of C_f over nh+I suffices, any fixed open subinterval I. Selberg makes summable the radii π/g of positive filters of three atoms that annihilate the tail Re z>ε and preserve the target; n+1/n avoids the remaining finite alias. Includes unattained supremum. The arithmetic bound remains open.
- 213-195-A, exact ordinary rate of local oscillation of the crossing and of B_f over primes: for any fixed interval I and fixed degree k, t^(−1)log(1+inf_P∫_I|B_f(t+s)−P(s)|ds)→sup(Reρ−1/2). Selberg plus positive filter of short radius and separation of exponentials in L¹ modulo polynomials. A subexponential subsequence would suffice; the arithmetic ceiling is not proved.
- 213-195-A, threshold of the local fit of the sum over primes. For k log(k+2)=o(t) the L¹ defect against polynomials of degree k preserves exactly the rate Δ. If k log(k+2)/t→c, the general floor is (Δ−c)_+ and is attained as exact rate with finitely many exceptions. Selberg filter, finite isolation and differences of step 1/(k+1); ceiling by Taylor in the finite case.
- 213-195-A, exact reduction of the local error to nine disjoint bands of primes. The annihilator (36−D²)^4 of the exponential kernel leaves sources at log p+r, |r|≤4; the remainder is absorbed in eight edge modes. The L¹ error after fitting preserves the rate Δ. Its subexponential estimate along a subsequence is open.
- 213-195-A ↔ 230–231-A, a single band with affine fit is an antecedent. Quantitative extension: logarithmic width (log X)^(−a), a fixed positive, detects with exact rate every supremum Δ>3a/(4+6a) when using Ingham's count also at the head. With finite exceptions it detects any Δ>0. The bound of the local fit along a subsequence is missing.
- 213-195-A ↔ 231/235, resolution of the affine defect. On a band of length L, interpolating θ on a mesh of step H≤X/√L changes √D by O(log X) by monotonicity and integer count. The exponent remains intact. The joint bound of the profile between nodes remains open.
- 213-195-A, falsifier of the exclusive use of masses per cell. A weighted subset of integers has total mass X+O(log X) and error O(X^δ+log X) in each cell of length √X of [X,2X], but √D grows like X^δ/√180 for any 0<δ<1/2. The spatial coherence of the errors matters even with relative precision 1+o(1).
- 213-195-A, reach of local statistics. Two ideal profiles in N=4m² cells share even all the counts of consecutive chains of length ≤m; their defects √D are respectively O(1) and of order m. The proof preserves the internal order of the chains.
- 213-195-A ↔ 235, detection with fixed list if the extreme abscissa β>1/2 has a finite family separated by a gap. The Fourier matrix of the powers has full rank already with K fixed, hence max_{1≤m≤K}|S_q(m)|≥c q^β at every large scale. K depends on the spectrum; no ceiling is proved for the arithmetic modes.
- 213-195-A ↔ 235, improvement of the fixed detector. It suffices that the extreme abscissa β>1/2 be attained. C² approximation of the filter with null mean and edges costs O(q^β) per unit of error, even with infinitely many extreme zeros and without gap. The arithmetic ceiling and the case of unattained supremum remain open for this fixed list.
- 213-195-A ↔ 235–236, converse of the fixed detector over integer scales. If the supremum β>1/2 is not attained, all fixed modes differ from the first cosine by o(q^β) and share its small subsequence at that normalization. The uniform floor c q^β for some fixed list is exactly equivalent to β being attained.
- 213-195-A ↔ 230/235–238, transfer of the crossings to prime scales. Ingham with spectral ceiling β<1 gives a prime at distance x^a for (1+β)/3<a<β; 238 covers β=1. The cost of displacing all fixed modes is o(x^β), so the characterization of the uniform floor also holds over prime q.
- 213-195-A ↔ 236–237, exact localization of the crossings by jumps. By PNT the original cosine decreases between events and gives 0≤F(p/2)≤log p at infinitely many prime upper extremes. The factor 2−u reverses the drift, suppresses the entry jump and preserves the exterior poles, giving false negatives of size log p at prime lower extremes if RH fails.
- 213-195-A ↔ 236, sampling by prime entries. Between consecutive p/2 and r/2, F(r/2)−log r≤F(x)≤F(p/2). The maximum of |F(p/2)| over 2X≤p≤4X preserves the whole exponent 1/2+B when B>0, even without attained abscissa. Simultaneous ceiling along a subsequence of bands open.
- 213-195-A ↔ 236/238, discrete second moment at the prime entries. With only the weight log p, the normalized average X⁻²Σ log p |F(p/2)|² preserves the exponent 2B. If B>0 there are X^(1−o(1)) entries of size ≥X^(1/2+B−δ) in each band for each δ>0. Bounding the average along a subsequence is missing.
- 213-195-A, second moment at prime entries under RH is O(1) by local L² sum over blocks of zeros and Brun–Titchmarsh. Diagonal of interior primes (3/2+o(1))log X unconditionally. After excluding the extreme prime, the sign requires cancellation down to O(1) between that exact diagonal and the distinct triples; that ceiling along a subsequence suffices.
- 213-195-A ↔ 233/236, sign dichotomy of triples. Under RH the normalized sum U∼−(3/2)log X; if β>1/2, U=X^(2β−1+o(1)) eventually positive. U≤0 in arbitrarily high bands suffices. Averaging the frequency per prime gives −3/2+o(1) unconditionally by orthogonality, but leaves open the sign of the arithmetic frequency 2.
- 213-195-A ↔ 233, limit of frequency-biased averages. The aggregate sign with mass X^(−o(1)) at k=2 would suffice by positivity of squares. If a sign is imposed off the diagonal pair by pair on the real primes, the sector 11p/12<r<p forces ν_p(2)≪log p/p for any distribution. The cancellation between sectors remains open.
- 213-195-A ↔ 233–234, exclusion of frequencies near rationals. PNT in progressions of fixed modulus and Σ_{d prime}1/d=∞ allow leaving the frequency 2 and making the normalized mean of triples ≤−A for any prescribed constant A, in every high band. The target frequency still weighs only O(1/p).
- 213-195-A ↔ 237, sign of triples for consecutive blocks without averaging frequencies. In arbitrarily high bands there are ≫√X/log X consecutive exterior primes with interior sum −(1/4+o(1))p log p at k=2. The rise of F(x)/√x from 0 to 1/10 demands that number of small entries. Control of the complement of the band missing.
- 213-195-A ↔ 230/236, density at the extreme amplitude. For β>1/2 attained there are c,η>0 and a fraction ≥η of prime entries with |F(p/2)|≥c X^β in every high band. Without maximum that fraction is o(1) for each c>0. Proof by uniform L² tail and sampling on short intervals; does not control the sign-change threshold in the case without maximum.
- 213-195-A, under RH the exceptional percentage at margin −p log p/10 per exterior prime is O(exp(−c(log X)^(1/4))). Spectral cut at exp(d√V), L² tail and sampling of the complete cosine by cells. The unconditional favorable block of 237/195-A does not imply this estimate.
- 213-195-A, consequence of the cardinality of the second moment: the rank statistic X^(1−η) of |F(p/2)| preserves the detection exponent for each fixed η in (0,1). ≤X^0.99 positive interior contributions in arbitrarily high bands suffice, of arbitrary magnitude. At the threshold √X log³X for the cosine the counting criterion is moreover necessary.
- 213-195-A ↔ 236/247, triples with cubic weight of half window. At threshold zero, ≤X^0.99 exceptions in arbitrarily high bands is equivalent to the global sign: under RH each U_p∼−p log p/1680, with an exterior zero there are X^(1−o(1)) positives per band. The unconditional count is open.
- 213-195-A, cubic with an arbitrary prime per cell: for N=ceil(X^η), 0<η<1/4 fixed, RH gives all signs negative; an exterior zero forces N^(1−o(1)) positives in every band and for every selection. Continuity in events and the zero mean of uw′ give oscillation O(X^(β−η+ε)) per cell. Control of the signs of a selection missing.
- 213-195-A, cubic sign if there are m distinct finite extreme zeros with β>1/2. In each band a fraction 1−o(1) of the primes has U_p>0 even without gap. With gap up to σ the complementary count costs O_ε(X^(1−(β−σ)/(m−1)+ε)) by Vandermonde and real sublevels. The majority for real primes without spectral hypothesis remains open.
- 213-195-A ↔ 230/242/247, log-Gaussian weight of zero Mellin mean. A positive fraction of exterior primes with U≤0 in arbitrarily high bands is equivalent to the global sign, even without spectral maximum. Interpolating at ≍log X nodes separated by Brun–Titchmarsh forces power saving over the whole interval. The compact interior support is lost and proving the positive fraction remains open.
- 213-195-A ↔ 242, improvement of the Gaussian majority. For each fixed A it suffices to have ≥X/(log X)^(1+A) primes with U≤0 in arbitrarily high bands. Disc of radius (log X)^(1/4) and ≍log X/log log X separated nodes extracted from the good set; the loss by concentration and the Cauchy remainder are controlled simultaneously.
- 213-195-A, Gaussian count under attained exterior maximum. Normal analytic family with uniform floor ⇒ bounded local order ⇒ O(X^(1−κ)) favorable entries for some κ>0, even with infinitely many extreme zeros and without gap. A favorable count X^(1−o(1)) would exclude this scenario; there is no unconditional bound of that strength.
- 213-195-A, lower count for the Gaussian detector at generic fixed dilation. For almost every λ∈[1,2] there are ≫√X/√log X consecutive primes with U(p/λ)≤0 in arbitrarily high bands, unconditionally; with β>1/2 one obtains ≫X^(3/2−β)/√log X. Crossing by Landau, derivative by Cauchy and density of dilations by PNT/Brun–Titchmarsh. Does not identify the endpoint λ=2 nor reach the sufficient inverse-logarithmic density.
- 213-195-A ↔ 230/238, Gaussian recurrence without spectral maximum. A positive filter that annihilates all zeros with Reρ≥σ and the absolute local floor force both excursions ≫X^b₀ in each [X,CX]. If 1/2<β<11/12, the short PNT places blocks of ≫X^(3/2−β)/√log X favorable signs in each band of sufficiently wide ratio, even at λ=2.
- 213-195-A ↔ 230/238/247, sign of the Gaussian linear sum. Under RH S(x)<−√x/5 eventually by the bias of squares. If RH fails, in each sufficiently wide band of fixed ratio there are X^(1−o(1)) primes of each sign at λ=2, even for β=1. The comparison of the weighted mean of log(2r/p) with 1 in bands of growing ratio would suffice.
- 213-195-A, linear Gaussian sum: Jensen bounds the real zeros per band of fixed ratio by o(log X/log log X), or by O(1) if β>1/2 is attained. If RH fails there appear blocks of X^(1−o(1)) consecutive primes of each sign in every sufficiently wide band. Finding only favorable blocks with that exponent does not discriminate the global sign.
- 213-195-A, antisymmetric identity at x=p/e. The prefix Σ_{p≤Y}(log p)/p² S(p/e) is strictly negative without RH: only pairs p≤Y<r of fixed sign survive. Its opposite J(Y) converges to exp(−1/2)/2 by PNT. The sign at one prime is equivalent to the direction of the jump of J; the resolved prefixes do not control those jumps.
- 213-195-A, cut J: exp(1/2)J−1/2=A−1+R exactly, A the Gaussian prime mass with weight log r/r. With β<1, the integer term of two discrepancies R is O_ε(Y^(2β−2+ε)); if β<3/4 it is smaller than Y^(−1/2). Linear sign and the endpoint β=1 open.
- 213-195-A, dyadic oscillation of the positive cut J. In each [X,2X] the range V of J satisfies log V/log X→β−1 for every β, even β=1. The total variation is measured with |S(p/e)| and Jensen bounds the reversals of direction. A range X^(−1/2+o(1)) along a subsequence would suffice without controlling the center nor each jump; remains open.
- 213-195-A ↔ 238, on [X,2X] the oscillation of the quadratic error R costs O(exp(−c(log X/log log X)^(1/3)) osc J), even for β=1. Identity dJ=B dθ and exp(−1/2)dA=B dy; short quadrature and few sign reversals. The control is of increments, not of the level of R.
- 213-195-A, fixed difference D₂(y)=A(2y)−A(y). Under RH it is positive of order y^(−1/2); with exterior zeros it exhibits both excursions even at y=p/√2 because 2^(ρ−1)−1 never vanishes. Prefixes Σ(log p)/p D₂(p/√2)>0 unconditionally and tend to (log 2)/2 by antisymmetry. Local comparison of two positive masses open.
- 213-195-A, global falsifier of the passage prefix→local sign. A sequence of integers with PNT in all fixed progressions and eventual exclusion of every fixed divisor preserves the positive prefixes and their limit, but D₂ changes sign with amplitude Y^(−α), 0<α<1/2. Uses rounding by classes of growing moduli; not a counterexample for the primes.
- 213-195-A, D₂ for real primes by Λ=(−μ log)*1. The explicit positive bias of squares is exp(1/8)(1−1/√2)/(2√Y); for every a>1 the Möbius sum with |log(d/Y)|≤a√log Y suffices. Both tails cost O(Y^(−a²/2+o(1))) in absolute value by Gaussian Mellin. Central cancellation open.
- 213-195-A, Möbius band of D₂: μ*1 allows changing log d to log(d/Y) with superpolynomially small remainder. Even the optimal centering has strictly positive limiting absolute cost, given by the median of |W(exp(−u))|. The root scale is not reached by optimizing only that constant; the signed cancellation remains.
- 213-195-A, translations of the Möbius identities. With only ratio 2 a positive L¹ floor remains at frequency 2π/log 2 for the centered weight. Ratios 2 and 3 together eliminate that floor: arbitrary L¹ approximation by finite combinations of identities, without rate nor control of the coefficients at root scale.
- 213-195-A, one-sided limit for the scales 2/3. A zero of real part b forces continuous L¹ error ≥exp(−(1−b+o(1))R) in the liminf sense if the translations are ≥−R and log(1+Σ|c|)=o(R²). Even the critical zeros prevent reaching root scale with R≤(1−δ)log Y. Upward translations can be arbitrary; the discrete cancellation remains free.
- 213-195-A, pointwise expansion of the weight u f by translations at a single ratio with explicit coefficients h and −Λ(n)/n. When truncating at R=mh there remains at u=−R+v the discrepancy hΣ f(v+jh)−∫ f(v+s)ds, strictly positive for fixed large v. The error mass moves to the endpoint and the sum with μ reconstructs the original difference with Λ.
- 213-195-A, truncated edge after μ*1: at Y=exp(mh−w) its signed limit is h g(w−h)−∫_[w−h,w]g. There is a unique phase w∈(h/2,h) that annihilates the constant. The remainder is exactly a weighted discrepancy of Λ over a half-line; root scale and control in bands missing.
- 213-195-A, independent cut of Λ. At every scale Y one can adjust N≍Y by finite search in the positive tail of φ to pay the signed remainder with O(log Y/Y), smaller than the root scale. The central comparison remains in a prefix of mixed signs and N depends on the arithmetic data.
- 213-195-A, cut by sign of the weight at ratio 2. The Mellin responses of the two halves are ±h g(h/2)/z²+O(|z|⁻³); joining them gives exactly 2sinh(hz/2)exp(z²/2). Any other fixed cut produces opposite terms of order 1/z. Bounds by separate moduli lose the Gaussian attenuation.
- 213-195-A, optimal positive separation with reserved smoothing. Splitting the difference of Gaussians of variance 1−v by sign and then convolving with g_v preserves the full weight. Each half attenuates by exp(−vγ²/2) and has the smallest possible mass 2Φ(a/√(1−v))−1 in that class. The uniform arithmetic comparison in Y remains open.
- 213-195-A, exact interior quadratic average when sliding the cut: 2∫R_I=||g_{1/2}*ν_I||²−||(g_{1/2}*ν_I)'||². The block |τ|≥1 has nonpositive sign for every band. The low frequency and the external pairs with explicit intersection weight remain; does not give the linear sign of A.
- 213-195-A, interior average with weight v^(−3/2) over the variances ≥v₀. It is exactly √(2/π)ν(I)²−2√v₀||g_{v₀/2}*ν||²₂. With zero mass it is negative at all combined frequencies. For the original discrepancy a single explicit mass remains; the identity does not decide the individual variance nor the external pairs.
- 213-195-A ↔ 226, falsifier at fixed variance for the interior average: in any band two positive densities can match any finite initial list of Lebesgue moments and produce opposite signs at the same variance, even though all their cumulative averages in variance are negative. Do not extrapolate that identity to the primes without arithmetic input.
- 213-195-A, signed bias of the sieve P⁻(n)>√n/c with fixed c>1. The balanced semiprimes add to D₂ the term −4 log c log 2/(log Y)²+O_c((log Y)⁻³); the sieved comparison remains negative unconditionally. Makes precise in sign the semiprime antecedent for absolute error.
- 213-195-A, additive sieve P⁻(n)>√n−√loglog n. Excluding the squares, the whole error of distinct semiprimes is O(Y⁻¹/²/√loglog Y) by progressions and Brun–Titchmarsh, without cancellation. Including the squares does add an explicit term of root order. Sign of the sieved comparison open.
- 213-195-A, additive sieve without squares: any H(n)=o(log n) alters D₂ by o(Y⁻¹/²) by upper sieve of pairs. For H(n)=log n the short consecutive gaps force spurious mass ≍Y⁻¹/² and drops of that mass ≥c/√Y along a subsequence. No optimal-constant threshold is asserted.
- 213-195-A, H=c log n without squares. Some fixed c₀>0 preserves the exact sign criterion thanks to the root margin under RH and the uniform bound limsup √Y E_c≤C c. For fixed large c even under RH the sieved comparison is negative along a subsequence, by counting of pairs within boxes and telescoping.
- 213-195-A, sieve with positive margin: for H/log n→∞ and H=n^o(1), the mass B_H of all survivors (squares admitted) satisfies √Y(B_H−1)→+∞ under RH. With an exterior zero it falls below 1 in each sufficiently wide band. A lower bound B_H≥1 in bands of growing ratio suffices; arithmetic estimate open.
- 213-195-A, spectral calibration of the sieve Hδ=n^δ(log n)², 0<δ<1/2. The sieved mass exceeds 1 eventually (or in bands of growing ratio) exactly when sup Reρ≤1/2+δ, endpoint included thanks to the floor of semiprimes by boxes. A sequence δ→0 without uniformity between scales suffices; the arithmetic bounds remain open.
- 213-195-A ↔ 371/400, B_H(Y)>1 unconditionally at every large scale for H(n)=√n exp(−d log n/Q(log n)), Q(t)=(log t)^(2/3)(log log t)^(1/3), some d>0. The elementary floor of pairs exceeds the Gaussian error of the known zero-free region. The moving exponent tends to 1/2 and does not cover any fixed δ<1/2.
- 213-195-A ↔ 238, 7/24<δ<1/2: for H=c n^δ log n the spurious mass is asymptotic to 4c exp((δ−1/2)²/2)Y^(δ−1/2) without RH. At β=1/2+δ the critical coefficient is identified by the Gaussian sum of the extreme zeros; if there is no maximum any c>0 will do. Critical equality case open.
- 213-195-A, H=c n^δ log n at all exponents 0<δ<1/2: the liminf of the normalized spurious mass is ≥2c exp((δ−1/2)²/2) by boxes and ordinary PNT. With c=1 it dominates all zeros of the extreme abscissa by Hadamard; equivalent to β≤1/2+δ including the edge. The exact constant below 7/24 is not determined.
- 213-195-A ↔ 102–103, arbitrary fixed mask of squares: under RH its capacity to compensate an ordinate γ, in units of the Gaussian multiplier, is ≤1/π against multiplicity m≥1, even choosing each w_p in [0,1]. A two-sided error o(Y⁻¹/²) is impossible by that route; the one-sided comparison is not affected.
- 213-195-A ↔ 102–103, binary mask of squares. Under RH a fixed subset of relative logarithmic density strictly below the constant threshold preserves B_w>1 with root margin. Modulation by finitely many ordinates and cumulative rounding with cost O(log Y/Y). Gives no arithmetic sign without RH.
- 213-195-A, ordinary density of squares. By PNT every mask of ordinary relative density λ behaves like the constant weight λ up to o(Y⁻¹/²), without RH. The selection that improves the logarithmic threshold has explicit oscillating ordinary proportion, with factors 1/(1+2iγ). Do not infer an improvement for natural density.
- 213-195-A ↔ 268, exact constant of semiprimes for H=c n^δ log n extended to δ>1/12. PNT in almost all intervals and Brun–Titchmarsh in short cells transfer the asymptotics to almost all prime starts and control the exceptional contribution. No new zero-free region is certified.
- 213-195-A ↔ 230/268, for H=c n^δ log n the spectral ceiling β<1/2+3δ already suffices for the exact constant 4c at every 0<δ<1/2. The quadratic mean of intervals at scale p^(2δ) is controlled by Ingham. At the edge β=1/2+δ the calibration of the constant reaches ALL δ without any hypothesis beyond being on that edge.
- 213-195-A, at β=1/2+δ the sieve H=c n^δ(log n+b) adds 4c exp(s²/2)Y^s(1+b/log Y+O(log⁻²Y)), s=δ−1/2. If there is a gap under the extreme line, at the critical coefficient c any b>0 gives eventual positive sign; the contact without correction b=0 remains open.
- 213-195-A, Gaussian critical contact. The phases align at t=−s. With gap and finite extreme front of rational rank ≤2, the convergents give deficit O(t⁻²) along a sequence and decide the negative sign there for each b<0 at critical c. Conditional result, without window enlargement.
- 213-195-A, critical contact without gap. With attained edge and critical c, for every fixed b the exceptions B_H≤1 occupy logarithmic length o(1) in each translated interval of fixed length. A single extreme ordinate controls the exceptional set. Conditional corollary, independently checked.
- 213-195-A, unconditional floor of pairs by boxes longer than the threshold. For H=c n^δ log n the factor 2c rises to 2c(1+δ²/32). The pairs that are too separated occupy two strips whose cost by Brun–Titchmarsh is quadratic in the widening. The lower bound of the total mass remains open.
- 213-195-A, translated boxes and upper sieve by separation. The semiprime floor improves from 2c to 2c(1+κ) with κ>0 absolute for each fixed δ in (0,1/2). An excessive separation pays both the width of the band of separations and the probability of falling in a single box. No uniformity in the initial scale nor new control of the prime deficit.
- 213-195-A, exceptional-length criterion for the subpower sieve. It suffices to control the logarithmic measure where B_H<1−Y^(−1/2) by X^(−η) in bands [X,C_X X] of growing ratio along a subsequence. With an exterior zero each sufficiently wide fixed band has exceptional measure ≥X^(−o(1)). Corollary of the filter of crossings and of the arithmetic contamination ceiling.
- 213-195-A, Gaussian local concentration in the exceptional-length criterion. If there is an exterior zero, in every sufficiently wide fixed band the adverse measure is ≥exp(−o(log X/log log X)), even without attained front. Polynomial interpolation from the central interval of the filter. It now suffices to have a saving exp(−η log X/log log X) in growing bands along a subsequence; arithmetic estimate open.

The mass of each sign in [t−log t−B,t+log t+B] has limit exponent Δ at all centers if an exterior zero exists, even without attained maximum. For mass corrections ≤X^0.49 a moment at a critical zero persists in the squarefree quadrature. In the lower-budget version the remaining bands still cost ≥X^(1/2−o(1)) in normalized absolute value.

Both sign masses retain exponent Δ at each center if there is an exterior zero; under RH they are subexponential. Only O(x/log t) indices remain in each proportional band. The subexponential upper bound of the off-diagonal correlations along a sequence of centers is open.
